An `Unresolved` operation is judged by its family, as for `CadIr::is_stateless`. A `Native` member states no operation, so this rule does not require a current state at `After(m)` and does not forbid one. Where `m` has no result in a configuration, `After(m)` names no state in it. A container that is a member of a container, ordered or unordered, has no result of its own there: its states are its own, and its parent takes its result only through a member that selects it (§5.8). Where it is ordered, `After(Container(c))` is the state at its rollback position, as the next sentence states, and where it is unordered `After(Container(c))` names no state, since its members have their own. `After(Member::Container(c))` for an ordered container `c` is the state at `c`'s rollback position, read under `c`'s `placement` (§5.2): it has no evaluation of its own, and a pick anchored there resolves in the current state or the evaluation at that rollback position (§5.4, §5.5). It never names a state of `c`'s parent: in an ordered parent, the state leaving a member that is a container is the state entering it. `Start` names only ordered containers. Each state has one spelling: the state entering member k > 0 of an ordered container `c` is `After` the nearest member before k that is a feature, and the state entering a member that no feature of `c` precedes is `Start(c)`. `CurrentState.at` and `StateBase::Current` name a stated rollback position by that spelling, through its member. Where `c`'s rollback is unstated (§5.2), the state at it has no spelling through a member, and `After(Container(c))` is its one spelling, in `CurrentState.at` and `StateBase::Current` too, whether `c` is a root of its scope or a member of a container; otherwise `After(Container(c))` occurs only as a selection anchor outside `c`.

A state at `P` depends on feature `f` when `f` is at or before `P` in `P`'s container chain, or when a feature at or before `P` in that chain depends on `f` transitively (D26). A `Tool(g)` evaluation (§5.4) depends on `g` and on what `g`'s definition depends on. A state that holds instance bodies (§8.1) also depends, through the occurrences of each instance path, on the features of the prototypes those occurrences place, which a name on an instance body may mention (§5.7). This order is computed from containers, dependencies, and instance paths, and every rule below uses it. Positions are ordered only within one scope: no position of one scope is before or after a position of another. A pick is ordered in the scope that holds its target, against its anchored state there (§5.8). Where the target is in the selection's own scope, that state is the selection's anchor, whatever the pick's context (a Fusion pick of another component of the same design). Where the target is in another scope, it is the state of that scope the pick resolves in: the `Pinned` position where the selection is pinned to a position of that scope, and otherwise that scope's current state that holds the target's container (§5.5). Dependencies between scopes are references (D26), and a cycle through them is a Warning, as any dependency cycle is.

### 5.4 Evaluations

```rust
pub struct Evaluation {
    pub id: EvaluationId,
    pub scope: ProductDefinitionId,
    pub configuration: Option<ConfigurationId>,
    pub of: Evaluated,
    pub status: EvaluationStatus,
    pub content: Option<StateContent>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub struct StateContent { pub base: StateBase, pub delta: StateDelta }
pub enum Evaluated { State(Position), Tool(FeatureId) }
pub enum EvaluationStatus { Current, Stale, Failed }
pub enum StateBase { Empty, Current(Position), Evaluation(EvaluationId) }
pub struct StateDelta {
    pub records: Topology,
    pub removed: Vec<RecordRef>,
    pub names: BTreeMap<EntityRef, Option<NameEntry>>,
    pub owners: BTreeMap<BodyId, Option<ProductDefinitionId>>,
    pub members: BTreeMap<OccurrenceId, Option<ProductDefinitionId>>,
    pub instance_bodies: BTreeMap<OccurrencePath, Option<Vec<BodyId>>>,
    pub poses: BTreeMap<OccurrencePath, Option<Transform>>,
}
```

An evaluation is a state of a scope under one configuration: the model at a position, or a feature's tool body. `content` holds the stored state. An evaluation with no content states only the status the source records for a state it does not store. `native_ref` names the source's record of the state where it has one (a SolidWorks PMARK, which `moPMarkRecord_c` joins to its feature, §3.1), so a writer to the same codec re-emits the chain from it.

- **States share records.** A state is its base with a delta applied: the base's records, minus `removed`, with each record of `delta.records` inserted, or replacing the base's record of the same id. `StateBase::Current(p)` is the extent of the scope's current state at position `p` (§5.5): that state's bodies and the records they reach (§5.6), their names, owners, and instance bodies, the occurrence membership of the definitions the scope spans, and that current state's poses; the bodies of other current states and other scopes are not part of it. `Empty` holds nothing; `Evaluation(e)` names an evaluation with content. A record id names the same entity in every state that holds it (§2.2), so an entity unchanged across states is stored once. Bases form a forest: no evaluation is its own ancestor.
- This is the storage the kernels use. A decoder of a delta-chain format (ASM, Parasolid, Creo increments) composes the stored deltas between two design positions into one neutral delta per position (§3.1), and follows the source's own chain: a format that chains back from the current model (ASM, Parasolid) gives each state the next later stored state as its base, and the last stored state before the current state's position `p` the base `Current(p)`. A decoder of a format that stores each state in full (FreeCAD) gives each state the nearest earlier stored state of its container as its base, and the first `Empty`, and shares records with that base as Full snapshots (below) states. In a kernel index space that the current geometry does not hold (§2.2), the states chain from `Empty`: a chain-back format gives the last stored state of that space the base `Empty` in place of `Current(p)`.
- **Full snapshots.** A decoder of a format that stores each state in full mints ids by one procedure, so that two decoders mint the same ids:
  - A body of an ordered container keeps one id through that container's states, the id it has in the first state that holds it. The i-th region of that body, and the j-th shell of its i-th region, keep the base's ids at the same positions.
  - Every other record is matched with the base's records of its kind, bottom-up by content: points, curves, surfaces, and pcurves, then vertices and edges, then loops, coedges, and faces. A record matches a base record when every field but `source_object` (§5.6) is equal once each id it holds is mapped through the matches already made, parent pointers included (a face's `shell`, a loop's `face`, a coedge's `owner_loop`). Loops, coedges, and faces refer to one another through those pointers, their child lists, and `radial_next`, so they are matched together: their matching pairs are the largest set of pairs under which every pair is equal with its references mapped through the earlier matches and through the set itself. A matched record keeps the base's id and `source_object` and is shared; every other record is new.
  - A new record takes its key (§2.2) from the stored shape that holds its state. Where several of the source's stored shapes hold one state (a first feature's `Shape` and `AddSubShape`), the first in the document's object order gives the key, and within one object its result property (`Shape`) before any other (`AddSubShape`); a container's repeat of its `Tip` is no stored shape (D33). A shared record keeps its key from the first state that holds it.
  - A `Tool(f)` state is based on `Empty`, and its body is a body of its own: every record of it is new and keyed by `f`'s tool shape (`AddSubShape`).
  - Example: a PartDesign Body holds a Pad, whose state is a box, and a Pocket that cuts a round hole through the box's top face. The Pad state is based on `Empty`. FreeCAD stores it as `Pad.Shape` and as `Pad.AddSubShape`, and the first gives the keys: `body#Pad.Shape`, `region#Pad.Shape.Solid1`, `shell#Pad.Shape.Shell1`, the top face `face#Pad.Shape.Face6`, its loop `loop#Pad.Shape.Wire6`, that loop's second coedge `coedge#Pad.Shape.Wire6.2`, and the top face's plane `surface#Pad.Shape.Face6.Surface`. The Pocket state is based on the Pad state. Its body, region, and shell keep the Pad state's ids. Its eight corner points and vertices, its twelve straight edges and their lines, and its six planes equal the Pad state's and are shared, with their `Pad.Shape` keys. In the Pocket state the top face has a second loop, so it matches no face of the base. The loop whose `face` it is then differs from the base's, and so do that loop's coedges, the coedges beside them through `radial_next`, and in turn every face, loop, and coedge of the shell: all are new, keyed by `Pocket.Shape` (`Face1` to `Face7`, `Wire1`, `Wire1.1`, …), as are the hole's cylinder, its circular edges, and their curves, points, and vertices. `Tool(Pocket)`, the cylinder that FreeCAD stores as `Pocket.AddSubShape`, is based on `Empty`: its body is `body#Pocket.AddSubShape`, and its other records are keyed by that shape too.
- **Delta maps.** Each map of a delta sets (`Some`) or removes (`None`) entries relative to its base's, and maps merge the same way down a chain of bases. `names` holds the state's name table (§5.7). `owners` holds the definition that owns a body. `members` holds the definition that owns an occurrence. `instance_bodies` holds an instance's bodies (§8.1; SolidWorks stores assembly-cut bodies per configuration, Inventor per state). `poses` holds a placed instance's placement in the state, where the source moves occurrences along the history (Fusion), and only where it differs from the placement the state's configuration resolves to (§5.11, D54). Its key is the instance's path from the scope's definition, outermost occurrence first (§5.8), which resolves against the occurrence membership of the state it is read in: the current listing with that state's `members` applied. So two instances of one component can hold different placements of the same nested occurrence (Fusion stores poses per component path), and a pose before a cut-and-paste names the occurrence under its earlier owner. The pose is the placement of the path's last occurrence in its owning definition in that state. In a state whose `members` entry names another owner for an occurrence, the placement the state's configuration resolves to is `Occurrence.transform` under that owner, and the state states a pose wherever the instance's placement in that owner differs from it. An instance with no pose entry is at that resolved placement, and a state of a configuration that is not active restates none of that configuration's own placements. The current state is the reference: the definition that owns a body or an occurrence in the current state lists it (`ProductDefinition.bodies`, `ProductDefinition.occurrences`), and the current state's poses are `CurrentState.poses` (§5.5). Every other state's `owners`, `members`, and `poses` state its differences from that, on either side of the current state's position: a Fusion cut-and-paste moves an occurrence to another component, so the states before it state the earlier owner in `members` when the current state is after it, and the states after it state the new owner when the current state is rolled back before it. In every state, a body with no owner entry belongs to the definition that lists it in the current state, else to the scope's definition, and an occurrence with no member entry belongs to the definition that lists it in the current state, else to the scope's definition. An occurrence that a design feature creates exists in a state only as §6.7 derives it, and a state holds no member or pose entry for an occurrence that does not exist in it. Every check of names, owners, members, instance bodies, and poses runs against the resolved state, never against `delta.records` alone.
- `State(p)` is the geometry at position `p`. `Tool(f)` is the tool body of feature `f` before its Boolean (FreeCAD `AddSubShape`): the body `f` builds and then combines with the state it enters. A feature has a tool body in a configuration where it is not stateless there and the operation that applies there builds such a body: one that states `Boolean::Apply`, in its `SolidOutput` or `SheetOutput` or as its own `boolean` (`Rib`, `Thicken`, `BoundaryFill`); a `Hole`, or an `Emboss` whose effect is not `Scribe`, which combine the body they build with their targets. `CadIr::has_tool_body(f, c)` is that predicate. An operation that states `Boolean::NewBody` has none: the body it builds is a body of the state after it. A `Combine` combines bodies of its input state and builds none. The shape a source stores for the material a dress-up adds or removes (a FreeCAD dress-up's `AddSubShape`, where it holds a shape) is the difference of the states before and after the feature, which the document holds, and stays in the feature's native record (Rule N case (b)). The shape a source stores for a pattern's instances (a FreeCAD LinkStage3 pattern's `AddSubShape`) follows from the seed's tool body and the layout (§6.5) and stays in the feature's native record.
- **Which states exist.** One rule decides which features have an evaluation:
  - A feature that is stateless in a configuration has no evaluation in it, and the state after it is the state before it (D34, D35). `CadIr::is_stateless(f, c)` is that predicate for feature `f` in configuration `c` (`None` in a scope with no configurations). It is true where `f`'s `suppressed` resolves to true in `c` (§5.11): a suppressed feature has no evaluation there, and a source's stored copy of the state before it (a FreeCAD suppressed feature's `Shape`) is not emitted. Otherwise it reads the `operation` of the definition that applies in `c`, and is true exactly for `Sketch` and `SpatialSketch`, `Spreadsheet`, `Datum`, a `Pattern` whose instances are `Members`, `TemplateInstance`, `Decal`, and a `Mesh` whose kind is `Section` (a sketch, a sheet, a datum or other construction feature, a feature that only generates other features, an appearance, and a section that only writes curves into a sketch), whose kind cannot change a state. An `Unresolved` operation is stateless where its family is `Sketch`, `SpatialSketch`, `Spreadsheet`, `Datum`, `TemplateInstance`, or `Decal`, whose every operation is stateless, and not otherwise; a `Native` operation is not stateless. A pick anchored after a stateless feature resolves in the state before it, which is the same state. In an unordered container a stateless member has no state before or after it (§5.3): what it holds is picked by its own targets (`Sketch`, `SketchEntity`, `Datum`, `Feature`, §5.8).
  - For every other feature, a decoder that reads or replays the state after it (§3.1) stores an evaluation with content, even where the delta is empty (a failed feature, a zero move), except where the current geometry holds that state (Keys, below). A feature that changes no geometry has an evaluation whenever the source stores the occurrence membership or the poses after it, whose delta changes no geometry of its own; its base follows the chain rule above: a Fusion new component, insert, joint, Move of components, or cut-and-paste, whose ASM history state is null and whose poses the operation table stores. An absent evaluation means the state was not read.
  - A delta is empty only when all seven of its parts are empty. A delta that changes members, owners, poses, instance bodies, or names is not empty.
  - A state the source does not store, or stores only in an encoding the decoder cannot apply, has no content. A SolidWorks imported feature's state is such a state: its bodies arrive in the next feature's delta (§3.1), and its state is not stored, which is not an empty delta.
  - An evaluation without content states a status only: where the source records a state it does not store as stale or failed (SolidWorks `swConfigurationNeedsUpdate` on a configuration whose partition is not stored, an NX failed update), an evaluation with no content states that status.
  - Selections into a state with no content keep their names and witnesses, and are checked where the state is stored.
- **Status.** `Current` means the source does not flag the state. `Stale` means the source marks it out of date (FreeCAD `Touched`, SolidWorks `swConfigurationNeedsUpdate`, Creo `local_need_regen`, NX update alert). `Failed` means the source records a failed rebuild (CATIA update error, NX failed update). An evaluation with no content is `Stale` or `Failed`. A feature is stale when a state that depends on it is.
- **Keys.** At most one evaluation per (scope, configuration, `of`). When the scope has configurations, `configuration` names one of them; it is `None` only when the scope has none. A decoder emits no evaluation for a state the current geometry holds (§5.5): in the active configuration, the state at a current state's position is that current state's extent. A configuration that is not active, the base included, has its geometry in evaluations. The state after a stored-geometry feature is an ordinary evaluation or current state, which holds the bodies the feature names (§5.10, D32).
- **Closure.** Each resolved state is closed: its references resolve inside it.

### 5.5 Current geometry

```rust
pub struct CurrentState {
    pub at: Position,
    pub bodies: Vec<BodyId>,
    pub poses: BTreeMap<OccurrencePath, Transform>,
    pub status: EvaluationStatus,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
```

`CadIr.geometry` is the source's current model: the bodies the source holds as the product, with each scope at its active configuration. The decoder states it; it is not derived from feature operands, because sources differ in what an operand does to its inputs (a FreeCAD Part Cut keeps its inputs as objects of their own, which it hides; a Fusion Combine consumes its tools; a CATIA Boolean absorbs its tool body). A current state's `native_ref` names the source's record of the state where it has one, as an evaluation's does (§5.4).

`CadIr.geometry` is a model-class arena because a geometry-only document, and a geometry-only writer, need a model that stands without the design class (§2.1). The current state of every scope is held outside evaluations: its geometry in `CadIr.geometry`, its body owners and occurrence membership in the product definitions' `bodies` and `occurrences`, and its instance bodies in `ProductDefinition.instance_bodies` (all model class), its names in `Design.names`, and its poses in `CurrentState.poses`. Every other state is an evaluation that states its difference from another state (§5.4).

- Each scope lists its current states. A `CurrentState` names a position and the bodies of `CadIr.geometry` that belong to the state there. Every listed body is a body of `CadIr.geometry`, and every body listed in `bodies` or in an `instance_bodies` entry of a definition a scope spans belongs to exactly one of that scope's current states or to its `unproduced` (below). A current state inside an ordered container `c` is at `c`'s rollback position, spelled through its member where the rollback is stated and as `After(Container(c))` where it is not (§5.3); a selection outside the container names the same state as `After(Container(c))`. Two FreeCAD Bodies with different `Tip`s are two current states; a CATIA part has one per body and per ordered geometrical set, at its rollback position, and one per geometrical-set result. The own result (§5.3) of a member of an unordered container, in the active configuration, is a current state at `After(m)` whatever its visibility: hiding is presentation (D20), so the `Base` and `Tool` that a FreeCAD Part Cut hides are current states beside the Cut's.
- **Unproduced geometry.** `unproduced` lists the bodies of `CadIr.geometry`, owned by definitions the scope spans (§5.1), that no member of the scope produces: a Rhino object that no history record lists among its descendants, or that several list (§5.2), a body of a Fusion design whose design stream holds no timeline item, a body of a definition the scope spans that a USD stage or a STEP product holds beside joints and no history (§6.7), and a body of a scope whose producing members the document does not hold. Such a body has no position: it is in no current state, and no evaluation states it. Its extent is the body and the records it reaches (§5.6), with their name entries, its owner, and the instance-body entries that list it; a pick anchored `Current` resolves in it as in each current state's extent (§5.8). No state of the scope depends on a feature through it (§5.3), so its name entries state no structured name (§5.7). No feature the scope holds produces it, so no feature override moves it, and a material override may select it (§5.11) without exchanging it. `set_active_configuration` leaves it in place (§4). A decoder mints no feature to hold it. A feature the source stores, whose own content is the geometry, is a `Stored` member (§5.10), and the bodies it holds are its result. A decoder lists a body here wherever the document holds no member that produces it. A `Definition` mesh that no feature's `tessellations` names is no entry: `unproduced` lists bodies, and the mesh states its definition itself (§8). A history read in part states what was read (§3.3): the members it read produce its bodies, which are not unproduced. A history read not at all leaves its bodies unproduced, with a loss naming the unread history. A writer whose target holds every body in a feature (SolidWorks, Inventor, NX, Creo, CATIA, FreeCAD) writes each unproduced body as its target's stored-geometry feature, which no edit regenerates either, and charges nothing: the geometry and what an edit does to it are the same. A writer to Rhino writes it as an object that no history record produces. A writer to Fusion writes it as a body of a design whose stream holds no timeline item where the scope holds no ordered container and no member that can change a state, and otherwise as a Base Feature ahead of the scope's other timeline items.
- **Extent.** The extent of a current state is its bodies and the records they reach, their name entries, their owners, the instance-body entries whose bodies are among them, the occurrence membership of the definitions the scope spans, and its poses. `StateBase::Current(p)` is that extent (§5.4). A selection whose anchored position is a current state's position, in the active configuration, resolves in that state's extent, not in all of `CadIr.geometry`: no evaluation repeats that state (§5.4), and `All { kind }`, `KeepSelected`, and every rule that reads every entity of a state read the extent. A pick anchored `Current` resolves in the current geometry of the scope it resolves in: the union of that scope's current-state extents and the extent of its unproduced bodies (§5.8).
- `CadIr.geometry`, `Design.names`, `ProductDefinition.instance_bodies`, and the current states' poses hold the state of each scope's active configuration. `Design.names` names the entities of `CadIr.geometry`. Changing the active configuration is `set_active_configuration` (§4), which exchanges each current state's extent and nothing else.
- **Poses.** `poses` holds a placed instance's placement in the current state where it differs from the placement its configuration resolves to, keyed by the instance's path under the rule of `delta.poses` (§5.4, D54). The resolved placement is `Occurrence.transform`, the placement the source stores on the occurrence (for Fusion, its current pose, §8.1), so a current state states a pose only where the instance's placement differs from it: a per-path pose of a nested instance (Fusion stores poses per component path), or, in a timeline rolled back before a Move or a joint, the placement the instance has at the rollback. `effective_transform` applies it (§4). A path has a pose in at most one current state of its scope. A scope that holds no current state states no pose: there, the placement of an instance nested inside an occurrence's prototype, for that occurrence alone, is a nested override of that occurrence (§8.1).
- With `design` out of scope, `CadIr.geometry` stands alone.

A body a later feature of an ordered container consumes, removes, or splits exists in the states before that feature, where the feature's operand selects it. In a CATIA body and an ordered geometrical set, a modification feature consumes the result it absorbs (Dassault's page Order and Absorption Concepts). A body the source keeps in its stored model but hides because a feature of its timeline consumed it (Fusion) belongs to the earlier state, not to the current geometry; the F3D writer restores it hidden (§3.4). A member of an unordered container that has its own result (§5.3) keeps that result as a current state when another member uses it (above).

### 5.6 Topology and record references

`Topology` holds the B-rep and carrier arenas: `bodies`, `regions`, `shells`, `faces`, `loops`, `coedges`, `edges`, `vertices`, `points`, `surfaces`, `curves`, `subds`, `pcurves`, `procedural_surfaces`, `procedural_curves`. `CadIr.geometry`, every state delta, every cage-defined feature (§6.6), and every witness body (§5.8) use it. One validator and one resolver serve all of them. Records in a `Topology` hold no structured or native name (§5.7) and no design reference; a body's or face's display `name` and colour are presentation (§8).

```rust

    pub procedural_curves: Vec<ProceduralCurve>,
}

}
pub struct RecordBounds(pub [Option<FiniteReal>; 4]);
pub struct ProceduralCurve { pub id: ProceduralCurveId, pub definition: ProceduralCurveDefinition, pub native_ref: Option<String> }

pub struct SubdSurface { pub id: SubdId, pub scheme: SubdScheme, pub cage: SubdCage, pub source_object: Option<SourceObjectAssociation>, pub native_ref: Option<String> }
pub enum SubdScheme { CatmullClark, TSpline }
pub struct SubdCage { vertices: Vec<SubdVertex>, edges: Vec<SubdEdge>, faces: Vec<SubdFace>, symmetries: Vec<SubdSymmetry> }
pub struct SubdVertex { pub point: FinitePoint3, pub tag: SubdVertexTag, pub secondary_grips: Option<SubdVertexGripLayout> }
pub enum SubdVertexTag { Smooth, Crease, Corner, Dart }
pub struct SubdEdge {
    vertices: [u32; 2],
    pub sharpness: [NonNegativeReal; 2],
    pub tag: SubdEdgeTag,
    pub knot_interval: Option<PositiveReal>,
    pub user_knot: Option<SubdUserKnot>,
    pub sector_coefficients: [FiniteReal; 2],
}
pub enum SubdEdgeTag { Smooth, SmoothX, Crease }
pub enum SubdUserKnot { Inherit, Override(NonNegativeReal) }
pub struct SubdFace { sides: Vec<SubdFaceSide> }
pub struct SubdFaceSide { pub edges: Vec<SubdEdgeUse> }
pub struct SubdEdgeUse { pub edge: u32, pub reversed: bool }
pub struct SubdSymmetry {
    pub kind: SubdSymmetryKind,
    pub plane: SubdPlaneFrame,
    face_pairs: Vec<[u32; 2]>,
    edge_pairs: Vec<[u32; 2]>,
    vertex_pairs: Vec<[u32; 2]>,
}
pub enum SubdSymmetryKind { Correspondence, Radial(SubdRadialSymmetry) }
pub struct SubdPlaneFrame { pub origin: FinitePoint3, first_axis: UnitVector3, second_axis: UnitVector3 }
pub struct SubdRadialSymmetry { pub segments: NonZeroU32, pub sweep: FiniteReal, pub radial_maps: Vec<SubdRadialSymmetryMap> }
pub struct SubdRadialSymmetryMap { pub selector: SubdRadialMapSelector, pub pairs: Vec<[u64; 2]> }
pub enum SubdRadialMapSelector { Ef, Er, Ff, Fr, Vf, Vr }
pub struct SubdVertexGripLayout { pub direction: SubdGripDirection, wedges: Vec<SubdGripWedge> }
pub enum SubdGripDirection { North, East, South, West }
pub enum SubdGripWedge {
    Phantom,
    Slot { edge: Option<u32>, sector_face: Option<u32>, spokes: Vec<Option<SubdSecondaryGrip>>, sectors: Vec<Option<SubdSecondaryGrip>> },
}
pub struct SubdSecondaryGrip { pub source_index: u32, pub point: FinitePoint3, pub weight: PositiveReal }

pub struct SourceObjectAssociation {
    pub format: CodecId,
    pub geometry_role: Option<SourceGeometryRole>,
    pub object_id: NonBlankString,
    pub instance_path: Vec<String>,
}
pub enum SourceGeometryRole { Independent, Support }
```

`unstated` is omitted for `None` (§2.5). The wire forms follow §2.5: `{"kind": "partial_classified", "outer": …, "inner": […]}`, `"members"`, `{"kind": "voids"}`, and `{"kind": "exterior", "voids": […]}`.

`LoopRing`, the three interval types, `EdgeCarrier`, `SubdEdge`, `SubdFace`, `SubdPlaneFrame`, `SubdSymmetry`, `SubdVertexGripLayout`, and `SubdCage` are checked (§2.8). A `LoopRing` holds at least one coedge, each once, and every `vertex_uses` entry's `after` names a coedge of the ring. A `ParameterInterval` and the `param_range` of an `EdgeCarrier` with a `curve` have `start ≤ end`; an `IncreasingParameterInterval` has `start < end`; a `DirectedParameterRange`'s two values differ. A `SubdEdge`'s two `vertices` differ. A `SubdFace` has at least three sides, and each side at least one edge use. A `SubdPlaneFrame`'s two axes are perpendicular: the absolute value of their dot product is at most 10⁻⁹. Its normal, `first_axis` × `second_axis`, is the axis of a radial symmetry and the normal of a mirror plane. In each of the `face_pairs`, `edge_pairs`, and `vertex_pairs` of a `SubdSymmetry`, no two pairs share a source and no two share a target. In a `SubdVertexGripLayout`, the number of a wedge's `sectors` is its number of `spokes` times that of the next wedge, the first wedge following the last: a sector grid has one position for each pair of a spoke and a next spoke. Each spoke and sector position holds a grip or `null`, an absent grip. A `Phantom` wedge has no spokes and no sectors. In a `SubdCage`, every vertex, edge, and face index, and every index pair in the `face_pairs`, `edge_pairs`, and `vertex_pairs` of a symmetry, names an entry of its list, and each face's edge uses form one closed directed ring: taken in order across its sides, a use running from its edge's first vertex to its second, or from the second to the first where it is `reversed`, each use starts at the vertex where the one before it ends, and the last ends where the first starts. In a `Slot` wedge of a vertex's `secondary_grips`, the `edge`, where stated, names an edge one of whose `vertices` is that vertex, and the `sector_face`, where stated, names a face one of whose edge uses names an edge one of whose `vertices` is that vertex; no two secondary grips of one cage share a `source_index`.

- **Structure.** body → region → shell → face → loop → coedge → edge → vertex → point, with surface, curve, and pcurve carriers; a shell may instead hold one subdivision cage (Subdivision cages, below). Every record names its parent (`Region.body`, `Shell.region`, `Face.shell`, `Loop.face`, `Coedge.owner_loop`) and every arena is strictly sorted by id (§2.2). `kind` states whether a body is a solid, a sheet, a wire, or a general body of mixed dimension. Where the source classifies the body (a STEP `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`, an IGES manifold solid B-rep object, a Parasolid body type, an Open CASCADE solid, a Rhino B-rep's solid flag), `kind` is that classification, whatever faces the document holds. Where it does not (an ACIS lump), a body of faces is a solid where the faces the document holds close, every edge on a curve that is not degenerate being used as often in one sense as in the other and every face `Unspecified` with no loops lying on a surface with no boundary (Faces and loops, below), and a sheet otherwise. A curve or a point that the source holds as an object of its own, outside any body (a Rhino curve or point object; an IGES curve or point entity that is not physically dependent; a curve or point that a STEP shape representation lists as an item, directly or in a `GEOMETRIC_SET`), is a `Wire` body of its own: one region and one shell, which lists a wire edge for each curve the object holds and a free vertex for each point (one edge for a Rhino curve object; an edge for each curve of an IGES composite curve or a USD curves prim; a free vertex for each point of an IGES copious-data point set). An edge's `param_range` is its curve's own domain, and its ends are vertices at that domain's two ends; edges of one object whose curves the source joins end to end share the vertex where they meet; where the curve is closed, the edge has no vertex and states no `param_range` (Edges, below). A curve with no finite domain that the source does not bound (a STEP `LINE` listed bare, an unbounded IGES line) has no ends to state and is no body: it stays a curve record with its `source_object`, and the decoder charges a loss naming the object. A decoder states one such body for each object and none for a group of them: a STEP set and the free entities of an IGES file are no body, and a name or style the source gives a set stays in the set's native record (part 11). The body states the object's display name, colour, and visibility (D21; for a Rhino object, its colour where the object's colour source is the object itself, §8), and each of its curve and point records states the object's identity as its `source_object` with `geometry_role: Independent`. FreeCAD's `Part::Vertex` is such a body (§6.6). A surface that the source holds as an object of its own, outside any body (a Rhino surface object; an IGES surface entity that is not physically dependent; a surface that a STEP shape representation lists as an item, directly or in a `GEOMETRIC_SET`; a USD `NurbsPatch` prim), is a body of its own: one region and one shell, which holds one face on the surface. Its kind follows the rule above for a body its source does not classify: a sheet, or a solid where its face is `Unspecified` with no loops and lies on a surface with no boundary. The face's loops are the boundary the source stores with the surface (an IGES trimmed surface's, a STEP `CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE`'s, a USD patch's trim curves), and it has none where the source stores none: it is then the whole of its surface's own domain (Faces and loops, below). A surface that the source bounds by parameter ranges (a Rhino plane surface's extents; a USD patch's `uRange` and `vRange`, and an IGES rational B-spline surface's U(0), U(1), V(0), V(1), where they narrow its knot domain; a STEP `RECTANGULAR_TRIMMED_SURFACE`) is a subset surface over those ranges (Procedural carriers, below). A surface with no finite domain that the source does not bound (a STEP `PLANE` that a shape representation lists bare as its own item; an IGES unbounded plane, cylinder, or cone) has no face to state and is no body: it stays a surface record with its `source_object`, and the decoder charges a loss naming the object. A plane, cylinder, or cone that a STEP `GEOMETRIC_SET` holds bare is a body of one face with no extent to state: the face is stated in its partial form with no loop (Faces and loops, below), and the decoder charges `topology.face-boundary-unstated` naming it. A decoder states one such body for each object and none for a group of them, as for curves. The body states the object's display name, colour, and visibility (D21; for a Rhino object, its colour where the object's colour source is the object itself, §8), and its surface record states the object's identity as its `source_object` with `geometry_role: Independent`. A curve, point, or surface that stays a record of its own keeps its style as an appearance bound to it and its layer as a layer item that names it (§8); its display name and visibility have no home there, and the decoder's loss names them. Geometry that a STEP file states as constructive or supplemental (the items of a `CONSTRUCTIVE_GEOMETRY_REPRESENTATION`, and of a representation that lists part of one for a saved view) is construction geometry, not an object of the shape: none of its curves, points, or surfaces is such a body.
- **Child lists (D29).** A child list whose order carries no meaning is derived from the children's parent pointers and is not stored: a shell's faces come from `Face.shell`, and a body's regions from `Region.body`, so a delta that adds or removes a face does not restate its shell (a delta in which a shell or a body loses or regains a child it does not state restates it: Unstated children, below). A child list whose order or classification carries meaning is stored and checked for reciprocity: a region's `shells`, the exterior first and every later shell a void of a solid region (a region whose exterior is not stated lists its shells in its mark: Unstated children, below); a face's `loops`; a loop ring's `coedges`. A shell's `members` lists its wire edges, its free vertices, and its cage, which have no parent pointer; a shell that holds only faces lists none. The records a body reaches are its regions, found through `Region.body`; their shells; the faces of each shell, found through `Face.shell`; the wire edges, free vertices, and cage each shell's `members` lists; and every record any of these names, transitively: loops, coedges, edges, vertices, points, and their surface, curve, pcurve, and procedural carriers. The extent of a state (§5.5), a `StateBase::Current` base (§5.4), and the records only some bodies reach (§4) are read so.
- **Faces and loops.** `Face.sense` states whether the face normal agrees with its surface's normal. `FaceLoops::Classified` names the outer loop and the inner loops in source order, where the source classifies them; `Unspecified` lists them in source order where it does not. A face `Unspecified` with no loops is the whole of its surface's own domain, which is finite: on a surface with no boundary the face is closed (a whole sphere or torus), and on any other it is bounded by its domain's sides, which no edge states (a free surface, Structure, above). Such a face shares no edge or vertex with another, so it is the only face of its shell. A surface record's own domain is the domain its carrier defines: a sphere's whole azimuth and its latitude from −π/2 to π/2 (Carriers, below), one turn of each angle of a torus, the knot domain of a NURBS surface, and for a placed surface its basis's, through every placement. A procedural surface that restricts a support to parameter ranges (a subset) has those ranges; any other procedural surface has its `record_bounds` where the source states all four, and otherwise, as an unknown surface does, the domain its source gives it, which this document does not evaluate (Annex A). A plane's domain is unbounded, and so are a cylinder's and a cone's along the axis, so a face on one has loops. A face that its source holds with no boundary on such a surface (an Open CASCADE face over a whole plane, the shape FreeCAD stores for a datum plane or a local coordinate system; a STEP plane, cylinder, or cone that a geometric set holds bare) has no extent to state. A datum states its own plane (§6.2) and no face; any other such face is stated in its partial form with no loop (Unstated children, below), and the decoder charges `topology.face-boundary-unstated` naming it (§3.2). A surface record has no boundary where its domain is finite and each side of it either meets the opposite side or collapses to one point, within the tolerance in force (§2.3), as a curve record's ends meet (Edges, below): a sphere, whose latitude sides collapse to its poles; a torus; a NURBS surface closed in both directions, or closed in one and collapsed at both ends of the other. Where the source states that a face's outer boundary is its surface's own (an IGES trimmed surface with no outer boundary, a STEP `CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE` whose `implicit_outer` is true), the face lies on a curve-bounded surface that states so (Annex A) and lists its inner loops alone: it is its support's whole domain less what they cut out. A face whose boundary the source stores is stated with every loop of it, or in its partial form (Unstated children, below): a decoder that cannot state the boundary in full never states the face `Unspecified` or `Classified` with fewer loops or none. Loops are simple cycles with reciprocal links; an outer loop runs counterclockwise about the face's oriented normal. A loop is a `Ring` of coedges in traversal order, a checked `LoopRing` (above), with the pole vertices it passes (`vertex_uses`, each after the coedge `after` names), or one `Vertex` at a surface singularity (a cone apex) with that pole's parameter-space images.
- **Unstated children.** A record whose child the document does not state, because the decoder or a reader gave it up (§3.3), says so and states every child it read. So does a face whose source states no boundary on a surface whose domain is unbounded (Faces and loops, above).
  - **A face** states `PartialUnspecified` or `PartialClassified`, as its source does not or does classify its loops. It lists the loops stated, in source order, with `outer` where the outer loop is stated, and its boundary is not stated in full: at least one loop of the face is not stated, or its source states no loop on a surface whose domain is unbounded and the face lists none. Its extent on its surface is not stated: it is not the region those loops bound.
  - **A region** states `unstated`:
    - `Voids`: `shells` holds its exterior first, as for any region, and a void is not stated.
    - `Exterior`: its exterior is not stated, `shells` is empty, and `voids` lists the voids stated, in source order.
    - `Unclassified`: which shell is its exterior is not stated, `shells` is empty, and the mark's `shells` lists those stated, in source order.
  - **A shell** states `unstated: members` where a face, a wire edge, a free vertex, or the cage of it is not stated, and **a body** where a region of it is not stated. A state delta in which a shell or a body loses or regains such a child restates that shell or body, with or without the mark.

  No tessellation, measure, or evaluation states an extent of a partial face, or a volume of a marked region or of a region that holds a marked shell or a partial face. A body keeps the kind its source classifies. A body its source does not classify takes its kind from the faces the document holds (Structure, above), and a mark on it or below it says that set is partial. An edit keeps a mark unless it states the missing child.
- **Coedges.** A coedge is one use of an edge by a loop. `sense` states whether its traversal agrees with its edge's curve. `radial_next` is the next coedge around the edge; radial rings close through it, and a coedge whose `radial_next` is itself bounds a laminar edge of a sheet. `pcurves` lists the coedge's parameter-space images on its face's surface in order, each with the interval of the pcurve's own parameter it uses (`DirectedParameterRange`, whose two values differ and run from the use's start to its end) and `isoparametric` where the source declares the image isoparametric. `use_curve` is a 3D carrier of this use alone, in place of the edge's curve, with its interval in traversal order. Wire edges and free vertices belong to exactly one shell, and so does every cage outside a form's `cage` (§6.6).
- **Edges.** `carrier` is the edge's curve and the parameter range admitted on it: with a `curve`, `param_range` is that curve's interval from the edge's start to its end, `start ≤ end`; with no `curve`, it holds the parameters of the edge's ends where the source states them; with neither, the edge has no carrier. `ends` holds the edge's start and end vertices; `None` is a closed edge with no vertex (a Parasolid ring edge, such as the circular edge of a through hole), which occurs only on a closed carrier (§10). A closed edge with no vertex states no `param_range`: its whole carrier is admitted. `tolerance` is the edge's own tolerance (§2.3), as a face's and a vertex's are theirs. A curve record's own domain is its `parameter_range` where it states one, and otherwise the domain its carrier defines: one turn of a circle or an ellipse, and the knot domain of a NURBS curve, clamped or periodic. A curve record is closed where that domain is finite and the curve evaluates at its two ends to one point, within the coincidence allowance (part 10). A closed edge with no vertex admits that whole domain. A curve record with no finite domain (a line, a parabola, a hyperbola, or a procedural curve, with no `parameter_range`) is not closed, and an edge on it has vertices or a `param_range`.
- **Bodies.** `transform` places the body in its owning definition: on a body of an ordered container with a `placement`, it holds that placement's resolved value, in the current geometry and in each evaluation of the container's states (resolved in the evaluation's configuration), and a geometry writer applies it (§5.2); a body of a definition that a FreeCAD `App::Link` places is in the object's local frame and has none (§6.7). World placement composes it with the occurrence chain (D25). `name` is the source's display name for the body (a Fusion body's browser name, `Body1`), `color` its display colour (D19), and `visible` whether the source displays it (D20). On the bodies of the states of a FreeCAD PartDesign Body, `visible` and `name` are `None`, except on its result bodies in the current geometry, which state the container object's `Visibility` and `Label` where no `App::Link` places the object. A member feature's display state is no body's: a FreeCAD PartDesign feature's `Visibility` stays in its native record (a UI state, Rule N case (b)), and its `Label` is `Feature.name`. An object that an `App::Link` places states its `Visibility` and `Label` as its own occurrence's `visible` and `name` (§6.7), and its bodies state none. The result of a member of an unordered container (a FreeCAD Part object) states the member's `Visibility` as its `visible` (§5.5).
- **Colour.** A `Color` is RGBA, each component in [0, 1]. `Body.color` and `Face.color` are display colours (D19); a colour that an appearance holds is the appearance's (§8).
- **Carriers.** Surfaces: plane, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, NURBS, polygonal, placed (`Transformed`), procedural, unknown. Curves: line, circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola, degenerate, composite, NURBS, polyline, placed (`Transformed`), procedural, unknown. Pcurves in `(u, v)`. The analytic, NURBS, polyline, and placed carriers have the parameterization below; decoders convert kernel conventions at decode and mark converted fields `derived`. `SurfaceGeometry::Solved` and `CurveGeometry::Solved` hold a solved carrier; `Procedural` names the procedural record that defines the carrier and holds its solved form as `cache` where the source stores one (D23). `Curve.parameter_range` bounds the curve where the source bounds it, `start < end`. `Pcurve.metadata` states the pcurve's source form: `AsmInline` an ASM pcurve stored inline in its coedge, with its wrapper sense, tail flags, `uv_offset`, and fit tolerance; `General` every other pcurve, with its support surface, offset, sense, parameter range, and fit tolerance where the source states them.

  A carrier's frame is its `axis` **a** (a plane's `normal`) and its reference direction **r** (a plane's `u_axis`; `ref_direction`; an ellipse's, a parabola's, and a hyperbola's `major_direction`), unit and perpendicular, with **s** = **a** × **r**. Angles are radians. The point of a carrier at its parameters is:

  | Carrier | Point |
  |---|---|
  | line | `origin` + t·`direction` |
  | circle | `center` + `radius`·(cos t·**r** + sin t·**s**) |
  | ellipse | `center` + `major_radius`·cos t·**r** + `minor_radius`·sin t·**s** |
  | parabola | `vertex` + `focal_distance`·t²·**r** + 2·`focal_distance`·t·**s** |
  | hyperbola | `center` + `major_radius`·cosh t·**r** + `minor_radius`·sinh t·**s** |
  | degenerate | `point`, at every t |
  | polyline | on the first segment whose two points' parameters enclose t, the point that divides the segment in the ratio in which t divides those parameters; a polyline that states no parameters takes each point's index, from 0, as its parameter |
  | plane | `origin` + u·**r** + v·**s** |
  | cylinder | `origin` + `radius`·(cos u·**r** + sin u·**s**) + v·**a** |
  | cone | `origin` + ρ·(cos u·**r** + `ratio`·sin u·**s**) + v·**a**, with ρ = `radius` + v·tan(`half_angle`) |
  | sphere | `center` + `radius`·cos v·(cos u·**r** + sin u·**s**) + `radius`·sin v·**a** |
  | torus | `center` + (`major_radius` + `minor_radius`·cos v)·(cos u·**r** + sin u·**s**) + `minor_radius`·sin v·**a** |
  | NURBS curve or surface | the rational B-spline of its poles, weights, and knots at the knot-domain parameter |
  | `Transformed` | its transform applied to its basis at the same parameters |

  A line's t is signed arc length in millimetres. A circle's t runs over one revolution in [0, 2π]. A cylinder's and a cone's v is signed axial distance in millimetres, and a cone's apex is where ρ is 0. A sphere's u is its azimuth and v its latitude, in [−π/2, π/2].
- **Procedural carriers.** Surfaces (extrusion, revolution, sum, sweep, offset, subset, ruled, blend, unknown) and curves (intersection, projection, offset, subset, blend spine, unknown), bidirectionally linked to their solved carriers. The construction is canonical (D23). `record_bounds` holds the four parameter bounds the source record states, `null` for each bound it leaves open.
- **Subdivision cages.** A cage is a `SubdSurface` of scheme `CatmullClark` or `TSpline`. Its `cage` holds vertices, edges, and faces, each named by its index in its list: an edge's `vertices` are vertex indices, and a face lists its sides in boundary order, a checked `SubdFace` (above), each side its edge uses in order. A Catmull–Clark face has one edge per side. A `TSpline` cage is evaluated with the NURCCS rule at extraordinary points, star smoothness 0, G1 caps, and degree 3 (§6.6). A T-spline side may hold several edges, each joint between them a T-junction, and a T-spline cage's edges may state unequal `knot_interval`s (Fusion forms, §6.6). `sharpness` and `tag` state an edge's crease at its two ends, `user_knot` a knot the user set, `sector_coefficients` the sector weights at its ends; a vertex's `tag` and `secondary_grips` state its crease kind and its grip layout. A vertex with no secondary grips has no `secondary_grips`: a layout with no wedges reads as absent, and a writer writes a layout with one or more wedges. `symmetries` holds each symmetry the source records, with its plane frame and the index pairs it maps. The `radial_maps` of a radial symmetry are the source's native maps in source order; their pairs are the correspondence between a source entity and its image. A cage that the source holds as an object of its own (a Rhino SubD object) is a body of its own: one region and one shell, whose `members` lists the cage and nothing else. The body is a solid where every edge of the cage borders two of its faces, and a sheet otherwise; it states the object's display name, colour, and visibility (D21; for a Rhino object, its colour where the object's colour source is the object itself, §8), and the cage states the object's identity as its `source_object`. A form's cages are its definition, in a `Topology` that holds cages only, and belong to no body (§6.6).
- **Source objects.** `source_object` is the identity of the source object a point, carrier, cage, or tessellation was read from (D21: identity only): its format, its object id, the instance path that reaches it, and whether the object stands alone (`Independent`) or supports another (`Support`).

```rust
pub enum EntityRef { Body(BodyId), Face(FaceId), Edge(EdgeId), Vertex(VertexId), Surface(SurfaceId), Curve(CurveId), Subd(SubdId) }
pub enum RecordRef {
    Body(BodyId), Region(RegionId), Shell(ShellId), Face(FaceId), Loop(LoopId), Coedge(CoedgeId), Edge(EdgeId), Vertex(VertexId),
    Point(PointId), Surface(SurfaceId), Curve(CurveId), Subd(SubdId), Pcurve(PcurveId),
    ProceduralSurface(ProceduralSurfaceId), ProceduralCurve(ProceduralCurveId),
}
```

An `EntityRef` names a nameable entity. A `RecordRef` names a record of any `Topology` arena, one variant per arena in the order above, for a delta's `removed` list.

**Types this part uses.** `Members<T, O>` is a list of `T` whose members are distinct by identity, and whose order marker `O: MemberOrder` is `Ordered` (source order kept) or `Unordered` (sorted by the members' identity keys in the order of §2.5). A member's identity key is `(target, context, native, domain)` for a `Picked` (§5.8), and the value itself for a member with no witness; no order is required of witness geometry; `Driver` is defined in §5.10's text; `CodecId` is a codec id (§2.2). The construction kinds of §5.9 (`Point`, `Direction`, `Axis`, `Plane`, `Frame`, `Curve`) are marker types of the construction module, distinct from the geometry records of the same names; a construction's value is one of §5.9's value types (`FinitePoint3`, `UnitVector3`, `AxisValue`, `PlaneValue`, `FrameValue`, `CurveValue`), and a `Witness.frame` is a `FrameValue`. The value types are §2.7's; the carrier geometry (`SolvedSurfaceGeometry`, `SolvedCurveGeometry`, their leaf carriers `LineCurve`, `CircleCurve`, `EllipseCurve`, `ParabolaCurve`, `HyperbolaCurve`, `PolylineCurve`, `NurbsCurve`, `PlaneSurface`, `CylinderSurface`, `ConeSurface`, `SphereSurface`, `TorusSurface`, `NurbsSurface`, and `PolygonalSurface`, each the payload of the like-named arm of every carrier enum that holds it, `PcurveGeometry` with `PcurveNurbs`, `ProceduralSurfaceDefinition`, and `ProceduralCurveDefinition`) is Annex A's. The id types are §2.2's.

```rust
pub enum InlineCurve {
    Line(LineCurve), Circle(CircleCurve), Ellipse(EllipseCurve), Parabola(ParabolaCurve), Hyperbola(HyperbolaCurve),
    Nurbs(NurbsCurve), Polyline(PolylineCurve),
    Transformed { basis: Box<InlineCurve>, transform: Transform },
}
pub enum InlineSurface {
    Plane(PlaneSurface), Cylinder(CylinderSurface), Cone(ConeSurface), Sphere(SphereSurface), Torus(TorusSurface),
    Nurbs(NurbsSurface), Polygonal(PolygonalSurface),
    Transformed { basis: Box<InlineSurface>, transform: Transform },
}
```

`InlineCurve` and `InlineSurface` are carrier geometry that names no record: the leaf carriers of Annex A, and an inline placement of one. Every carrier held outside a `Topology` takes them (a witness, a spatial sketch curve, a process profile curve), so nothing outside the topology hangs on a topology record. A chain is a list of curves in its holder and never a composite, and a point is its holder's point (`Witness.point`, `SpatialCurve::Point`) and never a degenerate curve. Neither type has an `Unknown` arm; a holder whose carrier the decoder did not read says so in its own form. A witness states none of its `curves` where it did not read one of them, and no `surface` where it did not read that (§5.8). A derived sketch entity states `solved: None` (§6.1). A profile curve states `geometry: None` (§7.3).
### 5.7 Names

```rust
pub struct NameTable(BTreeMap<EntityRef, NameEntry>);
pub struct NameEntry { pub name: Option<TopoName>, pub native: Option<NativeName> }
pub struct NativeName { pub codec: CodecId, pub value: NativeNameValue }
pub enum NativeNameValue { Text(NonBlankString), Integers(Vec<i64>), Bytes(Base64Bytes) }

#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum TopoName {
    Generated { kind: NameKind, feature: FeatureId, role: Option<GenerationRole>, generator: Option<Generator>, index: Option<u32> },
    Instance  { feature: FeatureId, instance: InstanceIndex, of: Box<TopoName> },
    Blend     { feature: FeatureId, between: Vec<TopoName>, index: Option<u32> },
    Bounded   { faces: BTreeSet<TopoName>, ends: BTreeSet<TopoName>, index: Option<u32> },
    Meeting   { faces: BTreeSet<TopoName>, index: Option<u32> },
    Modified  { feature: FeatureId, from: Box<TopoName> },
    Split     { feature: Option<FeatureId>, from: Box<TopoName>, piece: Option<u32> },
    Merged    { feature: Option<FeatureId>, from: BTreeSet<TopoName> },
    Root      { container: ContainerId },
}
pub enum NameKind { Body, Surface, Face, Curve, Edge, Vertex }
pub enum Generator {
    SketchEntity(SketchEntityId),
    SpatialSketchEntity(SpatialSketchEntityId),
    Entity(Box<TopoName>),
}
pub enum GenerationRole { Start, End, Side, Seam, Body, Hole(HoleFaceRole), Other(CodecName) }
pub enum HoleFaceRole { BoreWall, Bottom, HeadWall, HeadFloor, HeadCone }
```

A name identifies an entity by how the design produced it. An entity's record id persists only while the source's kernel keeps the entity; a name survives a rebuild by another application.

- **A structured name states meaning, and only meaning.** Every source name splits into three parts: the meaning (the producing feature, the role, the generating sketch entity, and wrappers for patterns, modifications, splits, and merges), a discriminator among entities of equal meaning, and the source's own allocations (SolidWorks producer ids and timestamps, Fusion feature-id counters, Creo geometry ids, FreeCAD tags and hashes, NX keys). `TopoName` holds the first two. Allocations live only in `NameEntry.native`: two allocations of one meaning name the same entity (Rule N case (b)).
- **Roles.** `Start` and `End` are the caps of a swept solid: `Start` the cap at the end of the span against the direction of the extrusion, the rotation, or the path, and `End` the cap along it, for every span (a symmetric extrude's cap below the profile plane, against its direction, is `Start`). `Side` is a face swept from a profile entity, `Seam` an edge or face a closed entity closes on, `Body` the body. `Hole(r)` is a face of a hole by its place in the hole's shape (§6.4): `BoreWall` the bore's wall, a tapered bore's cone included, `Bottom` its flat or drill-point bottom, `HeadWall` and `HeadFloor` a counterbore's or spotface's wall and floor, and `HeadCone` a countersink's cone or a counterdrill's entry cone. Fusion names them by token: `(1, 3)` is `BoreWall`, `(1, 5)`, `(1, 4)`, and `(1, 2)` the flat `Bottom`, the plane at the hole's stored depth along its drilling direction with its outward normal against that direction, and `(1, 6)` the drill-point `Bottom`, `(1, 7)` `HeadWall` and `(1, 8)` `HeadFloor` of a counterbore, and selector 2's `(2, 10)` `HeadCone`; the hole's `HoleBottom` says which bottom, and the head tokens' sizes and token 2 are listed in part 11. Fusion writes 4 or 2 in place of 5 on holes of scope type version 5 only, and nothing in the hole's form, its document, its bore's stored axis, or a fixed byte of its records says when, so the token is no part of the meaning and stays in the name's `native`; a Fusion writer names a flat bottom `(1, 5)`, the only flat-bottom token of scope type version 7. No stored file known to the project holds a Fusion tapered, spotface, or counterdrill head, so which tokens name their faces is not read (part 11). `Other(text)` keeps a source role code whose meaning is not established (`"<codec>:<code>"`, Rule N case (a), part 11); every unmapped role is `Other`, and a name with an `Other` role has no transferable meaning. `role: None` states that the source names the producing feature and no role (an edge named by the features that produced its two faces, part 11); a writer derives no role-based target name from it.
- **Generators.** A side face is generated by a sketch curve; a lateral edge by a sketch point, which is a sketch entity of its own (part 6); a face swept along a path by the path's spatial sketch entity; an entity derived from another by that entity's name. A SolidWorks shell names each inner face it makes `Shell(F, <name>)`, by the name of the face it offsets and with no ordinal, which is `Generated { kind: Face, feature: F, role: None, generator: Some(Entity(<name>)), index: None }`.
- **Index.** `index` on `Generated`, `Blend`, `Bounded`, and `Meeting` is the source's own discriminator among entities of equal meaning, stated only where the source stores one (a Creo half ordinal for the two halves of a face swept from a closed circle, a cap region number). A stored discriminator is stated whatever its value: a SolidWorks `EndFace(E, e, 0)` of a cap with one region has `index: Some(0)`. It is never a rank the decoder computes. Entities the source cannot tell apart share one name; a pick tells them apart by its `resolved` entities or its witness (§5.8).
- **Kind.** `TopoName::kind()` is derived: `Generated` states it; `Blend` is a face, `Bounded` an edge, `Meeting` a vertex, `Root` a body; `Instance`, `Modified`, `Split`, and `Merged` have the kind of what they wrap, and the members of `Merged` share one kind. `Surface` and `Curve` names identify carriers (Creo names surfaces, and one surface can carry several faces).
- **Paths.** `Bounded` names an edge by the set of faces beside it and, where the source records them, the set of faces at its ends, with no order in either set (Matching, below). A SolidWorks edge selection stores four face names: the two faces beside the edge, then the faces at its two ends, with no orientation. Each hop is a face name, so a decoder fills `Bounded` from the four hops through the producer-to-feature join, with no state needed; a hop whose producer joins to no feature leaves the pick `Native`. The hops' producer ids and timestamps stay in the pick's native name (`Picked.native`, and `NameEntry.native` where a table names the edge). `Meeting` names a vertex by its faces. `Blend` names a fillet or chamfer face; `between` holds the faces it joins only where the source stores them as the name (Creo, CATIA). A decoder never adds them by derivation, so one decode gives a blend face one spelling (D45). SolidWorks numbers a fillet's or chamfer's faces (`Fillet(F, n)`) from 1 to N, one per edge it rounds after tangent propagation, a value staying on each piece of a split face; which edge takes which `n` is not established, being neither the API's edge order nor the face node order (part 11). Fusion numbers them by a token that follows the order of the fillet's selected edges; that number is the `index`. Inventor names a fillet face by the match key of the edge it rounds, which stays in `native`. `between` is empty for all three. `Instance` names a copy by the feature that made it and its instance coordinates: an implicit pattern instance by its `InstanceIndex`, copy k of a `TransformBodies` copy by `[k]`, and the copy an `Extract` makes by `[1]`, as the mirror image is (§6.5). `Root` names a body whose identity is its container (a Creo implicit body, a FreeCAD PartDesign Body).
- **Splits and merges.** Sources keep no piece number: the pieces of a split face share one name in SolidWorks, NX, Creo, and Fusion, and FreeCAD numbers them in kernel order. `piece` is `None` unless the source states a piece; a pick tells pieces apart by its `resolved` entities or its witness (§5.8). `Split.feature` and `Merged.feature` name the feature that split or merged the entity where the source stores it; SolidWorks and Fusion store neither, and their decoders state `None`.
- **Equality** is structural over the fields above. A name contains no coordinate and no source allocation.
- **One name, possibly several entities.** A name repeats within a state where the source gives several entities one name. A pick by it matches every entity that carries it.
- **Native names.** `native` holds the source's own name in full. A name that refers to a table the source keeps for the whole definition is in full with that reference, and the table stays a native record of the definition (FreeCAD 1.x writes mapped names such as `;#14:1;:G0;XTR;:H11b0:8,F` as references into its `StringHasher` table). A writer to the same codec stamps it unchanged. A stored-geometry feature's entities are named by that feature where the source names them by it: a Fusion Base Feature face `(1, n, [-b])` is `Generated { kind: Face, feature: b, role: None, generator: None, index: Some(n) }`, the form a Fusion writer stamps (§3.4). An entity that no feature of the document produced has `name: None`, and so has one whose source name names no feature (Inventor `IMPORT_TAG` bodies); a source role code whose meaning is not established is an `Other` role, never `name: None`. An entry holds at least one of `name` and `native`.
- **Order.** Every feature a name mentions is one the named state depends on (§5.3). A name on an instance body may mention features of the prototypes that its path's occurrences place: the assembly state depends on them through those occurrences (§5.3).
- **Derivation.** Where a source name is opaque and a state holds the geometry, a decoder derives role and generator by geometry (the side face whose surface is the sweep of sketch line L), marks them `inferred` in the exactness annotations, and keeps the source name in `native`.
- An Inventor edge selector picks an edge by its neighbourhood in the state where Inventor matched the selection, which the part's construction-history archive holds: the tail of the kernel record in the `PmBRepSegment` segment, an ASM history (§3.1) whose `delta_state` chain frames and closes at the empty model. A selector resolves, through the matched attribute stamped with its source index and key, to a stored edge, which may lie in archived revisions only. The stamp state, the oldest in which that attribute is live, is the selecting feature's input. The first array is the feature digest of a `Bounded` name in that state: for the edge, its two side faces, and the faces at its end vertices, the feature of each entity's outermost name wrapper and of its newest `Modified` wrapper, keeping features older than the selector, side faces first. The digest does not in general name one edge, so the decoder reads the names from the archive: the pick is `Entity(Bounded { faces, ends, index: None })` with the side and end faces' names as the stamp state stores them, roles and generators included, anchored `Input`, with `resolved` the matched edge in that state and the selector record in `native` (both arrays, the key, the item and context references, and the two body words, which are the source index of the selected body). The second array is not established beyond its modifier tags and stays in `native` (part 11).
- A CATIA part stores the name of each face, edge, and vertex in the procedural report of its geometric container: the `CATStorageProperty` rows that open with `01 00 04 00` and a tag hold a header per feature build, which names the feature's record, and a member per named kernel object, which holds the object's tag, a key, and the members it derives from. A CATIA decoder states a face's name from its member and the chain of members it cites back to a keyed root: a key `0` member that cites a sketch element's member is `Generated` with role `Side`, and with that sketch entity as `generator` where the decoder joins the element to one; a member that cites one earlier cell is `Modified` from that cell's name; one that cites several is `Merged`; and the keys `1` and `2` are the role `Other` with the key (`"catia:key:1"`), since they name caps in some files only (§3.4). The chain names the feature's class only where the file's definitions are in the selector form. A CATIA pick of a face (a `FeatureRSUR` or another BRep reference object) heads a header whose member names the face by its tag, so a decoder states the pick by that face's name. A member's `kind` is a per-file class index, which the decoder does not read.

**Tables per state.** `Design.names` names the entities of `CadIr.geometry`. Each evaluation's `delta.names` gives its state's table relative to its base. A table holds only the names a source stores and the names a decoder derives for entities (Derivation); edges and vertices need no entry (D46).

**Matching.** A pick by an `Entity` name resolves in its anchored state by this rule:
- A name matches each entity whose table entry carries it.
- A `Bounded` name also matches an edge that the anchored state's adjacency places between faces matching every name of `faces`; these edges are its candidates. `ends` narrows the candidates only where there are several: it keeps each candidate whose end vertices lie on faces matching every name of `ends`, and an end name that names no entity of the state is ignored, and a narrowing that would keep no candidate is not applied. So a SolidWorks edge selection stored with the faces of a feature that a configuration suppresses still matches in that configuration. A `Meeting` name also matches each vertex where faces matching every name of `faces` meet.
- Every `index` in a name, at any depth (inside `Modified`, `Split`, `Instance`, and `Generator::Entity`, and in each name of `Bounded`, `Meeting`, `Blend`, and `Merged`), is a discriminator, not meaning: names match with every `index` left out, and the entities so matched are the pick's candidates. Each index the pick states then keeps, at its place in the name, the candidates whose entries state the same index at that place; a place where no candidate's entry states an index keeps them all. Every place is judged against all the candidates, so the result does not depend on the order of places. Names of one set that are equal with their indexes left out are one place, whose index is the set of the indexes they state. A name inside `Bounded.faces`, `Bounded.ends`, or `Meeting.faces` matches its faces by this same rule. A `Bounded` name's `ends` narrows the candidates its indexes keep.
- A pick that matches several entities resolves to all of them. Where it means one, its `resolved` entities or its witness choose (§5.8).
- A pick with a `Native` target, and a pick whose resolving definition has no scope in this document, is matched against no name table.

### 5.8 Selections

```rust
pub struct Selection<O: MemberOrder> { pub at: Anchor, pub picks: Picks<O>, pub native: Option<NativeSelections> }
pub type OrderedSelection = Selection<Ordered>;
pub type SetSelection = Selection<Unordered>;
pub enum Anchor { Input, Pinned(Position), Current, Native(NativeName) }
pub enum Picks<O: MemberOrder> {
    Unread,
    Named(Members<Picked, O>),
    Rule { terms: Vec<RuleTerm<O>>, excluded: Vec<RuleTerm<O>>, resolved: Option<Members<Picked, O>> },
}
pub struct Picked {
    pub target: PickTarget,
    pub context: Option<PickContext>,
    pub native: Option<NativeName>,
    pub domain: Option<PickDomain>,
    pub witness: Option<Witness>,
    pub resolved: Option<Vec<EntityRef>>,
}
pub enum PickTarget {
    Entity(TopoName),
    Native { within: Option<NativeOwner> },
    Sketch(SketchId),
    SketchEntity(SketchEntityId),
    SpatialSketchEntity(SpatialSketchEntityId),
    SketchRegion { sketch: SketchId, region: SketchRegion },
    SketchFrame { sketch: SketchId, entity: PrincipalEntity },
    Datum { feature: FeatureId, part: Option<DatumPart> },
    Principal { entity: PrincipalEntity, container: Option<ContainerId> },
    Feature(FeatureId),
    FeatureResult(FeatureId),
    TemplateInput { instance: FeatureId, input: u32 },
    Component,
    Publication(PublicationId),
}
pub enum NativeOwner { Sketch(SketchId), SpatialSketch(SpatialSketchId), Feature(FeatureId) }
pub enum PickContext {
    Occurrence(OccurrencePath),
    Definition(DefinitionRef),
    InContext {
        assembly: DefinitionRef,
        own: Option<OccurrencePath>,
        target: Option<OccurrencePath>,
    },
}
pub struct DefinitionRef { pub definition: ProductDefinitionId, pub configuration: Option<ConfigurationRef> }
pub struct OccurrencePath(pub Vec<PathStep>);
pub struct PathStep { pub occurrence: StepRef, pub configuration: Option<ConfigurationRef> }
pub enum StepRef { Occurrence(OccurrenceId), Native(NativeName) }
pub enum PrincipalEntity { XyPlane, XzPlane, YzPlane, XAxis, YAxis, ZAxis, Origin, Frame }
pub enum DatumPart { Principal(PrincipalEntity), Point(u32) }
pub struct Witness {
    pub point: Option<FinitePoint3>,
    pub direction: Option<UnitVector3>,
    pub endpoints: Option<[FinitePoint3; 2]>,
    pub frame: Option<FrameValue>,
    pub curves: Vec<InlineCurve>,
    pub surface: Option<InlineSurface>,
    pub body: Option<Box<Topology>>,
}
pub enum PickDomain {
    EdgeInterval { start: FiniteReal, end: FiniteReal },
    Limits { start: Option<Box<Picked>>, end: Option<Box<Picked>> },
    Fragment(Fragment),
    Containing(FinitePoint3),
}
```

Every operand that picks geometry or design entities is a selection: bodies, faces, edges, vertices, surfaces, curves, sketches and their entities, regions, and frames, datums and their parts, principal planes and axes, features and their results, template inputs, component occurrences, and publications. Feature definitions and process records hold no record id, except in a pick's `resolved` cache (below).

- **Anchors.** `Input` evaluates in the state entering the feature whose definition holds the selection, which is a member of an ordered container, and follows edits that insert features before it. `Input` occurs only in a feature's definition, in a sketch that the feature owns (a sketch is part of its owner's definition), and in the expression of a parameter that the feature owns. A feature that is not in an ordered container (a member of an unordered container: a CATIA geometrical-set element, a FreeCAD Part object, a joint with no order) anchors its selections `Current`, except an operand that selects the result of another member `m` of the same unordered container that has its own result (§5.3), which is anchored `Pinned(After(m))`. An operand that selects a live object with no producing member (the section curves of a Rhino loft, which are wire bodies, §5.6) is anchored `Current`; a decoder names the object by its source id (a `Native` pick) and states `resolved` with the object's wire edge, which that id identifies. `Pinned(p)` evaluates in one fixed state. `Current` evaluates in the current geometry of the scope the pick resolves in, the union of that scope's current-state extents and of its unproduced bodies (§5.5), and follows every edit (Fusion CAM selections). `Native` names a state of a definition that has no scope in this document, by the source's own name for it (an NX link to a part as it stood after one of its features).
- **Picks.** `Named` lists picks. `Rule` states a rule (below). A member the decoder could not resolve is a pick with a `Native` target. `Unread` states that the source holds a selection whose members the decoder did not read. `native` holds the source's group-level selection record where it has one.
- **Targets.**
  - `Entity` names a geometric entity by its structured name.
  - `Native` is a pick known only by its native name or its witness: a member the decoder could not resolve, an entity with no transferable name, an operand the source names by a consumer-local key (SolidWorks combine operands), or an operand the source stores only as frozen geometry (an Inventor "to face" plane). `within` names the sketch or feature the pick lies in, so the dependency on it is kept (a FreeCAD `Edge3` of a sketch, an NX section member).
  - `SketchRegion` picks one region of a sketch by its boundary (part 6). `SketchFrame` picks a sketch's plane, axes, normal, or origin. `Datum` picks a datum feature, or one principal entity of a coordinate-frame datum, or one point of a multi-point datum. `Principal` picks an origin plane, axis, point, or frame of the definition the pick resolves in, or of an ordered container that carries its own origin (a FreeCAD PartDesign Body). A pick of such a container's origin always names the `container`, also where the container's frame is its definition's (an object that an `App::Link` places, §6.7). A `Principal` pick whose context reaches a definition with no scope in this document (an `External` prototype) picks that definition's own origin, with no `container`; the origin of a container inside a document that was not read is a `Native` pick by the source's name for it.
  - `Feature(f)` picks a feature as an object (the joints a coupling acts on, the pattern a component pattern follows). `FeatureResult(f)` is the whole geometric result of feature `f`, and the one spelling of a pick of it (a FreeCAD `Cut.Tool` that links the `Box` object with no sub-element); an `Entity` pick of a body name occurs only where the source names a body. `TemplateInput` picks an input of a template instance, from inside the features the instance generates (part 6).
  - `Component` is the occurrence that the pick's context names. `Publication` picks a published entity (§5.11).
- **Context.** A pick resolves in the definition of the selection's owner unless `context` says otherwise. A design selection's owner definition is its feature's `component` where stated, else its scope's definition (§5.1); a Fusion pick inside the feature's own component therefore has no context. A process selection's owner definition is its setup's scope (part 7).
  - `Occurrence(path)` resolves the target in the prototype reached by the path from the owner's definition, outermost occurrence first: "face F of instance I" in a mate, an assembly cut, a drawing, or a manufacturing operation. A Fusion pick made through an occurrence stores that occurrence's GUID as the context of its selection prefix, and the decoder states the path from that occurrence up its owner chain; a context that names neither an occurrence nor a component is read as the picking component's own (part 11).
  - A pick through an occurrence picks what the instance shows: an instance that an assembly feature has changed shows instance bodies in place of its prototype's bodies (§6.7, §8.1). Where the pick's target is a body, a face, an edge, a vertex, or a surface, and its anchored state in the owner's scope holds instance bodies for the instance its `Occurrence(path)` names, the pick resolves in those bodies, in that state, and crosses into no other scope. Where that state holds none, the pick resolves along its path, crossing into another scope where the path leaves the owner's (below). Where an assembly definition along the path then holds instance bodies for the instance, in the state of its scope that the pick reads, the pick resolves in those of the outermost such definition, which show the instance as every definition below it leaves it; otherwise it resolves in the prototype. A pick of a datum, a sketch, or the occurrence itself resolves in the prototype. A pick whose path states a step configuration other than the one that occurrence uses reads the prototype in that configuration, and no instance bodies. Instance bodies are in the prototype's coordinates (§8.1), so a witness and a connector's frame are in those coordinates wherever the pick resolves, and the bodies' names are entries of the table of the state that holds them, which may mention the prototype's features (§5.7). Where no state the pick reads holds instance bodies for the instance, and one of those states depends on an assembly feature, not suppressed in that state's configuration, that may change the instance otherwise than through its definition, the document does not hold what the instance shows: the pick keeps its names and witness and is not checked. Such a feature holds the instance as a participant under an effect other than `Definitions`, or holds, under such an effect, `Unread` picks or a rule that states no `resolved` (a Creo assembly cut at top level, whose cut faces are not delivered; an NX assembly cut, whose effect is not stated; §6.7).
