Open curves bound no region and make a sheet or a thin wall.
- **Loop nesting.** `LoopNesting` states the rule by which an extrude or revolve turns its profile's closed loops into regions, where the source states one (FreeCAD's face makers: `Part/App/FaceMaker.h`, `FaceMakerCheese.h`, `FaceMakerBullseye.h`, and `FeatureExtrusion.h` at 1.1.4). `Alternate` is the rule above (FreeCAD `Bullseye`). `OneLevel` makes a loop inside an outer loop a hole and an island inside a hole an error, so the operation fails (FreeCAD `Cheese`, and the legacy `FaceMakerExtrusion`, which is `Cheese` that ignores the input's compound nesting). `Independent` makes every closed loop a region with no holes, overlapping where loops overlap (FreeCAD `Simple`). `EveryLevel` makes every band between consecutive nested loops a region, so a hole is also filled as a region of its own (FreeCAD `Ring`). On a profile with no island and no overlapping loops, `Alternate` and `OneLevel` give the same regions. A FreeCAD `Part::Extrusion` that stores no face maker restores the legacy one, so one that stores none or the legacy face maker is `OneLevel`. A PartDesign profile feature is `OneLevel` where its `AllowMultiFace` is false or absent and `Alternate` where it is true (`PartDesign/App/FeatureSketchBased.cpp`). A writer whose target has only the alternate rule writes `OneLevel` as it is where the profile holds no island. It writes `Independent` as one extrude or revolve per loop, of the loop's whole region, and `EveryLevel` as one by the alternate rule plus one per hole, of the hole's region by the alternate rule, each with the source's span and Boolean; these are several geometry features, which §3.4's rules for a construction govern, and it charges `export:feature.lowered`.
- **Unresolved sources.** A source the decoder cannot resolve is a `Native` pick `within` its sketch or feature (§5.8), so the dependency on that sketch or feature stays (D26).
- A path is a selection whose picks form one connected chain, in path order: sketch and spatial-sketch curves, edges, curves, or feature results. Tangent propagation along a path is a term with `Connected { continuity: G1 }` propagation (FreeCAD `SpineTangent`).

**Output and the Boolean.**

```rust
pub struct SolidOutput { pub body: Option<BodyForm>, pub boolean: Option<Boolean> }
pub enum BodyForm { Solid, Thin(ThinWall), Sheet }
pub struct ThinWall { pub thickness: Thickness, pub ends: Option<ThinEnds>, pub corner_round: Option<CornerRound> }
pub enum CornerRound { Sharp, Round(Dimension<PositiveLength>) }
pub enum Thickness {
    OneSide   { value: Dimension<PositiveLength>, side: Option<WallSide> },
    Symmetric(Dimension<PositiveLength>),
    Offsets   { outside: Dimension<Length>, inside: Dimension<Length> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum WallSide { Inside, Outside, Left, Right, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum ThinEnds { Capped(Dimension<PositiveLength>), Merged }
pub enum Boolean { NewBody, Apply { op: BooleanOp, targets: Option<Targets> } }
pub enum BooleanOp { Join, Cut, Intersect, Assemble, Sew, Compound, UnionTrim, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum Targets { All, Selected(SetSelection) }
pub struct SheetOutput { pub solid: Option<Solidify>, pub boolean: Option<Boolean> }
pub enum Solidify { Sheet, IfClosed, CapPlanarOpenings }
```

`SolidOutput` states what a profile-driven operation makes and how it changes existing bodies; extrude, revolve, sweep, helical sweep, primitive, loft, and implicit sweep carry it. `SheetOutput` states the same for an operation that builds sheets (patch, knit, offset copy). `Boolean` is the one home of the bodies an operation combines with: the rib, thicken, and boundary fill carry it alone, the hole and emboss carry its `Targets`, and `Combine` (§6.5) is the Boolean as an operation.

- `Sheet` is a surface result (Fusion surface extrude; FreeCAD `Solid = false`; CATIA GSD extrude and revolve; Creo surface forms; NX sheet body type). `Thin` is a solid wall about the profile curves (CATIA thin; Creo form bit 128; SolidWorks thin; NX extrude offset; NX sweep-along-guide offsets).
- `Thickness` is a wall's thickness and where it lies. `OneSide` puts the whole `value` on `side`. `Inside` and `Outside` grow the wall into or away from the material that a closed profile or a face bounds; for a face offset (thicken), `Outside` is along the face normal and `Inside` against it. `Left` and `Right` are the sides of an open profile: its chain traversed in pick order, starting along the first curve's own direction, seen looking against the profile normal. A source whose side rule is not established states `WallSide::Native` and keeps its flag as a native option (Rule N case (a), part 11): SolidWorks one-direction thin, whose reverse is a value of its wall type and no separate flag (`ThinWallType` 0 one direction, 1 one direction reverse: SolidWorks API `IExtrudeFeatureData2.ThinWallType`), is `WallSide::Native("sldprt:one_direction")` or `WallSide::Native("sldprt:one_direction_reverse")`, and CATIA states two thicknesses. A CATIA prism is thin where its `Thin` is 2 (the stored boolean is its value plus one, as `Sym`, the sweep modes, and the hole bottoms store theirs: inferred), and its wall is `ThickThin1` + `ThickThin2` thick, one on each side of the profile, either of which may be 0. Which side `ThickThin1` lies on is not established, so the CATIA decoder states `Thickness::Native("catia:ThickThin")` with `catia:ThickThin1` and `catia:ThickThin2` as native options until it is, and `Offsets` once it is (Rule N case (a), part 11). `NeutralFiber`, read from its name as splitting the wall equally about the profile whatever `ThickThin2` holds, is the native option `catia:NeutralFiber` (part 11). `Symmetric` splits its value equally between the sides. `Offsets` states the extent on each side, signed and measured into that side, so a negative value makes a band that does not touch the profile (Fusion shell inside and outside thickness, CATIA `TopOffset` and `BotOffset`, NX first and second offset; an NX non-symmetric offset with start `s` and end `e` measured along the outside direction is `outside: e` and `inside: −s`, through `Negated` where a parameter binds `s`). On an open profile, `outside` is the `Left` side. `Capped` closes the ends of a thin wall over a closed profile, with the cap thickness (SolidWorks cap ends). `Merged` extends the wall ends to existing material (CATIA `MergeThin`). `corner_round` applies to a wall over an open profile. `Round(r)` rounds each corner where two lines of the profile meet at an angle: the wall's face on the concave side of the corner is a cylinder of radius r tangent to both straight faces there. The face on the convex side is the concentric cylinder of radius r plus the thickness where the wall keeps its thickness through the corner; that is inferred, and neither a page nor a stored corner states it. `Sharp` leaves every corner sharp. `Round` says nothing of a corner that involves an arc or a spline, so it occurs only with a profile whose picked curves are all line segments (part 10): a source that sets the option on a profile with an arc or a spline keeps it in its native options with `corner_round: None`, and a writer of another codec charges a loss naming the feature. SolidWorks' auto-fillet corners is `Round`, typed from SolidWorks' Extrude PropertyManager page ("Creates a round at each edge where the lines meet at an angle"; its Fillet Radius "Sets the inside radius of the round"): r is that inside radius, the concave face's, and no stored rounded corner is established. That its carrier is the thin specification's radial display dimension `D7` is inferred from `D7` being the only radial dimension a thin specification owns, and the flag that turns the option on is not read. No stored file known to the project settles whether the option is on or whether `D7` is the inside or the convex face's radius, and `Round`'s inside radius is the page's (part 11). No stored byte is tied to the option, and the SolidWorks decoder states `corner_round: None` and keeps `sldprt:thin_auto_fillet` and `sldprt:thin_fillet_radius` (typed, carrier unread, part 11). A writer whose target has no corner round on a thin feature takes step 3 (§3.4).
- `Apply` combines the result with existing bodies. `targets` names them: `All`, or the `Selected` bodies (SolidWorks feature scope, `moPerBodyChooserData_c`; Fusion participant bodies; Inventor extrusion slot 24; NX target bodies). A SolidWorks feature scope with auto-select is `Selected` with the bodies SolidWorks stored at creation: it processes only those, so it differs from `All` after edits; the auto flag is the source setting `sldprt:auto_select`, which records how the list was chosen and not which bodies it holds, and no edit makes it change them (Rule N case (b)); a SolidWorks writer clears it when it writes `Selected`. A member of a `Body` container whose `Boolean` is `Apply` acts on that container's body (§5.2), and its `targets` is `None`. An assembly feature's operation acts on its participants (§6.7), and its `targets` is `None`. `NewBody` creates a body with no combination, which includes a surface result. A `Join` whose input state holds no target body is `NewBody`: a source's first solid feature with "merge result" set has nothing to merge, so it states `NewBody`, and no `sldprt:auto_select`.
- `Assemble` adds a tool body by its own polarity (CATIA Boolean assemble) and occurs only in `Combine`. `Compound` joins with no material interaction: the result is one body that holds each operand's solids as regions of its own, overlapping ones included, and it occurs only in `Combine` (FreeCAD `Part::Compound`, §6). A writer whose target has no such body leaves the operands as separate bodies and charges a loss naming the feature. `Sew` sews the result into the sheets it meets (NX Boolean Sew; a surface merge or knit, such as the SolidWorks filled surface's "merge result") and occurs only in an output. The "merge result" option of a SolidWorks solid feature is `Join`, or `NewBody` where it is cleared or where the feature's input state holds no body.
- `body: None` and `boolean: None` mean the decoder did not read the value (§2.4); the operation keeps every operand it read.
- `SheetOutput.solid` states whether a closed result becomes a solid: `Sheet` keeps a sheet, `IfClosed` forms a solid where the result closes (SolidWorks "try to form solid"), `CapPlanarOpenings` also caps planar openings (CATIA close surface).

**Spans and limits.**

```rust
pub enum Span<Q> {
    Between   { start: Limit<Q>, end: Limit<Q> },
    Symmetric { amount: Dimension<Q>, measure: Option<SymmetricMeasure> },
}
pub enum SymmetricMeasure { PerSide, Total }
pub enum Limit<Q> {
    AtOrigin, Amount(Dimension<Q>), ThroughAll, Next, Last,
    ToGeometry { target: SetSelection, offset: Option<LimitOffset>, extend: Option<Dimension<bool>>, far: Option<Dimension<bool>> },
    ToPlane(Construction<Plane>), ToPoint(Construction<Point>), Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum LimitOffset { Distance(Dimension<Length>), Translated(Dimension<Length>), Angle(Dimension<Angle>) }
```

A span places material along a direction (`Q = Length`) or about an axis (`Q = Angle`), measured from the operation's origin. A one-sided operand (a hole's depth, a rib's extent) is one `Limit<Length>`.

- `Between` fills from `start` to `end`. `end` is measured and searched along the direction, `start` against it. A one-sided operation has `start: AtOrigin`. A two-sided operation states a second limit (CATIA `SecondLimit`, SolidWorks direction 2, Fusion two sides, FreeCAD `Type2`, Creo per-side choices, Inventor second side).
- NX measures both limits along the direction from the section plane, each with its own kind (`Limits` start and end). A decoder stores NX's start value as an `Amount` against the direction, its parameter bound with `Dimension::Negated`, so the binding survives.
- `Symmetric` fills both sides of the origin equally. `measure` states whether `amount` is the extent of each side (CATIA mirrored extent, NX symmetric value in a file last saved in NX 11 or earlier) or the total (SolidWorks mid plane, FreeCAD `Midplane`, Creo symmetric, Inventor symmetric, NX symmetric value in a file last saved in NX 1934 or later). NX reads the value by the newest release in the file's save audit trail: in files last saved in NX 1934 or later the extrude spans its value about the section plane; in files last saved in NX 11 or earlier it spans the value on each side. `measure` decides how the stored `amount` is read, so where it is `None` (Fusion, and NX files last saved in a release from NX 12 to NX 1926; part 11) a writer of another codec does not write the amount, and charges a loss naming the feature (§2.4).
- `Amount` is a signed distance or angle from the origin. `ThroughAll` passes through every target body; in a revolve it is a full turn (Fusion full, Inventor full). `Next` stops at the first face the swept profile meets, `Last` at the last (CATIA, FreeCAD `UpToFirst`, `UpToLast`). Inventor to next is `Next` where its terminator is the body the feature acts on, and `ToGeometry` on the terminator where that is another body; it is not CATIA's up-thru-next.
- `ToGeometry` ends at faces, surfaces, or bodies (CATIA and SolidWorks up to surface; SolidWorks up to body and offset from surface; Fusion to object; FreeCAD `UpToFace`, `UpToShape`; NX until selected; Inventor to face). `offset` moves the limit by a `Distance` or a `Translated` distance, or, in a `Limit<Angle>`, by a `Distance` or an `Angle`; `Distance` offsets the target along its own normals by the distance (a parallel plane at that perpendicular distance from a plane, a cylinder, sphere, or torus with its radius changed by it), and `Translated` moves the target rigidly along the span's direction by the distance, a congruent copy; a positive value moves it further in the direction the limit is measured, along the span's direction for `end` and against it for `start`, whatever way the target faces: a SolidWorks revolve offsets its limit face by a length, and a CATIA offset takes the arm its parameter's magnitude type states. A source's reverse-offset flag is the offset's sign: a SolidWorks offset from surface with reverse offset clear ends `d` short of its target, on the sketch's side, so it is `Distance(−d)`, and with reverse offset set `Distance(d)`. SolidWorks' translate surface is `Translated` ("a translation of the reference surface, rather than a true offset", Extrude PropertyManager). SolidWorks stores it per direction in the end specification's closing block, the u32 32 and 28 bytes before the block's final word, and the decoder reads it only on end type 5, offset from surface: on other end types the word holds an uninitialised value that changes nothing, so a SolidWorks writer writes 1 on an end of type 5 that is `Translated` and 0 elsewhere (part 11). `extend: Some(true)` extends the target faces until the profile meets them (NX until extended; Fusion To Selected Face, "the input entity is extended"). `Some(false)` uses them as they are; where the source also ends the profile on the faces connected to them (Fusion To Adjacent Faces: "faces connected to the input entity are used"), the term that picks them carries `Connected` propagation. `far` applies where `target` picks bodies: `Some(true)` ends at the far side of the body the profile meets, `Some(false)` at its near side (Fusion Through Body and To Body, `isMinimumSolution`). (Fusion's extrude reference and API `ToEntityExtentDefinition.isChained` and `isMinimumSolution`.) Fusion stores the choice in the face-extend word, the third word of the extrude prologue after the operation and the travel direction, one word for both sides: it is fixed by the extent kind wherever Fusion offers no to-object choice (2 on one-sided and symmetric distances, 0 on through-all, to-plane, and two-sided distances), and takes 1 or 2 on to-face extents and 0 or 1 on to-body ones. Which code is which choice is typed, carrier unread (part 11); until it is read, a Fusion decoder keeps the word of a to-face or to-body extent as the native option `f3d:extent_word` and states `extend: None` and `far: None`.
- `ToPlane` ends at a plane: a datum, a principal plane, or a planar face used as a plane (Creo to selected; CATIA up to plane; Inventor to work plane). An offset from that plane is an `Offset` input of the construction. `ToPoint` ends where the swept profile reaches a point (SolidWorks up to vertex, NX through point, Inventor to work point).
- `Native` keeps a source kind whose meaning is not established (Rule N case (a), part 11): CATIA up thru next, whose end is not established (below), and NX percent and arc-length limits, which no stored file known to the project declares.
- CATIA stores a pad's or pocket's limit kind as `PrismLimitType`. 1 is `Amount`: its `Init` holds no element, and it carries the length. 5 and 6 are `ToGeometry`, whose `Init` holds the element. 4 and 7 end on a face of the body that the profile meets along the direction, and the report names the end by that face, so they are `Next` and `Last` in an order no stored file known to the project settles. Until the order is read the decoder states `Limit::Native("catia:limit:4")` and `Native("catia:limit:7")` and keeps the face each ends on as the native option `catia:limit_face` (typed, carrier unread; part 11); the length stored on such a limit is not used. 2, read as up thru next by elimination (CATIA's public user guide defines up to next and never names up thru next), makes an end face of its own that cites no body cell and ends at its stored depth; ending at a face it meets and ending at the depth are not separated (part 11). The decoder states `Limit::Native("catia:limit:2")` with the stored depth as its value, and a writer of another codec writes a blind extent of that depth and charges a loss naming the feature. 3 occurs on sheet-metal cutouts only. The automation numbering `CatLimitMode` + 1 does not fit: it puts up to plane on code 4, which holds no element. A configuration that changes a limit kind states a definition override (D16).

**Laws.**

```rust
pub enum Law<Q> {
    Constant(Dimension<Q>),
    Linear { start: Dimension<Q>, end: Dimension<Q> },
    Curve(OrderedSelection),
    Expression(Expression),
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
```

A `Law<Q>` is a function of quantity `Q` along a path parameter from 0 to 1: a constant, a linear ramp, a law curve the source selects, or an expression in `LawParameter` (§5.13) whose result has `Q`'s quantity. A twist is a `Law<Angle>`, a scale a `Law<FiniteReal>`, a radius or a line length a `Law<Length>` (CATIA, Creo `trajpar`, NX laws).

**Section and boundary conditions.**

```rust
pub enum SectionCondition {
    Free            { support: Option<Support> },
    Default,
    Direction       { direction: Construction<Direction>, angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>>, weight: Option<Dimension<PositiveReal>> },
    NormalToProfile { angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>>, weight: Option<Dimension<PositiveReal>> },
    Tangent         { support: Option<Support>, weight: Option<Dimension<PositiveReal>>, flip: Option<Dimension<bool>> },
    Curvature       { support: Option<Support>, weight: Option<Dimension<PositiveReal>>, flip: Option<Dimension<bool>> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum Support { Faces(SetSelection), Computed }
pub enum ProjectionDirection { SurfaceNormal, SketchNormal, Along(Construction<Direction>), Native(NonBlankString) }
```

- A `SectionCondition` states how a generated surface meets a loft section, a loft guide, or a patch boundary. `Free` constrains position only (a loft's free end, SolidWorks and CATIA contact); its `support` names faces the section lies on that the condition does not use, where the source states them (a CATIA blend limit's support at point continuity), for a section's `trim_support` (§6.3). `Default` is the source's explicit default. `Direction` leaves the section along a direction at `angle` from it; `NormalToProfile` leaves normal to the section's plane at `angle`. `Tangent` and `Curvature` meet `support` with G1 or G2 continuity.
- `support` names the faces the condition refers to; `Support::Computed` states an automatically computed support (CATIA `StartComputeTang`). `weight` is the source's tangent magnitude (loft start and end weights, Fusion `PatchScale`, where −1 means 0.5). `flip` reverses the tangent side. Fusion's patch continuity per boundary edge, `PatchContinuity` 0, 1, and 2, is `Free`, `Tangent`, and `Curvature` (API `SurfaceContinuityTypes`), and its `PatchFlip` chooses which of the two faces meeting at the edge a tangent or curvature edge is continuous with: false the face of the edge's first coedge, true the other; it is ignored for G0 and for an edge with one face (API `PatchFeatureInput.setContinuity`). A Fusion decoder states that face as `support`. Which stored value is "flipped" is typed, carrier unread (part 11); until it is read, the decoder states `support: None` and keeps the value as the native option `f3d:patch_flip`.
- `ProjectionDirection` states how a curve reaches a face: normal to the receiving surface, normal to the curve's sketch, or along a constructed direction.

### 6.1 Sketches

A sketch is a set of entities and the constraints between them, with a placement. Planar sketches hold entities in sketch coordinates on a placed plane; spatial sketches hold them in the coordinates of their definition. Both share one entity and constraint vocabulary, parameterized by the space. The arenas are `sketches`, `sketch_entities`, `sketch_constraints`, `spatial_sketches`, `spatial_sketch_entities`, and `spatial_sketch_constraints`. Sketch entities and constraints have stable ids (§2.2); constraints are canonical over the solved geometry (D9), and dimension values are `Dimension`s (D1, D10).

```rust
pub struct Sketch {
    pub id: SketchId,
    pub owner: FeatureId,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub plane: SketchPlane,
    pub solve: SketchSolve,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum SketchPlane { Placed(Construction<Frame>), Block }
pub struct SpatialSketch {
    pub id: SpatialSketchId,
    pub owner: FeatureId,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub solve: SketchSolve,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub struct SketchSolve { pub state: Option<SolveState>, pub status: EvaluationStatus }
pub enum SolveState { Full, Under, NotFull, Over, Inconsistent, Native(NonBlankString) }
```

- **Owner.** `owner` is the feature whose definition holds the sketch; a sketch is part of its owner's definition (§5.8). A sketch that is a history member of its own is owned by a feature whose operation is `Sketch(s)` (planar) or `SpatialSketch(s)`, which names the sketch and carries no other operand. A sketch the source keeps inside another feature (a Creo section; a CATIA hole's internal sketch) is owned by that feature and is no member of a container, as an inline construction is (§5.9). The sketch's selections are part of its owner's definition: an `Input` anchor in a sketch evaluates in the state entering the owner. A configuration that places a sketch on another plane or changes its entities overrides the owner's definition with one that names another sketch record of the same owner, which then swaps the sketch in that configuration (§5.11; SolidWorks configurations).
- **Placement.** `Placed` holds the plane frame as a `Construction<Frame>` (§5.9). The support is a `Whole` `Coincident` input that picks a datum plane, a principal plane, a planar face, or another sketch's plane (`SketchFrame`); the origin is an `Origin` `Coincident` input; the in-plane x axis is an `XAxis` input `Parallel` to an edge or axis, and a vertical reference is a `YAxis` input; an offset distance or angle from the support is a `Whole` `Offset` or `Angle` input with its dimension. CATIA's swap of the H and V directions puts the orientation input on `YAxis`; its reverse flags and NX's reference-direction flip set the input's `reversed`. `mode` keeps the source method (a FreeCAD attachment mode, the CATIA support, origin, and orientation modes, a Fusion `refType`, CATIA sliding or positioned). The construction's `after` holds, in the source's order, its flip of the normal as a `Flip` step (Creo `plane_flip`, FreeCAD `MapReversed`, NX reverse normal) and its displacement in the attached frame as `Translate` and `Rotate` steps (FreeCAD `AttachmentOffset`, Fusion `OffsetX/Y/Z` and `AngleZ`). `resolved` is the solved frame, a cache (K2). A sketch with free placement (FreeCAD) has no inputs and a resolved frame. A sketch whose support the decoder does not read states the `Unread` input of §5.9 (Unread roles): one input whose `role` is `None` and whose reference is an `Unread` selection of the support, with its `resolved` frame where the decoder reads the stored frame and no resolved value where it does not (a Creo sketch, whose section support references the decoder does not read; an Inventor sketch whose placement it does not resolve). A Creo sketch-plane datum that nothing else references is inline: its constraints are the sketch's inputs (§5.9).
- **Block.** `Block` marks a block definition: a sketch with no plane, whose entities are placed by block instances in other sketches (SolidWorks, Inventor). A block definition the source keeps outside its history is owned by a feature in a root `Group` container of the scope (§5.2), which gives it no place in any history order: the feature is stateless (§5.4) and, as a member of an unordered container, has no result (§5.3); a SolidWorks block definition, a history feature, stays in the timeline. Inventor keeps its definitions so: each is a participant of a folder record of type `d5260222` (the Blocks folder), which is participant 0 of the part's root label, ahead of every feature, and of no other label, though a definition may have been created after features it precedes there. The Inventor decoder takes that folder as the root `Group`, and gives it no place in its history order.
- **Solve state.** `state` is the source's record of how far the constraints determine the geometry: `Full` (FreeCAD `FullyConstrained` true), `NotFull` (FreeCAD false: under-constrained or unsolvable, the source does not say which), `Under`, `Over`, `Inconsistent` (CATIA `SolvingStatus`, NX `Sketch.Status`). `None` means not stated.
- **Solve status.** `status` is the status of the sketch's solved values (entity geometry, the resolved frame): `Current` where the source does not flag them, `Stale` (FreeCAD `Touched`), `Failed` (a recorded solve failure). The edit helpers mark it `Stale` when they edit a dimension of the sketch or a referent of its selections (§4).
- `SpatialSketch` has no placement: its coordinates are those of its definition.

```rust
pub trait SketchSpace {
    type Sketch: Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema;
    type Entity: Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema;
    type Constraint: Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema;
    type Point: Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema;
    type Direction: Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema;
    type Curve: Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema;
}
pub struct Planar;
pub struct Spatial;
// Planar:  SketchId, SketchEntityId, SketchConstraintId, FinitePoint2, UnitVector2, PlanarCurve
// Spatial: SpatialSketchId, SpatialSketchEntityId, SpatialSketchConstraintId, FinitePoint3, UnitVector3, SpatialCurve

pub struct SketchEntity<S: SketchSpace> {
    pub id: S::Entity,
    pub sketch: S::Sketch,
    pub definition: EntityDefinition<S>,
    pub roles: Vec<EntityRole<S>>,
    pub construction: Option<bool>,
    pub centerline: Option<bool>,
    pub native: Option<NativeName>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum EntityDefinition<S: SketchSpace> {
    Free(S::Curve),
    Defined { form: EntityForm<S>, solved: Option<S::Curve> },
}
pub enum EntityForm<S: SketchSpace> {
    Interpolated(InterpolatedSpline<S>),
    Conic { rho: Dimension<FiniteReal> },
    Derived(Derivation),
    Text(SketchText<S>),
    BlockInstance(BlockInstance),
    Instanced { instance: S::Entity, of: SketchEntityId },
    Frame,
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub struct EntityRole<S: SketchSpace> { pub of: S::Entity, pub role: DefiningRole }
pub enum DefiningRole {
    Start, End, Center, Apex, Focus(u8), MajorAxis, MinorAxis, XAxis, YAxis,
    Fit(u32), Pole(u32), Knot(u32), Handle(u32), Anchor, Insertion, Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum PlanarCurve {
    Point(FinitePoint2),
    Line { start: FinitePoint2, end: FinitePoint2 },
    InfiniteLine { through: FinitePoint2, direction: UnitVector2 },
    Circle { center: FinitePoint2, radius: PositiveLength },
    Arc { center: FinitePoint2, radius: PositiveLength, start: Angle, end: Angle },
    Ellipse { center: FinitePoint2, major: UnitVector2, radii: [PositiveLength; 2], range: Option<[Angle; 2]> },
    Parabola { vertex: FinitePoint2, axis: UnitVector2, focal: PositiveLength, range: Option<[FiniteReal; 2]> },
    Hyperbola { center: FinitePoint2, major: UnitVector2, radii: [PositiveLength; 2], range: Option<[FiniteReal; 2]> },
    Nurbs(PcurveNurbs),
    Spatial(SpatialCurve),
}
pub enum SpatialCurve { Point(FinitePoint3), Bounded(BoundedCurve) }
pub struct BoundedCurve { pub carrier: InlineCurve, pub range: Option<IncreasingParameterInterval> }
```

- **Spaces.** `SketchSpace` names the id, point, direction, and curve types of `Planar` and `Spatial`, as the comments in the sketch list them. Each associated type carries the wire traits (§5.9), so every record generic over a space derives them.
- **Free and defined entities.** A `Free` entity is geometry the constraints position: its curve is the solved value and the cache of the constraints (D9); its kind is the curve's kind. A `Defined` entity has a defining form beyond its curve, and `solved` is the form's cache: the NURBS of an interpolated spline, the conic arc of a rho conic, the projected curve of a derivation. `solved` is `None` only where the source stores no solved value: a derived entity whose source stores the link only (FreeCAD), text, a block instance.
- **Points are entities.** Every sketch point that the source stores as a record, or that a constraint, a selection, a name, or a role refers to, is an entity with a `Point` curve: isolated points, curve ends, centers, conic apexes, spline fit points and poles, text anchors, block insertion points. A source's stored sketch origin point is the sketch's own origin, the operand `Frame(Origin)`, and no entity (Operands, below). A point states what it bounds through `roles`: `{ of: line L, role: Start }` makes it L's start. A decoder follows the source's records: a point record that several curves name is one point entity with a `Start` or `End` role for each curve (Inventor, where a point record can end two or more curves; SolidWorks, whose curves name positions in the block's point roster), and two point records joined by a coincident relation are two entities and a `Coincident` relation. Where the source names an end by curve and position (FreeCAD `GeoId` and `PointPos`), the decoder emits the point entity with a positional key (§2.2). A constraint, a pick, and a name refer to a curve's end only through its point entity; a lateral edge swept from that end is generated by the point (§5.7).
- **Helpers.** `roles` also binds helper geometry to its parent: a FreeCAD pole circle is `Pole(i)` of its spline, an ellipse axis line is `MajorAxis` (FreeCAD internal alignment), a dimensioned spline handle is a `Handle(i)` line (below). Helpers are entities with their own curves and the `construction` flag.
- **Sketch coordinate systems.** A `Frame` entity is a sketch-local coordinate frame: a point entity, its `solved` the frame's origin, whose x and y axes are the construction `InfiniteLine` helpers with roles `XAxis` and `YAxis` of it, where a dimension or a relation uses them. A coordinate dimension is a `Distance` from the origin along one of them. A Creo sketch coordinate system is one (Creo uses it to dimension spline points by coordinates and to orient blend sections). A writer whose target has no such entity writes the point and the two construction lines with their relations, which hold the same geometry (§3.4).
- **Curves.** `PlanarCurve` lists the 2D carriers in sketch coordinates. An arc runs counterclockwise from `start` to `end`. `range` bounds a conic by its parameter; `None` is the full curve. `Spatial` holds a non-planar result inside a planar sketch; only a derived entity has one (CATIA `Imported3DArc`, Fusion included 3D geometry). `SpatialCurve::Bounded` holds a `BoundedCurve`: a part 8 curve carrier (an `InlineCurve`, §5.6) and the interval of its own parameter that the piece uses (§5.6, Annex A). `None` is the carrier's whole domain, as a curve record's is (one turn of a circle or an ellipse, the knot domain of a NURBS curve, §5.6), and a piece the source bounds inside that domain, an arc included, states its `range`.
- **Flags.** `construction` marks geometry that no profile uses (`None` where the source flag is unread, as in CATIA). A derived entity the source keeps for reference only (Creo reference projections, FreeCAD external geometry without `Defining`) has `construction: Some(true)`. `centerline` marks the line the source uses as the axis of revolution and of doubled (diameter) dimensions (Creo centerlines, Inventor axis lines, CATIA `CurrentCenterLine`). A SolidWorks centerline is a construction line.
- `native` holds the source's identity for the entity where it is no record id (a SolidWorks segment id, a Fusion curve id), for a writer to the same codec and for name derivation. Source flags whose meaning is not established are native options of the entity. Fusion stores 7 or 8 one-byte flags per sketch point, and the Fusion API's sketch-point properties give each property it exposes a home (API `SketchPoint`): `isFixed` is a `Fixed` relation; `isLinked`, a point that a projection, an inclusion, or a script places, is a `Derived` entity, and `isReference` its `construction` flag (above); `isVisible`, `isDeletable`, `isFullyConstrained`, and `is2D` have no design meaning, a display state or a value the constraints and coordinates derive (Rule N case (b)). The bytes are numbered 0 to 7 in stored order. Byte 6 marks a point a derivation placed (for project, include, and intersect alike), so the point bounds a `Derived` curve (below), whose `link` comes from the derivation record and not from the byte; byte 5 marks the stored sketch origin, which is no entity; byte 2 is never set; and `is2D` follows from the point's coordinates, held in no byte. Which of `isReference` and `isLinked` byte 6 is, and what bytes 0, 1, 3, 4, and 7 hold, are typed, carrier unread (part 11). Until they are read the decoder keeps the bytes as the native option `f3d:point_flags`.

```rust
pub struct InterpolatedSpline<S: SketchSpace> {
    pub degree: Option<NonZeroU32>,
    pub closed: Option<bool>,
    pub handles: BTreeMap<u32, SplineHandle<S>>,
}
pub struct SplineHandle<S: SketchSpace> {
    pub direction: Option<S::Direction>,
    pub magnitude: Option<Dimension<FiniteReal>>,
    pub curvature: Option<FiniteReal>,
}
pub struct Derivation { pub mode: DerivationMode, pub source: OrderedSelection, pub piece: Option<u32>, pub link: Option<LinkState> }
pub enum DerivationMode {
    Project, Include, Intersect, Silhouette, Offset { distance: Dimension<Length> },
    OntoFaces { faces: SetSelection, direction: Option<ProjectionDirection> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub struct SketchText<S: SketchSpace> { pub text: TextContent, pub layout: Option<TextLayout<S>> }
pub struct TextContent {
    pub content: NonBlankString,
    pub font: Option<NonBlankString>,
    pub height: Option<Dimension<Length>>,
    pub width_factor: Option<Dimension<FiniteReal>>,
    pub angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>>,
    pub horizontal: Option<TextAlign>,
    pub vertical: Option<TextAlign>,
    pub horizontal_box: Option<TextHorizontalBox>,
    pub vertical_box: Option<TextVerticalBox>,
    pub tracking: Option<Dimension<Length>>,
    pub oblique: Option<Dimension<Angle>>,
    pub filled: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
}
pub enum TextAlign { Start, Center, End, Baseline, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum TextHorizontalBox { Ink, Pen }
pub enum TextVerticalBox { Ink, CapHeight }
pub enum TextLayout<S: SketchSpace> { Frame(Vec<S::Entity>), Path { curve: S::Entity, reversed: Option<bool> } }
pub struct BlockInstance { pub block: SketchId, pub angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>>, pub scale: Option<Dimension<FiniteReal>> }
```

- **Splines.** A control-point spline is a `Free` entity with a `Nurbs` curve; its poles, where the source stores them as entities, carry `Pole(i)` roles. An interpolated spline passes through its fit points, the point entities with `Fit(0)` to `Fit(n−1)` roles (Creo `i_pnts`, SolidWorks spline points, Inventor fit-point groups, NX defining points). `handles` holds the tangent and curvature conditions at fit point `i`: the end tangents of a Creo spline (`tan_cond`), SolidWorks tangent handles with their magnitude, NX slope and curvature. A handle whose direction the source dimensions or constrains (SolidWorks tangent radial direction, a Creo spline tangency angle) is a construction `Line` helper with role `Handle(i)` of the spline, starting at fit point `i` along the tangent: `Angle` relations bind to it as to any line, and that handle's `direction` is `None`, because the helper and its relations state it (D52). `magnitude` keeps the weighting, which a dimension can drive. A handle nothing dimensions keeps its `direction` and has no helper. `solved` is the NURBS through the points.
- **Conics.** `Conic` is a conic arc from its `Start` to its `End` point, tangent there to the lines toward its `Apex` point, with shape ratio `rho` (SolidWorks conic, NX conic by rho). `solved` is the ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola arc, or the rational NURBS. A conic stored by its center, axes, and radii (a FreeCAD arc of ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola) is `Free`.
- **Derived entities.** `Derived` is an entity computed from model geometry: `Project` projects the source onto the sketch plane (SolidWorks convert entities, Creo used edges and references, Inventor projected loops, FreeCAD external geometry, CATIA projections, NX projected curves, Fusion Project); `Include` copies the source curve unprojected (Fusion Include 3D Geometry, SolidWorks convert entities and Inventor include geometry in a 3D sketch), so in a planar sketch its `solved` is `PlanarCurve::Spatial` unless the source lies in the sketch plane, and every derivation in a spatial sketch that copies model edges is `Include`; `Intersect` intersects the source with the sketch plane (Inventor cut edges, Fusion Intersect and Intersection Curve with the sketch plane); `Silhouette` takes the source's outline seen along the normal; `Offset` projects and offsets the source by a signed distance along the projected curve's left normal (Creo offset edges, SolidWorks offsets of model edges). `OntoFaces` projects the source onto the `faces` along `direction` (§6's `ProjectionDirection`; `SurfaceNormal` takes the closest point on the faces), so the result lies on those faces and in a planar sketch its `solved` is `PlanarCurve::Spatial` (Fusion Project to Surface). `source` selects the model entities; its anchor and contexts follow §5.8 (a SolidWorks in-context reference is an `InContext` pick). Where the source stores one model entity per output (Inventor projected loops store a sketch curve and an edge per pair), each derived entity's `source` picks that entity and `piece` is `None`. Inventor stores the pair as a link record: `f316de64` names the sketch entity and one edge selector, and the sketch entity is `Project` of that edge, its `source` the selector's `Bounded` pick read at its stamp state; `77d9b0fe` names a sketch point and a model point, and the point is `Project` of it (the origin's centre point, or a work point). Otherwise the entities that one source produces share an equal `source` and number their `piece` in the order the source stores their records; `piece` is only an identity among them, and a writer to another codec matches pieces to its own outputs by solved geometry. `link` is the source's record of associativity (`LinkState`, §5.10): `Current`, `OutOfDate`, `Broken` (FreeCAD `Missing`, a SolidWorks dangling reference), `Locked` (FreeCAD `Frozen`). A derived entity whose source the application isolates (CATIA isolate) is `Free`. A point a derived curve bounds is placed by that curve. An NX projection that is its own feature (`CPROJ`) is a `Curve` feature with `Projection` (§6.6), and the sketch entity that consumes it is `Derived` from that feature's result. Fusion stores one derivation record (type `F1451EC8`) per derivation, whose result list names the sketch curves it made in order, which is `piece`'s order; `source` comes from the selection record that follows it, and the curve's own genesis value carries no mode. The record's projection flag (byte 24 in class version 4, 23 in version 3, 21 in version 1) 0 is `Include`. With the flag 1, its kind word (the u32 at byte 45, 44, or 33) 2 is `Intersect`, of a picked face, body, or edge, and 1 and 3 are `Project`: 3 of one picked curve and 1 of a picked loop, chain, or face boundary. Kind 4 picks a whole body and gives closed loops with no junction of three curve ends and no repeated segment, which an outline (`Silhouette`) and a projection of every edge of a body whose edges all lie on its outline both give, so it is `DerivationMode::Native("f3d:project_body")` (typed, carrier unread; part 11), as is a version-1 record of the layout that stores its result list inline.
- **Offsets of sketch entities** are `Offset` relations (below); offsets of model geometry are derivations. A same-sketch copy is a constraint relation, never a derivation.
- **Text.** `Text` places its content at its `Anchor` point, rotated by `angle` from the sketch x axis, or fitted to a frame of entities, or laid along a curve (Fusion text frame and path). `width_factor` scales the nominal glyph width. `height` is the cap height, the distance from the baseline to the top of a flat capital letter. FreeCAD's stored size is it (below), and so is a Fusion sketch text's in Arial and Verdana. A Fusion text in another font, whose glyphs may fall short of the stored size, and a SolidWorks, Inventor, NX, or CATIA text, whose stored size is not established against a glyph outline, states `height: None`, and its decoder keeps the stored size as the native option `<codec>:text_height` (typed, carrier unread; part 11). `tracking` adds a distance between consecutive characters, and `oblique` shears the glyphs, x' = x + y tan(`oblique`). `horizontal` aligns against the box `horizontal_box` names, the ink's extent (`Ink`) or the pen's from its origin, leading space and side bearing included (`Pen`); `vertical` against the box `vertical_box` names, the ink's extent or the band from the baseline to the cap height, whose `Start` is the baseline, so `Baseline` does not occur with `CapHeight`. `filled: Some(false)` makes the glyphs wires, not faces. `TextContent` is also the content of a text curve (§6.6). A FreeCAD Draft `ShapeString` is a text curve whose `Size` is `height` where `ScaleToSize` is true; where it is false (every file saved before 1.0, which restores it false) the cap height is `Size` × 3072 × the capital M's height / (unitsPerEm × the FreeType face height), which the decoder computes from the font file. Its `Tracking` times `height` over the unscaled cap height is `tracking`; `ObliqueAngle` is `oblique`; `Justification` Left, Center, and Right are `Start`, `Center`, and `End`, and Bottom, Middle, and Top the same vertically; `KeepLeftMargin` true is `Pen` and false `Ink`; `JustificationReference` Cap Height is `CapHeight` and Shape Height `Ink`; `MakeFace` is `filled` (FreeCAD 1.1.4 `shapestring.py` and `FT2FC.cpp`).
- **Blocks.** A `BlockInstance` entity places the block definition `block` at its `Insertion` point, rotated by `angle` and scaled by `scale`. Each entity of the definition that the host sketch shows is an `Instanced` entity naming the instance and the definition entity, with its placed curve in `solved`; constraints in the host sketch refer to it.

```rust
pub struct SketchConstraint<S: SketchSpace> {
    pub id: S::Constraint,
    pub sketch: S::Sketch,
    pub relation: SketchRelation<S>,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub active: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum Operand<S: SketchSpace> { Entity(S::Entity), Frame(PrincipalEntity), Model(OrderedSelection) }
pub enum SketchRelation<S: SketchSpace> {
    Coincident    { a: Operand<S>, b: Operand<S> },
    Concentric    { a: Operand<S>, b: Operand<S> },
    Collinear     { a: Operand<S>, b: Operand<S> },
    Parallel      { a: Operand<S>, b: Operand<S> },
    Perpendicular { a: Operand<S>, b: Operand<S> },
    Tangent       { a: Operand<S>, b: Operand<S>, contact: Option<Contact<S>> },
    Curvature     { a: Operand<S>, b: Operand<S>, contact: Option<Contact<S>> },
    Horizontal    { a: Operand<S>, b: Option<Operand<S>> },
    Vertical      { a: Operand<S>, b: Option<Operand<S>> },
    Midpoint      { point: S::Entity, of: Operand<S> },
    Symmetric     { a: Operand<S>, b: Operand<S>, about: Operand<S> },
    Equal         { members: Vec<Operand<S>> },
    EqualDistance { first: [Operand<S>; 2], second: [Operand<S>; 2] },
    Fixed         { of: Operand<S> },
    Distance { a: Operand<S>, b: Operand<S>, along: Option<DistanceAxis<S>>, doubled: Option<bool>, value: Dimension<Length> },
    Angle    { between: AngleOperands<S>, sector: Option<AngleSector>, value: Dimension<Angle> },
    Radial   { of: S::Entity, measure: RadialMeasure, value: Dimension<Length> },
    Length   { of: Vec<S::Entity>, value: Dimension<Length> },
    Offset(SketchOffset<S>),
    Pattern(SketchPattern<S>),
    Polygon(SketchPolygon<S>),
    Slot(SketchSlot<S>),
    Pierce        { point: S::Entity, curve: Operand<S> },
    Weight        { pole: S::Entity, value: Dimension<PositiveReal> },
    FixedLength   { of: Vec<S::Entity> },
    FixedAngle    { of: Vec<S::Entity> },
    Native { kind: NonBlankString, operands: Vec<Operand<S>>, values: Vec<ScalarDimension> },
}
pub enum Contact<S: SketchSpace> { Via(S::Entity), Ends([S::Entity; 2]) }
pub enum DistanceAxis<S: SketchSpace> { Aligned, Horizontal, Vertical, Along(Operand<S>) }
pub enum AngleOperands<S: SketchSpace> { Between([Operand<S>; 2]), Sweep(S::Entity), Points([S::Entity; 3]) }
pub enum AngleSector {
    Minor,
    Major,
    Directed { second_reversed: bool, clockwise: bool },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum RadialMeasure { Radius, Diameter, MajorRadius, MinorRadius }
```

- **Operands.** An operand is a sketch entity (a point is a point entity), one of the sketch's own axes or its origin (`Frame` with `XAxis`, `YAxis`, or `Origin`: FreeCAD `GeoId` −1 and −2 and the root point, CATIA `AbsoluteAxis`, a source's stored sketch origin point), or a selection of model geometry (CATIA constraints to BRep features, SolidWorks pierce, normal, and reference dimensions to model edges, NX point on string). A sketch's own axes and origin are `Frame` operands, never `Model` picks of its own `SketchFrame`. A relation the source stores against a model entity is a `Model` pick of that entity, also where the entity lies on the sketch's own axes or origin, and an origin feature is picked as its `Datum`, never as `Principal` (§6.2): a SolidWorks point related to the Origin feature's point is `Model` picking `Datum { feature: Origin }`. A `Model` operand follows the anchors of §5.8. In a spatial sketch, `Frame` does not occur; principal axes and planes are `Model` picks of `Principal` targets.
- **Geometric relations.** `Coincident` of two points makes them equal; of a point and a curve, puts the point on the curve (FreeCAD `PointOnObject`, NX `PointOnCurve`; a `Model` chain operand is NX `PointOnString`). `Concentric` applies to circles, arcs, and ellipses. `Horizontal` and `Vertical` take one line, or two points. `Equal` sets equal length for lines and equal radius for circular entities, over two or more members. `Midpoint` puts `point` at the middle of a bounded curve. `Symmetric` mirrors `a` and `b` about a line, or about a point (FreeCAD point symmetry); a sketch mirror is `Symmetric` relations about the mirror line. `Fixed` locks an operand (CATIA reference, FreeCAD `Block`, NX `Fixed`).
- **Tangency.** `Tangent` and `Curvature` (G2) apply to two curves. `contact` names where: `Via(p)` at a point lying on both (FreeCAD via-point form), `Ends([p, q])` at an end of each, which also makes `p` and `q` coincide (FreeCAD endpoint form, Fusion endpoint branches). `None` means anywhere.
- **Dimensions.** A dimension's `value` is a `Dimension<T>` (D10). A driven (reference) dimension binds a parameter whose definition is `Driven` (D11, §5.12); a literal value is driving. `Distance` measures from `a` to `b`: `Aligned` is the Euclidean distance; `Horizontal` and `Vertical` are signed sketch-coordinate differences `b − a` (FreeCAD `DistanceX/Y`); `Along(o)` measures parallel to a line or axis. A decoder of a source that stores magnitudes orders `a` and `b` so the stated value is non-negative. A point's coordinate is a distance from `Frame(Origin)`. The length of one line is the distance between its end points. `doubled` states that the value is twice the distance, measured across a centerline (a diameter dimension of a revolved profile). A dimension that binds a parameter is named by that parameter (SolidWorks `D1` of `D1@Sketch1` is the parameter's `name`), and its `name` is `None`; `SketchConstraint.name` holds a relation's own name, and the name of a literal dimension that the source names and no parameter holds. A named FreeCAD dimension constraint has a parameter of its own (§5.14), whose `name` is the constraint's.
- `AngleOperands::Between` measures from the first line's direction to the second's. `sector` chooses which angle the value is where the source records one: `Minor` and `Major` the non-reflex or reflex angle (NX); `Directed` the angle swept from the first operand's direction to the second's, the second reversed where `second_reversed` is true, counterclockwise about the sketch normal or clockwise where `clockwise` is true, in [0, 2π). CATIA's four sectors are `Directed`: sector 0 is `{ second_reversed: false, clockwise: false }`, 1 is `{ true, false }`, 2 `{ true, true }`, and 3 `{ false, true }`. CATIA stores no sector number: it stores the two choices as attribute records the constraint lists, `CstAttr_Orientation` 3 reversing the second operand and `CstAttr_Side` 3 measuring clockwise, either at 1 or 2 meaning neither, with the operands in the order of the constraint's `elts` list, so `second_reversed` is Orientation 3 and `clockwise` is Side 3. Unlike `Minor` and `Major`, a `Directed` sector does not depend on the bound value. `Sweep` is the angle an arc or elliptic arc subtends. `Points` is the angle at its second point from the direction toward its first point to the direction toward its third, with `sector` as for `Between` (an Inventor three-point angle). `Radial` dimensions a circle, arc, or ellipse; `MajorRadius` and `MinorRadius` apply to ellipses (CATIA, Inventor). `RadialMeasure::Diameter` is the one statement of a diameter dimension: its parameter states no `display` (§5.12). `Length` is the total arc length of its curves (SolidWorks arc and spline length, NX perimeter).
- **State.** `active` is the source's activity flag, which a formula can drive (CATIA `activity_boolean`, Creo status bit, FreeCAD `IsActive`). A constraint has no solve status (D51): no source stores one (CATIA and NX compute theirs on demand), and a SolidWorks dangling relation is a `Model` operand whose selection does not resolve. The sketch's own solve state and status are `SketchSolve`. `Pierce` puts a point entity where a curve that does not lie in the sketch plane crosses that plane (SolidWorks pierce, relation 40 `ATPIERCE`, whose operand is a model curve). No stored file known to the project separates the point at the curve's crossing of the sketch plane from the point at the curve's end (part 11), and a sketch point lies in its plane, so where a curve ends off the plane only the crossing can hold it (inferred). The row holds the point as a local handle and the curve as an external-reference slot, which the decoder resolves to the path's feature. `Weight` sets the rational weight of the spline pole whose `Pole(i)` helper is `pole` (FreeCAD `Weight`). A SolidWorks coradial relation puts two arcs on one circle and is a `Concentric` and an `Equal` relation of the two. `FixedLength` holds each of its lines at its solved length, and `FixedAngle` each at its solved angle to the sketch's x axis; neither stores a value (NX constant length, "makes line have fixed length", and constant angle, "fixed angle relative to sketch coordinate system": the NX sketching guides of the University of Pennsylvania and TU Darmstadt). A writer whose target has neither writes a driving `Length` dimension, or an `Angle` dimension against `Frame(XAxis)`, whose literal is the solved value. `Native` keeps a relation whose meaning is not established (Rule N case (a), part 11), with its operands and values (the Creo codes of part 11).
- **Creo kinds.** Every documented Creo sketch constraint and dimension has a home: vertical, horizontal, perpendicular, parallel, tangent, midpoint, coincident (with point on entity and collinear), mirror, and equal are the relations of the same meaning; linear and ordinate dimensions are `Distance` (ordinate with `along`); radius, diameter, and revolved diameter are `Radial` and `Distance` with `doubled`; angle and arc angle are `Angle` `Between` and `Sweep`; arc length and perimeter are `Length`; ellipse radii are `Radial` with `MajorRadius` and `MinorRadius`, and conic rho is `Conic`; a spline tangency angle is an `Angle` on a `Handle` helper; a spline point coordinate is a `Distance` along a sketch coordinate-system axis; a reference dimension binds a `Driven` parameter; equal curvature, which PTC applies to a spline and a line or arc tangent at their end points, is `Curvature` with `contact: Ends` (PTC Creo sketcher help); any kind found later is `Native` until its meaning is established (part 11). Creo's stored `skamp_ptr` types: 1 is `Horizontal`, 2 `Vertical`, 4 `Tangent`, 5 `Perpendicular` (with an arc it puts the line through the arc's centre), 6 `Equal` of radii, 7 `Parallel`, 8 `Equal` of lengths, 9 `Collinear`, 16 `Concentric`, and 10 and 11 an arc that sweeps 90° and 180°, each an `Angle` of the arc's `Sweep` whose value is a literal. Types 12, 13, and 17, and the code of equal curvature, which no stored type relates to a spline, stay `Native` (typed, carrier unread; part 11).

```rust
pub struct SketchOffset<S: SketchSpace> { pub pairs: Vec<[S::Entity; 2]>, pub distance: Dimension<Length> }
pub struct SketchPolygon<S: SketchSpace> { pub center: S::Entity, pub edges: Vec<S::Entity>, pub circle: Option<S::Entity>, pub inscribed: Option<bool> }
pub struct SketchSlot<S: SketchSpace> { pub kind: SlotKind, pub centers: [S::Entity; 2], pub edges: Vec<S::Entity> }
pub enum SlotKind { Straight, CenterStraight, Arc, CenterArc, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub struct SketchPattern<S: SketchSpace> { pub seeds: Vec<S::Entity>, pub layout: SketchPatternLayout<S>, pub instances: Vec<SketchPatternInstance<S>> }
pub enum SketchPatternLayout<S: SketchSpace> {
    Linear   { directions: Vec<SketchPatternAxis<S>> },
    Circular { center: Operand<S>, spacing: Spacing<Angle>, sides: Option<RunSides<Angle>> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub struct SketchPatternAxis<S: SketchSpace> {
    pub direction: Option<SketchPatternDirection<S>>,
    pub spacing: Spacing<Length>,
    pub sides: Option<RunSides<Length>>,
}
pub enum SketchPatternDirection<S: SketchSpace> { Along { line: Operand<S>, reversed: Option<bool> }, Angle(Dimension<Angle>) }
pub struct SketchPatternInstance<S: SketchSpace> { pub index: InstanceIndex, pub entities: Vec<S::Entity>, pub suppressed: Option<bool> }
```

- **Offset.** Each pair is (source, result): the result lies at the signed `distance` along the source's left normal. Sources are sketch entities (SolidWorks offset entities, Fusion offset relation, NX offset loop).
- **Polygon and slot** are groups of ordinary lines and arcs held by one relation (polygon: Fusion, SolidWorks, Inventor, NX; slot: SolidWorks `sgSlot_c`). Their sizes are ordinary dimensions on the member entities. A polygon's `circle` is the construction circle the relation holds the polygon to, where the source stores one (a SolidWorks polygon's relation group 7 names it): `inscribed: Some(true)` holds the circle tangent to every edge, `Some(false)` puts every vertex on it, and `None` states that the source does not say which, which the solved geometry then shows.
- **Pattern.** A sketch pattern constrains copies of `seeds`. `Linear` has one or two directions; `SketchPatternDirection::Along` follows a line or axis, `Angle` states the direction from the sketch x axis. `spacing` is the feature patterns' `Spacing` and `sides` their `RunSides` (§6.5): `Pitch` gives count and the step between instances, `Span` count and the total extent, and `Fit`, only on a `Circular` layout, spreads the count over the whole turn; a `Linear` direction has no path or turn to fit. Each instance lists its entities in seed order at its index (row, column; or position; §6.5); a suppressed instance has `suppressed: Some(true)` and no entities (Fusion suppressed ordinals). The instance entities are `Free` entities.

```rust
pub struct SketchRegion { pub outer: Vec<BoundaryUse>, pub holes: Vec<Vec<BoundaryUse>> }
pub struct BoundaryUse { pub entity: SketchEntityId, pub fragment: Option<Fragment> }
pub struct Fragment { pub index: u32, pub count: u32 }
```

- **Profiles and regions.** A sketch stores no profile list: profiles are computed from its entities, and a source's stored profiles are caches of them (D9). A feature names what it uses with a `ProfileRef` (§6): the whole sketch, an open or closed chain of entities, or regions. A region is a face of the sketch's planar arrangement: an outer ring and hole rings of boundary uses, picked by `PickTarget::SketchRegion` (§5.8). A boundary use is a whole entity or, with `fragment`, the `index`-th of the `count` pieces into which the other non-construction curves of the sketch cut it (Fusion profile tracking paths). A cut point of an entity is a point of it, other than its own ends, where another such curve crosses or touches it: a tangent contact is a touch, the end of another curve on it is a touch, and collinear overlapping curves cut each other at the ends of the overlap. Coincident cut points are one cut point. The pieces run between consecutive cut points in the entity's parameter direction: an open curve from its start, a circle from its first cut point at or after angle 0, where angle 0 is the direction of the sketch x axis and angles run counterclockwise about the sketch normal. This is the piece order of the format: a decoder of any source states its fragments in this order. A use of a whole entity, or of the one piece of a circle with a single cut point, carries no `fragment`. Construction entities bound no region. Ring orientation follows the topology convention (§5.6): outer rings counterclockwise about the sketch normal.

### 6.2 Datums

```rust
pub struct Datum { pub element: DatumElement, pub link: Option<Link>, pub native_options: NativeOptions, pub source_settings: NativeOptions }
pub enum DatumElement {
    Points(Vec<Construction<Point>>),
    Axis(Construction<Axis>),
    Plane(Construction<Plane>),
    Frame(Construction<Frame>),
}
```

A datum feature is reference geometry: points, an axis, a plane, or a coordinate frame, each built by a construction (§5.9). Every format stores datums this way: NX DATUM_CSYS, DATUM_PLANE, POINT; Creo planes, axes, points, coordinate systems; SolidWorks planes, axes, points, coordinate systems; FreeCAD planes, lines, points, coordinate systems; Fusion work planes, axes, points; Inventor work features and UCS; CATIA points, planes, and axis systems.

- **Elements.** `Points` holds one or more points; a Creo datum point feature holds up to five or more, and each is picked by index. `Points` is never empty. A datum has no topology. Its value is its construction's `resolved` (D42); a source's display shape of a datum (a FreeCAD datum plane's face) is not stored. A datum whose construction the decoder does not read, so that it has no `resolved` value, no input other than an `Unread` one, and no step, is `Unresolved { family: Datum }` (§6), whatever element the source states; the option values the source stores beside it stay in the feature's native record (§3.1).
- **Display.** Display size and resize mode (FreeCAD `fcstd:Length`, `fcstd:Width`, `fcstd:ResizeMode`; the NX and Inventor display extents, `nx:display_extent` and `inventor:display_extent`) are `source_settings`: they size the datum's display, and a plane or axis is unbounded whatever its display (Rule N case (b)). Name and suppression are the feature's; visibility is presentation (D20).
- **Principal entities.** Every product definition has a fixed origin: three planes, three axes, a point, and its frame. An ordered container that carries its own origin (a FreeCAD PartDesign Body) has one too, and a pick of it always names `container` (§5.8). `PickTarget::Principal` picks them, in the definition the pick resolves in (§5.8). `PrincipalEntity::Frame` is the definition's coordinate frame itself (a Creo default coordinate system, an NX absolute CSYS).
- **Origin features.** A source that lists its origin entities as named members (SolidWorks Front, Top, Right, and Origin; Creo default planes and default coordinate system, constraint codes 513 to 515 and 1270/1271; the NX template DATUM_CSYS; CATIA xy, yz, and zx planes; the Inventor origin folder) has one datum feature for each, a member of the container the source lists it in (the scope's timeline in SolidWorks, Creo, NX, and Inventor; the part's root `Group` in CATIA, §5.2), whose construction is one `Coincident` input on the matching `Principal` entity with no `after` steps. A pick of an origin entity of such a source picks its feature as `Datum`, never `Principal` (a SolidWorks relation to the Origin feature's point). A source with built-in origins (Fusion, FreeCAD) has no such features; its picks name `Principal` directly.
- **Writers.** A writer whose target has built-in origin entities writes an origin feature as the built-in entity and maps picks of it there. A writer whose target lists origin features maps `Principal` picks to them, creating them where the document has none.
- **Picks.** `PickTarget::Datum { feature, part: None }` picks the whole datum: its single point, its axis, its plane, or its frame. `part` picks a principal entity of a `Frame` datum (an NX sketch on a DATUM_CSYS plane, a SolidWorks coordinate-system axis, an Inventor UCS plane) or one point of a `Points` datum. A sketch frame's parts are picked through `SketchFrame` (§5.8).
- **Linked datums.** A datum copied from another datum (NX EXTRACT_DATUM_PLANE, EXTRACT_DATUM_AXIS, NX WAVE datum links) is a datum whose construction is one `Coincident` input picking the source datum, or has no inputs where the source is unread, with the copied value in `resolved`. That pick is the one home of the source: its context states the part and the assembly the link runs through, and its anchor the state it reads (`Pinned(position)` for NX fix at current timestamp, `Native` where that state is outside the document). `link` states the rest of the link (§5.10): `associative` (NX `Associative`), a frozen placement in `transform` (an NX position-independent link), and the link's health in `state`; its `source` is `None`, and its `document` names the source definition only where the construction has no input. The undecoded NX `*_extract_parms` records of linked datums hold these fields' values (an extract body's record is another class, §6.5); which field holds which is typed, carrier unread (part 11), and until it is read the decoder keeps them in `native_options` under their NX names (`nx:<name>`).
- **Mapping.** CATIA GSD lines and circles are curve features with a `Construction<Curve>` (§6.6), not datums; CATIA GSD points, planes, and axis systems are datums. CATIA directions, NX smart directions, and SolidWorks temporary axes are inline constructions. A Fusion joint origin is a `Frame` datum, which joints pick as connectors (§6.7).

### 6.3 Swept solids and the loft

Extrude, revolve, sweep, helical sweep, rib, primitive, and loft build a body from a profile or a stated shape. Each carries a `SolidOutput` (§6).

#### Extrude and revolve

```rust
pub struct Extrude {
    pub profile: ProfileRef,
    pub loops: Option<LoopNesting>,
    pub direction: Option<ExtrudeDirection>,
    pub origin: Option<ExtrudeOrigin>,
    pub span: Option<Span<Length>>,
    pub draft: Option<ExtrudeDraft>,
    pub fit: Option<ProfileFit>,
    pub outside: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub sheet_cut: Option<SheetCutNormal>,
    pub output: SolidOutput,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub enum ExtrudeDirection {
    ProfileNormal { reversed: Option<Dimension<bool>> },
    Along { direction: Construction<Direction>, lengths_along_normal: Option<Dimension<bool>> },
}
pub enum ExtrudeOrigin {
    ProfilePlane, Offset(Dimension<Length>), Plane(Construction<Plane>), Point(Construction<Point>),
    Faces { faces: SetSelection, offset: Option<Dimension<Length>> },
}
pub struct ExtrudeDraft {
    pub end: Option<Dimension<Angle>>,
    pub start: Option<Dimension<Angle>>,
    pub neutral: Option<DraftNeutral>,
    pub holes: Option<HoleDraft>,
}
pub enum DraftNeutral { Origin, Start }
pub enum HoleDraft { WithRegion, WithOuter, Angles { end: Dimension<Angle>, start: Option<Dimension<Angle>> } }
pub struct ProfileFit {
    pub outer: Option<Dimension<Length>>,
    pub inner: Option<Dimension<Length>>,
    pub outer_join: Option<OffsetJoin>,
    pub inner_join: Option<OffsetJoin>,
}
```

- **Direction.** `ProfileNormal` extrudes along the normal of the profile plane, and `reversed` states the geometric sense: true where the material lies against the profile normal (Fusion, Inventor slot 3, FreeCAD `Reversed`, CATIA orientation). A FreeCAD Pocket cuts against the sketch normal where its `Reversed` is false, so the FreeCAD decoder inverts `Reversed` for a Pocket. `Along` extrudes along a constructed direction: an edge, an axis, a face normal, a sketch axis (FreeCAD `N_Axis`), or a fixed vector with no inputs (FreeCAD custom vector; the Inventor private direction record). Its reversal is a `Flip` step of the construction (§5.9). `lengths_along_normal` measures `Amount` limits along the profile normal (FreeCAD `AlongSketchNormal`).
- **Origin.** The origin is the plane the span is measured from: the profile plane, a plane offset from it along the direction, a constructed plane, the plane through a point normal to the direction, or faces with an offset (SolidWorks from condition, `moFromEndSpec_c`; Fusion start, profile offset; Inventor from plane; SolidWorks from vertex). `None` is not stated; a writer uses the profile plane. An origin offset is a different parameterization from a start limit: editing it moves both ends (NX value from the start limit is an `Offset` origin with `start: AtOrigin`).
- **Draft.** `end` tapers the material from the origin to `end`, `start` from the origin to `start`. A positive angle narrows the profile's outer loop away from the origin; a source's outward flag is the angle's sign (a positive FreeCAD `TaperAngle` widens it, so the FreeCAD decoder negates it: `Part::Extrusion` and PartDesign `Pad`). A symmetric span has no `start` draft; `end` tapers both sides (Fusion `TaperAngle`, `Side2TaperAngle`; FreeCAD `TaperAngle`, `TaperAngle2`; SolidWorks per direction; NX front and back angles; Inventor taper). `holes` states how the inner loops of a tapered profile's regions taper: `WithRegion` moves every boundary of a region by the same amount relative to its material, so a hole narrows where the outer loop widens (FreeCAD `InnerWireTaper` `Inverted`); `WithOuter` tapers each inner loop as the outer loop is tapered, in its own outward sense, so a hole widens where the outer loop widens (FreeCAD `SameAsOuter`, and every tapered PartDesign `Pad` and `Pocket`, which build their holes this way whatever they store) (`Part/App/ExtrusionHelper.cpp`, `Part/App/FeatureExtrusion.cpp`, and `PartDesign/App/FeatureExtrude.cpp` at 1.1.4). A FreeCAD `Part::Extrusion` that stores no value is `WithOuter` in a file FreeCAD 1.0 saved and `WithRegion` otherwise. `Angles` drafts each inner loop as a loop of its own at its own angle, `end` toward the span's end and `start` toward its start, whatever the outer loop's angle: a positive angle widens the hole away from the origin, moving the loop into the region's material as a positive `end` moves the outer loop, and an angle of 0 leaves the hole straight (a LinkStage3 FreeCAD pad's or pocket's inner taper, below). An NX drafted extrude tapers its inner loops `WithOuter` (part 11). A SolidWorks drafted extrude or cut tapers them `WithRegion` (part 11). A Fusion drafted extrude that adds material tapers them `WithRegion`. A positive Fusion `TaperAngle` widens the outer loop away from the profile, so the Fusion decoder negates `TaperAngle` and `Side2TaperAngle` of an extrude that adds material (part 11). No stored file known to the project settles how a Fusion cut tapers its inner loops or the sign of its angle, so for a cut the Fusion decoder states `draft: None` and keeps the angles as the native options `f3d:TaperAngle` and `f3d:Side2TaperAngle` (typed, carrier unread; part 11). No stored file known to the project settles how Inventor and Creo taper inner loops, and their decoders state `None` (part 11). A CATIA pad or pocket stores no draft: a CATIA draft is a `Draft` feature (§6.4), so the CATIA decoder states `draft: None`. `None` states nothing, and matters only for a profile with inner loops. A writer whose target tapers inner loops by the other rule writes, for an extrude that adds material, the outer loop's region tapered alone and then a tapered cut per hole over the same span, each cutting only the body that extrude made; these are several geometry features, which §3.4's rules for a construction govern, and it charges `export:feature.lowered`. For a cut, whose holes are islands the cut leaves standing, no such construction exists, and step 3 applies (§3.4). `neutral` states the plane at which the cross-section equals the profile. An extrude has three planes that can differ: the profile's own, the origin its span is measured from, and that one. `Origin` puts it at the extrude's origin, and the tapers run from there. `Start` puts it at the start limit: with the start limit at distance s from the origin, the profile at distance h is offset by (h − s)·tan θ for the `end` angle θ, in the sense in which a positive angle narrows the outer loop, so the one taper runs from the start limit to the end limit and `start` is absent (part 10). `None` does not state it; the two differ only where the start limit lies away from the origin. NX's from-edge draft (`TAPER_SIMPLE_FROM_EDGE`; `SimpleDraftType` `SimpleFromStart`) is `Start`, and its from-profile draft (`TAPER_SIMPLE_FROM_PROFILE`) `Origin` (part 11). The NX `Start` draft is not restated as an extrude whose origin lies at the start limit: that would write the end limit's parameter as a difference of two. A writer whose target drafts only from the origin writes, where every profile curve is a line or an arc, whose offsets are exact, the profile offset by −s·tan θ at the origin with the same θ, and charges `export:feature.lowered`; for another profile it charges a loss naming the feature. NX matched ends (`SimpleDraftType` `MatchedEnds`) is the native option `nx:matched_ends` (Rule N case (a), part 11). NX's symmetric-angle draft (`TAPER_SYMMETRIC`) is one angle θ applied from the section plane toward both limits: the profile lies at the section plane and each side narrows from it at θ toward its limit, each side face split at the section, so over a span whose origin is the section plane it is `ExtrudeDraft { start: Some(θ), end: Some(θ) }`, and over a `Symmetric` span `end: Some(θ)` alone (part 11). The NX decoder reads the draft class from the extrude record's draft slot, an inline sub-object after its side-face list that is null on an undrafted extrude, and states `neutral` from it: `Start` for the from-edge class, `Origin` for the from-profile and symmetric-angle classes. A draft the source stores as off is `draft: None` (§2.4).
- **Fit.** `fit` offsets the profile in its plane before the operation uses it: each region's outer loop by `outer` and each inner loop by `inner`, a positive value moving the loop outward from itself, so the region grows and its holes grow, with `outer_join` and `inner_join` the law at convex corners (`OffsetJoin`, §6.4: `Round` rounds them, `Sharp` extends their sides to meet). It is the LinkStage3 FreeCAD build's `Fit`, `InnerFit`, `FitJoin`, and `InnerFitJoin` on every PartDesign profile feature (realthunder's FreeCAD, `FeatureSketchBased.cpp` and `TopoShapeEx.cpp`); its `Tangent` join is `Sharp`, as FreeCAD's offset `Join` is (§6.4). An offset of 0 states no fit. A writer whose target has no fit writes the operation over a sketch that offsets the profile's loops (§6.1), a stateless feature, where the target's sketch offset has the same corner law, and otherwise charges a loss naming the feature.
- **LinkStage3 options.** The same build's `InnerTaperAngle` and `InnerTaperAngleRev` are `HoleDraft::Angles`: its `Extrusion::makeDraft` drafts the inner wires as loops of their own at those angles, positive widening, 0 by default. A later build of the fork renames them `TaperInnerAngle` and `TaperInnerAngleRev` and, restoring a file that stores the old names, puts each value in the other's place, so a decoder reads the names as the build that wrote the file wrote them. `NewSolid` true is `boolean: Some(NewBody)`: the feature takes no base, its result is its own tool solid, and the body's later features build on that solid. `AddSubType` additive, subtractive, and intersecting are `Join`, `Cut`, and `Intersect`.
- **Outside.** `outside: Some(true)` sweeps the part of the profile plane outside the profile's regions, so a cut removes the material outside the profile within the span and keeps the material inside it as a boss whose walls are the profile's edges swept along the direction, tapered from the sketch plane where the cut is drafted (SolidWorks flip side to cut). SolidWorks stores the flag at byte +6 of the 24-byte `moEndSpec_c`. `None` and `Some(false)` sweep the regions. `loops` states how the profile's loops nest into regions (§6), and `sheet_cut` how a cut of a sheet-metal wall is made (§6.6).
- **Native options.** Fusion's `Side1Offset` and `Side2Offset` are the offsets of each side's to-object limit from its target, `ToGeometry.offset` (§6): a Fusion extrude has its start offset and one to-entity offset per side and no other (API `ExtrudeFeature` and `ToEntityExtentDefinition.offset`, and the extrude reference's "distance to offset extrusion from selected object"). Fusion offsets the target along the target face's own outward normal, so a positive value ends beyond a target that faces away from the profile and short of one that faces it. The Fusion decoder states `offset: Distance(s · Side1Offset)`, through `Negated` where s is −1 and a parameter binds the value, s being the sign of the target face's outward normal against the side's direction in the state before the extrude, and a Fusion writer inverts the rule. On a target that is not a plane parallel to the profile, moving the target along the direction and offsetting its surface along its normals give different limits, and no stored file known to the project settles it; there, and where s cannot be read (target faces of both orientations, a historical face not resolved), the decoder states `offset: None` and keeps the value as the native option `f3d:Side1Offset` or `f3d:Side2Offset` (part 11). The Fusion extent word of a to-face or to-body extent is the native option `f3d:extent_word` until its codes are read (typed, carrier unread, §6); on every other extent the extent kind fixes it. The SolidWorks translate-surface flag is the native option `sldprt:translate_surface` (§6, part 11).

```rust
pub struct Revolve {
    pub profile: ProfileRef,
    pub loops: Option<LoopNesting>,
    pub axis: Option<Construction<Axis>>,
    pub span: Option<Span<Angle>>,
    pub fit: Option<ProfileFit>,
    pub output: SolidOutput,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
```

- The axis is a construction: a sketch line or sketch axis (FreeCAD `V_Axis`, `H_Axis`), an origin axis (FreeCAD `App::Line`), an edge, a cylinder's axis, or a datum axis (CATIA `Axis`; Creo instruction 21; Fusion axis role; SolidWorks `moLineRef_w`; NX smart point and direction; the Inventor private axis that names a sketch line). The axis direction, after the construction's `Flip` steps, fixes the positive rotation by the right-hand rule, so the steps state the geometric sense: the FreeCAD decoder inverts a Groove's `Reversed` as it does a Pocket's (§6.3, Direction). The origin of a revolve span is the profile. NX stores a start angle and an end angle in one rotational sense; the start angle is an `Amount` against the rotation, its parameter bound with `Negated`. Fusion's Project Axis (`isProjectAxis`) projects the selected axis onto the profile's plane: where it is true the axis is a construction with a `Whole` `Projection` input picking the selected axis and a `Whole` `Coincident` input picking the profile plane, and where it is false the construction picks the axis where it lies (API `RevolveFeatureInput.isProjectAxis`, "Setting this to true will use a projected axis, while setting it to false will keep it in its original location"). `loops` is the extrude's (§6), and `fit` the extrude's (Fit, above).

#### Sweep

```rust
pub struct Sweep {
    pub section: SweepSection,
    pub path: PathRef,
    pub controls: SweepControls,
    pub guides: Vec<SweepGuide>,
    pub extent: Option<PathExtent>,
    pub placement: Option<ProfilePlacement>,
    pub limits: SpineLimits,
    pub transition: Option<CornerTransition>,
    pub output: SolidOutput,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub enum CornerTransition { Mitre, Round, Open, Carried, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum SweepSection { Profile(ProfileRef), Generated { shape: SectionShape, turn: Option<SectionTurn> } }
pub enum SectionTurn {
    /// The path lies in a planar sketch: the section is turned to the sketch's plane.
    PathPlane,
```
