```rust
    /// Where the sweep starts (an open path's start; on a closed path the middle of its first curve) one side of
    /// a square section lies along the z axis of the definition's frame projected into the plane normal to the path.
    /// From there the section is carried with no rotation about the path's tangent.
    ZStart,
}
pub enum SectionShape {
    Circle   { diameter: Dimension<PositiveLength>, inner_diameter: Option<Dimension<PositiveLength>> },
    Square   { size: Dimension<PositiveLength> },
    Triangle { size: Dimension<PositiveLength>, apex: Option<Apex> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum Apex { Outward, Inward }
pub struct SweepControls { pub orientation: Option<SweepOrientation>, pub twist: Option<Twist>, pub scaling: Option<ScalingLaw> }
pub enum SweepOrientation {
    FollowPath, MinimumTwist, Frenet, Fixed, Guides(GuideFrame),
    Direction(Construction<Direction>), Surface(SetSelection), Point(Construction<Point>),
    Curve { path: PathRef, tangent: Option<Dimension<bool>>, curvilinear: Option<Dimension<bool>> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum GuideFrame { PathToFirst, FirstToSecond }
pub enum Twist { Angle(Dimension<Angle>), Law(Law<Angle>) }
pub enum ScalingLaw { Taper(Dimension<Angle>), Law(Law<FiniteReal>), Area, Perimeter, Point(Construction<Point>), Curve(PathRef), Native(NonBlankString) }
pub struct SweepGuide { pub path: PathRef, pub extent: Option<PathExtent> }
pub struct PathExtent { pub along: Option<Dimension<Fraction>>, pub against: Option<Dimension<Fraction>> }
pub enum ProfilePlacement { InPlace, Positioned(ProfilePosition) }
pub struct ProfilePosition {
    pub origin: Option<Construction<Point>>,
    pub direction: Option<Construction<Direction>>,
    pub angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>>,
    pub swap_axes: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
}
pub struct SpineLimits { pub start: Option<SetSelection>, pub end: Option<SetSelection> }
```

- A sweep moves one section along one path. Several sections along a path are a loft with a spine (below). A generated section is a shape the source states by size: a tube or pipe is a sweep of a `Circle` (NX tube; Fusion pipe; SolidWorks circular profile). A pipe hollowed by a wall thickness is `BodyForm::Thin` with a `OneSide` `Inside` thickness (Fusion `SectionThickness`, which grows inward); a pipe hollowed by an inner diameter states `inner_diameter` (NX tube). A section's `size` is a circle's outside diameter, a square's side, and an equilateral triangle's altitude, so the triangle's side is 2·size/√3. A triangle lies in the plane of the helix axis with one side parallel to that axis; `apex` states which way its opposite vertex points: `Outward` away from the axis, `Inward` toward it (Fusion coil "Triangular External" and "Triangular Internal"). `turn` states how a sweep's generated square or triangle turns about its path. `PathPlane` applies where the path is a chain of curves of a planar sketch whose normal is N: a square has two sides parallel to that plane and is centred on the path, and a triangle has its base parallel to it, its apex toward +N, and the midpoint of its altitude on the path, the point a coil's `Center` puts on the helix; the section keeps that relation along the whole path. Fusion pipes turn so (part 11). `ZStart` applies where the path is a chain of spatial sketch curves, planar or not. `PathPlane` does not hold on a planar path drawn in a spatial sketch. On a square in a plane normal or parallel to z the two arms give the same solid. `ZStart` falls under Rule H1 and is defined for a square: the Fusion decoder states `turn: Some(ZStart)` for a square on a path of spatial sketch curves where the stored faces agree, and `None` where they do not; it states `Some(PathPlane)` only for a path of 2D sketch curves. A triangle under `ZStart` has two solids for one value, mirror images in the side that lies along z, since the arm does not say on which side of the tangent the apex lies, and no stored file known to the project settles it (part 11): the Fusion decoder states `turn: None` for a triangle on a path of spatial sketch curves, with its stored turn kept as the native option `f3d:pipe_turn` and its faces as the feature's stored result. Not settled by any stored file known to the project: a path of 2D sketch curves running across the slope of a tilted sketch, which alone would separate the sketch's normal from z under `PathPlane` (part 11); a path of body edges, on which the carrying is not settled, so such a pipe states `turn: None` until the decoder can carry a frame along the path's curve (part 11); and a component placed with a rotation, which would separate the definition's z from the document's. `turn` is `None` for a circle. A pipe's triangle states `apex: None`, which only a coil's helix axis gives a meaning. Fusion's pipe sections are circular, square, and triangular, `Circle`, `Square`, and `Triangle` (API `PipeFeature.sectionType`); a Fusion pipe whose saved topology does not decide its section is `SectionShape::Native("f3d:pipe-section")`, with its size as the native option `f3d:section_size`, until the carrier of the section type is read (typed, carrier unread; part 11). A writer whose target has no generated triangle sweeps a triangle sketch along the path or helix (§3.4), placed as `apex` and the coil's `SectionPlacement` state it. A writer whose target has no generated square or triangle writes a pipe of `turn: Some(PathPlane)` as a sketch at the path's start, in the plane normal to the path's tangent, holding the section placed as `PathPlane` states, swept along the path with `FollowPath`, which on a path in one plane keeps the section's relation to that plane, and charges `export:feature.lowered`. A pipe's square or triangle whose `turn` is `None`, and a coil's triangle placed `Inside` or `Outside`, whose point on the helix no stored file known to the project settles, give the writer no placement to follow, and step 3 applies (part 11).
- **Orientation.** `FollowPath` keeps the section's angle to the path tangent (SolidWorks follow path, Fusion perpendicular, Inventor path, CATIA keep angle). SolidWorks stores a sweep's path alignment in bytes of the sweep record that are not framed, so its decoder states `orientation: None` with `sldprt:sweep_orientation` (typed, carrier unread). It keeps the two words of the record's closing object that take exactly 0 and 1, read as the start and end tangency, as the native flags `sldprt:sweep_start_tangency` and `sldprt:sweep_end_tangency`, which a SolidWorks writer returns unchanged. SolidWorks' "normal to the path" (its page's "Create the sweep normal to the path at the start", with the API's "valid only for 2D paths") is no rotation of the section on a sweep without guide curves, and the design has no arm for it: a writer of another codec that carries the sketched section at each end builds such a sweep. Whether the two words are the tangency options or another option, no stored file known to the project settles (part 11). `MinimumTwist` is a law the source documents as twist-minimizing (SolidWorks minimum twist, which applies to 3D paths; FreeCAD standard mode, corrected Frenet). Whether a source's keep-angle law equals another variant on a non-planar path is a decoder's mapping (part 11). `Frenet` follows the Frenet frame of the path (FreeCAD `Frenet`). `Fixed` keeps the section's orientation (FreeCAD fixed, SolidWorks keep normal constant, Fusion and Inventor parallel). `Direction` holds one section axis along a direction (FreeCAD binormal, CATIA pulling direction, NX vector). `Surface` holds it normal to faces (CATIA reference surface, Inventor guide surface, NX face normals). `Curve` follows an auxiliary curve (FreeCAD auxiliary mode with its tangent and curvilinear flags; NX another curve). `Point` turns toward a point (NX). `Guides` twists the intermediate sections with the guides: the angle between the section's in-plane x axis and a guide vector stays constant along the path, where the vector runs from the path to the first guide (`PathToFirst`) or from the first guide to the second (`FirstToSecond`) in each section's plane (SolidWorks follow path and 1st guide curve, follow 1st and 2nd guide curves, from the SolidWorks sweep documentation).
- **Twist and scaling.** `Twist::Angle` is the total twist over the path (Fusion `TwistAngle`, SolidWorks twist). `Twist::Law` is an angle law along the path (CATIA and NX angular laws). `ScalingLaw::Taper` is a draft angle of the section along the path (Fusion `TaperAngle`, Inventor taper).
- **Guides and extent.** A guide is a curve the section follows besides the path (Fusion rail; SolidWorks guide curves; CATIA explicit sweep guide; Inventor guide rail). `PathExtent` sweeps the fractions `along` and `against` of the path or guide on either side of the section (Fusion `AlongDistance`, `AgainstDistance`, `AlongRailDistance`, `AgainstRailDistance`).
- **Profile placement.** `InPlace` sweeps the profile where it lies. `Positioned` moves the profile so that `origin` lies on the path start and `direction` aligns with the first axis of the moving frame there, then rotates it by `angle` and swaps the frame axes where `swap_axes` is true (CATIA `PositionedProfile` with `PointPosi`, `DirectionPosi`, `AnglePosi`, `SwapAxesPosi`). `limits` are relimiting elements on the path (CATIA `RelimElem1/2`).
- **Transition.** `transition` states how the swept result passes a sharp corner of its path, where the path's tangent turns: `Mitre` extends the pieces swept along the two adjacent segments until they meet, and their intersection is the joint; `Round` turns the section about the axis through the corner point normal to both adjacent tangents, so a rounded piece joins the two (Open CASCADE `BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell::SetTransitionMode`, right corner and round corner). `Carried` adds no joint piece: the section crosses the corner without turning, each later path segment's frame law being premultiplied by the constant rotation that carries the frame at that segment's start onto the frame at the previous segment's end, so after the corner the section is no longer normal to the path. On a straight segment the later piece is an oblique prism of volume A·L·cos θ, for a section of area A, a segment of length L, and a turn θ; it is flat at a 90° turn in the section's plane and folds back through the earlier piece beyond it (Open CASCADE `BRepFill_PipeShell` `TransformInG0Law`, which builds no corner piece, at V7_8_0). FreeCAD stores the choice on every `Part::Sweep` and PartDesign pipe as `Transition`, 0 transformed `Carried`, 1 right corner `Mitre`, and 2 round corner `Round`. A writer whose target has no such transition takes step 3 (§3.4). `Open` leaves the pieces swept along the two adjacent segments as they are, with no surface joining them at the corner, so a gap or an overlap remains there (a SolidWorks ruled surface with connecting surfaces cleared: "Clear Connecting surface to remove any connecting surfaces", the Ruled Surface help and API `IRuledSurfaceFeatureData.Connect`).

#### Helical sweep and helix

```rust
pub struct HelicalSweep {
    pub section: HelicalSection,
    pub helix: Helix,
    pub output: SolidOutput,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub enum HelicalSection {
    Profile(ProfileRef),
    Generated { shape: SectionShape, placement: Option<SectionPlacement> },
}
pub enum SectionPlacement { Inside, Center, Outside }
pub struct Helix {
    pub placement: Construction<Frame>,
    pub start: Option<HelixStart>,
    pub shape: HelixShape,
    pub hand: Option<Dimension<Hand>>,
}
pub enum HelixStart {
    Radius { radius: RadialDimension<PositiveLength>, angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>> },
    Point(Construction<Point>),
    Circle(OrderedSelection),
}
pub enum HelixShape {
    Helix  { law: Option<HelixLaw>, taper: Option<HelixTaper> },
    Spiral { law: Option<SpiralLaw> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum HelixLaw {
    PitchHeight { pitch: Dimension<PositiveLength>, height: Dimension<PositiveLength> },
    PitchTurns  { pitch: Dimension<PositiveLength>, turns: Dimension<PositiveReal> },
    HeightTurns { height: Dimension<PositiveLength>, turns: Dimension<PositiveReal> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum HelixTaper { Angle(Dimension<Angle>), Growth(Dimension<Length>), Radius(Law<Length>) }
pub enum SpiralLaw {
    PitchTurns     { pitch: Dimension<NonZeroLength>, turns: Dimension<PositiveReal> },
    EndRadiusTurns { end: Dimension<PositiveLength>, turns: Dimension<PositiveReal> },
    EndRadiusPitch { end: Dimension<PositiveLength>, pitch: Dimension<NonZeroLength> },
}
```

- A helical sweep moves a section along a helix that the operation defines (FreeCAD additive and subtractive helix; Inventor coil). A coil is a helical sweep of a generated section (Fusion coil): the helix's `start` holds the coil diameter, and `placement` puts the section inside, on, or outside the helix. For a triangle, `Center` puts the midpoint of its altitude on the helix. Fusion stores the placement as a section-position word (1 inside, 2 center, 3 outside), whose offset depends on the record form (92, 88, 220, or 216). No stored file known to the project settles which point of a triangle `Inside` and `Outside` put on the helix (part 11). A helix curve feature holds the same `Helix` (§6.6).
- **Placement and start.** The placement's z axis is the helix axis and its advance direction. `start` fixes where the helix starts and its radius: `Radius` on the placement's x axis rotated by `angle` (FreeCAD, SolidWorks, a Fusion coil diameter); `Point` at a constructed point, which fixes radius and start direction (CATIA); `Circle` on a selected circle, which fixes both (SolidWorks helix on a sketch circle). `None` states that the swept profile fixes them (FreeCAD helix).
- **Shape.** `HelixLaw` holds the two values the source drives (FreeCAD `Mode`, Fusion and Inventor coil type; CATIA, SolidWorks, and FreeCAD helix curves); the third follows from them. `HelixTaper` makes the helix conical by a cone angle (FreeCAD `Angle`, Fusion taper, CATIA `Angle1/2`), by radial growth per turn (FreeCAD `Growth`), or by a radius law (CATIA `RadiusLaw`). `Spiral` is planar: `pitch` is the radial growth per turn and `end` the end radius (CATIA spiral; SolidWorks spiral).
- `hand` states the turning sense (FreeCAD `LeftHanded`, Fusion and Inventor rotation, CATIA, SolidWorks). Fusion clockwise, seen looking along the axis direction, is `Right` and counterclockwise `Left` (the compact coil's left-hand flag, the legacy `SpirePrimitive` clockwise flag; the ten-reference form's fixed counterclockwise is `Left`). Inventor's coil rotation is the helix's hand (API `CoilFeature.ClockwiseRotation`, which the Coil dialog names Rotation Left or Right); the flag is the slot-3 Boolean of the coil's property record, true for a right-handed coil (part 11).

#### Rib

```rust
pub struct Rib {
    pub profile: ProfileRef,
    pub thickness: Option<Thickness>,
    pub growth: Option<RibGrowth>,
    pub flipped: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub extent: Option<Limit<Length>>,
    pub draft: Option<Dimension<Angle>>,
    pub thickness_at: Option<RibEnd>,
    pub root_fillet: Option<Dimension<PositiveLength>>,
    pub extend_profile: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub boolean: Option<Boolean>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub enum RibGrowth { InPlane, Normal, Along(Construction<Direction>), Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum RibEnd { Root, Tip }
```

- A rib grows a wall of `thickness` about open profile curves until it meets material (SolidWorks, Creo, Inventor, NX, Fusion, CATIA stiffener). A web is a rib whose profile holds several curves (Fusion Web, whose direction, thickness, extent, flip, and draft are `Rib` fields). `extend_profile: Some(true)` extends the open ends of the profile curves along their end tangents until they meet material (Fusion Web extend curves, Inventor rib extend profile). `root_fillet` rounds, with a constant radius, the edges where the rib's walls meet the material it grows to (Fusion web and rib `filletRadius`, "applied along the edges where the web meets the target body", zero for none, which is `None`). `thickness_at` states at which end a drafted wall has the stated thickness: `Root` where the wall meets that material, `Tip` at its other end; it applies only with `draft` (Fusion `isThicknessFromTop`, "measured from the top of the web rather than the bottom when a draft angle is applied"; API `WebFeatureInput`). Which of Fusion's top and bottom is the root is typed, carrier unread (part 11); until it is read, a Fusion decoder states `thickness_at: None` and keeps the flag as the native option `f3d:thickness_start`. `thickness_at` decides how a drafted rib's stated thickness is read, so where a rib has a `draft` and `thickness_at` is `None`, a writer of another codec does not write the thickness and charges a loss naming the feature (§2.4). A writer whose target has no root fillet cannot construct one: the fillet would pick the sharp edges where the walls meet the material, which exist only between the rib and its fillet, in no state the document holds, so step 3 applies (§3.4).
- `InPlane` grows the wall in the profile plane, with its thickness normal to that plane; `Normal` grows it along the profile normal, with its thickness in the plane (SolidWorks parallel or normal to sketch; NX parallel or perpendicular to the section plane; CATIA stiffener from side and from top: "From top: The extrusion is performed normal to the profile's plane and the thickness is added in the profile's plane", the CATIA Part Design guide). `Along` is a fixed direction (the Inventor private direction record). `flipped` grows the wall toward the other side of the curves.
- `extent` is `Next`, an `Amount`, or a target (Inventor finite or to next; NX cap geometry with its cap offset). `None` is not stated; a writer grows the rib to the next material. A Creo rib stores where its open profile's ends meet the part: each of its two attachment instructions (892) names an existing face that holds one end of the profile and the side wall the rib makes, and the section holds that face's projection as the reference the end lies on. They are the profile's end conditions, not an extent or a Boolean target: the Creo decoder states each as a `Coincident` of the end point with that projected reference in the profile sketch, and `extent: None`.

#### Primitives

```rust
pub struct Primitive {
    pub shape: PrimitiveShape,
    pub placement: Option<Construction<Frame>>,
    pub output: SolidOutput,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub enum PrimitiveShape {
    Box      { size: [Dimension<PositiveLength>; 3] },
    Cylinder { radius: RadialDimension<PositiveLength>, height: Dimension<PositiveLength>, angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>> },
    Cone     { radii: [RadialDimension<NonNegativeLength>; 2], height: Dimension<PositiveLength>, angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>> },
    Sphere   { radius: RadialDimension<PositiveLength>, latitudes: Option<[Dimension<Angle>; 2]>, longitude: Option<Dimension<Angle>> },
    Torus    { radii: [RadialDimension<PositiveLength>; 2], latitudes: Option<[Dimension<Angle>; 2]>, longitude: Option<Dimension<Angle>> },
    Ellipsoid { radii: [Dimension<PositiveLength>; 3], latitudes: Option<[Dimension<Angle>; 2]>, longitude: Option<Dimension<Angle>> },
    Prism    { sides: Dimension<u32>, circumradius: Dimension<PositiveLength>, height: Dimension<PositiveLength> },
    Wedge    { y: [Dimension<Length>; 2], base: [Dimension<Length>; 4], top: [Dimension<Length>; 4] },
    Plane    { size: [Dimension<PositiveLength>; 2] },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
```

- Sources: FreeCAD `Part::Cylinder`, `Part::Box`, PartDesign additive primitives; Fusion box, cylinder, sphere, and torus; NX block and cylinder; CATIA GSD sphere and cylinder, which are `Sheet`s; STEP CSG primitives (ISO 10303-42). `angle`, `latitudes`, and `longitude` bound partial primitives (FreeCAD). The FreeCAD ellipsoid, prism, wedge, and plane are typed from FreeCAD's own definition (`Part/App/PrimitiveFeature.cpp`):
  - `Ellipsoid` is the sphere of radius `radii[0]` scaled along the frame's y axis to `radii[1]` and along z to `radii[2]`; `latitudes` and `longitude` bound it as they bound the sphere before the scaling. FreeCAD `Radius2` is `radii[0]`, `Radius1` is `radii[2]`, and `Radius3` is `radii[1]`, where a `Radius3` of 0 means `Radius2`; `Angle1` to `Angle3` are the latitudes and the longitude.
  - `Prism` extrudes a regular polygon of `sides` vertices on the circle of `circumradius` about z by `height` along z (FreeCAD `Polygon`, `Circumradius`, `Height`); `sides` is at least 3. Its first vertex lies on the frame's x axis (inferred: the source steps the radius vector about z by 2π/`sides`; part 11).
  - `Wedge` is the solid between two rectangles normal to y: at y = `y[0]` the rectangle x in [`base[0]`, `base[1]`], z in [`base[2]`, `base[3]`], and at y = `y[1]` the rectangle x in [`top[0]`, `top[1]`], z in [`top[2]`, `top[3]`] (FreeCAD `Ymin`, `Ymax`, `Xmin`, `Xmax`, `Zmin`, `Zmax`, `X2min`, `X2max`, `Z2min`, `Z2max`, Open CASCADE `BRepPrim_Wedge`).
  - `Plane` is the rectangular face x in [0, `size[0]`], y in [0, `size[1]`] of the frame's xy plane, a sheet (FreeCAD `Part::Plane` `Length` and `Width`).
  - A writer whose target has no wedge writes a ruled loft between its two rectangles (§3.4); where one of them is a segment or a point, the loft takes it only where the target lofts to such a section, and otherwise step 3 applies.

  NX block creation methods are no case (b): a block made from two diagonal points, or from two points and a height, depends on those points, and after an edit of them its sizes follow. Its typed form takes the points as construction inputs: the placement's `Origin` `Coincident` input picks the first point, and each size the points fix binds a parameter whose expression measures the second point's coordinate less the first's along that axis (`Measure` `Coordinate`, §5.13), where the block's axes are the definition's. Where NX stores the method and its points is typed, carrier unread (part 11); until it is read, the NX decoder states `Box` with literal sizes and keeps the method in `native_options` as `nx:block_method`.
- `placement` is the local frame (FreeCAD attachment or `Placement`, Fusion plane and centre, NX origin and orientation), and the one home of a primitive's source placement: the primitive's `Feature.placement` is `None` (§5.10), and a placement the source stores as the identity with no binding is `placement: None` (§2.4). A box spans the frame's positive octant; a cylinder and a cone stand on its xy plane about +z, and a cone's `radii[0]` is its radius at z = 0 and `radii[1]` its radius at z = `height` (FreeCAD `Radius1` and `Radius2`; a STEP `RIGHT_CIRCULAR_CONE`'s base radius `radius + height·tan(semi_angle)` and its `radius`, with the frame moved by −`height` along its axis); a sphere and a torus are centred on its origin, the torus about z. Decoders convert source conventions to these.

#### Loft

A loft carries sections between optional point ends, an optional second direction of sections, an optional spine, guides, correspondence, shape controls, and output. Lofts carry every surface built through sections: two-direction surfaces, blends between two curves (CATIA blend, with `Support` conditions), and ruled surfaces between two curves (`ruled: Some(true)`; FreeCAD `Part::RuledSurface`).

```rust
pub struct Loft {
    pub start: Option<PointSection>,
    pub sections: Vec<Section>,
    pub end: Option<PointSection>,
    pub cross: Vec<Section>,
    pub spine: Option<Spine>,
    pub guides: Vec<Guide>,
    pub correspondence: Option<Correspondence>,
    pub shape: LoftShape,
    pub output: SolidOutput,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub struct Section {
    pub form: SectionForm,
    pub flip: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub seam: Option<Seam>,
    pub condition: Option<SectionCondition>,
    pub trim_support: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub spine_point: Option<Construction<Point>>,
}
pub enum SectionForm { Profile(ProfileRef), Placed { profile: ProfileRef, placement: Construction<Frame> } }
pub enum Seam { Vertex(OrderedSelection), Parameter(FiniteReal) }
pub struct PointSection { pub point: Construction<Point>, pub condition: Option<PointCondition> }
pub enum PointCondition {
    Sharp,
    Tangent        { weight: Option<Dimension<PositiveReal>> },
    TangentToPlane { plane: Construction<Plane>, weight: Option<Dimension<PositiveReal>> },
}
pub struct Guide { pub path: PathRef, pub tangency: Option<SectionCondition>, pub influence: Option<GuideInfluence> }
pub enum GuideInfluence { NextGuide, NextSharp, NextEdge, Global }
pub enum Spine {
    Path       { path: PathRef, controls: SweepControls },
    Centerline { path: PathRef, sections: Option<Dimension<u32>>, stations: Vec<AreaStation> },
    Computed,
}
pub struct AreaStation { pub at: CenterlineAt, pub area: Dimension<PositiveArea>, pub driving: bool }
pub enum CenterlineAt { Fraction(Dimension<Fraction>), Distance(Dimension<NonNegativeLength>) }
pub struct Correspondence { pub mode: Option<CouplingMode>, pub connectors: Vec<Connector> }
pub enum CouplingMode { Ratio, Tangency, TangencyThenCurvature, Vertices, ArcLength, Parameter, BySegment, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub struct Connector { pub points: OrderedSelection }
pub struct LoftShape {
    pub style: Option<LoftStyle>,
    pub max_degree: Option<Dimension<NonZeroU32>>,
    pub rebuild: Option<Rebuild>,
    pub ruled: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub closed: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub relimit: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub merge_tangent_faces: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub smoothing: Option<LoftSmoothing>,
    pub section_law: Option<Interpolation>,
}
pub struct LoftSmoothing { pub angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>>, pub deviation: Option<Dimension<NonNegativeLength>> }
pub enum LoftStyle { Loose, Uniform, ChordLength, SqrtChordLength, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum Rebuild { Points(u32), Refit { tolerance: Option<Length> }, Degree(u32) }
```

- A section's profile is a `ProfileRef` (§6): sketch regions, sketch curves, model edges and faces, or free curves, wire bodies (§5.6) anchored `Current` (Rhino lofts through free curves, with `Seam::Parameter`). `Placed` puts a profile at a constructed frame away from its sketch (Creo parallel blend subsections, each a region of the one sketch with its own frame and its distance from the sketch as an input dimension). A section's `condition` and a guide's `tangency` are §6's `SectionCondition`.
- A point section exists only at `start` or `end`. A weight exists only inside a condition that has one. A point condition applies only to a point section. Spine and guides coexist (CATIA, NX Swept); a target that allows only one receives the other as a loss naming the feature.
- `Spine::Computed` states that the source computes the spine (CATIA `CalculatedSpine`); `spine: None` states that the source has none. `Centerline.sections` is SolidWorks' intermediate-section count. A spine path carries the sweep controls (NX Swept orientation, angular law, and scaling).
- Mapping: NX Swept, Creo swept blend, and FreeCAD multisection pipes are lofts with a `Spine::Path`; Inventor and Fusion edge-loop sections are `Profile` selections of edges; two-direction surfaces (SolidWorks boundary, NX through-curve mesh and studio surface, Creo boundary blend, Rhino network surface, FreeCAD `GeomFillSurface`) use `cross`.
- A source's loft degree (FreeCAD `MaxDegree`; the Rhino loft degree) is `max_degree`. `rebuild` states that the result approximates the exact loft, and how: `Points` rebuilds it with that many control points, `Refit` fits it within `tolerance`, and `Degree` is the degree of Rhino's rebuild option, a separate simplification of the result (Rhino's loft simplify options). NX Swept's preserve shape is `rebuild`: set, each section member gives a face of its own with the member's own curve across the section, a straight member a face of degree 1 and one span, and the result is the exact loft, `rebuild: None`; cleared, NX replaces each section by cubic B-splines that span several members before it sweeps, giving fewer faces than members with 7 or more knots across the section, which is `Refit`. Which tolerance NX refits to is not read, so the NX decoder states `tolerance: None`, and where the record's two candidate bytes disagree it keeps the option as `nx:preserve_shape` (typed, carrier unread; part 11).
- **Correspondence.** `correspondence` states how the sections are coupled to each other. `mode` is CATIA's `SectionCoupling` (`Ratio`, `Tangency`, `TangencyThenCurvature`, `Vertices`) or NX's alignment (`Parameter`, `ArcLength`, `BySegment`). NX stores a through-curves feature's alignment in the first byte of the record's option array (an older grammar stores each option value less one): 2 is `Parameter`, member k of one section joining member k of the next at equal parameter; 7 is the user's alignment points, `Correspondence { mode: None, connectors }` with one connector per point index joining that numbered vertex of each section; and for 3 no stored file known to the project settles `ArcLength` against `Parameter`, so the decoder states `CouplingMode::Native("nx:alignment:3")` until a record separates them (part 11). NX's distance, angles, and spine alignments are `Native`: no stored file known to the project holds them (Rule N case (a), part 11). NX's swept and ruled features store their alignment the same way, in the first option value of the record, with the through-curves codes: 2 `Parameter`, 3 as above, and 7 alignment points, the points stored per section string and stated as the coupling's `connectors`, so `CouplingMode` covers both. The label `SKIN` is shared by the swept, ruled, and bounded-plane classes, so the NX decoder takes the class from the record's selector (part 11). `connectors` are the couplings the user places, each the points one coupling joins in section order: CATIA `SectionCouplingPoints`, NX alignment points, and SolidWorks loft connectors (`moLoftSynchRef_c`).
- **Merging.** `merge_tangent_faces` merges result faces that meet tangentially into one face (SolidWorks Merge tangent faces; Inventor Merge Tangent Faces).
- **Style.** `style` states how the surface follows its sections between them (Rhino Loft style; definitions from the Rhino 8 Loft documentation): `Loose` makes the sections' control points the surface's control points, so the surface passes through the first and last sections and approximates the others; `Uniform` makes the surface's knot vectors uniform. `ChordLength` and `SqrtChordLength` make the surface a degree-3 interpolation of the sections in the loft direction, each section an isocurve at its knot: the sections are made compatible, with common degree and knots and control points P_k,j, and the knots run t_0 = 0 and t_{k+1} = t_k + c_k under `ChordLength`, t_k + √c_k under `SqrtChordLength`, where c_k = max_j |P_{k+1,j} − P_{k,j}|. The knots do not fix the surface alone: a cubic that interpolates n sections at n knots has two rows of control points more than sections, and the two arms fix them by end rules, neither of them a standard condition on a derivative, each stated for its own domain below. Take each compatible section as one vector D_k of all its control points (in homogeneous coordinates where rational; a closed section's repeated first point counted twice), e_k = |D_{k+1} − D_k|, and p the parabola through D_0, D_1, D_2 at parameters 0, e_0, and e_0 + e_1. On an open loft of three or more sections, under `ChordLength` the second control row is Q_1 = D_0 + (e_0 / 3) p′(0), the second-last row is formed likewise from the last three sections, and the rows between are fixed by S(t_k) = D_k at the knots. On an open loft of exactly three sections, under `SqrtChordLength` the end rows lie on the same parabola at the fractions w and 1 − w of E = e_0 + e_1, Q_1 = D_0 + (wE / 3) p′(0) and Q_3 = D_2 − ((1 − w)E / 3) p′(E), with w = f_0 / (f_0 + f_1) and f_k the distance between the first control points of sections k and k + 1. Whether this rule belongs to the style or to the version of Rhino that wrote the loft (Rhino 4), no stored file known to the project settles (part 11), nor whether e is taken in homogeneous or Euclidean coordinates for rational sections. Outside these domains (a closed loft, a loft of two sections, a `SqrtChordLength` loft of more than three sections) an arm states its knot spacing only and the end rows are unstated: closed lofts, the rows `SqrtChordLength` places over more than three sections, and rational sections are open (part 11). Both arms fall under Rule H1 with an exact oracle: the Rhino decoder states the arm where its rebuild gives the stored control net, or, outside these domains, where the stored knots follow the arm's spacing, and `LoftStyle::Native("rhino:loft_style:<n>")` otherwise. A Rhino history record states the command that made it by that command's id, a UUID, and stores no command name. The Rhino decoder types a record by that id, and the codec's format document lists the id of each command this document types. A record of the Loft command is a loft: its antecedents are the loft's sections, and its value 100 states their order. A loft whose value 100 the decoder does not read has sections whose order it does not know, and is `Unresolved { family: Loft }` (§3.3). A record of a command this document does not type is `FeatureOperation::Native` whose kind is `rhino:` followed by the command id, with its values as native options (Rule N case (a), part 11). Rhino stores the style in value 9 of a loft's history record, in the order of RhinoCommon's `LoftType` (Normal 0, "chord-length parameterization in the loft direction"; Loose 1; Tight 2, "square root of chord-length parameterization"; Straight 3; Uniform 5). 0 is `ChordLength` and 2 `SqrtChordLength`, as RhinoCommon's `LoftType` page defines them; the chord as the largest distance between corresponding control points, the degree, and values 1, 3, and 5 are open (part 11). The Rhino decoder maps value 9: 0 `ChordLength`, 1 `Loose`, 2 `SqrtChordLength`, 3 `ruled: Some(true)`, 5 `Uniform`, any other `LoftStyle::Native("rhino:loft_style:<n>")`. Value 1 is not the style. A writer whose target's interpolating loft spaces its sections otherwise, or ends the interpolation otherwise, charges a loss naming the feature; no loss is charged for the two arms on a loft inside their domains, since the rules above construct their surface; outside them a writer charges a loss naming the loft. Rhino's straight sections are `ruled`.
- **Relimitation.** `relimit: Some(true)` ends the result at the first and last section; `Some(false)` extends it along the spine and guides to their ends (CATIA `Relimitation`).
- **Support trimming.** `trim_support: Some(true)` splits the support that the section's condition names at the section's curve and makes the piece the curve bounds part of the result, joined to the loft along it; `Some(false)` leaves the support out of the result (CATIA blend `TrimSupport`, stored per limit, 2 true and the default false; CATIA's Blended Surfaces page sets the trim per support). The flag does not depend on the condition. No stored file known to the project settles which piece of a split support the result keeps (Rule N case (a), part 11). A writer of another codec writes the loft and charges a loss naming the feature where the flag is true, except where every support the flag trims is already bounded by the section's curve: there it joins each support whole to the loft along the curve.
- **Spine points.** A section's `spine_point` is the point of the spine the section belongs to, where the source states it (STEP `sectioned_spine.spine_points`, ISO 10303-42); with none, a section belongs to the point where its plane meets the spine.
- **Representation of the result.** CATIA canonical-shape detection (`catia:CanonicalShapeDetection`) and FreeCAD `Linearize` (`fcstd:Linearize`) choose whether planar, cylindrical, or straight pieces of the result are stored as planes, cylinders, and lines or as B-splines of the same shape: two values give one surface whatever the inputs (Rule N case (b)), so they are source settings.
- **Smoothing.** `smoothing` lets the result depart from the exact loft within two tolerances: `angle`, the angular discontinuity of the spine's tangent or the guides' normal below which the moving frame is smoothed, and `deviation`, the distance by which the surface may leave the guides; each is `None` where it is off (CATIA multi-sections surface angular correction and deviation, `GSMSmoothAngleThreshold` and `GSMSmoothDeviation`, the CATIA Generative Shape Design guide). The smoothing is the source's, and the result is its evaluation. A writer whose target has no smoothing writes the exact loft and charges a loss naming the feature.
- **Section law.** `section_law` states how the section changes from one section to the next where a loft has more than two: `Linear` blends each consecutive pair linearly, which leaves an edge at each intermediate section, and `Smooth` passes through every section with one smooth surface. NX Swept stores its interpolation in byte 2 of the record's option array: 02 is `Linear` and 04 is `Smooth`. The third value, 03, which NX calls blend, is settled by no stored file known to the project on three or more sections (on two sections every interpolation gives one surface), so on three or more sections it is `Interpolation::Native("nx:interpolation:3")` (Rule N case (a), part 11). On a sweep of fewer than three sections the byte changes no result, so the decoder states no `section_law` and keeps the byte among the record's source settings (Rule N case (b)). Bytes 6 and 7 of the array stay native options until a stored file separates them from byte 2 by its geometry (part 11). `Interpolation` is §6.4's.
- **Guide influence.** A guide's `influence` states how far along each section's boundary, from the point where the guide meets it, the guide shapes the surface: `NextGuide` to the next guide, `NextSharp` to the next sharp corner of the section, where two contiguous entities have no common tangent or equal curvature, `NextEdge` to the end of the section entity the guide meets, and `Global` the whole section (SolidWorks loft guide influence, API `swGuideCurveInfluence_e` and the Loft PropertyManager). A writer whose target has no such choice charges a loss naming the feature where `influence` is stated.
- **Area stations.** `Centerline.stations` places sections of a stated area along the centerline (an Inventor area loft, API `LoftSectionDimension`): each at a `Fraction` of the centerline's length between the first and the last section, or a `Distance` along it from the first section, with its `area`; `driving: false` makes the area a cache (K2) of the area the loft has there. An Inventor station sized by a scale factor of its "default size" stays in the native option `inventor:area_loft`: Autodesk's pages state that the factor scales the station's area against a default size they do not define, and no stored file known to the project settles the size it scales (Rule N case (a), part 11). A writer whose target has no area stations writes the loft without them and charges a loss naming the feature.

### 6.4 Dress-up and holes

A dress-up operation changes bodies that earlier features made: it rounds or bevels edges, hollows, tapers, offsets, or thickens faces, drills holes, adds threads, or embosses a profile. The family is `Fillet`, `Chamfer`, `Shell`, `Draft`, `Thicken`, `Offset`, `Hole`, `Thread`, `Emboss`, `Dome`, and `Decal`, a decal binding an image to faces with no change of geometry.

#### Values along a chain

```rust
pub struct Stations<Q> { pub points: Vec<ValueStation<Q>>, pub law: Option<Interpolation>, pub chain_start: Option<SetSelection> }
pub struct ValueStation<Q> { pub at: StationAt, pub value: Dimension<Q> }
pub enum StationAt { Parameter { along: Along, fraction: Dimension<Fraction> }, Point(Construction<Point>), Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum Along { Chain, Edge(OrderedSelection) }
pub enum Interpolation { Linear, Smooth, Native(NonBlankString) }
```

- `Stations` is a scalar that varies along the edge chain of one set: a variable fillet radius or a variable draft angle.
- `Parameter` places a station at a fraction of the whole chain (Fusion start, mid, and end radii; NX percent) or of one edge in the edge's own direction (SolidWorks control points, FreeCAD `Part::Fillet` per-edge start and end radii). `Point` places it at a constructed point on the chain: a vertex, a datum point, or a point at a distance along an edge (CATIA `FilletRadiusList`, NX point stations). `Native` keeps a station position whose meaning is not established (NX arc-length stations, which no stored file known to the project holds; Rule N case (a), part 11); its value stays typed.
- `law` interpolates between stations (CATIA `Variation` linear and cubic, SolidWorks straight and smooth transition, Part 111 `linear_blend` and `cubic_blend`).
- `chain_start` picks the vertex at fraction 0 of the chain where the source stores one; `None` states that the source stores no such vertex. A fillet's chain runs along its set's edges in their order (the set is an `OrderedSelection`), so with no `chain_start` fraction 0 is the start vertex of the first edge, in that edge's own direction; Fusion starts its chains this way and stores no vertex. A draft's fixed edges are a `SetSelection` with no order, so there fraction 0 is stated only by `chain_start`.
- Mapping: Fusion start, mid, and end radii are `Chain` stations at 0, the mid parameters, and 1, along the set's ordered edges, with `chain_start: None`. FreeCAD `Part::Fillet` per-edge radii r1 and r2 are `Edge` stations at 0 and 1.

#### Fillet

```rust
pub struct Fillet { pub sets: Vec<FilletSet>, pub controls: BlendControls, pub native_options: NativeOptions, pub source_settings: NativeOptions }
pub enum FilletSet {
    Edges { edges: OrderedSelection, section: FilletSection, spine: Option<PathRef>, hold: [Option<SetSelection>; 2] },
    Faces {
        first: FaceSide, second: FaceSide, section: FilletSection, spine: Option<PathRef>,
        near: Option<Construction<Point>>, trim: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    },
    FullRound { first: RoundSide, center: SetSelection, second: RoundSide },
}
pub struct FaceSide { pub faces: SetSelection, pub hold: Option<SetSelection> }
pub enum RoundSide { Automatic, Faces(SetSelection) }
pub struct FilletSection { pub size: Option<FilletSize>, pub profile: Option<FilletProfile>, pub weight: Option<Dimension<PositiveReal>> }
pub enum FilletSize {
    Radius(Dimension<PositiveLength>),
    Chord(Dimension<PositiveLength>),
    Offsets { first: Dimension<PositiveLength>, second: Dimension<PositiveLength> },
    Variable(Stations<NonNegativeLength>),
    Held,
    ByProfile,
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum FilletProfile {
    Circular,
    Conic(ConicShape),
    CurvatureContinuous { shape: Option<Dimension<Fraction>> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum ConicShape {
    Rho { rho: Option<Dimension<Fraction>> },
    BoundaryAndCenter { center: Dimension<PositiveLength> },
    CenterAndRho { center: Dimension<PositiveLength>, rho: Dimension<Fraction> },
    ShoulderRadius(Dimension<PositiveLength>),
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
```

- A fillet holds one or more sets, each with its own size and profile. Groups of edges with different radii are several sets of one feature (Inventor two-set fillets, Creo round sets).
- `Edges` rounds the edges its selection reaches, in source order: a Fusion variable fillet places its radii along that order, and Fusion numbers the faces it makes in that order (inferred, §5.7). Item picks that are faces or features are `Of { kind: Edge }` terms, loops are `LoopEdges` terms, and tangent propagation is `Connected { continuity: G1 }` (§5.8); CATIA propagation by intersection with features is an `Intersection` term, CATIA minimal propagation `Propagation::Minimal` (§5.8); a `PickDomain` restricts a pick to part of an edge (CATIA edge limits). The Creo ambiguity array of a round set is its picks' witnesses. `hold` bounds the blend on each side by a hold line where the source states one (the CATIA edge fillet's `Track1` and `Track2`): `hold[0]` the side whose face loop traverses the edge in the edge's own direction, as for `Offsets.first`, and `hold[1]` the other.
- `Faces` rounds between two face sets (CATIA face-face and shape fillet, NX face blend, SolidWorks face fillet, Creo surface-to-surface round). `hold` is a hold line or curve that bounds the blend on that side (CATIA `Track1`, `Track2`, `HoldCurve`; SolidWorks hold line). `near` is the help point that chooses among solutions. `trim` states whether the support faces are trimmed to the blend.
- `FullRound` replaces a center face set by a blend tangent to the two side sets (Inventor, Fusion, SolidWorks full round; CATIA tritangent with its removed face as `center`). `Automatic` states that the source computes the side from the center face (Fusion).
- `spine` orients the cross-sections (CATIA `RibbonSpine` and face-fillet `Spine`, Creo `spine_id`).
- SolidWorks keep features and round corners are `BlendControls.keep_features` and `round_corners` (below). SolidWorks stores a fillet's tangent propagation and keep features in the first item of its first edge-radius list, as the u32 at +0 and the u32 at +16 of the 58 bytes after the item's face list, which the SolidWorks decoder reads into the item term's propagation (1 `Connected { continuity: Some(G1) }`, 0 `Off`) and `keep_features`; where the block is not located the decoder states `None`. The byte at +37, which may carry the attachment-edges option, stays the native option `sldprt:attachment_edges` (part 11). The other 55 bytes of the block are constant, so the block holds no fourth option. No SolidWorks fillet stores an option that propagates visual properties: a fillet face's colour is a stored appearance of its own. The option of that name belongs to patterns (§6.5).
- `Radius` is a constant rolling-ball radius. `Chord` is a constant chord width between the support boundaries. `Offsets` are distinct setbacks on the two supports: `first` lies on the face whose loop traverses the edge in the edge's own direction for `Edges`, and on `first` for `Faces`. `Variable` is a radius by stations. `Held` states that the hold lines alone fix the width. `ByProfile` states that the conic profile alone fixes the width (`CenterAndRho`). `Native` keeps a size form whose meaning is not established (Rule N case (a)), so the rest of the round stays typed. Every Creo round size and cross section PTC documents has a home: circular by radius or chord, conic and D1×D2 conic (`Conic(Rho)`, with `Offsets` for D1×D2), C2 and D1×D2 C2 (`CurvatureContinuous` with its shape factor), variable, through curve (`Held`), and full round, and its normal-to-spine creation method is `spine` (PTC About Creation Methods and Cross Section Shapes); Creo's `round_choice` codes: 989 is an `Edges` set, `Radius` with one radius dimension and `Variable` with several; 986 is `FullRound` between its two edge references, with no radius dimension, its radius set by the geometry; 987 is a `Faces` set between two surfaces with one radius dimension; and 995 is a round of several sets, each a set of its own. Code 992 rounds between an edge and a surface with one radius dimension, and no stored file known to the project settles how its edge maps onto a `FaceSide`, so the decoder keeps its references as native options (typed, carrier unread; part 11).
- `profile` is the cross-section shape. `Conic` is a conic section sized by its `ConicShape`: `Rho` the conic ratio `rho`, `None` where the source does not state it, with the width from `size` (CATIA `ConicRatio`, SolidWorks conic rho, NX boundary and rho); `BoundaryAndCenter` the boundary from `size` and the center distance (NX); `CenterAndRho` the center distance and the ratio, which fix the width (NX); `ShoulderRadius` the radius at the shoulder point of a symmetric fillet (SolidWorks conic radius). SolidWorks stores one value, `ConicRhoOrRadius`, whose meaning follows its profile type. `CurvatureContinuous` is a G2 section (SolidWorks and NX curvature-continuous fillets); `shape` is Creo's C2 shape factor, from 0 to 0.95, whose effect on the section's spline PTC describes as analogous to rho's on a conic, so the section it gives is the evaluation, and a writer whose target has no such factor charges a loss naming the feature where it is stated. `weight` is the source's tangency weight of the section, whatever its profile (Fusion `TangencyWeight`, 0.1 to 2, stored on constant-radius, variable, and chordal fillets): a Fusion G1 fillet is `Circular` with `weight`, and a weight other than 1 makes the section non-circular, a shape the evaluation carries.

#### Chamfer

```rust
pub struct Chamfer { pub sets: Vec<ChamferSet>, pub controls: BlendControls, pub native_options: NativeOptions, pub source_settings: NativeOptions }
pub struct ChamferSet {
    pub edges: SetSelection,
    pub size: Option<ChamferSize>,
    pub reference: Option<SetSelection>,
    pub flip: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub measure: Option<ChamferMeasure>,
}
pub enum ChamferSize {
    Distance(Dimension<PositiveLength>),
    Distances { first: Dimension<PositiveLength>, second: Dimension<PositiveLength> },
    DistanceAngle { distance: Dimension<PositiveLength>, angle: Dimension<InteriorAngle> },
    WidthAngle    { width: Dimension<PositiveLength>, angle: Dimension<InteriorAngle> },
    HeightAngle   { height: Dimension<PositiveLength>, angle: Dimension<InteriorAngle> },
    Vertex(Vec<EdgeSetback>),
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum ChamferMeasure { AlongFaces, OffsetFaces, Native(NonBlankString) }
```

- `Distance` is an equal setback on both faces, `Distances` one per face, `DistanceAngle` a setback and the angle from the reference face. `first` and the `DistanceAngle` distance lie on the reference side. SolidWorks states a chamfer's form by the dimension parameters its `Chamfer_c` record owns, each slot name a role: `D1` and `D2` are `DistanceAngle`'s distance and angle, and `D1` and `D3` `Distances`' first and second, an equal-distance chamfer storing one value in both.
- The reference side is the face `reference` selects (CATIA `ReferenceFace`, Inventor chamfer face), else the face whose loop traverses the edge in the edge's own direction, swapped when `flip` is true (FreeCAD `FlipDirection`, NX `ReverseOffsets`).
- `measure` states whether the distances run along the faces or offset them (NX `OffsetMethod`, SolidWorks offset-face chamfer).
- `WidthAngle` is the chamfer face's width across the edge and its angle from the reference face; `HeightAngle` is the distance from the edge where the two faces meet to the chamfer face, and the angle (CATIA chordal and height chamfers: the chordal length is "the chamfer width", with Width = Length / cos(Angle), and the height the "distance between the intersection of the two adjacent faces and the chamfer face", with Height = Length · sin(Angle), the CATIA Part Design guide). CATIA's width formula gives the face's width only where the faces meet at a right angle; whether CATIA applies it on other edges is part 11's question (no stored file known to the project holds a chordal or height chamfer), and until it is settled the CATIA decoder states `WidthAngle` only for faces that meet at a right angle. A writer whose target has neither writes `DistanceAngle`, with the distance height / sin(angle), or width · cos(angle) on faces that meet at a right angle.
- `Vertex` cuts one vertex where three edges of one convexity meet by the plane through the three points at its distances from the vertex along those edges, each an arc length on its edge: one `EdgeSetback` per edge, and the set's `edges` an `Of { kind: Edge }` term over the vertex (SolidWorks vertex chamfer, API `IChamferFeatureData2`: "three distances along three adjacent edges ... an arc length value"). No stored file known to the project settles which edge its first distance runs along (part 11). A writer whose target has no vertex chamfer writes a plane through three points, each at its distance along its edge from the vertex, and a split that keeps the side of the plane away from the vertex, one geometry feature, and charges `export:feature.lowered`. Where the target places a point on an edge only by a fraction of the edge's length or parameter, the written points would not follow an edit of the edges, and step 3 applies (§3.4).
- `ChamferSize::Native` names a source form whose meaning is not established (Rule N case (a), part 11): the SolidWorks face-face chamfer, whose methods SolidWorks documents (symmetric, asymmetric, chord width, hold line) and whose section, and the point its distance is measured from between faces that do not meet, no stored file known to the project settles (part 11). Its values are native options under the source's own parameter names (§6).

#### Controls shared by fillet and chamfer

```rust
pub struct BlendControls {
    pub corner_style: Option<CornerStyle>,
    pub corners: Vec<Corner>,
    pub limits: Vec<BlendLimit>,
    pub keep: Option<SetSelection>,
    pub transitions: Vec<Transition>,
    pub overflow: Option<Overflow>,
    pub keep_features: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
    pub round_corners: Option<Dimension<bool>>,
}
pub enum CornerStyle { RollingBall, Setback, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub struct Corner { pub vertex: SetSelection, pub setbacks: Option<Setbacks> }
pub enum Setbacks { Uniform(Dimension<NonNegativeLength>), PerEdge(Vec<EdgeSetback>) }
pub struct EdgeSetback { pub edge: SetSelection, pub distance: Dimension<NonNegativeLength> }
pub struct BlendLimit { pub at: LimitAt, pub reversed: Option<Dimension<bool>> }
pub enum LimitAt { Element(SetSelection), Point(Construction<Point>) }
pub struct Transition {
    pub between: BTreeSet<u32>,
    pub at: Option<SetSelection>,
    pub kind: Option<TransitionKind>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
}
pub enum TransitionKind {
    Continue,
    Intersect,
    Stop,
    StopAt(LimitAt),
    CornerSphere { radius: Option<Dimension<PositiveLength>>, lengths: Vec<Dimension<NonNegativeLength>> },
    /// A ball of radius r stays tangent to the listed pieces and to the faces in `against`, inside every listed
    /// piece and outside only a piece in `against`, its centre at ρ − r from the centre locus of a piece it lies
    /// inside and ρ + r from one it lies outside (a cylinder's axis, a torus's centre circle, a fillet's ball-centre
    /// curve): a sphere where all radii are r; a torus about the R piece's axis, tube r, centre circle R − r, for
    /// r, r, R; and for r, R₁, R₂ the sweep of the ball whose centre stays at R₁ − r and R₂ − r from the two larger
    /// pieces' loci (R₁ = R₂ included), with, where the sweep reaches the face the pieces roll on, the ball rolling
    /// on the larger piece and on that face. r is `radius`; `None` is the smallest radius among the listed pieces.
    /// `against`: the faces, of the state entering the round and of no listed set, that the ball stays tangent to
    /// along the corner face; `None` states that it has no such support.
    RollingBall { radius: Option<Dimension<PositiveLength>>, against: Option<SetSelection> },
    /// The round of radius r swept outside one listed piece, the wrapped one, its centre at ρ + r from that piece's
    /// centre locus, tangent to `against`, where the rounds the corner continues have radius r. With three listed
    /// sets the wrapped piece is the largest and the sweep is the torus about its axis, tube r and centre circle
    /// R + r. With two, the corner continues the other listed set's round. With one, that set is wrapped by another
    /// feature's round of radius r. For a cylinder against a plane normal to its axis the sweep is the torus of tube
    /// r and centre circle R + r. r is `radius`; `None` is the smallest radius among the listed pieces. `against`
    /// is as on `RollingBall`.
    SweptAround { radius: Option<Dimension<PositiveLength>>, against: Option<SetSelection> },
    /// Two chain ends joined by the round continued across the corner: fillet faces at the pieces' radius, joined
    /// to both end pieces across the round's seam, rolling on the face both chains roll on and on the corner's
    /// faces between them; where they meet, the junction's fillets and each end piece open at the same angle within 0.1 rad.
    Blend,
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum Overflow { Default, KeepEdge, KeepSurface, Native(NonBlankString) }
```

- `corner_style` is the feature's choice of how blends meet at a vertex: `RollingBall` or `Setback` (Fusion `isRollingBallCorner`, one per feature, with asymmetric sets always `Setback`; Inventor `RollingBallWherePossible`). The Fusion and Inventor decoders state `None` until its carrier is read (typed, carrier unread; part 11). NX per-corner include (`Setback` `IncludeWithCorner` or `SeparateFromCorner`) is the native option `nx:corner_include` of the feature until its effect on the corner patch is established: no stored file known to the project settles it, and without a setback both values give one corner (Rule N case (a), part 11).
- A `Corner` treats a vertex where blended edges meet. `setbacks` are the distances from the vertex at which each blend starts its corner patch (CATIA `BlendVertexList`, NX and SolidWorks setbacks); `Uniform` applies one distance to every edge at the vertex. CATIA chamfer corner vertices are `Corner`s; their cap mode is the native option `catia:corner_cap_mode`, stored on a chamfer; CATIA's chamfer page names Corner Cap, on by default, with no statement of the cap's surface, and no stored file known to the project settles what the cap builds (Rule N case (a), part 11).
- A `BlendLimit` stops the blend at an element (a plane, face, surface, or curve: CATIA limiting elements, NX stop short at an intersection) or at a point on the chain (NX stop short at a distance, a point at an `Offset` along the edge). The blend keeps the side the element's normal points to, the other side when `reversed` is true.
- `keep` selects edges the blend leaves intact by rolling along them (CATIA `KeepEdgeList`, NX cliff edges). `overflow` states what a blend does where it runs past a neighbouring edge (SolidWorks overflow type). `keep_features: Some(true)` keeps in the result a cut or boss feature whose faces the blend would cover, and `Some(false)` lets the blend cover it; `round_corners: Some(true)` blends the corner where two filleted edges meet smoothly, in place of a sharp juncture (SolidWorks Keep Features and Round Corners: Constant Size Fillets help and API `ISimpleFilletFeatureData2` and `IChamferFeatureData2`). How the kept feature and the round corner are built is the evaluation's; a writer whose target has neither charges a loss naming the feature where one is true.
- A `Transition` states how the sets whose indices `between` lists meet, at the vertices or edges `at` selects. `Continue` carries the round through the junction as one rolling round and adds no surface of another kind: where the two listed pieces' ends do not coincide, the round's own fillet face at the pieces' ball spans between them, tangent to both, so tangent round geometry does not stop at sharp edges. `Intersect` extends overlapping pieces toward each other until they merge in a sharp boundary. `Stop` ends the round where its edge chain ends: the last piece is cut by the carriers of the faces that meet both rounded faces at the chain's end, a face whose carrier must be continued to close the end gains a face on that carrier, and no surface of another kind is added. `StopAt` ends the round at a datum point or plane. `CornerSphere` closes three overlapping pieces with a sphere, of the largest piece's radius unless `radius` states one, at the transition distances `lengths` along the edges, blended into the pieces by fillet surfaces. `RollingBall` closes the corner with the surface a ball of radius r sweeps while it stays tangent to the listed pieces and to the faces in `against`, inside every listed piece and outside only a piece in `against`, its centre at ρ − r from the centre locus of each piece it lies inside and at ρ + r from each it lies outside, where a piece's radius ρ is a cylinder's radius, a torus's tube, or a fillet's ball, and its centre locus the cylinder's axis, the torus's centre circle, or the fillet's ball-centre curve: a sphere of radius r where the radii are r, r, r; a torus about the R piece's axis with tube radius r and centre-circle radius R − r where they are r, r, R; and where they are r, R₁, R₂ with r the smallest (R₁ = R₂ included), the sweep of the ball whose centre stays at R₁ − r and R₂ − r from the two larger pieces' loci, joined, where the sweep reaches the face the pieces roll on, by the face of the ball rolling on the larger piece and on that face, which `against` names (under Rule H1: the decoder states the source's `Native` arm on a corner that holds a face outside this definition). `SweptAround` closes the corner with the round of radius r swept outside one listed piece, the wrapped one, its centre at ρ + r from that piece's centre locus and the ball tangent to `against`; it holds where the rounds the corner continues have radius r. So the two arms are told apart by the ball: inside every listed piece is `RollingBall`, outside one listed piece is `SweptAround`. The wrapped piece is the listed piece the ball stays outside of, and is derived, not stated: where three sets are listed it is the largest piece, larger than both others, and the round is the torus about its axis with tube r and centre-circle radius R + r; where two are listed the corner continues the other set's round; where one is listed it is that set, wrapped by another feature's round of radius r. A decoder and a writer find the two-set wrapped piece by its edges, as the listed set with no edge on `against`, the other having one. A cylinder against a plane normal to its axis gives the torus of tube r and centre-circle radius R + r. On both arms r is `radius`, and the smallest radius among the listed pieces where `radius` is `None`; where the corner continues a round that no listed set supplies, `radius` binds that round's radius parameter, a binding the decoder infers (below; D59). `against` holds the faces, of the state entering the round and of no listed set, that the ball stays tangent to along the corner face, and nothing else: a face that the corner face only continues across a seam is not in it, since `radius` carries the round that face belongs to. It selects in that state, as every selection of a feature does (§5.8), and it is an operand, not a cache of the stored corner (D59). On these two arms `against` `None` and `radius` `None` are defined values, as `CornerSphere.radius`'s `None` is: `against` `None` states that no face beyond the listed pieces supports the ball, where the listed pieces and `radius` fix it, and a decoder that has not determined the supports states the `Native` arm, never `None`. A face of no listed set that bounds the corner and that the ball does not stay on is outside it (the second plane a two-set torus borders). It is stated on these two arms only, and always on a two-set `SweptAround`, whose wrapped piece is found from it (part 10). By case: for the two-set sphere, nothing; for a two-set torus, the plane the ball rolls on; for the two-set r, R, R sweep, nothing, the round it continues being an earlier feature's that `radius` binds; for the one-set `RollingBall` torus, the plane, the two r cylinders of another feature that it meets being the round it continues, which `radius` carries; for the one-set `RollingBall` fillet, the outer cylinder; for the one-set `SweptAround`, the plane; with three sets, the face of another feature the ball stays tangent to where the corner borders one (the three-set `SweptAround`, the r, r, R torus, the r, R₁, R₂ sweep, and a sphere outside another feature's torus), and nothing otherwise. `Blend` joins one chain's end to the next chain's start by the round continued across the corner: fillet faces at the pieces' own radius, joined to both end pieces across the round's seam, rolling on the face both chains roll on and on the corner's faces between them; where they meet, the junction's fillets and each end piece open at the same angle within 0.1 rad, which is not an operand, and which the decoder's gate tests at every junction–end seam; it has no size of its own, and tangency to the end pieces is not part of it. A `Continue` between two subsets differs from it in that a `Blend`'s faces lie between the chain ends, across the corner's faces. `Native` keeps, under its source name, a type whose shape or sizes are not established. A transition's `native_options` is §6's map, each key filed by its Rule N case.
- Creo transitions are `Transition`s over round-set indices. Creo stores each transition's kind as `subft_rndtrans.type`, with the subsets it joins and the end of each (`subset_ids`, `subset_ends`). The code is PTC's Toolkit transition enumeration (`ProRoundTransType`: 1 intersect, 2 blend, 3 stop, 4 continue, 5 sphere corner, 6 patch, 7 a corner of three rounds, 12 rolling ball, 13 to 15, 18, and 19 stop cases, 16 stop at a reference).
- Code 1 is `Intersect`, under Rule H1: the Creo decoder states `Intersect` only where the stored pieces meet in a sharp edge with no face between them, and `Native("creo:1")` otherwise. Where no ridge lies between the pieces, `Intersect` and `Continue` give one shape; how code 1 reads at a round along a ridge edge is not read against the enumeration (part 11). Code 4 is `Continue`. Where both entries are one subset and the chain closes a loop, its pieces meeting across a seam edge, such a transition's `between` has one member. Between two different subsets it is under Rule H1: the faces between the pieces are the round's own fillet face at the pieces' ball, spanning from one listed piece's end to the other's, tangent to both, a piece of the round's own third subset, and a face on an earlier feature's carrier that the round bounds, none of them a surface of another kind. The Creo decoder states `Continue` where the pieces meet across a seam or the round-owned faces between them are of those kinds, and `Native("creo:4")` where another face lies between them or the adjacency is not read. Code 2 is `Blend`, under Rule H1. A stored blend is a run of round-owned faces joining the two chains' end pieces across the corner, fillet surfaces or a torus, the surface the rolling ball sweeps along a circular edge; where a later round feature rebuilt the corner, the round's faces stop against its faces. Where spline faces stand at the run's ends, no construction from the corner rebuilds them, and across such a patch the angle between the ball's two radii changes by more than across a junction seam of fillet faces; such a record is `Native("creo:2")` with the stored faces (part 11). A blend stores no size or radius law of its own. The file stores no angular tolerance, so the arm does not say tangent. No stored file known to the project joins pieces of different radii (part 11). The Creo decoder states `Blend` where every junction face is read and is a fillet face or a torus at the end pieces' radius to 1e-3 and the run joins both end pieces, and where, at every junction–end seam, the angle between the ball's radii changes by less than 0.1 rad. A seam whose angle does not read (a torus side or an unread row) is not stated under Rule H1's clause for a rule the decoder cannot test (§3.1), so on a record with such a seam the decoder states `Native("creo:2")`. It states `Native("creo:2")` with the stored faces otherwise as well: a rebuilt corner, a run with spline faces, a record with an unread junction face, and a record whose second end piece the junction does not touch.
- Code 3 is `Stop`. Every open end of a listed subset holds a record, and a round with subsets and no transition is a closed chain; binary files store code 4 at a closed chain's closing junction. At a stop, an earlier face that already bounds the solid there is kept, and where a face's carrier must be continued to close the end the round owns a face on that carrier, so no surface of another kind is added. PTC's three stop cases ("Each Stop Case geometry is configured based on the geometrical context") are one stored value, as the page says; the Toolkit enumeration gives the stop cases codes of their own, which no stored file known to the project holds.
- Code 5 is `CornerSphere`. Code 12 is `RollingBall` and code 7 `SweptAround`, each under Rule H1: the Creo decoder states the arm only where the stored corner faces meet its test, the ball's centre at the stated distance from each piece's centre locus at every centre to 1e-3 and, for `RollingBall`, the stored junction's ball of the radius r the definition gives, and `Native("creo:12")` or `Native("creo:7")` otherwise, keeping the corner's faces. Where the arm does not fix the stored code (a two-set `SweptAround` under code 12, a one-set `Continue` under code 7), the decoder keeps `subft_rndtrans.type` in the transition's `native_options` (`creo:transition_type`, case (a): codes 12 and 7 build different corners from three sets, and no stored file known to the project settles whether they agree on a two-set corner after an edit; part 11), and the Creo writer emits it. Where the corner continues a round that no listed set supplies, the decoder binds `radius` to that round's radius parameter, under Rule H1: the binding is inferred from the stored corner's seams and the equal radius, since the file stores no reference from the transition to the dimension, so the decoder looks first at the face across the corner's seam, and binds where it is a piece of a set of an earlier feature whose radius dimension equals the stored ball's r; where that face is the round's own r fillet in no set, it looks at the face across that fillet's seam and binds on the same test; and it states `Native` where neither finds one (D59). With three listed subsets, a corner whose ball lies inside only two listed pieces, the third being a piece missing from the visible body or a piece of no listed set holding the ball, or whose ball lies outside two of the three rounds, is `Native("creo:12")` (part 11). Where a three-set code-12 corner borders a face of another feature the ball stays tangent to it, and `against` holds that face; otherwise `against` holds nothing. Under code 7, a three-set junction face that fits `SweptAround` lies outside the largest listed piece at R + r and is tangent at every centre to the face of another feature it borders, and `against` holds that face. A code-7 corner whose continued sets' radii differ from the ball's, a sweep of circular arcs whose radius runs from one continued set's radius to the other's, is `Native("creo:7")` (part 11), as is a three-set code-7 corner that continues two listed pieces, is not read, or is a spline surface. With two listed subsets, code 12 gives `RollingBall` (r, R, R sweeps, the ball inside both listed pieces at every centre, and r, r, r spheres, inside both listed pieces and a third piece of radius r, a piece of the round in no listed set or the round's own cylinder) or `SweptAround` (tori, and faces whose wrapped piece is a fillet or a cylinder), and code 7 gives `SweptAround`. Where both listed sets or neither has an edge on `against`, the decoder states `Native` (part 11). By the rule, `against` is the plane on a two-set torus; nothing on a two-set sphere, the listed pieces and `radius` fixing the ball; and nothing on a two-set r, R, R sweep, whose radius `radius` binds, including where it borders another feature's cylinder that its ball does not touch, a piece of the round `radius` binds. The faces a corner only continues across a seam are not in it. The second plane a two-set code-7 torus borders is not in it. A code-12 face whose ball fits at every sample but the one the corner's two faces share, a face tangent to one piece only, and a face whose carrier is not read (type-40 rows) are `Native("creo:12")` (part 11). With one listed subset, code 12 is `RollingBall`: a torus inside the listed cylinder and at r from a plane normal to its axis, meeting two r cylinders of another feature, which are the round the corner continues and which `radius` carries, `against` holding the plane alone; or a fillet inside the listed cylinder and outside another feature's cylinder, `against` holding that cylinder, and the other feature's fillet and torus that the corner continues across seams being outside it; on both `radius` binds the other feature's set radius. A record that keeps no listed piece is `Native("creo:12")`. Code 7 is `SweptAround`, the listed set wrapped by another feature's round of radius r: every ball centre is outside the listed cylinder at R + r and at r from a plane normal to its axis read from its own row; `against` holds that plane, the other feature's r cylinders that the torus continues across seams being outside it, and `radius` binds that feature's set radius dimension. The decoder states it only where the transition's own feature owns the junction face. A record with no junction face, where the other feature owns the torus, is `Native("creo:7")`: what a one-set swept corner states there is open (part 11). A code-7 record that continues the listed round at its own ball is `Continue`; one that borders a fillet not tangent to it, or keeps no listed piece, is `Native("creo:7")`. The swept round is the one whose radius dimension `radius` binds. With four listed subsets, where a record holds one face of each construction, a `RollingBall` r, R, R sweep and `SweptAround`'s construction, no arm holds the record and the decoder states `Native("creo:12")` with its faces (part 11). Code 6 is `Native("creo:6")`. A code-6 record lists the one chain that ends in the corner, and its face is a ruled surface between two stored rails, trimmed by four edges: tangent to the rolling face along one, meeting the chain's last piece along another at a seam, not a tangency, and sharp to the two crossing chains along the other two; no construction from that boundary and its continuity is known to reproduce it (part 11). The stored patch face is a face of the evaluation after the round, and `Native("creo:6")` names the record; the two rails with their end tangents and the four edge conditions stay in the feature's native record (`native_ref`). No stored file known to the project holds PTC's optional fillet surface on a patch (Rule N case (a), part 11). No stored file known to the project holds `StopAt` (code 16) or codes 10, 13 to 15, 18, and 19. A decoder that reads round faces places a class-255 fragment on the chain it is seam-joined to and not on the subset of the class-254 piece whose carrier it shares.

#### Shell, thicken, offset

```rust
pub struct ShellFeature {
    pub bodies: Option<SetSelection>,
    pub removed: SetSelection,
    pub thickness: Option<Thickness>,
    pub faces: Vec<FaceThickness>,
    pub join: Option<OffsetJoin>,
    pub face_meeting: Option<FaceMeeting>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub struct FaceThickness { pub faces: SetSelection, pub thickness: Dimension<PositiveLength> }
pub enum OffsetJoin { Round, Sharp, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum FaceMeeting { Neighbours, All }
pub struct Thicken { pub faces: SetSelection, pub thickness: Option<Thickness>, pub boolean: Option<Boolean>, pub native_options: NativeOptions, pub source_settings: NativeOptions }
pub struct Offset {
    pub sets: Vec<OffsetSet>,
    pub result: OffsetResult,
    pub join: Option<OffsetJoin>,
    pub face_meeting: Option<FaceMeeting>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub struct OffsetSet { pub faces: SetSelection, pub distance: Option<Dimension<Length>> }
pub enum OffsetResult { Move, Copy(SheetOutput) }
```

- `ShellFeature.removed` selects the faces that open the shell; a `Named` selection with no picks states a closed hollow (NX shell all). `bodies` selects the bodies to shell where the source names them. `faces` gives a face set its own thickness on the default side (Creo, NX `FaceThicknesses`, SolidWorks multi-thickness, Part 111 `complex_shelled_solid`).
- `Thickness` is §6's type. For a shell, a `OneSide` thickness `Inside` grows the wall into the material and `Outside` away from it, `Offsets` holds the outside and inside values (Fusion), and `Symmetric` splits the value across the boundary. For `Thicken`, `Outside` is along the face normal and `Inside` against it; `Offsets` holds both offsets (CATIA `TopOffset` and `BotOffset`, NX first and second offset). `Thicken.boolean` combines the thickened body (Inventor, Fusion).
- `OffsetJoin` is the corner law between offset faces: rounded arcs or sharp intersection (FreeCAD `Join` `Arc` and `Intersection`, Fusion shell corner). FreeCAD's third Part `Join` value, `Tangent`, is `Sharp`: Open CASCADE dispatches only the arc and the intersection joins, and `Tangent` runs on to the neighbours' intersection (`BRepOffset_MakeOffset.cxx` at V7_8_0; in 2D, `BRepFill_OffsetWire.cxx` sends every value but the arc down its intersection branches). PartDesign's `Join` enumerates only `Arc` and `Intersection`, so its stored 1 is `Sharp`.
- FreeCAD states an offset mode on every PartDesign and Part thickness and offset object (`Mode`: `Skin`, `Pipe`, or `RectoVerso`), which it passes to Open CASCADE's `BRepOffset_Mode`. Open CASCADE stores the mode and never reads it: "currently, only one construction type is implemented" (`BRepOffsetAPI_MakeOffsetShape.hxx` and `BRepOffsetAPI_MakeThickSolid.hxx`, with no reader of `myMode` under `BRepOffset` at any tag from V6_9_1 to V7_9_0). Every value is therefore the offset the typed fields state, and `RectoVerso` on a shell is the same one-sided thickness as `Skin`: the mode is the source setting `fcstd:Mode`, a selector with no design meaning whatever the inputs (Rule N case (b)), which a FreeCAD writer restores. A FreeCAD writer that receives a `Symmetric` thickness cannot state it by `Mode`; two offsets of half the value would need the second to pick faces of the first's result, which no state the document holds contains, so step 3 applies (§3.4). `face_meeting` states which offset faces trim each other where their offsets meet: `All` intersects every offset face with every other, so offset faces that were not adjacent and meet after the offset trim each other and the result is the offset solid; `Neighbours` intersects each with its neighbours only, which gives the same result wherever no faces that are not adjacent meet, and no valid result where they do (the feature fails or leaves an invalid solid). FreeCAD's `Intersection` on `Part::Offset`, `Part::Thickness`, and PartDesign `Thickness` is `All` where true and `Neighbours` where false (Open CASCADE's complete intersection, `BRepOffset_MakeOffset.cxx` at V7_8_0). Other sources state `None`. `SelfIntersection` is the source setting `fcstd:SelfIntersection`: Open CASCADE stores it and never reads it (its one reader is commented out; Rule N case (b)).
- `Offset` moves faces by a signed distance along their oriented normals, per set (NX distance per face set).
