The SolidWorks Rip feature is `SheetMetalKind::Native("sldprt:rip")` with its edges, its gap, and its per-edge value kept: no stored file known to the project sets a result against it.
  - `Sketched { through: SketchWall }` with `Gap`: SolidWorks convert rips on a sketch make one straight slot per rip through the one wall the sketch lies on, as wide as the gap, centred on the line; under Rule H1 the decoder states the arm only where the stored slots agree. `Sketched { through: Projected }` with `Tear`: Creo sketched rips: the chain carried along its sketch's normal meets the sheet, and the sheet is split there through its thickness, normal to the sheet, with zero width. `SketchWall` and `Projected` give the same cut wherever the sketch lies on a wall, so they differ only where the carried chain goes on to another wall. The Creo cut is not in the wall the sketch lies on, and not along the swept surface. Where the chain crosses the outer face more than once, one crossing is cut; the section's flip fields cannot record which, and no stored file known to the project settles which of several crossings is cut (part 11). The Creo decoder states the arm under Rule H1, only where the stored lips or split surfaces agree, and `Native("creo:1006")` otherwise; the section's flip fields are kept as native options.
  - `KerfSide`: Inventor side value 2 is `Centered` (a conversion's rips are centred by `ConvertRip`'s definition); side value 1 is `Right`, the gap inside the named face, on m × d, under Rule H1. No stored file known to the project holds `Left`.

  Carriers. Inventor (feature record `914d8790`): kind 1 is `Ruling` and kind 2 `Line`, with the body, the gap, the point or points, and the face in its slots; side 2 is `Centered` and side 1 `Right`; side 0 and the face-extents kind, which no stored file known to the project holds, are `Native`. Creo: type 1006 (`PRO_FEAT_RIP`) with `misc_choice` 8 and one surface in instruction 119 is `Faces` under Rule H1; type 1006 with a section of one open chain is `Along { path: Sketched { through: Projected }, width: Tear }` under Rule H1; code 1062 is a deform area (`PRO_FEAT_DEFORM_AREA`), `Native("creo:1062")`; the edge rip with its seam types and the rip connect are held by no stored file known to the project and stay `Native`. SolidWorks: the Rip feature is `Native` as above; a convert rip is one of the `rips` of its `Convert` (below). Fusion: no stored file known to the project holds a rip, so its decoder has no carrier to read (part 11). A writer whose target has no rip writes a `Faces` rip as a cut of the picked faces' outlines through the sheet and charges `export:feature.lowered`; for an `Along` rip it takes step 3 (§3.4).
- `Convert` turns the solid `body` into sheet metal `thickness` thick, with a cut at each of `rips` and the face `fixed` staying in place, built as `from` states. `Faces` builds walls `thickness` thick on the solid's faces with a bend at each of `bends`, and `side` states where the sheet lies against the solid's faces: `Inside`, the solid's faces are the sheet's outer faces; `Outside`, they are its inner faces. `ThinSolid` takes a solid that is already walls `thickness` thick and recognises those walls as the sheet and its cylindrical walls as the bends, so it has no side and no bend list. A `ConvertBend` is an `Edge` of the solid where two walls meet, whose `radius` is the bend's inner radius and whose `None` takes `bend.radius`, or a cylindrical `Face` of it, which takes that face's radius r: the bend's inner radius is r where the sheet lies `Inside` against a concave face of the solid or `Outside` against a convex one, and r − `thickness` in the other two cases. `keep_solid` keeps the solid as a body beside the sheet. A `ConvertRip` is centred on its `path`, which is `Edges` or `Sketched`. On `Edges`, each wall ends `T cot(t/2) + gap / (2 sin(t/2))` back from the edge of the solid the rip names, the line where the solid's two faces meet, for T the `thickness` and t the angle between the faces. Under `Inside` that edge is the line where the walls' outer planes meet, which leaves the walls' inner edges `gap` apart; under `Outside` it is the line where their inner planes meet, which leaves them `gap + 2 T cos(t/2)` apart (the `Inside` result is inferred). SolidWorks Convert to Sheet Metal (`moSolidToSheetMetal_c`, its parameters in a `moCompSheetmetalFeat_c` that follows its bend features) is `Faces`. Its default radius is the bends' inner radius. A round-bend conversion's own radius is the radius of the solid's cylindrical face the bend lies on, so such bends are `ConvertBend::Face` bends (that the stored pick is a face is inferred: the radius is read, the pick is not); under Rule H1 the decoder states an `Edge` bend's own `radius` only where the stored bend's faces agree with it, and a `Face` bend only where its stored radius is that face's, and the conversion as `Native("sldprt:convert")` with its picks kept otherwise; a bend stores flag 1 with radius −1.0 where the default applies and flag 0 with its own radius otherwise; the relief u32 1 is obround, `0.5 × T` wide by the f64 0.5 beside it, so the decoder states `bend.relief` with `shape: Obround` and `width_ratio` 0.5, and the u32's values 0 and 2, which no body separates, as `ReliefShape::Native("sldprt:relief_kind")`; and a rip's stored gap of −1.0 decodes to the feature's default gap. The SolidWorks edge rips (`Rip` above) are the `Outside` case where the kept solid's faces are the sheet's inner faces; the `Inside` result elsewhere rests on no stored solid. `keep_solid` and `side` have no located flag, so no stored file known to the project settles the side's carrier. So under Rule H1 the decoder reads `side` from a kept solid (one whose faces coincide with the sheet's inner faces is `Outside`, with `keep_solid: Some(true)`) and states `None` otherwise; what would settle the side is a conversion stored with its solid (typed, carrier unread; part 11). A round bend's radius does not give the side: the sheet has both cylinders, so a stored radius equals one of its faces under either side. `Faces.side` decides how the walls, the face bends' radii, and the rips' gaps are built, so where it is `None` a writer of another codec does not default it: it takes step 3 (§3.4) or charges a loss naming the feature, and a writer of the same codec re-emits the source form. Neither SolidWorks nor Fusion stores the solid apart from its faces, so their decoders state as `body` the solid that owns `fixed`. The old layout stores no per-bend radius and no rip list, and its counted list holds pairs of face references (inferred from the class tags), not bend edges; whether the pairs are bends is not known, so an old-layout record stays `Native("sldprt:convert_v1")` with its face pairs kept, and joining them to the body is a decoder task (part 11). Fusion's ConvertToSheetMetal is `ThinSolid` with a sheet-metal rule: its first pick is the face under its stored point, which is `fixed`; the thickness, bend radius, and reliefs are in a rule the conversion writes, named after the material with "(Convert)", which is `rule`; it stores no bend list, its bends being the solid's cylindrical walls; it stores no rip, so `rips` is empty; and its second pick, the face opposite the first at the thickness (inferred: its recipe is not joined to a face), is kept as the source setting `f3d:convert_second_face`, since `thickness` comes from the rule. A writer whose target has only the other construction writes `ThinSolid` as `Faces`, with the solid's cylindrical faces as `ConvertBend::Face` bends and `side: Inside` (the solid's faces are the sheet's), where its target can, and charges `export:feature.lowered` naming the feature otherwise; it writes `Faces` to a target that has only `ThinSolid` as the built walls, charging `export:feature.lowered` naming the feature. A writer whose target has no conversion takes step 3 (§3.4).
- `BreakCorner` breaks the picked `corners` of the sheet through its thickness, as `shape` states; each of `corners` is an edge of the sheet's thickness at a corner. `Round` rounds each with radius `size`, tangent to both edges that meet at the corner, its axis normal to the sheet. `Chamfer` cuts each at 45 degrees, both legs equal to `size`, the cut face normal to the sheet. NX's break corner (`SBSM_BRCORNER`) is so: its `SC_collector` reference is `corners` and the expression reference after its `00` byte is `size`. Its picks are thickness edges, and under Rule H1 a record whose picks are not one thickness edge per broken corner is `SheetMetalKind::Native("nx:break_corner")` with its picks kept. Which stored value says round against chamfer is not separated, and it is not bit 1 of the method byte. So under Rule H1 the decoder states `Round` where the stored faces are cylinders, and `CornerBreak::Native("nx:break_corner")` with the method byte kept otherwise. No stored file known to the project holds an NX chamfer break. SolidWorks' break corner (`moBreakCornerFeat_c`) is so: a record whose size is a radial dimension is `Round`, and a record whose size is a plain linear dimension is `Chamfer`. No round-or-chamfer flag is found in the record, and the dimension's display is the only carrier seen (part 11), so under Rule H1 the decoder states the shape only where the built faces agree, and `CornerBreak::Native("sldprt:break_corner")` with the record kept otherwise. Its corners are a face or edge selection whose picks are not read (part 11), so under Rule H1 the decoder states `BreakCorner` only where the picks resolve to one thickness edge per broken corner, and `SheetMetalKind::Native("sldprt:break_corner")` with the record kept otherwise. A Corner-Trim record that stores no break size is relief work and stays `SheetMetalKind::Native`. Inventor's Corner Round (class `b54dd6f6`) is `Round` with its decoded radius; its Corner Chamfer (class `8598cc98`) is `BreakCorner` with `shape: Chamfer`; where it stores its size is not located (typed, carrier unread; part 11), so the decoder reads `size` from the stored faces, both legs of each cut (the legs' equality inferred), under Rule H1 states it only where the two legs agree, and keeps the Corner Chamfer as `SheetMetalKind::Native` with its picks where the faces are not read or disagree. A writer whose target has no corner break takes step 3 (§3.4).
- `Unfold` flattens the bends of its `BendSet` about the fixed face; `Refold` folds them back (Creo unbend and bend back, Fusion unfold and refold). Which references of a Fusion unfold are its bends and which its stationary face, and which control selects all bends, are read on assumptions, so the Fusion decoder states `fixed` and a `Selected` `bends` with `Unread` picks, the stored references in `Selection.native`, and keeps the control as the native option `f3d:unfold_all_bends` (Rule N case (a), part 11). The factor it unfolds with is read on assumptions too, as the material-trailer scalar of the rule its settings record names, and no stored file sets that rule against the rule that governs the body, so the decoder keeps the factor as the native option `f3d:unfold_k_factor` (Rule N case (a), part 11). Which unfold a Fusion refold folds back is the native option `f3d:refold_group` (Rule N case (a), part 11). `FlatPattern` derives the flat state (Fusion flat pattern; Inventor's flat-pattern timeline starts with it, §5.2).
- `Hem` folds the sheet back over itself at each of `edges`, about an axis on the edge (`position` `AtEdge`, or `TangentToSide`), with the thickness of its `rule`. `length` runs parallel to the face from the fold's outer apex to the hem's free end. `Flat` and `Open` fold through 180° to an inner radius of half the `gap` and return parallel to the face at `gap`; an open hem's gap is its own, and a flat hem's the tight gap the source stores, where it stores one. `Teardrop` folds to an inner radius of `radius` beyond 180°, with a straight return tangent to the fold whose inner face ends `gap` from the face. `Rolled` is an arc of inner radius `radius` through `angle`, tangent to the face at the edge, with no straight part (Fusion hem; the teardrop and the rolled form are thin, part 11). `side` states which face of the sheet the hem folds over. A hem is made on the end face of a wall, the face across its thickness, and each of `edges` is one of that face's two long edges, which lies on one of the sheet's two faces: `SelectedEdgeFace` folds about the picked edge, back over the sheet face that holds it, and `OppositeFace` about the end face's other long edge, over the other sheet face; `None` does not state it, and a writer of another codec then charges a loss naming the feature. Fusion's flip byte is 0 `SelectedEdgeFace` and 1 `OppositeFace`. The picked edge is read from the Hem scope's edge recipe, which names the end face, the sheet face whose edge is picked, and the two faces that bound the edge. The picked edge decides which face the hem folds over, and the base wall's growth side does not (the reading is thin; part 11). The rope and double forms, which Fusion states in words with their values (Length, Gap, Radius; Gap, Length, Setback), are `HemForm::Native` with their values as native options: no stored file known to the project holds a rope or double hem (Rule N case (a), part 11). A writer whose target has no hem writes a flat or open hem as a flange of 180° whose inside radius is half the `gap` and whose free end lies `length` from the fold's outer apex, and a rolled hem as a flange of inside radius `radius` through `angle`, and charges a loss naming the feature for a teardrop.
- `ContourFlange` makes a sheet from an open planar profile: the profile, each vertex replaced by a bend, is extruded normal to its plane as `extent` states, and thickened as `thickness` states about it. A vertex's bend has the radius `bend.radius` on the side `bend.radius_side` states, or the `radius` on the side `radius_side` of the `VertexBend` that names that vertex where the flange's bends differ; a side stated `None` leaves the radius's side unstated, which no writer defaults (`Bend`'s `radius_side`, above). `extent` is a `Span<Length>` measured from the profile's plane along its normal, with the extrude's conventions (§6.3): `Between`'s `end` lies along the normal and its `start` against it, so a flange on the normal's side of the plane has `start: AtOrigin` and one on the other side `end: AtOrigin`, and `Symmetric` places the plane midway. Each end other than `AtOrigin` is a distance (`Amount`) or an end on an entity (`ToPoint`, `ToPlane`, `ToGeometry`; no stored file known to the project holds a flange that ends on a plane or a face). A writer must know the side, so a decoder states `extent` only where the record or the stored faces give it, and the flange is `SheetMetalKind::Native` with its source kind otherwise. A `Symmetric` thickness makes the profile the sheet's mid-surface trace, so with inner radius r and thickness t each turn θ shortens the straight portions beside it by r_m·tan(θ/2) and joins them by an arc of mid-surface radius r_m = r + t/2; a `OneSide` thickness puts the wall on the profile's `Left` or `Right`. FreeCAD's SheetMetal `SMBaseBend` with side `Middle` is a `Symmetric` thickness, its `radius` the bend's with `radius_side: Inside` and its `length` the extent's one distance. Its sides `Inside` and `Outside`, which put one face of the sheet on the profile, are `Thickness::Native("fcstd:Inside")` and `Native("fcstd:Outside")` until a stored file known to the project shows which face, and the sense of its extrusion is not read, so under Rule H1 the decoder states the extent only where the stored faces give its side, and `Native("fcstd:SMBaseBend")` otherwise (typed, carrier unread; part 11). Where `edges` is stated, the flange is attached to those edges of existing sheet metal: its profile starts at each edge, in a plane normal to it, and is extruded along the edge over the extent `width` states (`Full` the edge's length; `Centered` a width centred on its midpoint; `FromEnds` the part of the edge left `first` in from its start and `second` in from its end; `FromReference` `width` of the edge's line, starting `offset` from the point `from` and running in the edge's direction, or ending there and running against it where `reversed`, so that it may run past the edge's end), joined to the face that holds the edges by a bend of `bend.radius`; `extent` is then `None`, and where `width` is `None` (the source's width kept as a native option) a writer of another codec does not default the footprint (§2.4). Inventor's contour flange is so, from Autodesk's Contour Flange Property Panel Reference ("adding a sheet metal face defined by an open profile ... to an edge or edge loop"), and its record is type `b07438a0`. The panel names four width extents: Edge; Width, centred or started at an offset from a picked face or plane ("Offset: Enables a flange to start along the selected edge at a specified distance from a selected perpendicular face or plane"); Offset ("offsets from each end of the edge"); and Between ("the portion of the selected edge lying between the From and To inputs"). The extent is a record of its own, of one family with the flanges', each storing its footprint on the edge's line: `9ccfdb97` is `Full`, the footprint the width parameter long; `38298930` with no reference point is `Centered`, the footprint's midpoint the stored edge's; `38298930` with a point is `FromReference`, the footprint starting `offset` from the point and running `width` along the edge, or ending there where the page's Flip Direction flag is set, which is `reversed`; and `fe193a84` is `FromEnds`, its ends the stored edge's end points moved in by the two offsets, either of which may be zero. The stored reference is a point on the edge's line; the face or plane the user picked is not in the record, so a writer whose target needs that face or plane charges `export:feature.lowered` naming the flange (where the face is stored: part 11). Under Rule H1 the decoder states `FromReference` only where the stored footprint agrees with the rule, and the native option `inventor:contour_flange_extent` otherwise; a `38298930` record that holds a point and a width and no offset stays that native option. No stored file known to the project holds Between, which stays `inventor:contour_flange_extent` (Rule N case (a), part 11). Which side the record's direction enumeration (`69b9505e`, values 0 and 1) puts the sheet on is not read, so under Rule H1 the decoder states the extent only where the stored faces give its side, and `Native("inventor:contour_flange")` otherwise (typed, carrier unread; part 11). Fusion's contour flange (type `7AFA0A65`) is so with `edges: None`: its `AlongDistance` parameter is the extent's one distance, its magnitude bound through `Dimension::Negated` where its expression is negative; the length's sign is not a side until the profile sketch's plane is read, so under Rule H1 the decoder states the extent only where that plane is read and the stored faces lie on one side of it, and `Native("f3d:ContourFlange")` otherwise; the f64 word beside it, ±1, is not the extent's sign, and is kept as a source setting; its `BendRadius` parameter is `bend.radius` with `radius_side: Inside`, and a stored `BendRadius` of 0 makes the flange `SheetMetalKind::Native` with its kind and the radius as a native option, as for a `Flange` (Rule N case (a), part 11). Where the record stores no `BendRadius`, the decoder reads the linked rule's first entry as the inside bend radius on an assumption, so the flange states `bend.radius: None` and keeps that value as the native option `f3d:contour_flange_rule_radius` (Rule N case (a), part 11). The side of the profile its thickness takes is read from Fusion's API's documented SideOne default as the profile's left, on an assumption, so the Fusion decoder states no side (`side: None` where it states a `OneSide` thickness), which a writer of another codec does not default (§2.4; Rule N case (a), part 11). A symmetric extent's marker is two u32 words of 1 in the record's head where the one-sided records hold zeros (inferred), so under Rule H1 the decoder states `Span::Symmetric` with `amount` `AlongDistance` and `measure: Some(PerSide)`, so that the parameter's binding survives, only where the stored faces agree, and the native option `f3d:contour_flange_extent` otherwise. A record that stores an `AgainstDistance` beside `AlongDistance` is `Span::Between` with both distances, one to each side of the profile sketch's plane, under the same Rule H1 gate; which side `AlongDistance` takes is not separated (part 11). A record of a holder form that picks an entity of the base Face feature as its end, in a file that stores no B-rep, does not give which face bounds it, and stays `Native("f3d:ContourFlange")` (part 11). The record's own length is kept as a source setting. SolidWorks' open base flange is so with `edges: None`: its first child is `profile`, a base bend sits at each of the profile's vertices, and its depth `D2` is the extent: in the sketch's own frame the end caps lie `D2` apart. The extent and its side are stored in a block of the flange's tail before its own `D2`: a reverse flag, a one-direction flag, an end code (0 blind, 6 mid-plane), and the depth, equal to `D2`. No edge-flange, miter-flange, or other sheet-metal flange record holds the block. So the decoder states a blind block as `Between` with `D2` on the normal's side, or against it where the reverse flag is set; a mid-plane block as `Span::Symmetric` with `amount` `D2` and `measure: Some(Total)` (such blocks store `D2` alone); and a two-direction block as `Between` with `D2` and `D3`, never `Symmetric`, since equal depths are two stored depths. The flange's own end caps are scored in the frame of the `D2` dimension's stored points. Under Rule H1 the decoder states the extent where a scored cap of the flange's own agrees with the block, and `Native("sldprt:base_flange")` with the block kept where they disagree, where the flange keeps no cap of its own, where no witness scores its caps, and where the block is not read. On a two-direction body `D2` lies along the sketch's normal and `D3` against it. Where the bends' inner radius is one value per flange, that value is `bend.radius`; where it differs by vertex, each vertex whose radius differs from the flange's is a `VertexBend`. The base bend's own `D1` is the inner radius or the outer: it is the radius on the profile's side of the bend. Which face of the bend the profile lies on follows from the block's thickness flag (below) and the profile's turn at the vertex, the inner face where the wall lies on the side away from the turn (inferred). A separate clause (inferred) makes `D1` the inner radius where the profile has a sketched arc at the vertex though it lies on the outer face; a bend with the inner radius, the profile on the outer face, and no sketched arc is not explained. So the decoder always binds `D1`, the user's dimension, as `bend.radius` or as a `VertexBend`'s `radius`, and states its side (`bend.radius_side`, or the `VertexBend`'s `radius_side`) from the stored faces: where both cylinders of the bend are read and `D1` equals one of them, the side is that cylinder's, the faces showing the cylinders where they differ by the thickness. A bend whose `D1` equals the inner cylinder states `Inside`, one whose `D1` equals the outer states `Outside`, and a bend whose `D1` equals neither of its cylinders makes its flange `Native("sldprt:base_flange")`. The profile-side rule is what a SolidWorks writer uses to choose which radius to write as `D1`, and what a decoder applies only where the bend's cylinders are not read. Where the extent block and the profile's face family are not read, what is unread is the face the profile lies on, which the side does not need. The side of the profile the thickness takes varies, and a stored flag gives it: the u32 47 bytes before the extent block's marker, one word before the reverse flag, is 0 where the profile lies on one face family and 1 where it lies on the other; flag 0 puts the wall on the right of the contour run from the flange's first end face, seen from the tip of the sketch's normal, and 1 on its left. `side` keeps §6's definition, the `Left` or `Right` of the profile's chain in pick order from its first curve's own direction, so a decoder applies that relation only where it reads the profile's chain and its first curve's direction against the flange's first end face: the first stored profile endpoint lies on that face where that is unambiguous, and the SolidWorks decoder reads the sketch's points and drops its lines (part 11). So under Rule H1 the decoder states `thickness` `OneSide` with its side where the block is read, the stored faces give which side of the profile the wall lies on, and the profile's chain is read against the first end face, keeps the flag as the native option `sldprt:thickness_reverse` wherever the block is read, and states `side: None` elsewhere, which a writer of another codec does not default (§2.4). A writer whose target has no contour flange takes step 3 (§3.4).
- `ExtendWall` carries an existing wall on from `edge`, in the wall's own surface, until it meets the plane `to`. Creo's wall extension is so (`misc_choice[0]` 512, with no section and no dimension, instruction 4435 naming the edge and 4438 the plane): a face of the wall lies on the named plane (the reading is thin; part 11). A Creo wall (feature type 952) states its construction in the bits of `misc_choice[0]`, read against its sketch, its dimensions, and its surfaces. Bit 4 attaches the wall to the edge its instruction 10 names and bends it there, with a coaxial cylinder pair of radii R and R + T; an unattached wall's bends are its own contour's. Bits 2 and 8, never set together, mark a wall sketched as its side profile, where a wall with neither is sketched as an outline in its own plane: the sketch normal of a wall with either bit lies along the bend axis, and the sketch plane of a wall with neither holds the bend axis. Bit 8 states the profile's extent normal to its sketch, a dimension of type 62, and a bit-2 wall holds no such dimension. An attached wall without bit 2 states its bend angle (a dimension of type 205). Bit 128 gives the bend a relief (dimensions of types 9, 10, and 21 together, and instructions 4490 to 4493), whose shape the code of instruction 132 does not separate. So the Creo decoder states a wall with no bit as a `Wall`; an unattached bit-8 wall as a `ContourFlange` whose `profile` is its sketch and whose `extent` is `Between` with `start` the type-62 dimension and `end: AtOrigin`, since a bit-8 wall starts in its sketch plane at a datum point (instruction 4488) and runs its width on the side away from the sketch's normal; an unattached bit-2 wall as a `ContourFlange` whose `extent` is `Between` with `AtOrigin` at one end and at the other a `ToPoint` at the end of the edge instruction 4487 names away from the sketch plane, as `end` where that point lies along the sketch's normal and as `start` where it lies against it, since the wall's far end lies at that point (an end on an earlier feature's plane would fit too, but the stored reference is the edge); the edge is an earlier feature's and never the wall's own, and no stored dimension equals the extent, so under Rule H1 the decoder states it only where the edge resolves and the faces agree, and `Native("creo:wall")` otherwise (later features consume the edge and hide it, so the decoder resolves it from the stored hidden geometry, not the final body; part 11); an attached bit-2 wall as a `ContourFlange` on its attach edge with `width: Full`, as it holds no width dimension and its faces span its attach edge, so under Rule H1 the decoder states `width: Full` only where the stored faces agree, and `Native("creo:wall")` otherwise; and on either `bend.relief` with `ReliefShape::Native("creo:132:<code>")` where bit 128 is set (part 11). An attached wall with neither bit, sketched as an outline in its own plane, is a `Flange` on its attach edge with `outline` its sketch, `height_datum` the sharp the outline's free ends stand on, no `angle`, and `bend.radius` the inner radius of its bend pair. Its sweep has one home, the parameter's: the outline sketch's plane is `SketchPlane::Placed` with a `Construction<Frame>` through the attach edge (a `Coincident` input on the edge, which fixes the axis and its direction, the edge's stored one) at an angle to a plane through the edge (an `Angle` input on that plane, §5.9: the base wall's face where it holds the edge, else the earlier feature's coplanar plane through it, below), whose `ScalarDimension::Angle` binds the type-205 dimension. The stored sketch plane contains the attach edge and lies at the stored angle's magnitude to a plane through that edge: the base wall's own face, or, where the edge's own feature has no plane at that angle in the stored table, an earlier feature's coplanar plane that holds the edge, which the `Angle` input then names. The attach edge is the sharp on the sketch face's side: on the parent's inner face, which lies R from the bend axis, where the sketch plane is the wall's inner face, and on its outer face, which lies R + T from it, where the sketch plane is the outer face; the edge itself lies d/cos(φ/2) from the axis for that face's radius d and the bend's sweep φ (d√2 at 90 degrees). Otherwise the edge lies in the sketch plane and on the line through the outline's free ends, and the bend pair that would identify the sketch face does not fit. The stored value's sign is the sign of the right-hand turn about the edge's stored direction from the base face's normal, with the face's orientation applied, to the sketch's normal; where an earlier feature's coplanar plane holds the edge, its orientation does not give the sign, since coplanar faces of other features carry either orientation. At ±90 degrees both signs give one plane, so there the sign fixes only the sense of the sketch's normal; a +90 wall whose turn is negative is not explained (part 11). So the decoder binds the dimension directly where that turn is the construction's positive sense (§5.9) and through `Dimension::Negated` where it is the opposite; a writer to Creo re-emits the stored type-205 sign where the wall came from a Creo file (the binding, direct or `Negated`, carries it), and writes the sign from the turn by the same rule otherwise. Under Rule H1 the decoder states that construction only where the stored sketch plane holds the attach edge and lies at the dimension's angle to the base wall's face, and otherwise states the plane's solved position and keeps the dimension as the native option `creo:wall_angle`, which a writer of another format charges as `export:parameter.flattened` naming the wall, the wall's angle then driven by no parameter: so on walls that store no attach edge (their placement holds only instructions 1910 and 10), and on a wall whose edge's stored face coordinates fit two placements. A wall that stores no type-205 dimension states the plane's solved position. The outline is an open chain with two free ends and its sketch plane holds the bend axis; the free ends lie not on the bend's tangent line but on the sharp of the sketch face's side, the line where the sketch face meets the plane of the parent face on that side; the material runs from the sketch face across the thickness, which no stored flag states (the section's two flip fields are both 1); and the type-205 dimension is the angle between the walls. So under Rule H1 the decoder states `outline` only where the stored faces identify the sketch face and the free ends lie on its sharp, and `Native("creo:wall")` otherwise (the walls that miss, and those whose section, bend pair, or face is not read). The type-205 dimension being the angle between the walls, a Creo flange stated without an `outline` would take `angle` as 180° less its magnitude, under Rule H1; none is, since a wall the outline rule misses is `Native`. An attached bit-8 wall is a `ContourFlange` on the edge instruction 4487 names with `width: FromReference` from the instruction-4488 point at `offset` zero, its `width` the type-62 dimension, running against the sketch's normal (`reversed` where the edge's direction lies along it): it starts in its sketch plane at that point, a datum point made just before it, and runs its type-62 width against the sketch's normal along that edge, instruction 10 naming no edge, so under Rule H1 the decoder states it only where the 4487 edge resolves and the wall's span agrees, and `Native("creo:wall")` otherwise. The other walls are `SheetMetalKind::Native("creo:wall")` with their bits, sketch, and dimensions kept (Rule N case (a), part 11). Bit 32 (a wall with it states its outside radius, as some walls without it do) and bit 16 (unread) stay native options of the wall, as does the side its material lies on, which the sign of the bend angle does not follow; no bit marks a part's first wall.
- `ExtrudedHole` pierces the sheet along `bore` and forms the material around the hole into a flange normal to the sheet. `entry` is the face the punch enters, and the flange rises beyond the sheet's other face: its bore's wall lies on `bore`, a circle or a profile, its outer wall one thickness further out, its tip lies `height` from the entry face, the thickness included, and `root_fillet` rounds its root with that radius on the die side and that radius plus the thickness on the punch side, `None` leaving the root sharp (CATIA `CATSm_ExtrudedHolePunch`: the bore radius is half the stated diameter and the outer radius that plus the thickness, the tip lies at `Height` from the entry face, and `RadiusActivity` 1 gives a root torus of minor radii `Radius1` and `Radius1` plus the thickness, tangent to both cylinders and both sheet faces, where 2 leaves none). CATIA maps the hole's position and `MinorDiameter` (`DefinitionType` 3), or the length of `DefinitionType` 1, to a `Circle` bore, `Height` with `HeightType` 1 and `ConeOption` 1 to `height`, and `Radius1` to `root_fillet` where `RadiusActivity` is 1. A CATIA extruded hole with `ConeOption` 2 or another definition or height type is `Native("catia:CATSm_ExtrudedHolePunch")` with its values as native options (Rule N case (a), part 11). A CATIA flanged cutout (`CATSm_FlangedCutoutPunch`) is an `ExtrudedHole` whose bore is its sketch, a `Profile`: its flange's hole-side faces lie half the slot's width from the slot's axis, and its tip `Height` from the entry face, the thickness included (the reading is thin; part 11). Which stored field names `entry` is not read, so the CATIA decoder states `entry: None` (typed, carrier unread; part 11), and a writer of another codec then takes step 3 (§3.4).
- `Stamp` forms the sheet by a punch along the normal of `entry`, the face the punch enters, the result rising beyond the sheet's other face. Each form's outline is the sharp contour of the punch-side wall face on the entry face, before its bends round it: the bends are tangent fillets of that sharp shape, the rim bend, where the wall leaves the sheet, of radius `rim_radius` on the die-side face and `rim_radius` plus the thickness on the punch side, and the floor bend, where the wall meets the floor, of `floor_radius` on the punch side and that plus the thickness on the die side, even where the two fillets meet and leave no straight wall. A form holds the radii of the bends it has: `Raised` and `Bridge` both, `Louver` the rim bend's, and `Bead`, whose section is one arc, neither; `None` takes the governing default. `Raised` offsets a floor from the entry face by `height`, measured from the entry face to the floor's face on the same side, inside walls at `wall_angle` to the sheet plane. `Bridge` raises a strip `width` wide, its plateau `height` above the sheet on two legs at `wall_angle`, `length` the strip's base length on the entry face between the legs' sharp contours, its sides cut free of the sheet by slots as wide as the sheet is thick, each running `relief_length` straight past the lower bend's tangent line and ending in a half-round; `placement` puts the strip's centre on the entry face and its length along the frame's x. `Louver` cuts the sheet along `open_edge`, a line of `profile`, and presses the flap the profile bounds to `depth` below the entry face at that edge, tilted at `flap_angle` to the sheet, between side walls at `wall_angle`. `Bead` raises a crown along `path`, an open sketch curve: its section on the entry face's side is an arc of radius `section_radius` whose rise above the entry face is `height`, the other face's arc has `section_radius` plus the thickness on the same centre, and its ends are spheres of `end_radius` and `end_radius` plus the thickness. `StiffeningRib` presses a groove across one bend from its outer side, `bend` picking the bend's face and `at` a point whose position along the bend's axis places the rib, and only that axial position counts: the rib is symmetric about its mid-plane, the plane through that point normal to the bend's axis, and its groove runs square to the bisector of the two flanges wherever the point lies around the axis; the point need not lie on the bend face. The groove's bottom is a cylinder of radius `bottom_radius` whose axis runs across the bend; `length` is the chord, in the mid-plane, between the two flanges' outer faces along the groove's bottom, square to the bisector of the two flanges, and the bottom's axis lies `bottom_radius` from that chord on the outer corner's side. Its side walls stand at `wall_angle` against the sheet, and its rims are fillets of `rim_radius` on the inner-face side and `rim_radius` plus the thickness on the outer. CATIA maps `CATSm_NewSurfacePunch` to `Raised` with its sketch as a `Profile` outline, `Height`, and `Angle`, the container's `Radius1` as `rim_radius` and `Radius2` as `floor_radius`; `CATSm_PointPunch` to `Raised` with a `Circle` outline of diameter `LENGTH`; `CATSm_BridgePunch` to `Bridge`, its radii as the surface stamp's (whether a relief slot's width or its end is a parameter of its own is not separated, part 11); `CATSm_LouverPunch` to `Louver`, `LouverAngle1` the flap's angle and `LouverAngle2` the walls', its `Radius1` the rim bend's radius and its `Radius2` a native option until a stored file ties it to a bend; and `CATSm_BeadPunch` to `Bead`, its `SectionRadius`, `EndRadius`, and `Height`; and `CATSm_StiffeningRibPunch` to `StiffeningRib`, its face reference `FeatureFSUR` the `bend`, the origin of its own `Axis1` `at`, and `Length`, `ANGLE`, `Radius2`, and the container's `Radius1` its `length`, `wall_angle`, `bottom_radius`, and `rim_radius`. The point is the origin of the rib record's own `Axis1` (`OX`, `OY`, `OZ`), not a field of the point-on-surface record its tangent plane names; it lies in the plane tangent to the bend at the picked point, and the stored direction is the bend's inward normal there and orients nothing. So the decoder states `at` from the `Axis1` origin and checks it against the symmetry plane of the rib's own faces where they decode, matching the rib to the bend whose faces it interrupts (the nearest bend axis can give a false tilt). The stored point may be the picked point moved along the axis, and around it too, which the rib's positioning sketch would explain (inferred; the sketch is not read), so whether `at` binds a sketch point there is a decoder's reading (part 11). A suffix value the CATIA decoder would report as unset (`e7`) stores 1, and its neighbour `e8` stores 0 (a codec reading), so every rib record with a container stores both radii. `Length` is the chord between the flanges' outer faces along the groove's bottom; it does not run between vertices, and the chord lies along the generator deeper behind the outer faces. The groove runs square to the bisector of the two flanges, and the bottom's axis lies `Radius2` from the chord on the outer corner's side. The groove's bottom has radius `Radius2`; the walls stand at the stored angle; and `Radius1` rounds the rims at `Radius1` and `Radius1` plus the thickness. An older-form rib that stores `Radius1` 1 builds sharp rims, which `rim_radius` cannot state, and whether the form or the value makes them sharp is not separated (part 11). So the whole rib is under Rule H1: the decoder states `StiffeningRib` only where the stored faces agree with every field, and `Native("catia:CATSm_StiffeningRibPunch")` with its parameters kept otherwise (sharp-rimmed ribs, a rib whose container record the reader misparses, and a rib whose faces' symmetry plane misses `at`). `IntersectRadius` is a source setting of the rib, `catia:intersect_radius`: where it differs from `Radius1` the rims follow `Radius1`. A stamp radius stored as `e7` is 1 by the same codec reading, and builds a round of that radius on the concave side. The louver, the bead, and the bridge's reliefs are thin (part 11). Which stored field names `entry`, the record that places a bridge, and the record that names a bead's path are not read, so the CATIA decoder states `entry` and `placement` `None` and the bead's sketch as its `path` (typed, carrier unread; part 11), and a writer of another codec takes step 3 (§3.4) where `entry` is `None`. A writer whose target has no such stamp takes step 3.
- `ToolForm` forms the sheet over a tool body: `tool` names the tool's definition, `placement` places it in the part, and `constraints` define that placement, each a joint between a face of the part and a face of the tool, which it picks through a `Definition` context that names `tool` (§5.8, §6.7). The tool's surfaces, carried by the placement, become the sheet's driving side, and its other side lies one thickness away along the tool face's outward normal, so the sheet lies outside the tool's material (Creo form, feature type 956, which places a tool part by the assembly constraint codes of §6.7 and merges a copy of its surfaces; each copied surface keeps its kind and radius, and the placed tool planes are parallel to their copies). The map from tool ids to the copies' ids stays in the native record, as a `Linked` copy's does (§5.10). Which of the tool's surfaces the result keeps, and what Creo's form kind (`misc_choice[0]` 0, 1, or 2) and its other references (instructions 55, 4111, 4499, 4262, 118, and 180) make the result do, are not read: kind 0 copies every tool surface and kinds 1 and 2 a subset by a rule not read, so they are native options of the feature (`creo:form_kind`, `creo:<code>`; Rule N case (a), part 11), and a writer of another codec charges a loss naming the feature where they are present. A writer whose target has no form tool takes step 3 (§3.4).
- An Inventor corner record (class `7f588068`) is no sheet-metal kind: it is its flange's container of corner treatments, sharing the plate's operands and the flange's result collection, and its item list is empty, it makes no face, and no face's name cites it. The Inventor decoder emits no feature and no native option for it and reads the corner treatment from the flange that owns it. A record whose list is not empty is `Native("inventor:Corner")` (no stored file known to the project holds one; part 11).
- Every other sheet-metal kind is `Native` with the source kind name: no stored file known to the project settles its stored operands and the shape it makes (Rule N case (a), part 11): a contour flange of another format, lofted flange, corner seam and relief, the stamps and punches other than the extruded hole, the stamps, and the tool form (the CATIA curve stamp, dowel, and multi-corner relief), Creo's feature code 1062, the Creo walls and the rips named above, and the SolidWorks conversion of the old layout. A corner round or chamfer of sheet-metal edges is a fillet or chamfer, except a break-corner record of NX, SolidWorks, or Inventor, which is a `BreakCorner` where its rule above holds and `SheetMetalKind::Native` otherwise.
- A Creo sheet-metal cut (instruction 955, in the extrude form or the thin form) is an `Extrude` with a `Cut` Boolean, its thin form `body: Some(Thin(..))`; `sheet_cut` states the faces of the wall that its side faces are normal to, the cut being made as if the part were flat: `Defining`, the face the wall is built from (Creo's driving surface), `Opposite`, the other face (its offset surface), or `Both`, a cut through the thickness in the flat state, possible only where the cut region can be unbent and bent back (PTC About Sheet Metal Cuts). Which value of code 5039 (2.0 or 3.0) is which is typed, carrier unread (part 11): on a flat wall every value cuts the same faces, so only cuts whose side faces cross a bend can separate them, by edge geometry the decoder does not read; until it is read the decoder keeps it as the native option `creo:smt_cut_normal`. A writer whose target has no such choice charges a loss naming the feature.
- CATIA healing is a `Knit` with `healing`; SolidWorks, CATIA, and Fusion untrim is an `Extend` to `Natural`; CATIA sew surface is a `Graft` (§6.5); and CATIA combine, parallel, and smooth curves are `Combined`, `Offset`, and `Smoothed` curve features, and a CATIA corner a `Corner` (above). NX untrim, and an NX unsew that selects faces, are `Native` operations (Rule N case (a), part 11): no stored file known to the project holds an NX untrim or an NX unsew that selects faces. Fusion's surface untrim chooses the trim loops it removes, and `edges` reaches the edges of those loops: all loops are an `Of { kind: Edge }` term seeded by the picked faces (§5.8), and the exterior loop, the interior loops, or picked loops are the edges of those loops. Its exterior-boundary extension, a length that applies where the exterior boundary is removed, has no typed field: what it is measured from and along, and what a negative value does, are not established, so it is the native option `f3d:untrim_extension` (Rule N case (a), part 11). CATIA stores the federation as `ElementsToFederate`, a face reference record that names the seed, and `FederationPropagation`, which names the mode: 4 on joins that name a seed and 1 or the default on those that name none. Which code is which mode is not read, so the decoder states `federation: None` and keeps both fields as native options (typed, carrier unread; part 11).

#### Meshes

A mesh operation edits mesh bodies: the `Definition` tessellations that a mesh import contributes (§5.10) and that earlier mesh operations make.

```rust
pub struct MeshFeature { pub source: SetSelection, pub kind: MeshKind, pub native_options: NativeOptions, pub source_settings: NativeOptions }
pub enum MeshKind {
    Section { sketch: SketchId },
    PlaneCut { plane: Option<Construction<Plane>>, cut: Option<MeshCut>, fill: Option<MeshFill> },
    Reduce { target: Option<ReduceTarget> },
    Repair,
    Remesh { edge_length: Option<Dimension<PositiveLength>>, shape: Option<Dimension<Fraction>> },
    Smooth { smoothness: Option<Dimension<Fraction>> },
    Combine { tools: OrderedSelection, op: Option<BooleanOp> },
    Remove,
    ReverseNormals,
    Convert { method: Option<MeshConversion> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum MeshCut { Trim { flip: Option<bool> }, SplitBodies }
pub enum MeshFill { Open, Minimal }
pub enum ReduceTarget { Deviation(Dimension<NonNegativeLength>), Proportion(Dimension<Fraction>), FaceCount(Dimension<u32>) }
pub enum MeshConversion { Faceted, Native(NonBlankString) }
```

- `source` selects the mesh bodies the operation takes, in the state before the feature, and `kind` states what it does to each. A mesh operation is not a B-rep operation with a mesh operand: `Combine`, `Split`, `TransformBodies`, and the other operations of §6.4 and §6.5 take bodies, and a mesh body is a tessellation, not a body (§5.6, §8).
- **Operands.** No pick target names a mesh body or a face group of one (part 11). So every pick of a mesh operation is a `Native` pick, its native name the source's reference to the mesh body, and the meshes before and after the operation are the tessellations the source stores, each stating its state (§8). A mesh operation whose kind is read and whose operand records are not is `Mesh` with that kind and an `Unread` `source`; one whose kind is not read is `Unresolved { family: Mesh }`.
- **Results.** A mesh operation's result is the source's own construction where no rule below states it (a reduced, remeshed, smoothed, or repaired mesh, and the B-rep a conversion builds), which the source stores after the feature (K2). A body it stores is the evaluation's (§5.4). A mesh it stores is a `Definition` tessellation whose `state` is `None` where the current geometry holds it and the evaluation after the feature where it does not (§8).
- **Modes.** A selector that chooses among a source's algorithms is typed only where the format document or the vendor's text lets a reader construct the result of the arm it selects (Rule N, §3.1): `MeshCut`, `MeshFill`, and `MeshConversion::Faceted` are so, and every other mode below is native (Rule N case (a), part 11).
- `Section` puts the curves where the mesh bodies meet a plane into the sketch `sketch`; it changes no body, so it is stateless (§5.4). The curves are that sketch's entities where the decoder reads them (part 11). Fusion's section record stores no plane, and that the plane is the sketch's is not established, so the section states no plane (Rule N case (a), part 11).
- `PlaneCut` cuts each mesh body with `plane`. `Trim` keeps the piece on the side the plane's oriented normal points to, or the other piece where `flip` is true; `SplitBodies` keeps both pieces, each a mesh body of its own. `fill` states how a kept piece is closed at the cut: `Open` leaves the cut open, and `Minimal` closes it with the fewest triangles that cover, in the plane, the region the cut bounds: triangles between the cut's own vertices, every choice of which gives the same surface, so which the source takes is its own. Fusion stores the cut as a selector, 0 `Trim` and 1 `SplitBodies`, the fill as a selector, 0 `Open` and 1 `Minimal`, and the plane as sixteen matrix components. The convention, unit, and frame of the components, and which control byte states the kept side, are not read, so the Fusion decoder states `plane: None` and `flip: None` and keeps them as the native options `f3d:plane_cut_matrix` and `f3d:plane_cut_side` (typed, carrier unread; part 11). Its other cut and fill selectors are native options with `cut` or `fill` `None` (Rule N case (a), part 11).
- `Reduce` lowers each mesh body's triangle count to `target`: `Deviation`, the largest distance of the result from the source mesh; `Proportion`, the fraction of the source's triangles the result keeps; `FaceCount`, the result's triangle count. Each names the quantity that bounds the result, which a reader measures on any result, and selects no algorithm. Fusion stores the target as a selector, 0 `Deviation`, 1 `Proportion` from a percentage, and 2 `FaceCount`. Its distribution selector, which Fusion calls adaptive (0) and uniform (1), names an algorithm whose result no text constructs, so it is the native option `f3d:mesh_distribution` (Rule N case (a), part 11).
- `Repair` repairs each mesh body. Fusion stores its method as a selector whose values the format names closing holes (0), stitching and removing (1), and rebuilding with a density and an offset (3), and a rebuild selector whose values Fusion calls fast (0) and accurate (2). No text constructs what any of them builds, so the method, the rebuild selector, the density, and the offset are the native options `f3d:mesh_repair_method`, `f3d:mesh_rebuild_mode`, `f3d:mesh_rebuild_density`, and `f3d:mesh_rebuild_offset` (Rule N case (a), part 11).
- `Remesh` makes a new triangulation of each mesh body, with `edge_length` the source's edge length and `shape` its shape preservation, a fraction from 0 to 1; its distribution is the native option `f3d:mesh_distribution`, as for `Reduce`, and a uniform distribution stores no shape preservation. `Smooth` smooths each mesh body by `smoothness`, a fraction from 0 to 1.
- `Combine` combines the mesh bodies of `source`, the targets, with those of `tools`, in source order, by `op`: `Join`, `Cut`, or `Intersect`. Fusion stores the operation of a version-2 record as 0 `Join`, 1 `Cut`, and 2 `Intersect`. A version-1 record's selector, selector 3, and the fields that state which tool bodies the result keeps and which component it goes into are native options, with `op: None` where the selector is not one of the three (Rule N case (a), part 11).
- `Remove` removes the mesh bodies `source` selects from the state. `ReverseNormals` reverses the orientation of each mesh body `source` selects: every triangle's winding and every normal, so that its outward side becomes its inward side.
- `Convert` makes a B-rep body of each mesh body `source` selects by `method`. `Faceted` makes each facet of the mesh a planar face of the body. Fusion stores the method as 3 `Faceted`; its 1, which Fusion calls prismatic, names an algorithm whose result no text constructs, so it and any other value are `MeshConversion::Native("f3d:mesh_convert_method")` with the value as that native option (Rule N case (a), part 11).
- `Native` keeps a mesh operation whose meaning or operands are not established (Rule N case (a), part 11): Fusion's face-group generation and combination (`Native("f3d:GenerateFaceGroups")`, `Native("f3d:CombineFaceGroups")`), its separate (`Native("f3d:MeshSeparate")`), and its mesh shell (`Native("f3d:MeshShell")`), with their values as native options.
- A writer whose target has no mesh operation of the kind charges a loss naming the feature, and writes the stored mesh after the feature as a mesh import where the document names that mesh (Results, above).

### 6.7 Assembly operations

An assembly operation is a feature of the scope that holds an assembly's design (§5.1): the scope of the assembly definition, or a Fusion root scope with `Feature.component` naming the component. It may name an occurrence owned by any definition its scope spans (§5.1). Six operations place, connect, group, repeat, and mirror occurrences: `Place`, `PlaceSet`, `Joint`, `RigidGroup`, `ComponentPattern`, and `MirrorComponents`. An assembly feature, a feature of that scope whose definition states `assembly` (§5.10), changes bodies of the occurrences it names, its participants (Assembly features, below). A feature of that scope that changes only bodies the assembly's own definition owns states no `assembly`, also where an operand picks an occurrence's geometry. A component whose content is a copy of another definition's geometry is a stored-geometry feature with a link (§5.10, Derived, inserted, and linked components, below).

#### Placement

```rust
pub struct Place {
    pub occurrence: OccurrenceId,
    pub placement: Option<Construction<Frame>>,
    pub scale: Option<ScaleFactors>,
    pub base: Option<PlacementBase>,
    pub constraints: Vec<Joint>,
    pub packaged: Option<bool>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub enum PlacementBase { Parent, OwnOccurrence }
pub struct PlaceSet { pub occurrences: Vec<OccurrenceId>, pub native_options: NativeOptions, pub source_settings: NativeOptions }
```

- A `Place` feature exists where the source orders a component's placement with its features (§8.1): a Creo component feature (its placements interleave with datums and cuts), a Fusion new component, Component Insert, CopyPaste, CutPaste, or DerivedInstance item. A Fusion body feature made with New Component is that new-component item directly followed by the feature, a member of the new component's design whose `Boolean` is `NewBody`. A FreeCAD `App::Link` is a document object, and decodes as a `Place` feature in its group (§5.2). The feature names an occurrence, which is a member of the `occurrences` of a definition the scope spans (§8.1): in Fusion, the component the occurrence is inserted into.
- **FreeCAD links.** An object that an `App::Link` of its own document places (a PartDesign Body, `Link.LinkedObject`) is a product definition of kind `Object` (§8.1), stored `Embedded`. It owns the object's result bodies, in the object's local frame and with no `Body.transform`, and has no scope of its own: the document's scope spans it, and the object's features name it as their `component` (§5.1). The object's own appearance in the document is an occurrence of that definition at the object's `Placement`, which no feature creates: for a PartDesign Body, the container's `placement` defines it (§5.2), and its `resolved` is the cache of that occurrence's `transform` (D56). A link whose `LinkTransform` is false is an occurrence at the link's `Placement`, which `Place.placement` defines. A link whose `LinkTransform` is true is an occurrence at the link's `Placement` composed after the object's own placement, `base: Some(OwnOccurrence)` (below), so an edit of the object's placement moves it: in FreeCAD 1.1.4 a true link follows such an edit and a false one does not. A document selection that reaches the object's result, a process pick with `workpiece: None` included, picks it with context `Occurrence([its own occurrence])`, and its witness is in the document frame. A workpiece that selects the object picks it with context `Definition(object)`, and its `placement` replaces that occurrence's transform (§7.1); a pick of the object's entities in a `WorkpieceSelection` of that workpiece carries the same context, and its witness is in the object's frame.
- `PlaceSet` places several occurrences in one feature, each as a `Place` with no `placement`, `base`, or `constraints` would place it: a Fusion Component Insert or DerivedInstance item that inserts more than one occurrence. `occurrences` lists them in source order, each once; each is a member of the `occurrences` of a definition the scope spans, and `Occurrence.transform` holds its placement. Where the decoder does not join a Fusion insert's relations to occurrences, the feature is `Unresolved { family: Place }`, or `Unresolved { family: PlaceSet }` where the placement count it stores is read and is above one, and a `PlaceSet` whose members are partly joined lists the members it joins, one or more, and keeps the members it does not join as the native option `f3d:insert_members` (typed, carrier unread; part 11). A writer whose target places one occurrence per feature writes one `Place` per occurrence, in order, and charges nothing: the placements and the existence are the same.
- **Existence.** An occurrence that a design feature creates (a `Place`, a `PlaceSet`, a `Combine` whose `new_component` names it, a component pattern, a component mirror) exists in a state exactly when the creating feature is at or before the state's position (§5.3); a creating feature in an unordered container, which has no order (a FreeCAD `App::Link`), gives its occurrence existence in every state of its definition. This is derived from the feature's position and stored nowhere: no delta states it. An occurrence that a `Place` or a `PlaceSet` names takes its existence from the first of them in §5.3's order that names it, its creating feature; a later `Place` that names it (a Fusion cut-and-paste) changes its owner and creates nothing. One that a `Combine`'s `new_component` names takes its existence from that combine, and it is before every `Place` or `PlaceSet` that names it (§5.3). One named only by a component pattern or mirror takes its existence from that feature. An occurrence no feature creates exists in every state of its definition. An occurrence has at most one creating feature.
- `placement` defines the occurrence's base placement where the source stores a placement that can be bound (the `Placement` of a FreeCAD `App::Link`, or its copy `LinkPlacement`, whose components expressions bind), as a construction whose steps can be bound (§5.9). `base` states what it is relative to: `Parent`, the occurrence's placement in its parent's frame; `OwnOccurrence`, a placement composed after the transform of the placed definition's own occurrence in the scope (a FreeCAD object's own appearance, above), so the occurrence's base placement is `placement` · that transform and follows an edit of it. FreeCAD `LinkTransform` false is `Parent` and true `OwnOccurrence`, `placement` being the link's `Placement` in both, and a FreeCAD writer writes `LinkTransform` from `base`; every other decoder states `Parent`. A writer whose target has no such placement writes the composition as a plain placement and charges a loss naming the feature. `Occurrence.transform` holds the value (§8.1). Under `Parent` it is the construction's `resolved` composed with `scale` (below), and under `OwnOccurrence` that product composed with the own occurrence's transform. `resolved` is a cache (K2), checked against `Occurrence.transform` through that composition (D56). `None`, with `base: None`, where the source stores no such placement; the value is then `Occurrence.transform` alone. `Feature.placement` is `None` on a `Place` (§5.10).
- `scale` defines the scale the source composes with `placement` on the occurrence, applied in the placed definition's own axes before `placement` (FreeCAD `Link.Scale`, and `ScaleVector`, which is authoritative where it is not uniform), with factors an expression can bind. A `PerAxis` scale states no `frame`: its axes are the placed definition's own. The occurrence's base placement is then `placement` · `scale` (under `OwnOccurrence`, `placement` · `scale` · the own occurrence's transform), and `Occurrence.transform` holds its value (D56). `scale` is stated only with a `placement`, and only on an occurrence whose placement is that product: an element of a FreeCAD link array, whose placement composes the link's placement and scale with the element's own, states its map in `Occurrence.transform` alone. A source whose instance scale no expression can bind (Creo View, STEP, IGES, USD, Rhino) states it only in `Occurrence.transform`. `None` where the source stores no scale, or a scale of one on every axis; a stored factor of zero is no `scale` either, and the occurrence's map is then singular (part 10).
- `constraints` are the constraints the source stores inside the component's own record (Creo `place_instruction_ptrs`). A constraint the source lists as its own entry is a `Joint` feature. Each placement constraint has at least one connector that picks into the placed occurrence.
- `packaged` states an occurrence that the source positions by transform alone and leaves free to move (Creo `placed_flag` 0).
- `Occurrence.transform` is the occurrence's base placement (§8.1), the placement the source stores on the occurrence: for Fusion, the occurrence record's matrix, which is its current pose. Its current placement is its resolution through the configuration that applies to it (§4, §5.11), and then the current state's pose for its instance path (§5.5). Where a later feature moves the occurrence (a Fusion Move of components, §6.5; a joint), each state in which an instance's placement differs from that resolution states it by path: `delta.poses` in an evaluation (§5.4), `CurrentState.poses` in the current state (§5.5).
- The Fusion item kind (new component, insert, copy, cut-and-paste) is the source setting `f3d:item_kind`: the occurrence's prototype and the feature's place among the `Place` features that name it state what the item did, and the kind records how the user made it, which no edit of the design reads again (Rule N case (b)). A cut-and-paste is a `Place` that names an occurrence an earlier `Place` created (Existence, above), and changes the occurrence's owner. A Fusion copy or cut-and-paste whose occurrence the decoder does not read is `FeatureOperation::Native` with its kind and its fields as native options (typed, carrier unread; part 11). A Fusion capture position, which records occurrence poses as rows of an occurrence selector and a matrix, is `FeatureOperation::Native` of kind `f3d:Position` with its rows as native options, repeated targets kept as separate rows: whether a matrix is the occurrence's pose in its assembly context is not established (Rule N case (a), part 11). The definition that owns the occurrence in the current state lists it, and every other state whose owner differs states it in `delta.members` (§5.4): the states before the feature when the current state is after it, the states after it when the current state is rolled back before it.

#### Joints

```rust
pub struct Joint {
    pub connectors: [JointConnector; 2],
    pub kind: JointKind,
    pub alignment: Option<Alignment>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub enum JointConnector {
    Frame(Construction<Frame>),
    Plane(Construction<Plane>),
    Axis(Construction<Axis>),
    Point(Construction<Point>),
    Entity(OrderedSelection),
}
pub enum Alignment { Aligned, Opposed, Nearest, Native(NonBlankString) }

pub enum JointKind {
    Motion { motion: JointMotion, axes: Option<Construction<Frame>>, offset: JointOffset, limits: Vec<AxisLimits>, drives: Vec<JointDrive> },
    Coincident { offset: Option<Dimension<Length>> },
    Concentric,
    Insert { offset: Option<Dimension<Length>> },
    Distance { distance: Option<Dimension<Length>>, limits: Option<Bounds<Length>> },
    Angle { angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>>, limits: Option<Bounds<Angle>> },
    Parallel,
    Perpendicular,
    Tangent { contact: Option<TangentContact> },
    PointOnAxis { distance: Option<Dimension<Length>> },
    Symmetric { plane: Construction<Plane> },
    Width { pair: Box<[JointConnector; 2]>, mode: Option<WidthMode> },
    Slot { position: Option<SlotPosition>, lock_rotation: Option<Dimension<bool>> },
    Path { position: Option<PathPosition>, pitch_yaw: Option<PathAxisControl>, roll: Option<PathRollControl> },
    Coupling { coupling: Coupling, joints: Option<OrderedSelection> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum JointMotion {
    Rigid,
    Revolute    { axis: FrameAxis },
    Slider      { axis: FrameAxis },
    Cylindrical { axis: FrameAxis },
    Planar      { axis: FrameAxis },
    Ball,
    PinSlot     { axis: FrameAxis, slide: FrameAxis },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub struct JointOffset {
    pub x: Option<Dimension<Length>>,
    pub y: Option<Dimension<Length>>,
    pub z: Option<Dimension<Length>>,
    pub angle: Option<Dimension<Angle>>,
}
pub enum AxisLimits {
    Rotation    { axis: FrameAxis, limits: Option<Bounds<Angle>>, rest: Option<Dimension<Angle>> },
    Translation { axis: FrameAxis, limits: Option<Bounds<Length>>, rest: Option<Dimension<Length>> },
}
pub struct Bounds<Q> { pub min: Option<Dimension<Q>>, pub max: Option<Dimension<Q>> }
pub enum Coupling {
    Gear       { ratio: Option<Dimension<FiniteReal>>, radii: [Option<Dimension<Length>>; 2] },
    Belt       { ratio: Option<Dimension<FiniteReal>>, radii: [Option<Dimension<Length>>; 2] },
    RackPinion { ratio: Option<Dimension<FiniteReal>>, pitch_radius: Option<Dimension<Length>> },
    Screw      { pitch: Option<Dimension<Length>> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub struct JointDrive {
    pub axis: DriveAxis,
    pub mode: DriveMode,
    pub target_position: Option<FiniteReal>,
    pub target_velocity: Option<FiniteReal>,
    pub stiffness: Option<NonNegativeReal>,
    pub damping: Option<NonNegativeReal>,
    pub max_force: Option<PositiveReal>,
}
pub enum DriveAxis { Rotation { axis: FrameAxis }, Translation { axis: FrameAxis } }
pub enum DriveMode { Force, Acceleration }
pub enum TangentContact { Outside, Inside }
pub enum WidthMode { Centered, Free, Gap { distance: Dimension<NonNegativeLength>, from: Option<PairElement> }, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum SlotPosition { Free, Centered, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum PathPosition {
    Free,
    Distance { distance: Dimension<NonNegativeLength>, from_end: Option<Dimension<bool>> },
    Percent  { fraction: Dimension<Fraction>, from_end: Option<Dimension<bool>> },
}
pub enum PathAxisControl { Free, FollowPath { axis: FrameAxis, flip: Option<Dimension<bool>> } }
pub enum PathRollControl { Free, UpVector { vector: Construction<Direction>, axis: FrameAxis, flip: Option<Dimension<bool>> } }
```

`FrameAxis` is §5.9's. A `JointDrive` is a motor or spring on one degree of freedom of a `Motion` joint, a rotation about or a translation along an axis of the first connector's frame. Its output is `stiffness · (target_position − position) + damping · (target_velocity − velocity)`, limited to `max_force` (unlimited where `None`), with positions in radians or millimetres, velocities per second, and every coefficient in §2.3's canonical units; `Force` applies it as a force or a torque, `Acceleration` as an acceleration independent of the bodies' masses. `TangentContact` states whether a `Tangent` joint's elements touch from outside or from inside.

A joint is a design feature: a SolidWorks mate, an Inventor, CATIA, or NX constraint, a FreeCAD joint, a Fusion joint, a USD physics joint, a STEP kinematic pair. It relates two connectors. A model record that references a joint (a physics solver setting) names the joint feature's `FeatureId` (D30) and follows §2.1: the reference is absent when `design` is out of scope.

- **Connectors.** A connector is a construction (§5.9) of the element the joint relates: a frame, a plane, an axis, or a point. `Entity` relates the picked entity itself: a face whose surface the relation uses (`Tangent`), the faces a rigid or native mate fixes (SolidWorks lock, in-place, and slot mates), or a pick whose geometric kind the decoder cannot read (a Creo surface id, a CATIA geometry label). The inputs select geometry through occurrence contexts (§5.8): face F of instance I is `Picked { target: Entity(F), context: Some(Occurrence(path to I)) }`. A connector on a whole occurrence picks `Component`. A connector on a Fusion joint origin picks that `Frame` datum (§6.2). A connector on the world is a construction with no inputs: its frame is the frame of the joint's own definition moved by its `after` steps (a USD joint whose body is unset, whose local frame is relative to the world). With no steps, its `resolved` value is its definition (§5.9); with steps, `resolved`, where stated, is the frame they give, a cache (K2).
- **Frames.** A connector's `resolved` value is in the coordinates of the definition its picks resolve in: the prototype at the end of the context path, or the joint's own definition. Its assembly placement is that value under the path's composed placement. The construction's `after` steps are the source's connector offset (FreeCAD `Offset1`/`Offset2`, a USD local frame relative to its body). A motion kind that names an axis holds `axis`, the axis of the first connector's frame about or along which it moves (a Fusion revolute about the joint origin's X, Y, or Z axis); a format that always uses z states `Z`. Where the motion's axis is no axis of that frame, `axes` is the frame whose axes the motion, its limits, and its drives name: a Fusion joint whose direction is custom, "defined by an entity" (API `JointDirections.CustomJointDirection`, and for a revolute `customRotationAxisEntity`, a linear edge, sketch line, planar face, or cylindrical face), has a frame whose z axis lies on that entity's line, and its motion names `Z`.
- **Kinds.** `Motion` states the degrees of freedom the joint leaves (Fusion, Inventor, FreeCAD, USD joints): `Rigid` none, `Revolute` rotation about `axis`, `Slider` translation along `axis`, `Cylindrical` both, `Planar` translation in the plane normal to `axis` and rotation about it, `Ball` rotation about the origin, `PinSlot` rotation about `axis` and translation along `slide`, another axis of the same frame (Fusion pin-slot). `Rigid` fixes the current relative placement of the two connectors and needs no frame, so its connectors may be any variant: SolidWorks lock and in-place mates pick faces or geometry labels as `Entity` connectors. A writer whose target requires joint origins for a rigid joint uses the occurrences' origins. `Slot` puts a pin in a slot: the axis of the second element (a cylindrical face or an axis) stays on the slot's centre path between the first element's side faces, free to slide along it and to turn about itself, as `PinSlot` leaves the same two freedoms (SolidWorks slot mate). Its connectors are `Entity` picks of the slot faces and the pin, because the source stores no frame and a decoder does not invent one. `position` states where the pin lies along the slot: `Free` anywhere, `Centered` at the middle of the slot's centre path; a SolidWorks position at a distance or a percent of the slot's length from an end is `SlotPosition::Native` with its value as the native option `sldprt:slot_position`, since no stored file known to the project settles whether the end is the end arc's centre or its tangent end (Rule N case (a), part 11). `lock_rotation` stops the pin turning (SolidWorks slot mate, `swSlotMateConstraintOptions_e` and Lock Rotation). Every other `Motion` kind leaves a degree of freedom and relates `Frame` connectors. Fusion's as-built creation mode (`f3d:joint_mode`) is no case (b): the solved connectors state its outcome, and after an edit of the geometry the connectors pick, whether the joint keeps the components where they stand or moves the second onto the first decides the placement. Which it does is not settled: no stored file known to the project holds an as-built joint whose pick a later feature moved, so it stays in `native_options` (Rule N case (a), part 11). A SolidWorks mirror orientation is `MirrorResult.orientation` (Component patterns and mirrors, below). An axis limit's `rest` is the joint coordinate at which that degree of freedom rests within its range, in its axis's quantity (Fusion's rest value, enabled by its own flag: API `JointLimits.restValue` and `isRestValueEnabled`, and the joint help, "Sets the resting position for components within the range of motion"); a value Fusion stores with its flag cleared is the source setting `f3d:rest_value_disabled`, an inactive setting that no edit of the joint's inputs brings into effect (Rule N case (b)). `offset` displaces the second connector from the first. `Coincident` puts the second element on the first, with `offset` signed along the first element's normal; `Distance` is an unsigned separation; `Concentric` makes two axes coincide; `Insert` makes two circles coaxial with coincident or offset planes; `PointOnAxis` puts the first point at `distance` from the second axis; `Symmetric` makes the two elements mirror images in `plane`; `Width` holds the second element between the two elements of `pair`: `Centered` (and `mode: None`) centres it, so the two gaps are equal, and `Free` lets it move between them (SolidWorks width mate centred and free). `Gap` places the held element so that the distance from the `from` element of `pair` (`PairElement`, §6.6) to the held element's face that faces it is `distance`; `from: None` does not state which, and a writer of another codec then charges a loss naming the joint. SolidWorks' width mate in dimension mode is `Gap`, typed from SolidWorks' Width Mates page ("a distance or angle dimension from one selection set to the closest opposing selection set of faces or planes"); no stored file known to the project holds a width mate with a value, and which element its flip selects is not read, so the decoder states `from: None` and keeps the flip native (typed, carrier unread; part 11). An angle dimension stays native, and the percent mode is `WidthMode::Native("sldprt:percent")` (Rule N case (a), part 11). SolidWorks states each mate's kind twice, as the record's class and as the API's `swMateType_e` code of its `moBCMate_c`entry. `Path` keeps a point of the second element on a path, the chain its first connector picks: `position` places it anywhere (`Free`), at a `Distance` along the path, or at a `Percent` of the path's length, from the path's start, or from its end where `from_end` is true; `pitch_yaw` holds one axis of the second element's definition frame tangent to the path (`FollowPath`, reversed by `flip`), and `roll` holds one axis along a constructed direction (`UpVector`), never the axis `pitch_yaw` holds (SolidWorks path mate, Path Mate help). `from_end` decides how the stored distance or percent is read, so where it is `None` a writer of another codec does not write the value and charges a loss naming the feature (§2.4). Which end SolidWorks measures an unflipped value from is typed, carrier unread (part 11). A writer whose target has no path joint writes the solved placement as a `Rigid` motion and charges a loss naming the feature.
- **Alignment** states the relative sense of the connectors' z axes or normals: `Opposed` is `z₁ = −z₀`. `Nearest` states that the source fixes no sense and the solver keeps the nearer one (CATIA undefined orientation, SolidWorks closest); the solved sense is in the connectors' resolved frames. It is the only home of the sense (SolidWorks mate alignment, Inventor mate versus flush, CATIA `CstAttr_Orientation`, Fusion's frame-sense byte).
- **Bounds** hold at least one bound. `AxisLimits` names a degree of freedom the motion leaves, at most once per axis, and states `limits`, `rest`, or both. `Distance` and `Angle` limits are SolidWorks limit mates.
- **Couplings** relate the rotations or translations of the two connectors. `ratio` is the second member's rotation per rotation of the first, each about its own axis, negative when they turn opposite ways (`Gear`, `Belt`), or the pinion rotation in radians per millimetre of rack travel, positive when the rack moves along its axis as the pinion turns positively about its own (`RackPinion`). `radii`, `pitch_radius`, and `pitch` are the lengths the source states instead (FreeCAD `Distance`, `Distance2`). Where the coupling acts on two other joints (USD coupled hinges, Fusion motion links), `joints` picks them as `Feature` targets, gear or pinion first.
- **Dimensions and state.** Every value is a `Dimension` (D1), so a design parameter drives it (Creo `dim_id`, Inventor `d0`, SolidWorks mate dimensions). Suppression is `Feature.suppressed`; a configuration overrides it (D14), and a different mate value per configuration is a parameter override (D16). The joint feature is canonical over any copy of its suppression (D30).
- **Containers.** Joints are members of the scope's containers in source order. A mates folder is a `Folder`. Sources that solve constraints with no order (CATIA, NX, FreeCAD `JointGroup`) put them in an unordered `Group`. A source with joints and no history (USD, STEP) holds them in an unordered `Group` root container of the root definition's scope (§8.1); a joint the source lists under a product below the root names that product as its `component` (§5.1). A body of a definition that scope spans, which no member of the scope produces, is unproduced (§5.5).
- **Grounding** is occurrence state (`OccurrenceDesign.grounded`, §5.1), and no joint. A USD fixed joint to the world is a `Rigid` motion with a world connector.
- **Flexible sub-assemblies.** The sub-assembly's own joints are canonical. A copy of them that a flexible instance keeps (FreeCAD `AssemblyLink` with `Rigid` false) is regenerated by the writer; the instance's nested overrides, base and per configuration, are the cache of solving them (§5.1, §5.11, §8.1). The configuration SolidWorks generates for a flexible instance is not stored as a configuration (D47, §5.11).

| Source | Mapping |
|---|---|
