| SolidWorks | coincident, concentric, distance, parallel, perpendicular, tangent, angle, symmetric, width as named; limit distance and limit angle as `Distance` and `Angle` with limits; lock and in-place as `JointMotion::Rigid` with `Entity` connectors; gear and belt as couplings; slot as `Slot` with `Entity` connectors; path as `Path`, whose record caches the point of the path its distance is measured from, so a decoder states `from_end` by matching that point to an end of the resolved path(part 11); the mate record's alignment, the u16 13 bytes before its first operand, 1 `Aligned`, 2 `Opposed`, and 0, where an operand is a line, none; a distance mate's value, its record's `D1` length parameter; coordinate as `Coincident` of two `Point` connectors where its operands are two component sketch points; whether the class also stores coincidences of coordinate systems is open (part 11) |
| Inventor | mate `Coincident` (`Opposed`); flush `Coincident` (`Aligned`); angle, tangent, insert as named; the proxy kind (`42df52ce` plane, `896cf08e` axis, point) selects the connector variant. An operand names its occurrence, the component's body, whose moniker integer is the body record's source index, the entity kind, and the picked plane, axis, cylinder, or point by cached geometry only: no field of a moniker or a constraint names the picked face. So the connector's pick has a `Native` target with that geometry as its witness, and a decoder may fill `resolved` by matching it against the component's faces |
| CATIA | offset `Coincident { offset }`; coincidence `Coincident` or `Concentric` by element; surface contact `Coincident` or `Tangent`; angle; fix together a `RigidGroup` of any size (Rigid groups, below); fix is grounding |
| Creo | by stored code: 5 (mate) `Coincident { offset }` with `Opposed`, the faces' outward normalsopposed, and 26 (align) the same with `Aligned`, the offset signed along the first face's outward normal; 27 `Parallel` with `Aligned` and 42 `Parallel` with `Opposed`, the distance free; 43 `Concentric` on two axes, their senses free; 7 (insert) `Concentric` on the axes of two cylindrical faces, whose radii are free and which relates no plane; 81 (csys) and 52 (default) `Coincident` on `Frame` connectors with `Aligned`; 81 with the offset instructions 313, 314, and 312 a `Rigid` `Motion` whose `offset` holds x, y, and the angle about z from them; 155 with 159, which always pair on one frame pair beside a mate that sets z, a `Slider` `Motion` along z with the same offsets, and 165 in 155's place the same with `Opposed`; 183 `Coincident` on `Point` connectors; 4050 `Place.packaged`; fix is grounding; angle offset `Angle`; point and edge on surface `Coincident` with `Point` or `Axis` connectors; point on line `PointOnAxis`. 1450, 315, 23, 25, 49, 110, 192, 2092, 5127, 4570, and 4580 are `Native` (`creo:<code>`), typed, carrier unread (part 11) |
| Fusion | Assemble and As-built joints as `Motion`, whose kinds are Fusion's joint types (API `JointTypes`: rigid, revolute, slider, cylindrical, pin-slot, planar, ball), the motion record's freedom code stating the kind and its `axis` (1 `Revolute { axis: Y }`, 2 `Revolute { axis: Z }`, 8 `Slider { axis: Z }`; any other code `JointMotion::Native("f3d:freedom:<codes>")`, typed, carrier unread, part 11); an as-built scope with no connector and no joint record as a `RigidGroup` (Rigid groups, below); joint-origin snaps as construction inputs; solved frames as `resolved`; motion links as couplings |
| FreeCAD, USD | joint kinds as named; FreeCAD `Placement1`/`Placement2` and USD local frames as `resolved` and `after` |

#### Rigid groups

```rust
pub struct RigidGroup {
    pub members: BTreeSet<OccurrencePath>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
```

A `RigidGroup` holds its members in the placement they have relative to one another, so that they move as one. `members` are paths from the definition that owns the group, so a group in an assembly can hold an occurrence inside a sub-assembly, and the empty path is that definition's own origin; a member inside a pattern instance is named by the path step to the occurrence the pattern made (`ComponentInstance.occurrences`), and a listing that names an occurrence the file does not hold is no member, kept in the group's `native_options`. The group states no pose: where a source's solved state is read, a member's pose in the group is its `Occurrence.transform` (Rule D), so the members keep their placements and the group holds them there. Fusion's as-built scope (type `AA8B3D40`) in its group form, with no connector record and no joint record, is so: a group holds occurrence references, up to hundreds in one group, and the scope refers to nothing else (part 11). Each member is a locator that stores the group's frame in the member's own space (identity where its flag is 1), and the decoder keeps the locators as native options. Fusion applies the locator: a member's locator references its occurrence's operation table, a timeline of the occurrence's pose after each operation, and the members' poses composed with their locators give one group frame at the group's own step and at every later step, and at the tables' final entries. So the Fusion decoder takes each member's `Occurrence.transform` from its operation table's final entry, where the locators and the tables' poses agree; the placement records are not those poses (below). The locators are equal across saves of one design. The occurrence placement records, which can hold the insert pose or an earlier matrix, can break the group's frame. The decoder reads a member's pose by one order: the table its locator names; where its wrapper holds a second tracking record, the table at the context's path extended by the child occurrence that record names; the table at the context's path; the root at the identity or at the context's pose; else the context's pose composed with the path's placement-record matrices, the context being the path prefix every table-resolved member admits. It reads the path in the version-4 table header and drops a table whose final entry removes its instance. The group's snapshot record (`1ABFB679`) holds an earlier step's poses, not the solved state. Two further decoder rules hold. A table whose final entry holds no matrix gives the identity, for a member and for a context alike. A placement record is a member's pose only where no table reaches its occurrence. The decoder states a group with the members that resolve, keeping an unresolved listing in the group's `native_options`; groups whose members no parsed table reaches, and copies of one group whose frames differ even from tables, are decoder readings (part 11). Fusion's include-child-components option is not stored, and a member list need not be closed under descendants, so the members are the occurrences as picked, nested ones included. The group's name is stored only where the user renamed it, and its kind string is the command's localised name, which is not kept. A CATIA fix together is a `RigidGroup` of any size, which CATIA stores as one record: an `AsmBloc` record whose definition names the catalog type `FixTogether`. The record names no member: each member is a connector owned by one component instance, which picks no geometry, listed by the product's connection table. Its `Activity` is `Feature.suppressed`, its default name `Feature.name`, and the list of 2 `Boolean` records it owns, whose values are unread, goes to `native_options`; a record whose members do not resolve is `FeatureOperation::Native` with the kind `catia:FixTogether` (part 11). CATIA stores no pose per member (no record of a group holds the 9 to 12 values a matrix or offset would), so its members keep their stored placements. An NX bond of two or more components is a `RigidGroup`. NX stores a bond as an assembly constraint of type code 0c in the compact grammar (NX Open's `Constraint.Type` Bond, 11, stored plus one; the arity of Fix and two other codes checks the order). A bond of components only picks geometry on every member, and the decoder keeps its picks as native options. A bond with a datum-frame member is its component pattern's own constraint, not a `RigidGroup` and not a feature: such a bond joins a component-pattern record, so the NX decoder keeps it with that pattern (Component patterns and mirrors, below). No bond stores a pose, so its members keep their placements, as CATIA's do. Inventor stores no rigid group; its rigid joints pick two connectors each. A writer keeps the members' placements and writes the group, or, where its target has no rigid group, a fixed joint between one member and each other member, and charges no loss, since the result does not move differently; a writer to CATIA writes a group as a fix together, which holds its members where they stand.

#### Component patterns and mirrors

```rust
pub struct ComponentPattern {
    pub seeds: OrderedSelection,
    pub layout: PatternLayout,
    pub instances: Vec<ComponentInstance>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub struct ComponentInstance { pub index: InstanceIndex, pub occurrences: Vec<OccurrenceId> }

pub struct MirrorComponents {
    pub seeds: OrderedSelection,
    pub plane: Construction<Plane>,
    pub results: Vec<MirrorResult>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub struct MirrorResult { pub occurrence: OccurrenceId, pub orientation: Option<MirrorOrientation> }
pub enum MirrorOrientation {
    SeedAxes { reversed: MirrorReversal, about: Option<MirrorPivot> },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum MirrorReversal { X, Y, Z, All }
pub enum MirrorPivot { ExtentCentre, CentreOfMass, Origin }
```

- `seeds` pick `Component`s. `layout` is a part-level layout (§6.5). A component pattern that follows a pattern is `Follow`, its pick naming a part pattern feature through an occurrence context (CATIA Reuse Pattern, a SolidWorks pattern-driven pattern) or an assembly pattern. A SolidWorks chain pattern is `Chain` (§6.5); one the chain layout does not hold is `PatternLayout::Native` (part 11).
- `instances` lists the occurrences the pattern creates, which exist in the states at and after the pattern, unless a `Place` names them (Placement, above). `index` holds the instance coordinates, as in `TopoName::Instance` (§6.5); `occurrences[k]` is the copy of `seeds[k]`. The seed position is not an instance. An index the layout counts and `instances` omits is a skipped instance. A SolidWorks local pattern (`moLocalLPattern_c`, `moLocalCirPattern_c`, `moLocalChainPattern_c`) stores the ids of its instances' components, which the decoder joins to the occurrences, with each instance's index from its `moLPatternItemId_c`; instances are never matched by transform.
- An NX component pattern's bonds with a datum-frame member (assembly constraints of code 0c, each joining a component-pattern record) are kept with the pattern, each with its members and picks. A bond that ties an element's frame to that element's own component, restating `instances`, one that ties it to another element's (a stale constraint left by an edit, by inference), and a lone element frame are the pattern's source setting `nx:pattern_constraints`. A bond that ties a component outside the pattern to its direction frames or to its reference frames is the pattern's native option `nx:pattern_frame_bonds`, since that the outside component carries the geometry the pattern's direction or reference is picked on is inferred and not read. They are no `RigidGroup` and no feature: a writer of another format writes the pattern from `layout` and `instances` and charges the native option as a loss, and an NX writer re-emits the bonds.
- `results[k]` is the mirror of `seeds[k]`: its `occurrence`, and its `orientation`. `None` is the opposite-hand result, the seed's placement reflected across `plane`. `SeedAxes` is a copy of the seed, not its mirror image: the seed's placement reflected across `plane`, then the seed reversed along `reversed`, an axis of the seed's own frame (`All` reverses the three), through the point `about` names: `ExtentCentre` the centre of the seed model's box in the seed's own frame, `CentreOfMass` the seed's centre of mass, and `Origin` the seed's origin; `None`, not stated. One reversed axis or all three are the only cases, because the result is a copy and the reflection already reverses one sense. The translation is derived, not stored: after an edit of the plane, of the seed's placement, or of the seed's geometry the orientation decides the result's placement, which `Occurrence.transform` caches (K2). A `Native` orientation keeps a mode the design does not construct, with the result's stored placement. The result's prototype and `orientation` state the mirror's kind: the seed's prototype under a reflecting transform, with `orientation: None` (Fusion); the seed's prototype with `SeedAxes`, so that the result's placement is proper (a SolidWorks copy orientation, below); or another definition (an opposite-hand part). An opposite-hand definition's scope starts with a linked stored-geometry feature whose `transform` reflects; where that definition is external, its prototype is enough.
- A SolidWorks component mirror (`moMirrorCompFeat_c`) holds the plane's reference and one data object per seed, whose u16 code states the copy's orientation: stored code 0, 1, and 2 is `SeedAxes` with `reversed` Z, X, and Y, and 3 is `All` (from the page; an inferred match, held by no stored file known to the project). The result is the seed reflected in the plane and then reversed along one axis of the seed's own frame through a centre of the seed. The vendor's pages construct the same. Its Mirror Type "Center of mass" ("the center of mass of the selected components mirrors about the mirror plane") and, from the 2020 release, "Component origin" ("the component origins are mirrored about the mirror plane") construct `CentreOfMass` and `Origin` by their text. "Center of bounding box" does not by text alone, since the page does not say which frame the box is aligned to; the stored placements give the seed model's box in the seed's own frame, which is `ExtentCentre`. Its four orientations, from "X mirrored, Y mirrored" to "X mirrored and flipped, Y mirrored and flipped", are the reflection followed by a reversal of the seed's Z, X, Y, and all three axes; its orientation taken from a picked reference ("Align to selection") does not let a reader construct the axes, and is `MirrorOrientation::Native` (typing it adds an arm; part 11). Where every reversed axis is one the seed is symmetric along, the extent centre and the centre of mass coincide, so the stored results cannot tell them apart, and the stored value that names the choice is not located; no stored file known to the project settles it. So under Rule H1 the SolidWorks decoder states `about` only where the stored placement agrees with one centre and no other, and `None` where more than one agrees. Where no centre agrees it states `Native("sldprt:mirror_orientation")` with the occurrence's stored placement. `CentreOfMass`, `Origin`, and `All` are typed from the vendor's enumeration, are held by no stored file known to the project, and are stated under Rule H1 likewise (part 11). Since no stored file known to the project separates `ExtentCentre` from `CentreOfMass`, the decoder computes the seed's centre of mass before it states `ExtentCentre`, and states `None` where the two agree. A writer whose target stores a free placement writes the derived one.
- The SolidWorks decoder joins a mirror's seeds and results from the record. Word i of the record's word array is the transform stamp of seed i's component, and in the newer layout a pair table names the seed's component id as well. A result component's record names the mirror feature, and within a feature the k-th smallest result reference is the k-th result component in stream order; the seed references ranked the same way give the stamp-joined seeds in stream order. A seed's stamp may be absent or shared by several components, and a result may be referenced through chains that exist already. A mirror with a seed or a result that does not join is a `Native` operation (typed, carrier unread; part 11). Where the result is a new opposite-hand document, whose path the data object holds, it is not joined to its result component (part 11).
- Each occurrence a pattern or mirror creates is named by one such feature. It may also be a `Place` feature's occurrence: a Creo pattern member is a full component feature with its own placement constraints and its own placeamong the features, so it is a `Place` that the pattern also lists, and it takes its existence from the `Place`.

#### Assembly features

```rust
pub struct AssemblyContext {
    pub participants: BTreeMap<Option<ContextEffect>, SetSelection>,
}
pub enum ContextEffect { Instances, Definitions, Native(NonBlankString) }
```

An assembly feature is a feature of the scope that holds an assembly's design whose definition states `assembly`: it runs its `operation` (an extrude or revolve cut, a hole, a split, a fillet, a Boolean with a tool body) in the assembly over its participants, the occurrences, or bodies through occurrence contexts, that it changes. `participants` holds them by effect: each key states what the feature changes for the participants its selection holds, `None` where the source does not state it, and each participant is in one selection. Every source but Creo states one effect for a feature. Creo's intersect list gives each participant its own display level (PTC, About the Intersection Tab User Interface: the Intersected Models table's Display column), so a Creo feature with participants at top level and at part level holds two entries. On the wire `participants` is an array of `[effect, selection]` pairs in key order (§2.5). A feature whose source lists no participant holds no entry. A feature scope that the source keeps as a rule over components is a `Rule` selection with an `Affected` term (§5.8). SolidWorks' All components, which "Applies the feature to all components in the model every time the feature regenerates" (SOLIDWORKS help, Feature Scope in Assemblies), is one `Affected` term. Creo's Automatic Update, which intersects on regeneration each component added before the feature and removes none from the list (PTC, About the Intersection Tab User Interface), is stated in the entry of the feature's default display level, the level Creo gives a component it adds: an `Explicit` term of the listed components of that level, where the list holds any, and then an `Affected` term. The listed components of another level stay in that level's entry. The term reads the anchored state, so it reaches the occurrences that exist entering the feature (Existence, above): a Creo component placed after the feature is not intersected, and a component that no feature creates exists in every state. A component that another entry of the context picks is a participant under that entry only. SolidWorks' Auto-select, which chooses the intersected components once ("only the components on the initial list are regenerated", SOLIDWORKS help, Feature Scope in Assemblies), is a `Named` selection, and its flag is the operation's source setting `sldprt:auto_select`, as on a part feature's scope (§6). Where SolidWorks and Creo store these options is not read (typed, carrier unread; part 11). A writer whose target lists participants and cannot store the rule writes the selection's `resolved` where it is stated, otherwise the seeds of its `Explicit` terms, and charges a loss naming the feature. A selection that is only an `Affected` term and states no `resolved` is not written as an empty participant list: the loss names the feature, and the target is not told that the feature changes no component. The context is part of the definition, so a configuration that overrides the definition states it in the override (§5.11). The operation is stated as on any feature (part 6): `Unresolved` with its family where it is known without its operands, and `Native` where its meaning is not established (Rule N case (a)), each with `assembly` stated. A context whose participants the decoder did not read holds one entry, with `Unread` picks (§5.8).

- `Instances` changes only the instances of the participants under it. A participant whose instance already shows instance bodies in the feature's anchored state, the result of an earlier assembly feature, is changed from those bodies, and the feature's picks of that instance resolve in them (§5.8, Context): Inventor's weld preparations and post-weld machining are assembly features run in that order (Autodesk, About Weld Feature Groups). The result is `instance_bodies` of the assembly definition at each participant's path (§8.1): SolidWorks `caBody` streams, the Inventor assembly carrier. Creo stores the cut faces per occurrence (`ASMCUT_COPY`) and no trimmed body. The faces are stored state, which a decoder cannot assemble into instance bodies without a kernel: they stay in their native record, the instance bodies are not delivered, and the decoder charges a loss naming the feature, while the feature itself is typed. This is no case of Rule N: two sets of cut faces are two instance bodies.
- `Definitions` changes the definitions of the participants under it. Each changed definition's scope holds a resulting feature with `driven_by` naming the feature whose definition states the context (§5.10): a CATIA resulting hole or pocket, a SolidWorks feature propagated to parts, a Creo `ASSEM_CUT` with part visibility. Isolating the result clears `driven_by`.
- `participants` is the one statement of the bodies the feature changes, so its operation states no operand that chooses them: every `Boolean::Apply.targets` and `Targets` in it, and its `ShellFeature.bodies`, `Combine.target`, and `SplitMode::ByTools.targets`, are `None`, and it is no operation whose such operand is required (`DeleteBodies`, `TransformBodies`, `Flex`, `Graft`, `Knit`, `Mesh`, a `Split` in `Mutual` mode, a `SheetMetal` `Convert`). Every other operand is stated as on any feature: a profile, a hole's positions, the edges a fillet rounds, a split's tools and kept side (a CATIA splitting surface), and a body the feature uses without changing it, which is a `Combine`'s `tools`: the body a CATIA assembly Remove removes from its participants or an Add adds to them (CATIA V5 Assembly Design guide, Assembly Remove and Assembly Add), and the solid an NX assembly cut subtracts from its target components. Each is a selection of the feature's definition, anchored as its other selections are (§5.8, Anchors). A pick of an occurrence's geometry carries that occurrence's context (§5.8, Context), as a CATIA tool body in another part does; a pick of a body the assembly's own definition owns carries none. An entity operand the operation changes, such as an edge a fillet rounds, resolves in a participant: in the instance bodies the anchored state shows for it, where it shows them, and otherwise in its prototype (§5.8, Context).
- A Fusion feature that picks bodies of another component changes that component's definition directly and states no `assembly` (§5.10).

| Source | Spelling |
|---|---|
| SolidWorks | `moAsmFeatData_c` cut, revolve cut, hole: `Instances`; `swAssemblyFeatureEffectedComponents` is derived from `participants`; propagate to parts: `Definitions`; All components is an `Affected` term, and Auto-select a `Named` selection with the source setting `sldprt:auto_select`; where the scope is stored is not read (typed, carrier unread; part 11) |
| Creo | assembly CUT, HOLE, slot, and material removal, and a solidify that removes material where it carries a type-76 instruction: each type-76 intersect instruction is a participant, a `Component` pick through the occurrence path its `memb_id_tab1` stores, and the display level its `geometry2_id` stores is its effect: 0, top level, is `Instances` (the cut faces, where the assembly stores them, are an `ASMCUT_COPY` that names the feature, or the leader of its pattern, and the path), and the length of the path, part level, is `Definitions` (the participant's part holds the resulting `ASSEM_CUT`, whose feature id the instruction's `geometry1_id` stores); any other stored level is `ContextEffect::Native("creo:visibility_level:<k>")` with k the stored level (part 11). A solidify that removes material (feature type 916, form 512, instruction 1103, §6.5) with a type-76 instruction is a `Split` in `ByTools` mode: the quilt is the tool, and the participants are the targets. A cut that holds instruction 1864 is a surface trim (PTC, About a Surface Trim Created with the Extrude Tool): the instruction names the quilt it trims by an id of the assembly, with no occurrence path, a quilt that the cut's topology increment also lists and that an earlier feature of the assembly names. It changes a body the assembly owns, holds no intersect instruction, and states no `assembly`; the volume split (type 988) holds no intersect instruction and states none either. A member of a pattern that holds no intersect instruction of its own states its leader's participants, each under the leader's effect: under the pattern option that intersects every instance with the model at once (`pat_type` bit 8, §6.5), the `ASMCUT_COPY` that names the leader holds every member's cut faces (part 11). Any other cut, hole, slot, or material removal with no intersect instruction states `assembly` and holds no entry. Automatic Update is an `Affected` term in the entry of the feature's default display level; the record that stores it and that level is not read (typed, carrier unread; part 11), so until then the participants are the stored instructions. |
| CATIA | Split, Hole, Hole Series, Pocket, Remove, Add with `_ImpactedComp` as `participants`: `Definitions` |
| Inventor | assembly cut, hole, weld preparation: `Instances`, the cut bodies from the assembly carrier (`AmBREPSegment`) |
| NX | assembly cut: `None` until a stored file shows its bodies, or `Instances` where the decoder finds per-instance bodies (no stored file known to the project holds one; part 11); NX promotion is a linked stored-geometry feature of the referencing part, and a feature that acts on the promoted body changes that copy only |

#### Derived, inserted, and linked components

A component whose geometry is copied from another definition is a `Stored { origin: Linked(link) }` feature (§5.10) in the receiving scope; a new component holding it has a `Place` where the source orders one. `Link.source`'s picks carry the contexts the link runs through, with the configuration each level reads; `document` names the source definition and its configuration only where `source` is absent or unread.

A component that places another design without copying its geometry is an occurrence of that design's definition, and `Linked` is reserved for the derived copies of the table below. A Fusion external (XRef) component whose design the decode reads, as a member of the `.f3z` archive (§3.1), is a `File` definition with its own scope, whose `document` holds its member path, lineage, and version URNs (§8.1); one whose design is not read is an `External` definition.

| Source | `Link` |
|---|---|
| SolidWorks insert or derived part (`moStock_c`), mirror part (`moMirrorStock_c`) | `source` picks the bodies through a `PickContext::Definition` context that states the part's configuration; a mirror part's reflecting `transform` |
| SolidWorks in-context reference | `source` picks with a `PickContext::InContext` context built from the reference chain, with the configuration of each level on `assembly` and on each path step; the backed-up copy is the picks' witnesses: curves in `curves`, a face group or body in `body` (§5.8) |
| Inventor derived part, iPart member | `document` the factory, with the table row as its configuration; `scale` (`ScaleForDerivedMember`); `transform` |
| Creo merge, copy geometry | `transform` from `local_sys`; copy geometry's `source` picks with a `PickContext::InContext` context (`own_ref_id`); the `new_ids` remap and `ref_revnum` stay in the native record (allocations, Rule N case (b)) |
| NX WAVE link, extract body | `source` anchored at the linked state, or `Anchor::Native` where the source part is not read; Position Dependent as `PickContext::InContext`; time stamps decide `state` |
| CATIA copy with link, contextual reference | `source` picks a publication or an entity; the contextual instance as the context's `own` path; red mark is `OutOfDate`; "as result" with no link is `Snapshot` |
| FreeCAD ShapeBinder, SubShapeBinder | `source` anchored `Pinned(After(m))` in the other Body; `Relative` binders as `PickContext::InContext`; `BindMode` 0 is `associative` |
| Fusion Derived Base Feature, DerivedInstance | `document` the external design; `ExternalDocument.version` the version URN |

## 7. The process layer

The `process` class holds manufacturing definitions and their evaluations. Its shapes follow what six CAM data models store: Fusion, FreeCAD, Creo NC, CAMWorks, and the NX and Mastercam documentation. A shared concept takes its ISO 14649 (STEP-NC) name. No source's catalogue is the vocabulary: Rule N (§3.1) decides what is typed, so a typed variant names a manufacturing concept whose meaning stored files, ISO 14649, or the vendor's documentation establishes, however many sources store it, and the source's own kind name is kept verbatim beside every classification.

```rust
pub struct Process {
    pub setups: Vec<Setup>, pub operations: Vec<Operation>, pub features: Vec<MachiningFeature>,
    pub groups: Vec<ProcessGroup>, pub tools: Vec<Tool>, pub presets: Vec<Preset>, pub machines: Vec<Machine>,
    pub programs: Vec<Program>, pub parameters: Vec<ProcessParameter>, pub toolpaths: Vec<Toolpath>,
    pub states: Vec<ProcessState>,
}
pub struct Choice<T> { pub value: Option<T>, pub parameters: BTreeSet<ProcessParameterId> }
pub struct WorkpieceSelection { pub workpiece: Option<u32>, pub selection: OrderedSelection }
pub struct ProcessConstruction<K: ConstructionKind> { pub workpiece: Option<u32>, pub construction: Construction<K> }
```

- Process records refer to the design through selections (§5.8), constructions (§5.9), design parameters (§5.13, §7.7), and design states used as bases (§7.9). The design layer refers to no process record (§2.1).
- **Scope.** A setup names the design scope it machines (`Setup.scope`: a Creo manufacturing assembly, a Fusion root component, a FreeCAD document's definition). Process picks, process parameter references (`through` paths, §5.13), and occurrence paths resolve from that definition, and per-configuration process records name configurations of that scope (§7.3, §7.8, §7.9). An operation, its toolpaths and process states, and the parameters they own resolve from their operation's setup. A record no setup holds (a machining feature, group, tool, preset, machine, or program, and the parameters it owns) resolves from the scope of the setups that use it: the setups of the operations that list the machining feature or group or use the tool or preset, the setups that name the machine, and the setups the program outputs. Those setups machine one scope; a record no setup uses holds no selection and no `through` path.
- Every process selection is anchored `Current` or `Pinned`. `Current` follows every design edit (Fusion resolves every CAM reference in the final design). A Creo NC sequence regenerates between two design features of the manufacturing model, so its selections are anchored `Pinned(After(f))`; a writer derives the sequence's place in the target timeline from the anchor.
- Sources store an operation's settings as named values. Creo names its settings by code, and these codes are read: code 2 is the `Cutting` feed, the stored drilling cycle's feed; code 28 is the clearance above the hole at which a drilling cycle starts to feed, the cycle's `retract`, its `ret_to`; codes 197 and 276 are the holder diameter and the tangent lead step; and a tool's parameter 0 is its cutter diameter, 1 a drill's point angle, and 2 an end mill's corner radius. Code 5 is the spindle speed, `Technology.spindle` as `Rotation`; code 54 the sequence's tool; code 96, present with the value 0, the cutter-location output that writes the tool axis at every point, a source setting of the operation's program output; the operation's code 29 its output file's name, `ProgramOutput.filename`, and codes 41 and 42 its pre- and post-machining files; and the workcell's codes 127, 128, and 129 its machine id, location, and controller, `Machine.control` the last. Code 82 is a drilling cycle's pull-out distance, a named cycle parameter; code 6 is the dwell, `CycleSettings.dwell`, and code 134 the tapping cycle's feed (part 11). Milling step depth is code 9 or 27, and turning step depth is no code of its sequence. Every other Creo code keeps its `creo:<n>` name (part 11): code 4 holds values that look like a tolerance, which nothing stored states independently. A setting with no typed field is a parameter owned by its record (§7.7), whose meaning rides on its source name until a typed field holds it (Rule N case (a), part 11): the toolpath an operation stores is the stored result of what its settings do. The height modes, leads, plunge entry, links and retraction, drilling cycle settings, step rules, finishing steps, and compensation are typed (§7.3, §7.5); the tool and holder fields an operation copies are its tool's (§7.6); the smoothing filter and the tolerances derived from `tolerance` have no design meaning (§7.7); and every other Fusion setting name stays a parameter (§7.5, part 11). Process records carry no `native_options` map. A classification's `Unclassified` arm carries no text, because the record's `native_kind` holds the source's name.
- A `Choice` holds a selection among variants: a stock rule, a WCS mode, a height reference, a coolant mode. Where the source holds the choice in parameters, `parameters` names every one it is read from, and each holds the source's own value, of the kind the source gives it: Fusion's `'default'` for a `Relative` stock rule, `'axesZX'` for `Axes`, `'disabled'` for coolant `Off`, the Boolean `tool_clockwise` for a spindle direction. A source may spread one choice over several parameters, each of which an expression may drive (FreeCAD states a cutter compensation by `UseComp`, `Side`, and `Direction`, and a drilling cycle's kind by several flags); `value` is the decoder's reading of them together, by the codec's table. The parameters' expressions are canonical and `value` is the variant they map to, a cache (K2), absent where one of their values is absent (an edit helper clears it when any of them changes, §4). `parameters` names only the parameters the variant is read from: the variant's own fields hold their values or bind their own parameters, each binding in its field (a `RadialLimit::From`'s `offset`, an `Absolute` diameter, a `LineTurn::Angle`'s `angle`), and `parameters` does not name them. So an edit of a field's parameter changes that field and leaves the arm, and an edit helper clears `value` only when a parameter that selects the variant changes, which removes the cached arm and no parameter; the codec then restores the arm by its table and re-reads its fields' bindings from its own table of setting names. The cached arm holds no operand of its own: an arm that reads the user's selections or points names, by its `slot`, a `Reference` geometry of the same operation that holds them (§7.3), so clearing it removes no user input. A field of a cached arm read from a stored result (a `LineTurn::Angle`'s `along`, and a `from` read from the toolpath) is lost with the arm, and is restored only by a toolpath made after the edit (§7.3). A writer of another codec writes `value`, and a writer of the same codec writes the parameters. Where `parameters` is empty the source holds the choice as a constant, and `value` is present. Fusion may compute a stock mode or a WCS orientation mode by formula.
- **Workpiece selections.** A process record that selects workpiece geometry holds one `WorkpieceSelection` per workpiece, in source order: `workpiece`, an index into the `workpieces` of its operation's setup, and the selection of that workpiece's entities. `workpiece: None` is a selection of design entities that no workpiece places, read in the definition's frame (FreeCAD picks may target design objects directly), so a pick of a body of an ordered container reads it under the container's `placement` (§5.2), and a pick of an object that an `App::Link` places picks it through the object's own occurrence (§6.7); a record holds at most one such entry. A record that no setup holds (a machining feature) indexes the `workpieces` of each setup whose operations use it, and those setups list the same workpiece at that index. Its picks name design entities, with witnesses in design coordinates, and the design-class pick types hold no process reference: the workpiece is named on the process side. Two model clones of one body, placed differently, are two entries whose selections may name the same design entity (FreeCAD stores its base geometry in this grouped form: `Base` lists (object, sub-elements) pairs, and its picks may target model clones). A construction in a process record that picks workpiece geometry is a `ProcessConstruction`, which names its workpiece the same way: the WCS axes, origin, and frame (§7.2) and the `Points`, `Direction`, and `Axis` geometry sources (§7.3). Its construction's picks name design entities of that workpiece, and its `resolved` value is in setup space, the picks' geometry under the workpiece's `placement`; with `workpiece: None` it reads design entities in the definition's frame. Quantities, counts, and booleans are `ProcessDimension<T>` (§5.14), which store no value when bound and bind a process or a design parameter.

### 7.1 Setups, order, and programs

```rust
pub struct Setup {
    pub id: SetupId,
    pub scope: ProductDefinitionId,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub job: Option<Choice<JobKind>>,
    pub axes: Option<AxisClass>,
    pub steps: Vec<Step>,
    pub workpieces: Vec<WorkpieceSetup>,
    pub fixtures: Option<SetSelection>,
    pub stock: Option<Choice<StockRule>>,
    pub wcs: Wcs,
    pub work_offsets: Vec<Choice<WorkOffset>>,
    pub machine: Option<MachineId>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum JobKind { Milling, Turning, Jet, WireEdm, Additive, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub enum AxisClass { Planar, TwoAndHalf, Three, Indexed, Simultaneous }
pub struct WorkpieceSetup { pub workpiece: SetSelection, pub placement: Option<Transform> }
pub enum WorkOffset { Default, Number(NonZeroU32) }
pub enum Step { Operation(OperationId), Folder { name: Option<String>, steps: Vec<Step> }, Function(FunctionStep) }
pub struct FunctionStep { pub function: NcFunction, pub suppressed: Option<bool>, pub native_ref: Option<String> }
pub enum NcFunction { Stop, OptionalStop, Message(String), WorkOffset(WorkOffset), Code(String), Native(NonBlankString) }

pub struct Program {
    pub id: ProgramId, pub name: Option<String>, pub steps: Vec<ProgramStep>, pub post: Option<NonBlankString>,
    pub machine: Option<MachineId>, pub output: ProgramOutput, pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum ProgramStep {
    Setup(SetupId), Operation(OperationId), Function(FunctionStep),
    Group { name: Option<String>, steps: Vec<ProgramStep> },
}
pub struct ProgramOutput { pub filename: Option<NonBlankString>, pub folder: Option<String>, pub extension: Option<NonBlankString>, pub unit: Option<Choice<UnitSymbol>> }
```

A setup is one placement of workpieces on a machine: a Fusion setup, a FreeCAD Job, a Creo operation, a CAMWorks operation setup, an ISO 14649 `setup`.

- **Order.** A setup holds its steps in machining order, with folders. Order lives only in `Setup.steps` and `Program.steps`; ids carry no order (in Fusion child lists, id order can differ from machining order). Where the source orders only by program (NX), a setup's steps follow program order.
- **Membership.** Every operation is in exactly one setup: it is one of the setup's steps, or an input of a modifier in that setup (§7.3). A FreeCAD dressup replaces its base in the Job's operation list, so the base is in no step.
- **Functions.** A `FunctionStep` is a step that machines nothing (ISO 14649 `Nc_function`): a stop, an optional stop, an operator message, a work offset change, or raw NC code (FreeCAD Stop, Comment, Fixture, and Custom objects in the operation list). `suppressed` is FreeCAD's `Active` inverted.
- **Job and axes.** `job` is the process family; `axes` is the motion class the setup is programmed for. FreeCAD `JobType` states both: Lathe is `Turning`; 2D, 2.5D, and Multiaxis are `Milling` with `Planar`, `TwoAndHalf`, and `Simultaneous`. `job` is a `Choice` because a source can drive it by a named parameter (Fusion `job_type`). Wire EDM occurs in Creo and in CAMWorks settings.
- **Setup space.** Each `WorkpieceSetup` selects design bodies or occurrences. Its `placement` maps the selected body's local frame into the setup's space, in place of `Body.transform` (§5.2, §5.6), or, for an object that an `App::Link` places, in place of the transform of the object's own occurrence (§6.7): a FreeCAD clone's placement places the Body's result itself, not the Body's own placement (ISO 14649 `workpiece_setup.its_origin`; FreeCAD model clones). Without one, setup space is design space, and the selected bodies are read in the definition's frame. A FreeCAD model clone is no design feature: it is a workpiece selecting the cloned object, with the clone's placement. The clone's stored shape is the cloned object's result under that placement, a copy (K1) that is not stored. A pick into a clone names the cloned design entity, with its witness in design coordinates, inside a `WorkpieceSelection` that names the clone's workpiece (above). The WCS, fixed points, owned profiles, and toolpath frames are in setup space. An NX MCS group is a setup, and each WORKPIECE group below it a `WorkpieceSetup` of that setup.
- **Fixtures.** `fixtures` selects the fixture and clamp geometry of the setup (Fusion `job_fixture`, a model selection slot; ISO 14649 `its_fixture_usage` of a `setup`; Creo, the bit-128 occurrences of the manufacturing assembly, which lie outside the stock and which no stored toolpath enters). Fusion's fixture clearances are parameters owned by the setup (§7.7).
- **Work offsets.** `work_offsets` lists the offsets the setup is output at, in output order. `Number(n)` is the control's n-th work offset (1 is G54). `Default` is the source's explicit default (Fusion `job_workOffset` 0). Each entry is a `Choice`, since a source can drive it by a named parameter: Fusion's `job_workOffset` holds the source's number, which the codec maps to `Default` for 0 and `Number(n)` otherwise. FreeCAD `Fixtures` is a list; how a writer orders output across offsets (FreeCAD `OrderOutputBy`) is a program parameter.
- **Programs.** A program is an ordered NC output, independent of setups (Fusion programs; ISO 14649 `workplan`). `Setup(s)` outputs all of `s`'s steps in their order, so a FreeCAD Job is one setup and one program whose steps are `[Setup(job)]`, and its order is stated once. NX program groups and Mastercam toolpath groups nest as `Group`. `post` is the source's identifier of its post processor (a Fusion `user://` URI, a FreeCAD script name). `ProgramOutput` states the output file's `filename`, `folder`, and `extension`, and the length `unit` the program is output in (a `Choice`, which Fusion drives by `nc_program_unit`). A source that stores the output path as a template with substitutions (FreeCAD `PostProcessorOutputFile` `%D/%d.nc`) keeps the template in the program's native record, a setting of the application's post-processing (Rule N case (c)), and the fields the template states are `None`. Post properties and arguments, output order, and split output are parameters owned by the program. NC code and post scripts are outside CADIR (Fusion stores neither).
- ISO 14649 `Parallel`, `Selective`, `If_statement`, and `While_statement` have no type: no CAD source writes them.

### 7.2 Stock and work coordinate system

```rust
pub enum StockRule {
    Relative(BoxOffsets),
    RelativeCylinder(CylinderOffsets),
    Fixed { shape: StockShape, placement: StockPlacement },
    Solid(SetSelection),
    PreviousSetup(SetupId),
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub struct BoxOffsets { pub low: [Option<ProcessDimension<Length>>; 3], pub high: [Option<ProcessDimension<Length>>; 3] }
pub struct CylinderOffsets {
    pub axis: Option<ProcessConstruction<Axis>>,
    pub radial: Option<ProcessDimension<Length>>,
    pub front: Option<ProcessDimension<Length>>,
    pub back: Option<ProcessDimension<Length>>,
}
pub enum StockShape {
    Box { size: [ProcessDimension<Length>; 3] },
    Cylinder { diameter: ProcessDimension<Length>, length: ProcessDimension<Length> },
    Tube { outer: ProcessDimension<Length>, inner: ProcessDimension<Length>, length: ProcessDimension<Length> },
}
pub enum StockPlacement { Aligned([BoxAlignment; 3]), Transform(Transform) }
pub struct BoxAlignment { pub side: Option<BoxSide>, pub offset: Option<ProcessDimension<Length>> }
pub enum BoxSide { Low, Center, High }

pub struct Wcs { pub orientation: Option<Choice<WcsOrientation>>, pub origin: Option<Choice<WcsOrigin>>, pub placement: Option<Transform> }
pub enum WcsOrientation {
    Model,
    Axes { primary: AxisSpec, secondary: AxisSpec, flips: [Option<ProcessDimension<bool>>; 3] },
    Frame(ProcessConstruction<Frame>),
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub struct AxisSpec { pub axis: FrameAxis, pub direction: ProcessConstruction<Direction> }
pub enum WcsOrigin { ModelOrigin, FrameOrigin, StockPoint(BoxPoint), ModelPoint(BoxPoint), Point(ProcessConstruction<Point>), Native(NonBlankString) }
pub struct BoxPoint { pub x: BoxSide, pub y: BoxSide, pub z: BoxSide }
```

A source states stock and WCS as a rule over the model, as a plain placement, or both.

- **Stock rules.** Fusion stores rules only, with no resolved solid or frame. `Relative` is a box around the model bounds with six offsets: Fusion `default` (whose `top 1` stock point lies at the bounds plus the offsets) and FreeCAD `StockFromBase`; a Fusion side offset binds one parameter in four slots. `RelativeCylinder` is a cylinder about `axis`, or where `axis` is `None` about the setup's z axis through the centre of the model's bounds, as long as the model's extent along that axis and as wide as the smallest such cylinder that holds the model, grown in radius by `radial` and at its +z and −z ends by `front` and `back`. Fusion's `relativecylinder` is so: it stores `job_stockLength` as the model's length along the axis, its z extent, and `job_stockDiameter` as the model's diameter about the axis, rounded up by a rounding value that is 0 in this mode (Fusion's "Round up to nearest", a setup parameter), with the radial offset outside it, and its stock front is the high-z end (`jobSafeZ_mode` `stock front`). Fusion maps `job_stockAxis` to `axis` where `job_stockAxisEnabled` is true, and `job_stockRadialOffset`, `job_stockOffsetFront`, and `job_stockOffsetBack` to the offsets; Fusion's Stock page defines the offsets' directions. That the offset grows the radius is inferred, since no stock solid is stored; and on round parts the smallest cylinder about the axis and the larger of the model's extents across it coincide, so no stored file known to the project settles which one Fusion uses (part 11). Fusion's relative tube (`relativetube`) is `StockRule::Native` with that mode name, its values setup parameters under Fusion's names (`job_stockDiameterInner` caches the model's inner diameter rounded down; Rule N case (a), part 11). `Fixed` is a box, cylinder, or tube of stated size, aligned per axis to the model bounds (Fusion `fixedbox`, `fixedcylinder`, `fixedtube`) or placed by a transform (FreeCAD `StockCreateBox` and `StockCreateCylinder`, an ISO 14649 rawpiece). `Solid` selects a design body (Fusion `solid`, a FreeCAD existing solid). A Creo manufacturing assembly states each component's role in bits of its component feature's `misc_choice[0]`: 64 the stock (Creo's workpiece, into whose model the NC sequences write their features and removed material), 32 the model the process makes, 128 a fixture (below), and 8192 a substitute: a component that the assembly holds unplaced (`placed_flag` 0) for a simplified representation to show in place of a member (every component that a status-3, 4, or 6 row's substitution table names carries it), which states no role of its own; an occurrence of a manufacturing assembly assembled on a role-32 or role-64 component at its own placement is such a substitute. The Creo stock is a `Solid` that selects the bit-64 occurrences, and the setup's `workpieces` select the bit-32 occurrences; a bit-8192 occurrence is in neither: a representation shows it only through `MemberAction::ReplaceBy` (§8.1).
- **The stock solid** is the process state `Stock(setup)` (§7.9), not part of the rule. FreeCAD stores it.
- **WCS.** `orientation` and `origin` are rules. `placement` is the WCS frame in setup space: the rules' cache where rules exist, and the only statement where the source stores a frame without a rule. An ISO 14649 setup places its workpieces and states no WCS rule, so its WCS is the identity of setup space. A Fusion WCS axis is a `ProcessConstruction<Direction>` whose input selects an edge or face, and its flip is a `ProcessDimension<bool>` of `flips`, which Fusion drives by `wcs_orientation_flipX`, `flipY`, and `flipZ`; a Fusion, Creo, or NX coordinate system is a `ProcessConstruction<Frame>` with one `Whole` `Coincident` input that picks it. Each names the workpiece whose geometry it picks (part 7). `FrameOrigin` is the origin of the `Frame` orientation (a Creo csys states both). FreeCAD has no WCS rule because its setup frame is the document frame, so a FreeCAD decoder states `Model` and `ModelOrigin`.
- A writer emits the rules, and each choice's parameter expression where it has one. A reader that needs a frame uses `placement` when present.

### 7.3 Operations

```rust
pub struct Operation {
    pub id: OperationId, pub name: Option<String>, pub comment: Option<String>,
    pub kind: OperationKind, pub native_kind: NativeName,
    pub tooling: Option<Tooling>, pub features: Vec<MachiningFeatureId>, pub groups: Vec<ProcessGroupId>,
    pub geometry: Vec<ProcessGeometry>, pub heights: BTreeMap<HeightRole, Height>, pub radii: BTreeMap<RadiusRole, Choice<RadialLimit>>,
    pub axial: BTreeMap<AxialRole, AxialLimit>,
    pub technology: Technology,
    pub tool_frame: Option<Wcs>, pub tool_axis: Option<ToolAxisControl>,
    pub leads: Option<Leads>, pub plunge: Option<PlungeStrategy>, pub linking: Option<Linking>, pub cycle: Option<CycleSettings>,
    pub suppressed: Option<ProcessDimension<bool>>, pub configuration_states: BTreeMap<ConfigurationId, bool>,
    pub optional: Option<ProcessDimension<bool>>, pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum OperationKind {
    Machining { class: OperationClass, phase: Option<Phase> },
    Modifier { modifier: ModifierKind, inputs: Vec<OperationId> },
}
pub enum Phase { Rough, SemiFinish, Finish }
pub enum OperationClass {
    Milling(MillingClass), Drilling(DrillingClass), Turning(TurningClass), Probing,
    ThreadMilling, Engraving, Chamfering, Jet, WireEdm, Additive, Unclassified,
}
pub enum MillingClass { Plane, Side, BottomAndSide, Freeform }
pub enum DrillingClass { Drilling, CenterDrilling, Countersinking, Multistep, Boring, Reaming, BackBoring, Tapping, ThreadDrilling }

pub enum ModifierKind { LeadInOut, Ramp, Tags, Dogbone, Trim, Boundary, Pattern, Transform, AxisMap, DragKnife, ProbeCorrection, Unclassified }
pub enum Tooling { Tool(ToolId), Preset(PresetId) }
pub enum ToolAxisControl {
    InPlane { plane: WorkpieceSelection },
    ThroughLine { line: WorkpieceSelection },
    NormalToSurface { surfaces: WorkpieceSelection },
    AlongRuling { surfaces: WorkpieceSelection },
    Native(NonBlankString),
}

pub struct ProcessGeometry {
    pub role: GeometryRole,
    pub source: GeometrySource,
    pub slot: Option<NonBlankString>,

}

pub enum GeometrySource {
    Selection(Vec<WorkpieceSelection>),
    Points(Vec<ProcessConstruction<Point>>),
    Direction(ProcessConstruction<Direction>),

}
pub struct ProfileCurve { pub geometry: Option<BoundedCurve>, pub source: Option<OrderedSelection> }
pub enum HeightRole { Clearance, Retract, Feed, Top, Bottom }
pub struct Height { pub from: Option<Choice<HeightFrom>>, pub offset: Option<ProcessDimension<Length>> }
pub enum RadiusRole { Outer, Inner, OuterClearance, InnerClearance, OuterRetract }

    Absolute(RadialDimension<Length, ParamRef>),

    StockOuter, StockInner, SelectionMin(NonBlankString), SelectionMax(NonBlankString),

}

pub struct AxialLimit { pub base: Choice<AxialFrom>, pub offset: Option<ProcessDimension<Length>>, pub point: Option<Choice<LimitPoint>> }

pub enum HeightFrom { Wcs, StockTop, StockBottom, ModelTop, ModelBottom, Height(HeightRole), Selection(NonBlankString), Geometry, Native(NonBlankString) }
pub struct Leads { pub entry: Option<Lead>, pub exit: Option<Lead> }
pub struct Lead {

    pub arc_radius: PLength, pub arc_sweep: PAngle, pub line_length: PLength, pub vertical_radius: PLength,
    pub line_turn: Option<Choice<LineTurn>>,
    pub from_axis: Option<ProcessDimension<bool>>, pub helical: Option<ProcessDimension<bool>>,

pub enum LineTurn { Tangent, Perpendicular, Angle { angle: ProcessDimension<Angle>, from: Option<Choice<LeadAngleFrom>>, along: Option<LeadAlong> } }
pub enum LeadAngleFrom { Cut, SpindleAxis }

pub struct PlungeStrategy { pub kind: Option<Choice<PlungeKind>>, pub angle: PAngle, pub helix_diameter: PLength, pub helix_taper: PAngle, pub start_above: PLength }

pub struct Linking {

    pub pull_out: PLength, pub pass_clearance: Option<PassClearance>,

pub struct CycleSettings {
    pub kind: Option<Choice<CycleKind>>, pub increment: PLength, pub increment_reduction: PLength,
    pub minimum_increment: PLength, pub full_retract_after: PLength, pub chip_break_retract: PLength,
    pub dwell: Option<ProcessDimension<Duration>>,
    pub depth: Option<HoleDepth>,

```

An operation is one machining step with one tool (ISO 14649 `machining_workingstep`), or a modifier of other operations' toolpaths.

- **Classification.** `class` is the ISO 14649 operation class: the milling classes of part 11 (`Plane_milling`, `Side_milling`, `Bottom_and_side_milling`, `Freeform_operation`), its drilling classes, the turning classes of part 12, and `Touch_probing`. `phase` is ISO's rough and finish split, `None` where the source does not state it. Six classes are shared by sources and absent from ISO: thread milling (Fusion `thread`, FreeCAD ThreadMilling), engraving (Fusion `engrave` and `trace`, FreeCAD Engrave and Vcarve), chamfering (Fusion `chamfer2d`, FreeCAD Deburr), jet cutting, wire EDM, and additive. ISO's machining strategy (zigzag, contour-parallel) and finer distinctions (Fusion adaptive against pocket clearing) are parameters: of the settings Fusion stores, those its stored toolpaths settle are typed (Leads to Cycle settings below, §7.5), and the pass pattern a strategy chooses is not among them (Rule N case (a), part 11). The cut direction, climb or conventional, is `Technology.cut_mode` (§7.5). Fusion `path3d` (Trace) is `Engraving`; `flat` is `Milling(Plane)` with phase `Finish`; `bore`, which mills helically with an end mill and stores no boring cycle, and `circular` are `Milling(Side)`; `turningPart` is `Turning(CuttingIn)`; FreeCAD Helix is `Milling(Side)`.
- **Native kind.** `native_kind` is the source's operation type, verbatim: a Fusion strategy string, a FreeCAD proxy class, an NX template name, a Creo sequence type. A writer to the same codec writes it; another writer chooses its kind from `class` and `phase`. The name-to-class table lives in each codec. Where a source derives the class from a parameter (a Fusion `drill` by its cycle type), that parameter is canonical and `class` is its cache.
- **Modifiers.** A modifier takes the toolpaths of its `inputs`, in order, and produces its own: FreeCAD dressups (which may be chained), FreeCAD Array and Copy, Fusion `toolpath_trim` and `subtoolpath`, Mastercam Transform and Trim. An input may be a modifier. A modifier with no `tooling` uses its first input's.
- **Tooling.** `Tool` names a tool used with no stated preset. `Preset` names a preset or tool controller (§7.6), which names its tool (a Fusion preset reference resolves to a preset of the operation's own tool). An operation with no tool has `None`.
- **Geometry** holds what the operation machines or avoids, by role. `Machine` is the drive geometry (contours, pockets, faces, holes); a source that stores no role (FreeCAD `Base`) gives `Machine`. `Exclude` removes picks (FreeCAD Drilling `Disabled`). `slot` is the source's input name where it has several of one role (Fusion `pockets`, `stockContours`). `Reference` is a geometry that a limit, a height, or a radial base names by `slot` (`RadiusFrom::SelectionMin`, `SelectionMax`, and `Positions`, and `HeightFrom::Selection`, below), and the selection the `selection back` axial base keeps: `slot` is the one home of its input name, and such geometry has role `Reference`, never `Native` with that name. A `Selection` source holds one `WorkpieceSelection` per workpiece it selects (part 7, above); each entry's selection follows §5.8: a chain keeps seed and members as a `Rule`, cached chain curves are witnesses, and a reference the source lost (as Fusion can store) is a pick with a `Native` target. `Points`, `Direction`, and `Axis` hold process constructions (part 7, above): a Fusion `CadPoint` with its reference, or a fixed point (FreeCAD `Locations`, tag positions) as a construction with no inputs (§5.9). `Start` geometry is a start point the operation uses: a start point the source stores as inactive (FreeCAD `StartPoint` with `UseStartPoint` false) is no `Start` geometry, and the point and its flag stay in the operation's native record: an inactive point leaves the toolpath unchanged (Rule N case (b)). `Profile` is planar geometry the operation owns, as solved curves with no constraints, each a `BoundedCurve` (§6.1), each with the model entities it was taken from where the source records them; a curve whose carrier the decoder did not read states `geometry: None` and keeps its place in `curves` and its `source` (Creo turning sections, which store solved entities and no dimension or constraint; Creo mill windows; CAMWorks feature sketches). A Creo turning section's `id_map` pairs each entity taken from the model with the `crv_id` of the stock model's edge it was projected from, a negative id marking an entity drawn in the section, while `ext_type` and `abs_id` locate the profile's two ends on its own entities. A Creo `source` picks that edge of the bit-64 stock occurrence (§7.2) through its occurrence context, which tells the stocks of a setup apart, and only where the edge's chord in one of its face charts equals the entity's to the model's tolerance; an id saved against a stock that later edits changed, whose geometry matches no stored edge or edges under other ids, is stated `None` by the decoder. There is no process sketch arena.
- `tool_frame` is the operation's own tool orientation, a frame rule of the setup WCS's form (§7.2) with `placement` as its resolved frame (Fusion `overrideToolView`, with its orientation and origin modes; an ISO 14649 operation's tool direction; an NX operation's tool axis). `None` uses the setup's WCS.
- **Tool axis.** `tool_axis` states how the tool axis is controlled through the operation; `None` is a fixed axis, the operation's tool frame. `InPlane`: the tool axis stays parallel to the picked plane, so the rotary axis is the plane's normal. `ThroughLine`: every position's tool axis meets the picked line at the point of the line nearest the tool's contact point on the part, so on faces parallel to the line the axis is perpendicular to it; without the contact-point rule a writer could not build the axis, which would meet the line at an angle the type leaves free. `NormalToSurface`: the tool axis is the picked surfaces' normal at the contact point. `AlongRuling`: the tool's side runs along the rulings of the picked ruled surfaces, its axis one tool radius off them (flank milling). One field holds one control, so two conflicting axis controls in one operation cannot be stated. No arm meets Rule H1's threshold of designs, so under Rule H1 the decoder states an arm only where the stored toolpath agrees with it, and `Native` with the instruction codes otherwise. Creo's carriers:
  - `InPlane`: a mill sequence with `mfg_info_ptr.attributes` bit 22 and instruction 920, whose `geometry1_id` is the plane, reached through `memb_id_tab1` where `memb_num1` is 1, a plane of another member of the reference assembly. The plane's normal is the rotary axis and no tool axis leaves the plane; no stored file known to the project settles a plane oblique to the model's axes.
  - `ThroughLine`: a bit-21 sequence with instruction 4073 followed by 4079, whose `geometry1_id` is a line: every tool-axis line of its toolpath meets the line, at every point but each path's first and last. The axis meets the line at the foot of the perpendicular from the tool's contact point, and at a right angle where the faces are parallel to the line; the contact-point rule does not meet Rule H1's threshold, so under Rule H1 the decoder states `ThroughLine` only where the toolpath's axes follow it, and `Native` with the instruction codes otherwise. The edge rows that follow it (instruction 4070, 4071, or 4076, then 4078) bound the region the tool covers, one ball radius inset, and are kept as native options of the operation until its region maps them, as is instruction 197, which names their curve feature and changes no toolpath.
  - `NormalToSurface`: a bit-21 sequence whose instruction 966 names, at offset 1.0, each surface its instruction 63 names, `surfaces` its 966 rows: the tool axis is the named surface's normal at the tips that touch it, with no lead or tilt. That the offset is an on and off flag is guessed: the fixed-axis sequences that carry 966 hold offset 0.
  - `AlongRuling`: a tool-motion sub-feature of type 1017, `surfaces` its instruction-63 rows: the tool axis runs along the ruling of the named surface, one tool radius off it; the points that depart from it near the face's end are a decoder reading (part 11).
  The named surfaces are ruled surfaces between two splines, not extrusions. A sequence's `tool_axis` is the control its tool-motion sub-feature states where it has one, so the sequence whose toolpath is a type-1017 sub-feature is `AlongRuling`, and the sequence's other axis instructions, a coordinate system (instruction 5134) or a datum point and a plane (2044 with 122), are kept as native options beside the typed arm; a sequence whose toolpath fits no form keeps its control as `Native` with the instruction codes; the coded parameters 100, 101, 236, and 259 stay in the operation's native record.
- **Leads.** `leads` states how the tool enters and leaves each cut, ending tangent to it: a straight move of `line_length` tangent to an arc of `arc_radius` that sweeps `arc_sweep` in the cutting plane, then a quarter arc of `vertical_radius` in the vertical plane that lands the tool on the cutting level along the cut; the exit mirrors the entry, a radius or length of 0 omits its motion, and `enabled: Some(false)` makes no lead. `line_turn` states the straight move's direction: `Tangent` is the tangent line, in line with what follows it; `Perpendicular` makes it meet what follows it at a right angle, perpendicular to the cut where the lead has no arc and along the arc's radius where it has one; `Angle { angle, from, along }` makes it a straight move of `line_length` whose line makes the undirected angle `angle` with the line `from` names, 0° along that line and 90° square to it: `Cut` the cut's tangent where the lead joins it, and `SpindleAxis` the spindle axis of a turning operation. Of the four moves at that angle, `along` and a side pick one, read in the order the tool runs it and in the terms of `from`: for `Cut`, `Forward` runs with the cut's direction of travel where the lead joins it and `Backward` against it, and the move lies on the cut's side away from the material; for `SpindleAxis`, and where `from` is `None`, `along` gives the axial sign, `Forward` toward the front and `Backward` toward the back, and the radial sign is away from the material's side of the pass, outward on an outside pass or a face and inward on an inside one; finishing moves are read in the cut's terms. So every combination of `from` and `along` picks one move. The stated fields leave one move where `angle` is 90°, the move square to the line on the side away from the material, and where `angle` is 0° with `from: Cut`; elsewhere they leave one where `along` is stated, read in the axis's terms where `from` is `None`. `along: None` does not state the sense. At 90° `along` has no effect, and a writer ignores it. Every move that is not bent lies on the side of the cut away from the material. The sense is a fact of the lead and not of its reference. In the axis's terms, roughing and facing entries are `Backward` and their exits `Forward`, each exit the reverse of its pass's entry whatever the cut it leaves, so facing exits leave their inward radial cuts at 45° toward the front and outward, backward to the cut. In the cut's terms, finishing entries and exits are `Forward`. Fusion stores no sense, so `along` binds no parameter. A writer whose target takes a signed lead angle computes the sign from `angle`, `from`, and `along` with the side they read; a writer whose target holds only an unsigned angle and a reference charges a loss naming the operation where `along` differs from the target's own rule. `Angle` is stated only where the source stores an angle and the lead has no arc, and an `angle` of 0° or 90° is the source's stored angle, equal in effect to `Tangent` or `Perpendicular`; `from: None` does not state the reference; `None` does not state it. A source that stores the choice as a boolean (a perpendicular flag) binds that parameter through the `Choice`. `from_axis` starts the entry on the axis of the hole or circle the pass cuts. `helical` makes the lead arcs rise along the tool axis, where `Some(false)` keeps them in the cutting plane. Fusion `doLeadIn` and `doLeadOut` with `entry_*` and `exit_*` are the two leads, `exit_sameAsEntry` copying the entry into the exit: on the contour strategies the lead arcs take `entry_radius` and `entry_verticalRadius`, on the strategies that store `verticalLeadRadius` the vertical lead arcs sit at it, so it binds `vertical_radius` there, and the line takes `entry_distance` on `contour2d` operations; an operation with `doLeadIn` false holds no lead-in move. On the strategies that store `leadRadius` (adaptive, thread, bore, and circular) it binds the entry's `arc_radius`, with two rules: on a thread, bore, or circular pass the arc's radius is the smaller of `arc_radius` and half the radius of the circle the tool centre cuts; on adaptive clearing the re-entries at the cutting level use it, and the entries from above after the vertical arc do not, following fixed shapes set by the tool diameter or a constant, which are the strategy's own and need no field. The adaptive rule is under Rule H1: the decoder binds `arc_radius` there only where the stored re-entry arcs sit at `leadRadius`, and keeps the setting as a named process parameter otherwise; off-radius arcs that match no setting of their operation are a decoder reading (part 11). No stored file known to the project settles `entry_sweep`, since at 90° a sweep and its supplement coincide, and pocket clearing scales its horizontal leads to fit between passes, so its leads are the strategy's own (part 11); `entry_perpendicular` and `exit_perpendicular` bind `line_turn`, false `Tangent` and true `Perpendicular`: with the flag false the line is tangent to the lead arc that follows it, or in line with the cut that follows it; with it true the line is perpendicular to the cut, or runs along the arc's radius. The perpendicular line with an arc is still to establish (part 11). On thread, bore, and circular passes Fusion `leadToCenter` is `from_axis`, the entry starting on the hole's axis, where `leadDistance` is the entry's `line_length` (a level straight before the lead arc), and `useHelicalLeads` is `helical`. On turning passes `exit_angle` is the exit's `angle` and `exit_distance` its `line_length`, and `entry_angle` the entry's `angle`, `exit_sameAsEntry` copying it into the exit; no stored file known to the project settles a turning lead with an arc. `from` is stated where a tapered join of the pass separates the two references, or as `Cut` where the leads agree in the cut's terms and not in the axis's (below), and is `None` elsewhere; where it is stated it is the reference the pass's leads hold, and its `Choice` binds `useFixedLeads` where the pass stores it, `true` as `SpindleAxis` and `false` as `Cut`. That binding is inferred: the setting is one of three readings that fit the separating leads, the strategy (roughing the axis, finishing and facing the cut) and the document being the other two; no stored file known to the project settles `false` as `Cut` (part 11). A tapered cut separates the two references, both ways: the leads of a profile finishing pass with no setting stored that join tapered cuts hold the stored angle to the cut, and the leads of roughing passes with `useFixedLeads` true that join tapered cuts hold it to the spindle axis. A bent lead keeps the stored length and not the angle, running close to the cut it joins, which a turn where a 45-degree move would cross the profile or a limit would explain (inferred). On axial cuts and radial cuts at 45 degrees the two references give one move. On the flat pass `leadInLinearMove` and `leadOutLinearMove` are the entry's and the exit's `line_length`. `Angle` and the flat pass's lengths are under Rule H1: the decoder states each only where the stored lead moves agree, and the setting as a named process parameter otherwise; it states `from`'s arm only where every unbent lead of the pass at a tapered join agrees with it, and `None` on a pass whose joins are all axial, or radial at 45°, which give one move under both arms; and it reads `along` only from a stored toolpath that is current against the settings, stating its arm for an entry or an exit only where every unbent move of that lead agrees with it in the terms of `from`'s arm (the axis's where `from` is `None`), and `None` where there is no toolpath, where the stored toolpath is stale, or where `angle` is 90°. Where `from` would be `None` and the lead's unbent moves agree in the cut's terms but not in the axis's, the two references do not give one move: the decoder then states `from: Cut`, read from the toolpath under Rule H1, and `along` in the cut's terms. FreeCAD's LeadInOut dressup states the same lead: its `Arc` style is the arc of `RadiusIn` sweeping `AngleIn` after a line of `ExtendLeadIn`, `ArcZ` the vertical arc, and `Tangent` the line (`Path/Dressup/Gui/LeadInOut.py`); it has no style that joins a horizontal and a vertical arc, so a FreeCAD writer charges a loss naming the operation for a lead with both.
- **Plunge.** `plunge` states how the tool enters each level: along the tool axis (`ToolAxis`), down a helix whose diameter is `helix_diameter`, measured at the tool centre (`Helix`), or along the cut (`Ramp`), descending at `angle` above the horizontal, the first entry starting `start_above` the top height, or higher by the radius of the arc through which a strategy rolls into its first ramp (ISO 14649 `Plunge_toolaxis`, `Plunge_helix`, and `Plunge_ramp`). Fusion `rampType` `plunge`, `helix`, and `profile` give no ramp move, helical arcs, and straight ramps; the slope is `rampAngle`, the helix radius half `helicalRampDiameter`, and the first ramp starts `rampClearanceHeight` above the top on `contour2d` and adaptive operations. Fusion `doRamp` binds `kind` as well: `Ramp` where true and `ToolAxis` where false. `helix_taper` is a helical ramp's stored taper angle, the angle from the tool axis at which its helix narrows downward, stated only with `kind` `Helix`: Fusion `rampTaperAngle`. A stored helix narrows by 0.94° to 0.98° at a stored 1°, a shortfall that is not explained, and by 0° at 0°, so under Rule H1 the decoder states it only where the stored helix narrows within that band (0.94° to 0.98° at 1°, 0° at 0°), and the setting as a named process parameter otherwise. Fusion's 2D and 3D pocket strategies start it higher: above the top by `rampClearanceHeight` and an excess that is constant within a document whatever the clearance, and that excess equals the lead-in radius; some start below the top, which is not explained. Where `entry_radius` and `entry_verticalRadius` are equal, each at its default of a tenth of the tool diameter, which of the two the strategy adds is not separated. `start_above` binds `rampClearanceHeight` on the pocket strategies as on the others, and `zigzag` is `PlungeKind::Native` (part 11). FreeCAD Adaptive's `HelixAngle` is `angle`; its RampEntry dressup's `Angle` is measured from the vertical, so it is 90° less `angle`.
- **Links.** `linking` states how the tool moves between two passes on one level: `stay_down` lets it link at depth, over no more than `stay_down_distance`, where the strategy finds a link clear of uncut material, else it retracts; `lift` is the height by which a link that stays down is raised above the cutting level, which links being the strategy's choice; `retract` `Full` lifts every retracting link to the retract height or above, and `Minimum` lets a link stay below it, as high as the strategy needs. Fusion `keepToolDown`, `stayDownDistance`, and `retractionPolicy` are these: with `keepToolDown` false no operation links at depth over twice the tool diameter; with it true a link at depth stays within `stayDownDistance`, which twice the tool diameter does not bound; `full` keeps no retracting link below the retract height, and `minimum` lets one stay below it. FreeCAD's pocket `KeepToolDown` is `stay_down`, and its LeadInOut `RetractThreshold` a `stay_down_distance`. Fusion's `liftHeight` is `lift`, on the stay-down links of adaptive clearing that hold a direct link move and no rapid: with `liftHeight` 0 a link rises by nothing; with it above 0 a link rises by exactly `liftHeight` or by nothing. The links that do not rise are the short ones; that the limit is 0.48 of the tool diameter is inferred. Pocket operations with a height above 0 link by ramps and transition moves and lift no link, so the setting is typed for adaptive clearing and stays a parameter elsewhere. `retractionPolicy` `shortest` is `RetractPolicy::Native`, and the minimum's `safeDistance` stays a parameter: the height at which a retracting link's rapid ends scales with it, by a factor that is not 1 and differs by policy or strategy, and no stored level gives the factor (part 11). `pull_out` is how far a turning roughing pass leaves the material at its end, at 45°, the same distance along the axis and along the radius. `pass_clearance` places a turning roughing pass's start: the pass starts `axial` in front of its front limit (`Operation.axial`'s `Front`), the tool's nose included, and where it starts against material the tool comes in rapid to `radial` short of the pass's radius and feeds the rest. Fusion `retractLength` is `pull_out` on profile roughing: a pass pulls out at 45° by it, or shorter; the groove roughing pass pulls out along the axis instead, which is not explained, and the decoder states no `pull_out` there. `clearanceZ` and `clearanceX` are `pass_clearance.axial` and `radial`; Fusion stores one value for both (`depthOfCut * 0.5`), so which drives which follows their names: the pass starts with the tool's backmost point `clearanceZ` in front of its front limit, and on the limit where neither is stored; the rapid stops `clearanceX` short of the pass radius on entries against material. Neither meets Rule H1's threshold, so under Rule H1 the decoder states each only where the stored passes agree, and the setting as a named process parameter otherwise.
- **Cycle settings.** `cycle` states, once for a drilling operation, the cycle values of §7.8 from which it generates its cycles: the kind, the peck increment, its reduction and minimum, the depth after which the tool retracts fully, the chip-break retract, and the dwell. On a probing operation it states `probe_at` and no other field. The cycle's feeds in and out are the operation's `Plunge` and `Retract` feeds. Fusion `cycleType`, `peckingDepth`, `peckingDepthReduction`, `minimumPeckingDepth`, `accumulatedPeckingDepth`, `chipBreakDistance`, and `dwellingPeriod` are these: `cycleType` names the stored cycles' kind, the peck is the cycles' increment (a stale toolpath can differ), the accumulated depth and the chip break agree with the cycles, and the cycles' plunge feed is `tool_feedPlunge` and their retract feed `tool_feedRetract`; the reduction, the minimum, and the dwell take their meanings from the cycle reference. A circular pocket milling cycle's radial step between its circles is the operation's stepover (`Technology.stepover`, §7.5), not a value of the cycle: Fusion `cycleStepover` binds it; under Rule H1 the decoder states it only where the stored cycle's stepover agrees, and the setting as a named process parameter otherwise. FreeCAD Drilling's `PeckDepth` with `PeckEnabled` is a `Deep` increment, `chipBreakEnabled` `ChipBreak`, and `DwellTime` with `DwellEnabled` the dwell; it has no reduction, minimum, accumulated depth, or chip-break distance, which a FreeCAD writer charges as losses. `probe_at` states where a probing cycle touches: `Nominal` at the feature's nominal point, `Picked` at the point picked on the face. Fusion `probe_use_selection_point`, bound through the `Choice`, false is `Nominal`, touching at the nominal point, and true is `Picked`, touching at the stored pick point; under Rule H1 the decoder states it only where the stored cycle's point agrees, and the setting as a named process parameter otherwise. `depth` states how far a drilling cycle goes below the operation's `Bottom` height: by the tip length (half the tool diameter over the tangent of half its tip angle) where `tip_through` is true, so the full diameter reaches the bottom, and then by `break_through`. Fusion `drillTipThroughBottom` and `breakThroughDepth` are these. No stored file known to the project settles `break_through` without `tip_through`, and the whole `depth` falls under Rule H1: the Fusion decoder states it only where the stored cycles' depth agrees, and `None` with both settings kept as named process parameters otherwise.
