For one `of`, states keyed `None` and states keyed `Some` do not both occur. A decoder stores content only where the source stores the state's geometry. A null stored shape (a FreeCAD `removalshape` of 0 bytes) is no stored state: the decoder emits no process state for it, since a state with an empty delta would claim an empty volume. A state with no content states the status the source records for it, or the link below. Fusion stores in-process meshes by identifier only, and the identifiers stay native.
- A Creo material-removal feature is a feature of the manufacturing model's design timeline that removes the volume an NC sequence machines. Its operation is `MaterialRemoval` (§6), which names no process record; its results are design states (§5.4). A writer whose target has no such feature writes its state as stored geometry (§3.4). Where the manufacturing model is an assembly, the feature is an assembly feature (§6.7) whose participants are the workpiece occurrences it cuts. The `Removal` state of the sequence's operation names it in `feature` (D49); Creo stores no removed volume, so that state has no content. `feature` occurs only on a `Removal` state, for a source whose material-removal result is a design feature. A decoder that states the operation whose removal a material-removal feature is, with `process` in scope, states that operation's `Removal` state naming the feature; a `MaterialRemoval` feature that no state names is one whose operation the decoder did not join to it.
- **Staleness.** Editing a design state or design parameter that an operation depends on marks `Stale` the operation's toolpaths and states (the edit helpers, §4). Editing an operation, its parameters, tooling, or features does the same, and also marks the states of later operations in machining order and the toolpaths of modifiers that take it.

## 8. The geometry and product layers

The model class holds the current geometry, `CadIr.geometry`, whose records are §5.6's, and the other arenas of `Model` (§2): products and occurrences (§8.1), presentation, drawings and PMI, physics, assets, and declared measures. Each record below is stated here, or, where this part names it without its fields, in Annex A, in the wire form of §2.5, and every quantity in it is in the canonical units of §2.3.

- **Topology.** The B-rep and carrier records and their rules are §5.6's.
- **Products and assemblies.** §8.1.
- **Instance targets.** Every model-class target that can name an instance (appearance bindings, attributes, PMI, presentation items, physics and solver targets, and the `Entity` arm of a drawing or annotation reference) is an `InstanceTarget<E>`, whose `E` is the record's target enum below (`AppearanceTarget`, `AttributeTarget`, `PmiTarget`, `PresentationItem`, `PhysicsTarget`, `SolverTarget`: a body, face, edge, product definition, occurrence, and the others), or `ReferenceEntity` for a reference.

  ```rust
  pub struct InstanceTarget<E> { pub entity: E, pub path: Option<OccurrencePath>, pub state: Option<StateRef> }
  pub struct StateRef { pub configuration: Option<ConfigurationId>, pub of: Evaluated }
  pub struct ReferenceSelection { pub target: ReferenceTarget, pub native: Option<NativeName> }
  pub enum ReferenceTarget {
      Null,
      Entity(InstanceTarget<ReferenceEntity>),
      Feature(FeatureId),
      Drawing { drawing: DrawingId, part: Option<DrawingPart> },
      Annotation(SemanticAnnotationId),
      Pmi(PmiId),
      External { document: String, object: String },
      Unresolved,
  }
  pub enum DrawingPart { Curve(u32), Unread }
  pub enum ReferenceEntity { Topology(EntityRef), Definition(ProductDefinitionId), Occurrence(OccurrenceId) }
  ```

  - `path` names the placed instance whose prototype holds `entity`, outermost occurrence first (§5.8). With `path: None` the record targets the entity in a definition that owns it, and so in every placement of that definition; a model-class record holds no definition of its own. A whole placed instance is its last occurrence as `entity` with the steps above it as `path`.
  - `state` names the state whose geometry holds `entity`, in the scope of the definition that holds it, by the `StateRef` that `DeclaredTarget::State` also uses. `state: None` is the current geometry. A target with a path and no state resolves in the geometry of the configuration that instance selects (part 9): the current geometry when that configuration is active, else that configuration's evaluation. One spelling: a target into a state that the current geometry holds, or that its path's instance selects, has `state: None`. Appearances, attributes, and PMI on the bodies of a configuration that is not active name its evaluation here, a tessellation of them names it in `Tessellation.state`, and so does each binding of an appearance that a SolidWorks display state linked to that configuration holds (§5.11). With `design` out of scope every `state` is `None` (§2.1). `set_active_configuration` rewrites `state` on the targets of the extents it exchanges (§4).
  - **References.** A drawing relationship or an annotation reference is a `ReferenceSelection`. `Entity` is an instance target whose entity reaches bodies, faces, edges, and vertices (`EntityRef`), product definitions, and occurrences, so no field holds a source's sub-element string. A decoder resolves the source's object token and sub-element string (`Edge3` of instance I) to the entity of the geometry it decoded; where it cannot, and no arm names the target, it is `Unresolved` and the source's token and string stay in `native`. `Feature` names a feature (a drawing view of a feature's result), the §2.1 case of a model record that reads the design class, absent with `design` out of scope. `External` names an object of a document that was not read, and `Null` the source's explicit empty reference. A reference into the geometry the document holds needs no name or witness, because that geometry is always in the document. `Drawing` names a drawing record: with `part: None` the record as a whole (a page's view, a section's base view, the view a balloon is attached to); with `Curve` the curve at that index of its `curves` (a view edge a dimension measures: FreeCAD `References2D` `EdgeN` of a view), stated only where the decoder establishes which curve the source's sub-element names; and with `Unread` a part of the record that the decoder did not resolve to a curve (a view vertex), the source's string staying in `native`. `Annotation` names a semantic annotation and `Pmi` a PMI annotation (a STEP `DRAUGHTING_MODEL_ITEM_ASSOCIATION` from a drawing annotation to the semantic PMI it presents). A source object that is both a drawing record and a semantic annotation is named as `Drawing`. `Unresolved` is a target the decoder did not resolve, or one that none of these arms names (a mesh, a record kept only as native); a target that an arm names is never `Unresolved`.
- A model-class record that references a record of `CadIr.geometry` resolves in the current geometry.

**Presentation.** Tessellations, appearances and their bindings, presentation layers, presentation documents, view presentations, and attributes.

```rust

- **Tessellations.** A tessellation is an indexed triangle mesh, and `of` states what it is. `Body` is a mesh the source stores to display one body of the geometry: `faces` names the faces it covers, empty where the source does not state face ownership, and its vertex positions are in the coordinates of the definition that owns the body. `Display` is a mesh the source stores to display the geometry of its `definition`, its bodies or the instances it places, tied to no one body (an NX part's JT preview, a Creo display strip, a SolidWorks display face that joins no decoded face, a STEP tessellated item that several exact bodies of one product share), in the definition's coordinates. `Definition` is a mesh that is itself geometry of its `definition`, which no B-rep holds: a mesh body (a Fusion mesh body, a FreeCAD mesh object, a Rhino mesh object, a USD `Mesh` prim, an AP242 tessellated part), in the definition's coordinates. A definition owns such a mesh as it owns its bodies, and an occurrence places it with the definition. `Pmi` is a mesh that draws its `pmi`, a presentation annotation (the filled areas of an AP242 tessellated annotation occurrence), in the coordinates its `placement` is stated in. `Unresolved` is a mesh for which the decoder establishes none of these: one that no product lists or that several list, or one whose role it did not read. It is in the coordinates of the source record that holds it, which the document does not place, and `source_object` keeps the source's association. A `Definition` mesh's `name` is the source's display name of the mesh body, `color` its own display colour (D19), and `visible` whether the source displays it (D20), as a body's are (§5.6): a Fusion mesh body's display name; a FreeCAD mesh object's `Label` and `Visibility`; a Rhino mesh object's name, its colour where the object's colour source is the object itself, and its own visibility flag. The visibility of a Rhino object's layer is the layer's (D20), and a colour that the object takes from its layer, its render material, or its parent instance is not the object's, so the mesh states no `color` for it. `colors` holds the colours a source stores per element of a mesh, of any arm, as it holds texture coordinates: one per vertex, one per triangle corner in triangle order, or one per triangle (a Rhino mesh's vertex colours, on a mesh object or on a body's display mesh). A USD `Mesh` prim's `displayColor`, with its `displayOpacity` as `a`, is the mesh's `color` where its interpolation is `constant`, and its `colors` otherwise: `vertex` and `varying` per vertex, `faceVarying` per corner, and `uniform` per triangle, each triangle taking its face's value; an indexed primvar is expanded, and where the two primvars differ in interpolation both are expanded to the finer one. A mesh that stores a colour of its own and colours per element states both. A colour the source stores as a material, or binds to a display mesh, is an appearance bound to the tessellation (Appearances, below): a USD material, a PVZ mesh appearance, an NX JT material diffuse, a SolidWorks DisplayFace colour. Where a mesh body is the whole geometry of a definition of its own that its own occurrence places, the definition and the occurrence state its names and visibility, and the mesh states neither `name` nor `visible`: the definition's `source_name` and `label` hold its source name and label, and the occurrence's `name` and `visible` its display name and visibility (§8.1). A USD `Mesh` prim is such a mesh: the prim's name is its definition's `source_name`, and its `displayName` and `visibility` are its occurrence's `name` and `visible`. So is a FreeCAD mesh object that an `App::Link` places, which states its `Label` and `Visibility` on its own occurrence (§6.7). The name of a PVZ geometry member is the name of the archive member that holds a definition's geometry: it is the `object_id` of the `source_object` of each mesh read from the member, and no body or mesh states it as `name`. The other arms state none of the three: a `Body`, `Display`, or `Pmi` mesh shows the name and visibility of what it displays (the body; the occurrences that place the definition, and the definition's `source_name` and `label`; the annotation), and a `Body` mesh the colour of its body; of an `Unresolved` mesh the decoder did not establish what it displays. A decoder states `Definition` only where the source holds no exact geometry that the mesh displays, and mints no body to carry a mesh. A writer writes a `Definition` mesh as the target's mesh body of that definition. It writes a `Body`, `Display`, or `Pmi` mesh only as the target's display data for what the mesh displays, never as geometry. It writes an `Unresolved` mesh only to the format `source_object` names, and elsewhere charges a loss naming it. For a `Body`, `Display`, or `Pmi` mesh, `state` names the state whose geometry the mesh displays, as an instance target's `state` does (`None`: the current geometry). For a `Definition` mesh, `state` names the state in which the mesh is geometry of its definition: `None` is the current geometry, and a stated state is one that holds the mesh where the current geometry does not (a mesh a later feature replaced; a mesh of a configuration that is not active, which names that configuration's evaluation). A mesh the current geometry holds is stated once, with `None`, whichever feature made it; which earlier states also hold it the document does not state (part 11). A decoder states a `Definition` mesh only where it has established one of the two. A source with no history of mesh features holds current meshes only (a FreeCAD mesh object, a Rhino mesh object, a USD `Mesh` prim, an AP242 tessellated part). A stored mesh of a source with such a history (Fusion) that the decoder has joined to neither stays in its native record (typed, carrier unread; part 11). An `Unresolved` mesh states no `state`, since the decoder did not read which geometry it belongs to. A triangle row holds zero-based vertex indices in the source's winding; a strip lists the vertex rows it spans, in mesh order. `chordal_deflection` is the source's chordal tolerance. `feature_edges` are undirected vertex-index pairs; `triangle_groups` partition the triangle ordinals into the source's face or region groups, in order, and a group's `face` names the face of the tessellation's body whose triangles it holds; `texture_assignments` assign texture assets to disjoint sets of triangle ordinals; each `TextureCoordinates` set, unique by `name` in its tessellation, holds one `(u, v)` value per vertex or per triangle corner. A channel holds a per-element payload the source stores beside the mesh: its addressing (vertex order, or one selector per corner or per triangle), the byte size of one element, the source's channel kind and flag words, and its bytes. `Tessellation` is checked (§2.8): its triangle rows and strips index its vertices, and each strip holds at least three rows. Its triangle ordinal lists are strictly increasing and name its triangles; `triangle_groups` partition them; `texture_assignments` are disjoint. A tessellation with a group that states a `face` is `of: Body`, the face is a face of that body, and the face is one of the arm's `faces` when that list is not empty. Its `TextureCoordinates` names are distinct, and each set holds one value per vertex or per triangle corner as its `addressing` states. `colors` holds one value per vertex, per triangle corner, or per triangle, as its `addressing` states; `Corner` and `Triangle` occur only on a mesh that lists its triangles. A channel's byte length is a whole number of `item_size` elements, one per vertex, or, with `Corner` or `Triangle` addressing, one per index of `indices`, which holds one index per triangle corner or per triangle. Its feature-edge pairs are canonical: each index names a vertex, in each pair the first index is below the second, and the pairs are in strictly increasing order. Its normals are one per vertex or one per triangle corner.
- **Point clouds.** A point cloud is a set of points that a source stores apart from any body or mesh: it has no topology and no triangles, and it is in the current geometry. `definition` names the product definition that holds it, in whose coordinates `positions` lie. `positions` lists the points in source order, and a point's ordinal is its identity: `normals`, `colors`, and each channel hold one entry per point in that order, or are empty where the source stores none. A normal is the vector the source stores at the point and need not be a unit vector. A colour's `a` is its opacity. A channel holds one number per point, and its `name` states the quantity: `intensity` is a point's scalar intensity. A quantity the source does not name, and the source's derived data (a fitting plane, bounds, flags), stay in the native record that `native_ref` names. `name` is the source's display name, `color` its own display colour (D19), apart from the per-point `colors`, and `visible` whether the source displays it (D20), as a body's are (§5.6). A Rhino `ON_PointCloud` is a point cloud, and only that: its points are `positions`, in millimetres; its point normals `normals`; its point colours `colors`, with `a` = 1 − alpha/255, since Rhino's alpha byte is transparency; its point values, which Rhino states are scalar intensity values, the channel `intensity`; and its object name, its colour where the object's colour source is the object itself, and its own visibility flag `name`, `color`, and `visible`. The visibility of its layer is the layer's (D20), and a colour it takes from its layer, its render material, or its parent instance is not the object's. An array whose count differs from the point count has no per-point meaning and stays in the native record. A FreeCAD points object is a point cloud: its `Points::PropertyPointKernel` is `positions`, its `Points::PropertyNormalList` `normals`, its `Points::PropertyGreyValueList`, each point's grayscale intensity, the channel `intensity`, and its `Label` and `Visibility` `name` and `visible`.
- **Appearances.** An appearance is a material or render asset: its name, its library, asset, and visual identities, its physical-material token, its schema and category, its base colour, its other shader scalars by schema property name, and its textures. A texture names its asset and the shader slot it feeds, with its 2D mapping (channel, offsets, scales, a counterclockwise `rotation`, repeat flags, real-world offsets and scales, and the tessellation texture-coordinate set it reads by name, `None` for the source's default set) and its bump or normal-map reading. A binding assigns one appearance to one target: a topology entity, a carrier, an occurrence, a product definition as a whole, a tessellation or one of its triangle groups by the tessellation's id and the group's `source_id`, or a neutral record named by its arena (the field name of its arena in §2's `Model`, §5's `Design`, or `Topology`) and id (`Record`). `Unresolved` is a target the decoder did not resolve to a record of the document: the source assigns the appearance to an object, and the decoder did not join that object to an entity it decoded, or the document holds no record of it (the owner of a SolidWorks appearance record, the object of an NX RMFastLoad colour assignment, the object a CATIA colour packet styles, the item of a STEP styled item). `Definition` is a product definition as a whole: the appearance a source assigns to a part or an assembly itself (a SolidWorks or Inventor part appearance, which a body's appearance shows through, SolidWorks' Appearance Hierarchy and Inventor's About Appearances help; a Creo part or assembly appearance; the style of a STEP component's or assembly node's shape representation, which ranks below the component's solids, inferred, part 11), which colours every entity of the definition and of the instances it places, below what the definition states on them (§4). Its binding has `path: None` and is stated in the definition it names, since a placed instance as a whole is its occurrence. `precedence` states how a binding stands against what the definitions inside the one that states it state for the entities under its target (§4). `Outer` holds over all of it, so that the binding shows whatever those definitions state: a SolidWorks component appearance, which "overrides all appearance assignments in the component's faces, features, bodies, or parts" (Appearance Hierarchy); a STEP assembly node's style, which shows on every constituent whatever the parts state (CAx-IF Recommended Practices for Model Styling and Organization, §4.2.1); a CATIA product's colour, which overrides the child's (About Color Determination); a FreeCAD link's `OverrideMaterial`, which applies the link's appearance to every face of the linked object; and a USD binding `strongerThanDescendants` (`UsdShadeMaterialBindingAPI`). `Nearest` holds over what they state on its own target or a farther one, and under what they state on a nearer one: a USD binding `weakerThanDescendants`, the default. A USD binding on a prim that the document states as an occurrence is stated on that occurrence, with `path: None`; one inside a definition is resolved to the bodies and tessellations it reaches, by its strength. The values of other sources are inferred from what their vendors' staff and users report, and from no stored file (part 11): `Outer` for a STEP instance's style, an Inventor or NX component's override, and a Creo component's appearance in an assembly; `Nearest` for a Creo assembly's own appearance and for a Fusion occurrence's or root component's appearance override, which a body's or a face's appearance inside the component shows through. A binding states `precedence` exactly where a definition inside the one that states it can state a nearer target: on an `Occurrence`, on a `Definition` that owns an occurrence, and on a `Body` or a `Tessellation` with a `path`; on every other binding it is `None`. A writer to a format that orders such a statement the other way writes, for the entities under the binding's target, the colours `effective_display_color` resolves, on the targets its format shows them on, and charges a loss naming the binding where an entity under it then shows another colour. The binding states what the decoder read of the object: `source_entity_id` where it read the source's identity of the object, and `native_ref`, the native record that holds the assignment. A writer of the binding's codec may re-emit that native record (W2, §3.4); a writer that does not applies no `Unresolved` binding and charges a loss naming it. `visible: Some(false)` states that the target is not displayed through this binding (a STEP styled item that an `INVISIBILITY` names), which hides it (§4). `source_entity_id`, `object_type`, and `channels` are the source's identity, type, and change-version channels for the assigned entity, never for the record that assigns it or for the appearance. Beside a resolved target they are Rule N case (b); on an `Unresolved` binding `source_entity_id` is the one statement of which object is assigned, a typed fact whose join is unread (§3.1). An appearance's shader scalars, keyed by their schema's property names, and its texture schemas belong to one application's render-material model, which has no neutral home by scope, as lights do (Rule N case (c)).
- **Layers and view state.** A presentation layer has a name, a parent layer, a description, and a visibility (D20), and lists the items assigned to it, in no meaningful order, `Source` naming a source item that no neutral type models; a hidden layer hides the items of the layers below it through `parent` (Rhino sublayers). A presentation document holds a source's document-wide GUI state: its schema version, its active view, and its ordered states, each a camera (position, and orientation as an axis and an angle, nonzero) or a `Native` state element by its source name, with its attributes and the display assets it names: GUI state, an application setting (Rule N case (c)). FreeCAD's `<Expand>` element of `GuiDocument.xml` lists the expanded tree items: it is `expanded` on each, not a presentation state. A view presentation is the persisted display state of one source object (a FreeCAD view provider): the object, its order, its tree expansion, its visibility (canonical over a `Visibility` property, D22), display mode, selection style, line width, point size, and its other properties by source name.
- **Attributes.** A source attribute attaches a name and an ordered list of typed values to one target, each value `null` where the source states none at that position. An attribute is the home of every user-visible source property that no typed field holds (§5.12, D3), and every writer writes it. A decoder never states a record's native value as a `SourceAttribute`: it goes to the record's native maps (the `native_options` and `source_settings` of an operation, a PMI annotation, or a parameter, §6, §8, and §5.12). A value is a number, text, a Boolean, a numeric vector, an ordered map with repeated keys kept, a typed JSON tree, a link to a local object (`Reference`, by the source's object name; `SubReference`, with sub-element names; `EmptyReference`, an empty link slot) or to an object of another document (`ExternalReference`), or `Parameter`, the design parameter that a property is where the source states its value by an expression: a link to a dimension, a parameter, or a measure, or an expression bound to the property (§5.12). An attribute on a `Configuration` target is that configuration's value of the like-named attribute of its scope's definition: the part-attribute columns of an NX part family are attributes on the configuration, user string attributes of the family's template.

**Drawings and PMI.** Drawings (sheets, views, curves, templates), semantic annotations, and PMI.

pub struct SemanticAnnotation {

    pub object: String,
    pub kind: SemanticAnnotationKind,
    pub runtime_type: String,
    pub order: u32,
    pub text: Vec<String>,
    pub references: BTreeMap<NonBlankString, Vec<ReferenceSelection>>,
    pub value: Option<FiniteReal>,
    pub reference_anchors: Vec<[FiniteReal; 2]>,
    pub text_style: AnnotationTextStyle,
    pub format: Option<String>,
    pub number_format: Option<NumberFormat>,
    pub position: Option<[FiniteReal; 3]>,
    pub dimension_kind: Option<AnnotationDimensionKind>,
    pub text_override: Option<String>,
    pub upper_tolerance: Option<FiniteReal>,
    pub lower_tolerance: Option<FiniteReal>,
    pub measured_on: Option<MeasuredOn>,
    pub basic: Option<bool>,
    pub reflex: Option<bool>,
    pub negated: Option<bool>,
    pub line_directions: Option<LineDirections>,
    pub parameters: BTreeMap<NonBlankString, String>,
    pub assets: Vec<String>,
    pub native_ref: String,
}
pub enum SemanticAnnotationKind { Dimension, Text, Balloon, Leader, Symbol, Other }
pub struct AnnotationTextStyle { pub height: Option<PositiveLength>, pub font_family: Option<String> }
pub enum MeasuredOn { Model, View }
pub struct LineDirections { pub dimension_line: Angle, pub extension_lines: Angle }
pub enum AnnotationDimensionKind {
    Distance, HorizontalDistance, VerticalDistance, Radius, Diameter, Angle, ThreePointAngle,
    Area { holes_excluded: Option<bool> },
    Extent { axis: ViewAxis },
    Other { native_type: String },
}
pub struct NumberFormat { pub prefix: String, pub suffix: String, pub decimals: Option<u8>, pub trim_zeros: bool, pub round_to: Option<FiniteReal>, pub unit_shown: Option<bool> }

pub struct PmiAnnotation {
    pub id: PmiId,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub visible: Option<bool>,
    pub targets: Vec<InstanceTarget<PmiTarget>>,
    pub definition: PmiDefinition,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
    pub native_options: NativeOptions,
    pub source_settings: NativeOptions,
}
pub enum PmiTarget {
    Body { body: BodyId }, Face { face: FaceId }, Edge { edge: EdgeId }, Vertex { vertex: VertexId },
    Point { point: PointId }, Curve { curve: CurveId }, Product { product: ProductDefinitionId },
    Occurrence { occurrence: OccurrenceId }, ShapeAspect { source_id: NonBlankString },
}

    Datum { identification: String },

    GeometricTolerance {

        magnitude: PmiMagnitude,

        defined_area_unit: Option<String>,
        defined_area_second_unit: Option<PmiValue>,
        datum_system: Option<PmiId>,
        modifiers: Vec<String>,
        displacement: Option<Length>,
        maximum_upper: Option<PositiveLength>,
        zones: Vec<ToleranceZone>,
    },
    Dimension(PmiDimension),
    Presentation { text: Option<String>, placement: Option<Transform>, semantics: Vec<PmiId> },

pub struct ToleranceZone { pub form: ToleranceZoneForm, pub projections: Vec<ToleranceProjection> }
pub enum ToleranceZoneForm { CylindricalOrCircular, Spherical, Other(String) }
pub struct ToleranceProjection { pub boundaries: Vec<InstanceTarget<PmiTarget>>, pub end: InstanceTarget<PmiTarget>, pub length: PositiveLength, pub offset: Option<Length> }
pub struct PmiDimension { pub dimension: PmiDimensionKind, pub nominal: Option<Dimension<PmiValue>>, pub tolerance: Option<Tolerance>, pub decimals: Option<u8>, pub modifiers: BTreeSet<DimensionModifier> }

    Straightness, Flatness, Roundness, Cylindricity, Coaxiality, LineProfile, SurfaceProfile, Angularity,

```

- **Drawings.** A drawing record is a page, template, view, projection, section, detail, or drawing annotation (`kind`), with the application object and the exact runtime type that persist it and its order among the drawing records. `views` lists the drawing records a page shows or a view collection holds (FreeCAD `DrawPage.Views`, and the `Views` of a projection group or a clip group; a STEP sheet revision's views), in source order, or in id order where the source's list is a set (STEP). A record may be listed by more than one page. `base_view` is the view a section or detail view is cut or magnified from (FreeCAD `BaseView`). `template`, `views`, and `base_view` are the one home of the source properties they state: `relationships` holds an entry of such a property only where its target is no drawing record of the kind the field names (an explicit empty link, an external object, a non-template object), and then as that `ReferenceSelection`. `relationships` groups `ReferenceSelection`s (below) by the source property that holds them. A page states its template. A view states its origin on the page (`position`), its `scale`, its model projection `direction` and horizontal model axis `x_direction` (each nonzero), its counterclockwise `rotation` on the page, and its curves in source order, in the view frame (x right, y up, before scale and rotation), each with its hidden-line class, its presentation visibility apart from that class, and its source class. A page states its sheet size and its title-block fields; a template its page-space curves and positioned texts, each text with its height, or `height: None` where the source gives none and the renderer's default size applies (an SVG text with no `font-size`). `scale_from` states where a view's scale comes from: the sheet's (`Sheet`), a scale chosen to fit the sheet (`Fit`), or the view's own `scale` (`Own`). `projection` is a sheet's or a projection group's projection angle, first or third, a group with `None` taking its sheet's. `perspective` makes a view a perspective projection at that focus distance. `edge_classes` states which edge classes a view's hidden-line projection draws besides its visible hard edges, which every projection draws: `drawn` holds each class drawn, among visible smooth, seam, and iso-parameter lines and hidden hard, smooth, seam, and iso lines, and a class it does not hold is not drawn; `iso_count` is the number of iso lines (FreeCAD TechDraw `DrawView`, `DrawPage`, `DrawProjGroup`, and `DrawViewPart` at 1.1.4: `SmoothVisible`, `SeamVisible`, `IsoVisible`, `HardHidden`, `SmoothHidden`, `SeamHidden`, `IsoHidden`, and `IsoCount`). `parameters` keeps the other values by source name. Some have no design meaning (FreeCAD `LockPosition`, a UI lock, `KeepUpdated`, a rebuild policy, and the caches `BoxCorners` and `SavedGeometry`: Rule N case (b)). `hidden_line` states how a view's hidden-line projection computes its curves: `Exact` from the exact geometry, `Polygonal` from the shape's triangulation, so every curve is drawn as a chain of line segments (FreeCAD `CoarseView` true). FreeCAD's `ScrubCount` runs passes that remove projected edges lying on other projected edges and leaves the drawn point set unchanged, so it stays in `parameters` with no design meaning (case (b)) (FreeCAD 1.1.4 `DrawViewPart.cpp` and `GeometryObject.cpp`).
- **Semantic annotations.** A semantic annotation is the meaning of a drawing annotation apart from its appearance: its kind, its text fragments, its references grouped by source role, the measured `value` it stores, its page-space reference anchors (at most one point, or two on a `Dimension` with a `dimension_kind`: its two end anchors), its text height and font, its format, its position, its dimension kind (`Other` with the source's selector), its override text, and its tolerances. `measured_on` states whether a dimension measures the model's references (`Model`) or the view's projected geometry divided by the view's scale (`View`); `basic` marks a theoretically exact dimension; `reflex` states that an angle dimension gives the reflex angle, 2π less the measured one. An `Area` dimension measures one face: without its holes where `holes_excluded` is true, the area inside its outer boundary where false (FreeCAD TechDraw `DrawViewDimension` `MeasureType`, `TheoreticalExact`, `Inverted`, and `UseActualArea` at 1.1.4). `negated` states that a dimension that is not an angle shows the negative of its measured value (FreeCAD `Inverted` on a length: 30.0 shows −30.00 mm; on an angle `Inverted` is `reflex`, 90° showing 270.00°). `line_directions` lays out a distance dimension's lines: the dimension line along `dimension_line` and the extension lines along `extension_lines`, angles in the view plane counterclockwise from the view's x axis, the measured value unchanged (FreeCAD `AngleOverride` true with `LineAngle` and `ExtensionAngle`; false is `None`). A `number_format`'s `unit_shown` appends the unit symbol to a length's shown number (FreeCAD `ShowUnits`: 30.00 against 30.00 mm; an angle always shows °) (FreeCAD 1.1.4 `DrawViewDimension.cpp`, `DimensionFormatter.cpp`, and `QGIViewDimension.cpp`). FreeCAD's `DistanceZ`, which FreeCAD 1.1.4 gives no value, stays `Other` with its name (case (b)). `number_format` is the meaning of the source's `format` text where a decoder parses it: `prefix` and `suffix` around the number, `decimals` the digits after the point, `trim_zeros` the removal of trailing zeros and a trailing point, and `round_to` a rounding to that increment, printed with its decimals; a writer of the source's codec writes `format`, and another writer writes from `number_format`. FreeCAD's `FormatSpec` `%.Nf` is `decimals: N`, `%.Nw` `decimals: N` with `trim_zeros`, and `%Xr` `round_to: X`, the text around the specifier being the prefix and suffix; a specifier of another conversion leaves `number_format` `None`. `Arbitrary` true makes `FormatSpec` the shown text, `text_override`, and `EqualTolerance` true states `lower_tolerance` as the negated `upper_tolerance`, which the two fields hold (FreeCAD 1.1.4 `DimensionFormatter.cpp`). A FreeCAD balloon's `Text` at (`OriginX`, `OriginY`) of its view is `text` with one reference anchor; a rich annotation's `AnnoText` is `text`; a landmark dimension measures 3D points (`measured_on: Model`); and `Extent` measures the extent of its edges, or of every edge of the view, along the view's x or y (`DrawViewDimExtent`). A leader's way points stay in `parameters`, since a leader holds at most one anchor, and balloon and leader shapes, end symbols, kinks, wraps, scales, and frames are presentation (Rule N case (c)).
- **PMI.** A PMI annotation is one semantic or presentation annotation of the model, with the entities it qualifies: a datum and its identifier; a datum system, its datum references ordered by `precedence` from 1, the references of one precedence forming one compartment; a datum target, its form, and its basis; a geometric tolerance, with its characteristic, its zone magnitude, its zone units, its datum system, and its modifiers; a dimension; or a presentation, with its text, its placement, and the semantic annotations it depicts. An annotation's `native_options` and `source_settings` hold its native values by Rule N case, with the meaning an operation's have (§6): `native_options` the values whose meaning is not established (case (a)) and those of typed facts whose carrier is unread (§3.1), and `source_settings` those with no design meaning (case (b)). A `PmiValue` is a number and its quantity: a `Length`, an `Angle`, or a dimensionless `Ratio`; `PmiMagnitude` is checked (§2.8): its value is not negative. `DatumReferences` is checked (§2.8): the references of one compartment have the same `common_group`; a compartment of one reference states none, a compartment of several states one, and no two compartments state the same group. A dimension's `nominal` is a `Dimension<PmiValue>` (D28): a literal, or the design parameter that drives the annotation, whose kind is the nominal's quantity; `tolerance` is the dimension's tolerance, `Tolerance` as §5.12 defines it: deviations, a fit, the general tolerance, a basic dimension, or a single limit. `decimals` is the key the rule by decimals looks the dimension up by (`ByDecimals`, §8.1), a stored fact of the semantic dimension (Rule N), and not the places it displays: where a source stores that number apart from the places it displays, the stored key decides the tolerance in force, and displayed places that differ from it are case (b), kept in the annotation's `source_settings`. SolidWorks stores the key on each DimXpert dimension record as `BlockToleranceDecimalPlaces`, apart from the displayed precision of its semantic dimension records (`DimSemData.valPrecision`), which is `sldprt:val_precision`; the SolidWorks decoder reads `decimals` from the DimXpert record (part 11). A source that stores no separate key states its displayed places as the key, which is inferred: a rule by decimals keys on the places shown. STEP AP242 qualifies a dimension's nominal with `VALUE_FORMAT_TYPE_QUALIFIER` (`NR2 x.y`, the digit after the point the places; `NR2S` is the signed form for tolerance values). Creo states `decimals` on parameters only (§5.12): its decoder mints no `PmiDimension` for a model dimension (below). Where `nominal` binds a parameter, the parameter's `tolerance` and `decimals` are canonical (D60, D61): the dimension states a `tolerance` of its own only where it differs from the parameter's, compared as values, an equal one being a Warning, and a `decimals` of its own only where it differs from the parameter's. D61 alone governs a bound dimension, whatever the arm, `General`, `Basic`, and `SingleLimit` included. `Basic` and `SingleLimit` qualify the nominal, so they occur only where `nominal` is stated, and `General` needs a stated `nominal` under `Iso2768`, which looks up its size range (§8.1). A STEP file has no parameters, so its basic and single-limit dimensions bind none: AP242's `theoretical` note is `Basic`, and its `maximum` qualifier is `SingleLimit(Maximum)` (a drawing shows such a radius as "2X R0.1 MAX"); a SolidWorks DimXpert kind 1 record is `Basic`. A PMI dimension's tolerance is in the dimension's quantity, which comes from `dimension`: `Angular` is an angle, every other kind but `Other` is a length, and `Other` has its `nominal`'s, or none where `nominal` is not stated. A stated `nominal`'s quantity agrees with `dimension`: `Angular` takes an angle, every other kind but `Other` a length, and only `Other` may take a `Ratio` (part 10). On a PMI dimension a `Deviations` is in the canonical unit of that quantity and states the deviations about the nominal, each the limit less the nominal, so a deviation below the nominal is negative. A source that displays the tolerance as limits, the least and the greatest value the dimension may take, states the same `Deviations`, and the display form is kept in the annotation's `source_settings` (case (b)), as the parameter side keeps `creo:tol_type` (§5.12). A source that stores a designation states `Fit`, its stored deviations in `deviations` with the arm §5.12 gives them (`Cell`, `Own`, or `Unchecked`), so the designation stays typed whatever deviations it stores. A designation whose stored deviations are both 0 states `deviations: None`: the designation is the fact, and a 0/0 pair is neither the designation's cell nor deviations of the source's own (§5.12). `General` states that a dimension has no tolerance of its own and takes the `general_tolerance` of its annotation's context definition (§8.1) by its quantity, under `ByDecimals` the entry at its `decimals`, so `General` needs a context definition (part 10). A PMI annotation's context definition derives from what is stored and no field holds it (Rule D): for a target with a `path`, the definition that holds the path's first occurrence, and for a target with no `path`, the definition that owns the target entity: for a vertex, an edge, a face, or a body the definition holding the body, for a point the definition holding the body of each vertex whose `point` it is, for a curve the definition holding the body of each edge whose carrier it is and of each coedge whose `use_curve` it is, for a `Product` target the definition it names, and for an `Occurrence` target the definition holding that occurrence. A vertex's body is the body of an edge it ends, of the face whose loop uses it, or of the shell that holds it free; an edge's is the body of the face whose loop holds a coedge of it, or of the shell that holds it as a wire edge; a face's is the body of the region its shell bounds. A point or a curve has no owner field, so one that no vertex, edge, or coedge uses has no context definition, as a `ShapeAspect` target or an annotation with no target has none. Every context definition of one annotation's targets is the same one (part 10), so a dimension authored in an assembly between two parts' faces takes the assembly's rule. The vendor's block and general block tolerances are rules of this kind, applied by SolidWorks DimXpert "on dimensions that do not contain tolerances" of its annotation dimensions; the SolidWorks decoder states no `general_tolerance` while the stored form of the method in force is not located (§8.1), so it states no `General` either, and no other source known to the project stores a general tolerance for annotation dimensions. A CATIA 3D-annotation dimension that names the class `ANSI B4.3-1978-f` can store its own asymmetric limits, which no symmetric class value equals. Such a dimension whose nominal binds, by inference, the feature parameter whose stored pair equals its own takes the parameter's `Deviations` as its tolerance, and the class name is the parameter's native option (§5.12). Such a dimension that is oriented, binds no parameter, and stores no nominal states its own `Deviations` as a length, the quantity its kind gives, and the class name is kept in the annotation's `native_options` (case (a); part 11). A `LimitsAndFits` is a limits-and-fits designation: `form_variance` the fundamental deviation's letter, stored in capitals, `zone` the feature it applies to, a hole (`Hole`) or a shaft (`Shaft`), `grade` the tolerance grade, and `source` the standard whose table defines it, where the source names one. `FitStandard` has one spelling per standard: `Iso286` is ISO 286, the standard of Creo fits (§5.12) and of the cells SolidWorks fits equal. `AnsiB41` is ANSI B4.1, which defines it, typed so that two decoders do not spell it two ways: no stored file known to the project names it, and no decoder states it (Inventor fits that equal its cells name no standard). `Native` holds any other standard's name as the source spells it. Where an annotation stores a hole and a shaft designation together, `Fit`'s `fit` is the designation of the feature the dimension sizes and `mate` the mating designation, whose `zone` is the other (§5.12). Which one the dimension sizes comes from the stored order, the first being the dimension's own, which is inferred: the Inventor designation record holds its `hole_fit` slot before its `shaft_fit` slot, and nothing states which one a dimension sizes; the SolidWorks and Inventor records each have the two slots. A decoder states `source` only where the source names the standard, and a cell match fills nothing (§2.4): no SolidWorks or Inventor dimension record names one, so their fits state `source: None`. `deviations` is read, not computed, under one rule for every format (§5.12): a SolidWorks or Inventor fit whose deviations equal the standard's cell states `Cell`, and one whose deviations differ states `Own`, its designation staying typed; a fit that states `deviations` and no `source` is legal. A writer to a target that holds fits writes a PMI dimension's `fit` and `mate`, writes the deviations as the target's override where they are `Own`, or where the target's own cell differs from `Cell` or `Unchecked`, and charges `export:fit.restated` naming the annotation where it cannot; a writer to a target without fits writes the deviations. A designation has one spelling, its letter and its grade stated apart: a decoder that meets the combined form, the letter and grade whole in `form_variance` with an empty `grade` (`G6`), splits it, and the normalizer (§3.1) splits it in the same way. `zone` is the one home of the feature: `form_variance` is stored in capitals, and a writer spells the letters by `zone` where the standard uses case (ISO 286: capitals for a hole, small letters for a shaft). A STEP decoder reads as a dimension only ISO 10303's `dimensional_size`, `dimensional_location`, `angular_size`, and `angular_location` and their subtypes: `PRESENTATION_SIZE` sizes a presentation area, and the `*_ELEMENT_LOCATION` entities of AP209 files are finite-element analysis records. `DirectedLocation` is a `Location` measured from an origin to a target: its annotation's first target is the origin and its second the target. `CurveLength` is the length along the picked curve between its ends: a Creo `Arc Length` dimension. A Creo model dimension's tolerance is in the dimension's own record (`tol_ptr`), and every model dimension stores such a record, so a record is not a dimension the model presents, and the Creo decoder mints no `PmiDimension` for a model dimension: the record gives the dimension's parameter its `tolerance`, its `decimals`, and its native options as §5.12 states, and the model's settings give the definition's `general_tolerance` (§8.1). No stored file known to the project shows a configuration that overrides a tolerance. A STEP decoder maps `DIRECTED_DIMENSIONAL_LOCATION`, alone or in a complex instance, to it with the relating shape aspect first, as ISO 10303's `shape_dimension_schema` defines it ("measured from the origin, given by relating_shape_aspect, to the target, given by related_shape_aspect"), and a STEP writer writes the origin as the relating aspect. An exporter may name its relating aspect `ORIGIN`, and a file exported from CATIA V5 can store as related the datum face its own presentation draws as the origin (part 11). An `Area` or `Curve` datum target is a region given explicitly by the faces or curves `basis` names, which need not lie on the part (CAx-IF Recommended Practices for PMI 4.1, §6.6.2).
- **Tolerance zones and dimension modifiers.** `displacement` is the offset of an unequally disposed tolerance zone from the true profile, positive toward the outside of the material (ISO 1101, the UZ modifier). `maximum_upper` is the largest value that a tolerance with a maximum- or least-material modifier may take: it exceeds the magnitude and occurs only with such a modifier. `zones` states the forms of the tolerance zone: `CylindricalOrCircular`, a zone within a cylinder or within a circle; `Spherical`, a zone within a sphere; `Other`, the source's name of another form. A zone's `projections` each state a projected zone: it extends `length` from the toleranced feature toward the shape aspect `end`, bounded by `boundaries`, and starts `offset` from the feature where the source states an offset. Zones and projections are in source order, which carries no meaning. Each of these fields is the one home of its fact: a decoder that states `displacement`, `maximum_upper`, or a zone writes no modifier text for it into `modifiers`. A STEP decoder reads `UNEQUALLY_DISPOSED_GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE.displacement`, `GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE_WITH_MAXIMUM_TOLERANCE.maximum_upper_tolerance`, the `TOLERANCE_ZONE_FORM` names `cylindrical or circular` and `spherical`, and each `PROJECTED_ZONE_DEFINITION` of a zone, with its offset in the `PROJECTED_ZONE_DEFINITION_WITH_OFFSET` form; a SolidWorks `GdtPosition.ZoneType` 2 is a `Spherical` zone. `SphericalDiameter` and `SphericalRadius` size a sphere, and their quantity is a length (STEP `DIMENSIONAL_SIZE` named `spherical diameter` or `spherical radius`; a SolidWorks diameter or radius whose one direct feature reference is a sphere). A dimension's `modifiers` qualify it. They are a set (§2.5), so each is stated once and their order carries no meaning: `Reference`, a dimension given for information only (STEP's `auxiliary` dimensional note); `Statistical`, a tolerance applied by statistical process control (`statistical`); `ControlledRadius`, a radius with no flats or reversals within its tolerance zone (`controlled radius`), each as ASME Y14.5 Dimensioning and Tolerancing defines it; and `Other`, the source's text of another modifier. A basic dimension is `tolerance: Some(Basic)` and no modifier (above).

**Physics.** Materials, mass properties, rigid bodies, colliders, articulations, scenes, and solver settings.

```rust
pub struct PhysicalMaterial {
    pub id: PhysicalMaterialId,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub density: Option<PositiveReal>,
    pub static_friction: Option<NonNegativeReal>,
    pub dynamic_friction: Option<NonNegativeReal>,
    pub restitution: Option<NonNegativeReal>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub struct MassProperties {
    pub id: MassPropertiesId,
    pub target: InstanceTarget<PhysicsTarget>,
    pub mass: Option<PositiveReal>,
    pub density: Option<PositiveReal>,
    pub center_of_mass: Option<FinitePoint3>,
    pub inertia: Option<PrincipalInertia>,
    pub material: Option<PhysicalMaterialId>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub struct PrincipalInertia { pub moments: [NonNegativeReal; 3], pub axes: Option<Transform> }
pub enum PhysicsTarget { Body { body: BodyId }, Occurrence { occurrence: OccurrenceId }, Definition { definition: ProductDefinitionId } }
pub struct RigidBody {
    pub id: RigidBodyId,
    pub target: InstanceTarget<PhysicsTarget>,
    pub kinematic: bool,
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub linear_velocity: Option<FiniteVector3>,
    pub angular_velocity: Option<FiniteVector3>,
    pub starts_asleep: bool,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub struct Collider {
    pub id: ColliderId,
    pub target: InstanceTarget<PhysicsTarget>,
    pub shape: ColliderShape,
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub material: Option<PhysicalMaterialId>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum ColliderShape { Exact, ConvexHull, ConvexDecomposition, BoundingBox, BoundingSphere, Simplified, Native { name: String } }
pub struct Articulation { pub id: ArticulationId, pub root: InstanceTarget<PhysicsTarget>, pub native_ref: Option<String> }
pub struct PhysicsScene {
    pub id: PhysicsSceneId,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub gravity_direction: Option<UnitVector3>,
    pub gravity_magnitude: Option<NonNegativeReal>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub struct SolverSettings {
    pub id: SolverSettingsId,
    pub solver: String,
    pub schema: String,
    pub target: InstanceTarget<SolverTarget>,
    pub values: BTreeMap<String, SolverValue>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum SolverTarget {
    Scene { scene: PhysicsSceneId }, Occurrence { occurrence: OccurrenceId }, Definition { definition: ProductDefinitionId },
    Body { body: BodyId }, Collider { collider: ColliderId }, Joint { joint: FeatureId },
    PhysicalMaterial { material: PhysicalMaterialId }, Articulation { articulation: ArticulationId },
}
pub enum SolverValue {
    Bool { value: bool },
    Integer { value: i64 },
    Real { value: FiniteReal, dimension: Quantity },
    Unbounded { negative: bool },
    Reals { values: Vec<FiniteReal>, dimension: Quantity },
    Token { value: String },
    Tokens { values: Vec<String> },
    Targets { targets: Vec<InstanceTarget<SolverTarget>> },
}
```

- A material holds the bulk and contact properties of a substance: its density, its static and dynamic friction, and its restitution. Densities are kilograms per cubic millimetre (§2.3).
- Mass properties describe one target: its mass, its density, its centre of mass in the target's coordinates, its principal moments of inertia with the frame of their axes, and its material. A stated mass takes precedence over a density, and a density over the material's. The base material of a definition or body (§5.11) is the `material` of the mass-properties record that targets it. A source's stored mass and centre of mass (a SolidWorks part's) are `MassProperties`; its stored volume is a declared measure (below).
- A rigid body is a target that a simulation moves as one: `kinematic` moves it only by its animated placement, `enabled` includes it, and its initial velocities are in the coordinates its target's placement maps into; `starts_asleep` holds it at rest until a contact or a force wakes it. A collider is the contact geometry of a target, with its shape and its contact material; `BoundingBox` is a box fitted to the target's geometry (UsdPhysics `boundingCube`: "An optimally fitting box collider is computed around the mesh", `schema.usda`). An articulation names the root of a tree of rigid bodies that joints connect and a simulation solves as one system. A scene states the gravity on its rigid bodies: its direction, against the up axis where `None`, and its magnitude, standard gravity where `None`.
- Solver settings hold the properties that one solver schema (`physx`, with an instance name where the schema applies more than once, as in `PhysxLimitAPI:angular`) states for one target, by schema name: one engine's settings, with no neutral home by scope (Rule N case (c)). A `Real` or `Reals` value is in canonical units of its `dimension`, a `Quantity` (§5.12). A solver setting that targets a joint names the `FeatureId` of a `Joint` feature (`SolverTarget::Joint`); `JointId` and the `assembly_joints` arena do not exist (D30).

**Assets and declared measures.**

```rust
pub struct Asset { pub id: AssetId, pub name: Option<NonBlankString>, pub media_type: Option<NonBlankString>, pub content: AssetContent, pub native_ref: Option<String> }
pub enum AssetContent { Embedded { data: Base64Bytes }, External { uri: NonBlankString } }
pub struct DeclaredMeasure {
    pub id: DeclaredMeasureId,
    pub target: DeclaredTarget,
    pub quantity: DeclaredQuantity,
    pub label: Option<String>,
    pub basis: Option<MeasureBasis>,
    pub precision: Option<NonNegativeReal>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum MeasureBasis { Validation, Cache }
pub enum DeclaredTarget { Definition { definition: ProductDefinitionId }, Bodies { bodies: Vec<BodyId> }, State(StateRef), Unresolved }
pub enum DeclaredQuantity {
    Volume { value: FiniteReal },
    SolidArea { value: FiniteReal },
    WettedArea { value: FiniteReal },
    SolidCentroid { value: FinitePoint3 },
    SheetArea { value: FiniteReal },
    SheetCentroid { value: FinitePoint3 },
}
```

- An asset is a resource that model, drawing, or presentation records name: bytes embedded in the document, or an external resource by its URI, with its display name and IANA media type.
- A declared measure states a quantity that the source stores for its own bodies, so that a reader can compare it with what it measures on the geometry: the enclosed volume of the solids, the area of every face of the solids or of their outer shells only (`WettedArea`), the centroid of their volume, the area of the sheets, or the centroid of the sheets' area. Its target is a definition's bodies in the definition's coordinates (a solid quantity covers its solids and a sheet quantity its sheets, and a body whose `visible` is false is not covered), listed bodies, a state of the design (`State`, whether or not that state's geometry is stored), or `Unresolved`, a target the source names that resolves to no bodies. `label` is the description the source stores with it. It holds only a quantity that no physics record holds: a source's stored mass and centre of mass are `MassProperties`, never a declared measure. `basis` states whether the value can predate the bodies: `Validation`, a value written with the bodies for a reader to check a transfer against (a STEP validation property); `Cache`, the source's own last computation, which an edit after it leaves stale (the volume and area a SolidWorks part stores with its mass properties). `None` states neither. `precision` is the bound within which the stored value holds the value the source computed, in the quantity's canonical unit and for each coordinate of a centroid: a value stored with six fractional digits holds it within half a unit of its last digit.
- **Native namespaces.** Format id → arena → ID-sorted records; `unknowns` holds given-up parts' stubs.

### 8.1 Products, occurrences, and documents

```rust
pub struct ProductDefinition {
    pub id: ProductDefinitionId,
    pub kind: Option<ProductDefinitionKind>,
    pub source_name: Option<String>,
    pub label: Option<String>,
    pub description: Option<String>,
    pub part_number: Option<String>,
    pub bom_properties: BTreeMap<NonBlankString, String>,
    pub generated_from: Option<GeneratedFrom>,
    pub storage: Storage,
    pub bodies: Vec<BodyId>,
    pub occurrences: Vec<OccurrenceId>,
    pub instance_bodies: Vec<InstanceBodies>,
    pub representations: Vec<Representation>,
    pub units: Option<UnitSystem>,
    pub general_tolerance: Option<GeneralTolerance>,
    pub active: Option<bool>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum ProductDefinitionKind { Part, Assembly, Group, LinkGroup, Object }
/// The tolerance of a dimension that states `Tolerance::General`.
pub struct GeneralTolerance {
    pub linear: Option<LinearGeneral>,
    pub angular: Option<AngularGeneral>,
}
pub enum LinearGeneral {
    /// ISO 2768-1 table 1 applied to every length, radius, and diameter: the symmetric deviation by the
    /// class and the nominal size's range.
    Iso2768(LinearGeneralClass),
    /// The deviations by the dimension's `decimals`, the key the rule looks a dimension up by.
    ByDecimals(BTreeMap<u8, Deviations>),
    /// One pair of deviations for every length, radius, and diameter.
    Uniform(Deviations),
}
pub enum AngularGeneral {
    /// The deviations by the dimension's `decimals`, the key the rule looks a dimension up by.
    ByDecimals(BTreeMap<u8, Deviations>),
    /// One pair of deviations for every angle.
    Uniform(Deviations),
}
pub enum LinearGeneralClass { Fine, Medium, Coarse, VeryCoarse }
pub struct GeneratedFrom { pub definition: Option<ProductDefinitionId>, pub configuration: ConfigurationRef }
pub struct Representation {
    pub name: NonBlankString,
    pub content: RepresentationContent,
    pub features: Vec<FeatureId>,
    pub default: Option<bool>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub enum RepresentationContent { Bodies(Vec<BodyId>), Members(MemberRule), Document(ExternalDocument), Unread }
pub struct MemberRule { pub unlisted: Option<MemberAction>, pub members: Vec<RepresentationMember> }
pub struct RepresentationMember { pub path: OccurrencePath, pub action: MemberAction }
pub enum MemberAction {
    Include,
    Exclude,
    Substitute(NonBlankString),
    ReplaceBy(Vec<OccurrencePath>),
    Detail(RepresentationDetail),
    Native(NonBlankString),
}
pub enum RepresentationDetail { Geometry, Graphics, LightGraphics, Symbol, BoundingBox, Envelope }
pub enum Storage { Embedded, File { document: ExternalDocument, source: Option<SourceMeta> }, External(ExternalDocument) }
pub struct ExternalDocument {
    pub path: Option<NonBlankString>,
    pub document_id: Option<NonBlankString>,
    pub version: Option<NonBlankString>,
    pub stamp: Option<NonBlankString>,
    pub object: Option<NonBlankString>,
}
pub struct Occurrence {
    pub id: OccurrenceId,
    pub prototype: ProductDefinitionId,
    pub transform: Option<Transform>,
    pub suppressed: Option<bool>,
    pub visible: Option<bool>,
    pub representation: Option<NonBlankString>,
    pub overrides: Vec<NestedOverride>,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub native_ref: Option<String>,
}
pub struct NestedOverride {
    pub path: OccurrencePath,
    pub transform: Option<Transform>,
    pub suppressed: Option<bool>,
    pub visible: Option<bool>,
    pub representation: Option<NonBlankString>,
}
pub struct InstanceBodies { pub occurrence: OccurrencePath, pub bodies: Vec<BodyId> }
```

- **Definitions and occurrences.** A product definition owns bodies, occurrences, the tessellations whose `of` is `Definition` naming it, and the point clouds whose `definition` names it (§8). Every body of `CadIr.geometry` is owned by exactly one definition. The definition lists it in `bodies`, except a body that an `instance_bodies` entry shows in place of a prototype's bodies: that entry lists it, and no definition's `bodies` lists it. A body the file holds outside every other definition is the root definition's. Its names and BOM fields are stated in Annex A. `kind` is the source's kind of the definition. A source whose definitions are part and assembly documents (SolidWorks, Inventor, Creo, NX, CATIA) states `Part` or `Assembly`, by the document that holds the definition. FreeCAD states its own kinds: `Part` for an `App::Part`, `Group` for a group, `LinkGroup` for a link group, and `Object` for any other object (a PartDesign Body that an `App::Link` places, §6.7). A source that gives its definitions no kind (a Fusion component, which holds bodies and occurrences alike) states `None`. `source_name` is the source's stable object name, and `label` the user-visible label where it differs from that name. For a SolidWorks definition stored as a file, `source_name` is the document's name without its extension (inferred); what the document name of another format's file is, a Creo file name with its two suffixes (`name.prt.3`) among them, is not read (part 11). A Creo model's common name is its definition's `label`, and an instance's its configuration's (§5.11): binary releases store it as `ptc_common_name` on the generic and on every instance record. `description` and `part_number` hold the description and part-number fields the source itself defines (FreeCAD `Description`, and `PartNumber`, or `Id` on an `App::Part`; Inventor's `Description` and `Part Number` design-tracking properties; a Creo model's name as its part number), and `bom_properties` the other BOM identity fields the source itself defines, by exact property name (FreeCAD `Label2`, `StockCode`, `Vendor`, and `Manufacturer`, and `PartNumber` on an `App::Part`, whose part number is its `Id`; Inventor's `Category` summary property). A document's summary title is the `bom_properties` entry `Title` for every source: each decoder maps its source's summary title property to that key (Inventor's `Title`), and `PartNumber::DocumentName` reads it (§5.11). Every other source property, a user-defined custom property included whatever its name (a SolidWorks custom property `Description` or `PartNo`), is a model-class attribute (§5.12), and a configuration's own value of one, a SolidWorks configuration-specific custom property among them, is an attribute on `AttributeTarget::Configuration`, with its value's type and link (§5.11). A definition lists no sketches: a sketch belongs to its owner feature's definition (§6.1). `generated_from` states that the definition is a saved copy of a configuration of another definition, a table-driven factory, family, or generic: `definition` is that definition, a definition of `External` storage where it is named and not in the package, and `None` only where the member's own record proves its membership and names no factory; `configuration` is the factory's configuration it was generated from. The member's own content is the design, and a reader follows it where it and the factory's row differ. Inventor's member files carry it: a member generated from a table names its factory in the document-reference stream `UFRxDoc`, and its record `21c92603` holds the member's own row, its name first (the `Named` configuration), a cell differing from the factory's row where the factory's table was edited after generation (inferred). So the decoder states `definition` as the listed factory where that factory's table names the member, and as a definition of `External` storage where the listed factory is not in the package; on a member that lists another factory than the one whose table names it, or whose listed factory names it in no table, `configuration` does not resolve, so the decoder states no `generated_from` and keeps the link as the native option `inventor:generated_from`. The member's row record is kept as a native option, since where the factory is absent it is the only record of which parameters the table drives. NX stores the link as `PART_family_instance`, and a Creo instance file names its generic where it is stored on its own, by a carrier that is not located (part 11). A writer to a format with table-driven members writes the member into its factory only where the factory is in the package; otherwise it writes the member's own geometry and history and charges `export:feature.lowered` naming the link. An occurrence places a prototype definition inside its owning definition. A sub-assembly used twice is one definition with two occurrences; its children are stated once, in it. The placed instance tree is computed by walking occurrences from every definition that no occurrence places: the root definition, and each other definition of the root file that no occurrence places. An `OccurrencePath` (§5.8) names one placed instance.
- **Storage.** An `Embedded` definition is stored in the file of the definition that places it (a Fusion component in its document, a FreeCAD object that an `App::Link` of its own document places, §6.7), or, where no definition places it, in the root file. A `File` definition was read from its own file in the decode set, or is the root definition. The root definition stands for the decode's root file, and every document that holds a model record has one, a single-part file and a geometry-only file included. Where the file holds one definition at its top that no definition of the file places (a part or assembly document, a Fusion design's root component, a FreeCAD document, a Rhino model, a USD stage, a PVZ structure's one unplaced definition, an IGES or SAT file's model), that definition is the root. A decoder never wraps it in another, and states it where the source's record of it is not read, with that record's fields unstated. Where the file holds several definitions at its top and none places another (a STEP file with several root products, or a PVZ structure with more than one definition that no child occurrence targets), the root stands for the file alone: it places none of them, its `kind` is absent, and it holds what the file records about itself and the bodies the file holds outside them. Each of those definitions is stored in the root file, so it is `Embedded`, and no occurrence places it. The root definition is `File` with `source: None`: its source is `CadIr.source`, its digest `decode_digest`, and it has no `file_digests` entry (§3.1). Its `document` holds the identities the root file records about itself (a FreeCAD document's `Uid` as `document_id`), never the path or name the caller passed, and is empty where the file records none. A component file's definition, an archive member's included (a Fusion XRef design read from its `.f3z`, whose `document` holds its member path and lineage and version URNs, §6.7), is `File` with its own `source`: `document` keeps that file's identity so that a writer of the assembly can name it, and `source` holds that file's own format, attributes, and dialect layers (a `SourceMeta`, §2.7, as `CadIr.source` holds the root file's; §3.1). A writer resolves an `Inherit` target for that file from `source` and takes its output name from the caller, never from `document.path` (§3.4). An `External` definition names a document that was not read: it has no bodies, occurrences, or scope here. `ExternalDocument` holds every identity the source records for the link (CATIA stores a path and an id; Fusion a lineage and a version; FreeCAD a path and a stamp), and `object` the object inside the document that the link names. A link whose target the source left empty is an `External` definition with no identity.
- **Occurrence state.** `transform`, `suppressed`, `visible`, and `representation` are the occurrence's base values (D13); its current values are their resolution through the configuration that applies to it (§4, §5.11), which `effective_transform`, `effective_visibility`, and `effective_suppression` apply. `suppressed` states that the source holds the instance out of the product. `visible` is the instance's display state (D20). `overrides` changes the placement, suppression, visibility, or representation of an instance nested inside this occurrence's prototype, for this occurrence only, in every configuration (a flexible sub-assembly, an NX position override, a SolidWorks top assembly that hides one instance of a bolt in a sub-assembly used twice; its colour is an appearance binding with an instance target). A configuration's `OccurrenceOverride.nested` changes them in that configuration, field by field over this base list (§5.11). The arrangements of its prototype that an occurrence uses (an NX component's arrangement in use) are `OccurrenceDesign.arrangements` (§5.1, §5.11). The configuration of its prototype that an occurrence uses, whether it is grounded, and whether it is flexible are design content (§5.1), as are per-configuration occurrence states (§5.11). Model-class records name a placed instance by an instance target (§8). Every placement of an occurrence (`transform`, a `NestedOverride`'s, a configuration's or an arrangement's override, a pose, §5.4, §5.5) is an affine map of the prototype's coordinates into its parent's, as the source states it: a rigid placement; one that reflects, where the source places a mirror image of the prototype (a Fusion component mirror, §6.7; an IGES left-handed transformation matrix; a negative link scale); or one that scales, where the source scales the instance (a Creo View or FreeCAD link scale, a STEP mapped item's `scale`, an IGES subfigure instance's scale, a USD or Rhino instance transform), not necessarily uniformly. A decoder states the map the source composes and does not separate it into factors. Where the format defines its stored matrix as a rotation, or as a rotation and one scale (IGES Type 124, Creo View), the decoder states that rotation orthonormal, so rounding in the stored coefficients is no scale. A writer writes the map as §3.4 states.
- **Activation.** `ProductDefinition.active: Some(false)` is a reference-level deactivation, which removes the definition's shape and bill-of-materials entry wherever it is placed (CATIA `_ComponentActivationState`). An instance-level deactivation is `Occurrence.suppressed`; neither is `visible`.
- **Instance bodies.** `instance_bodies` states that, in this definition, the instance at a path shows the listed bodies of `CadIr.geometry` in place of its prototype's bodies: the result of an assembly-level cut or hole on that instance (SolidWorks, Creo, Inventor store such bodies per instance). It holds the active configuration's state (§5.5). The bodies are in the prototype's coordinates. A geometry writer emits them for that instance (part 9). A later pick of a body entity through that instance resolves in them (§5.8, Context). So a decoder that states instance bodies states the names the source gives their entities: an entity the instance keeps from its prototype carries the name it has in the prototype's state, and an entity the assembly feature made is named by that feature (§5.7).
- **Representations.** A representation is a named content that an occurrence can show in place of its prototype's full content. `Bodies` is a subset of the definition's bodies (NX reference sets, in every NX part). `features` lists the datum and curve features a representation also shows (an NX reference set's datums and curves), a reference into the design class that is empty with `design` out of scope (§2.1). A writer whose target has no such membership writes the bodies and charges a loss naming the representation. `Members` is a rule over the instances inside the definition (Creo simplified representations, in the `sld_configs` table of an assembly): each member's path names an instance, which the representation includes, excludes, shows in another representation of its prototype (`Substitute`, by name), shows as other occurrences of the definition in its place (`ReplaceBy`, which names them; those occurrences are shown only through it), shows at a reduced level of detail (`Detail`: `Geometry` its complete geometry, `Graphics` display data only, `LightGraphics` light-weight display data, `Symbol` a symbol, `BoundingBox` its bounding box, `Envelope` its default envelope), or treats by an action whose stored code is not read (`Native`) (PTC Types of Simplified Representations, and the TOOLKIT's `PRO_SIMPREP_*` actions). `unlisted` states the action the representation applies to an instance no member names, the source's default rule: `Include`, `Exclude`, a `Detail`, or a `Native` action whose code is not read; `None` does not state it. `Substitute` and `ReplaceBy` name what stands for one member, so neither is a default (part 10). PTC defines the default rule as an action, which may be a level of detail (Creo Object TOOLKIT, Simplified Representations). Creo's codes: a `state_type` 1 representation includes the instances it does not list and its status-1 rows `Exclude`, and a `state_type` 2 one excludes them and its status-2 rows `Include`; the `state_type` 2 reading is inferred (part 11). Statuses 4 and 5 show a member in its own named representation, `Substitute` with that name. Statuses 3 and 6 show a member as other components: each such row carries a substitution table naming top-level components of the same assembly, each flagged by bit 8192 of its `misc_choice[0]` and unplaced (`placed_flag` 0), while no row of status 1, 2, 5, or 9 carries one, so they are `ReplaceBy` those components' paths. Nothing stored separates what 3 and 6 do, and the native option `creo:simprep_status` keeps the code (Rule N case (a), part 11). Creo's reverse action ("Reverse the default rule for this component") is `Include` under an `Exclude` default and `Exclude` under an `Include` default; under a default that is a level of detail the page does not say what it shows, and such a row is `Native`; its automatic action, which retrieves data on demand and presents the master, is `Include`, the retrieval policy being no design fact (Rule N case (b)) and staying in the representation's native record (PTC Creo Object TOOLKIT, Simplified Representations). Which stored status is reverse or automatic is not read (typed, carrier unread; part 11). Status 9 is the one status left. Its rows name no representation and carry no substitution table, so it is no substitution, and nothing stored for its members differs from an included member's. The decoder states `MemberAction::Native("creo:simprep_status:9")` for it (Rule N case (a), part 11). The `state_type` 8 records of the same table are no representations: they are component display states, which are `Display` arrangements (§5.11), and a decoder writes no `Representation` for them. A component's bit 33554432 is none of envelope, family instance, interchange member, or shrinkwrap; it goes with components the saved assembly did not load, and is the component's native option `creo:not_retrieved` (inferred; Rule N case (a), part 11). A geometry writer emits an instance's geometry for `Include` and `Detail(Geometry)`; a target without the other details receives `Include`, a detail being a display choice, or `Exclude` for a symbol or a bounding box it cannot show. `Document` is an alternate document that stands for the definition (CATIA representations: `CATShape`, `cgr`, `CATPart`; `PRDBAGREP`). `Unread` is a representation whose content the decoder did not read. `default` marks the one the source shows by default. `Occurrence.representation` names the one an occurrence shows (a Creo `simpl_rep` on a component). A geometry writer emits for each occurrence only the bodies its representation holds (part 9).
- **Units.** `units` is the unit system the definition's source document is authored and displayed in (length, angle, mass, and time units). Stored values are in the document's canonical units (§2.3).
- **General tolerance.** `general_tolerance` is the definition's rule for every dimension that states no tolerance of its own: a model parameter whose `tolerance` is `Tolerance::General` (§5.12) takes its definition's, and a PMI dimension whose `tolerance` is `General` takes its annotation's context definition's (§8); a parameter with `tolerance: None`, whose tolerance is not stated or not read, takes nothing from it. It holds one rule in force for lengths and one for angles. An angle takes `angular`: under `ByDecimals` the entry at its `decimals`, under `Uniform` the one value. A length, a radius, or a diameter takes `linear`: under `Iso2768` the class's deviation in ISO 2768-1 table 1 for the range that holds the absolute value of its nominal, under `ByDecimals` the entry at its `decimals`, under `Uniform` the one value; a PMI dimension takes the entry at its `decimals` (§8). `Iso2768` is table 1 as the standard has it, cited by class and range and not transcribed here, so a reader takes its values from the standard, applied to every length, radius, and diameter: a size at or below 0.5, a size above the class's last range, and a class's empty cell take no general tolerance, and the arm does not apply the standard's table 2 (broken edges) or table 3 (angles). Each entry of `ByDecimals` and the value of `Uniform` is a `Deviations` (§5.12) in the quantity's canonical unit, `lower` below `upper` (part 10), so a rule whose deviations differ above and below is stated as it is, and a source's symmetric value a is `lower` −a and `upper` a; `Iso2768`'s table 1 values are symmetric. A dimension for which the rule in force states no entry (a `decimals` the map does not hold, no `decimals`, or a size outside the class's ranges) takes none and states no `General`, which would be a second spelling of no tolerance (part 10). A source's stored values for a method not in force are a different fact from the rule in force, and are properties of the definition: Creo's linear array on an ISO model, a stored alternative with no effect while the class is in force, is `creo:linear_tol_by_decimals`, kept for a Creo writer, and SolidWorks's record of every method's values stays the definition's native options (below). `Iso2768` is Creo's reading: Creo models store the standard, a linear and an angular array by decimal places, and with the ISO standard the class and its tables, which equal ISO 2768-1 cell for cell. Above 0.5 a dimension of an ISO model holds the class value; no radius follows the broken-edge table where it differs from table 1, and no stored file known to the project holds an angular table.
