At or below 0.5 Creo gives a size the first range's value, which the standard does not. `ByDecimals` is Creo's arrays: for lengths in models without the ISO standard, where a dimension holds the entry at its `decimals`, and for angles in every model. `Uniform`, and `ByDecimals` for lengths, are SolidWorks DimXpert's methods, which apply "on dimensions that do not contain tolerances" (SOLIDWORKS help, Document Properties, DimXpert), each constructible from the vendor's text alone. The block tolerance "Sets up three block tolerances, each having a number of decimal places and tolerance values. DimXpert applies the Value as a symmetric plus and minus tolerance" for lengths, and for angles "Sets the tolerance value to use for all angular dimensions, including those applied to cones and countersinks, and angle dimensions created between two features. DimXpert applies the Tolerance value as a symmetric plus and minus tolerance": `linear: ByDecimals` with `angular: Uniform`. The general block tolerance is, "When specified, the tolerance value that applies to all linear dimensions, which includes distance, length, radial, and diameter dimensions (all non-angle dimensions)", and "the tolerance that applies to all angle dimensions, which includes the angle between two surfaces, cone angle, and chamfer angle dimensions": `linear: Uniform` with `angular: Uniform`. The page states symmetry for the block method only, and the general block value's symmetry is inferred from "the tolerance value". The ISO 2768 method's page names the standard and the class ("based on ISO 2768-1 Tolerances for linear and angular dimensions without individual tolerance indications") and quotes no value. The SolidWorks record stores each method's fields: one length for every length, one angle for every angle, and one angle for every angle in the method by decimal places; the record stores lengths in millimetres, the document preference that holds the same table storing metres and radians, and a 0 pair in the record is not the setting where the document's preference holds a value with its flag set. `ByDecimals` holds a lower and an upper deviation per entry because the vendor defines a row so: Inventor's Default Tolerance tab "Sets default linear and angular precision levels and tolerances for part dimensions", each row a precision ("the number of decimal places") with "the upper and lower range for the precision level", in separate linear and angular tables (Autodesk Inventor help, Default Tolerance Tab Reference, by Rule N's documentation clause). No stored file known to the project shows where Inventor stores a row, the table's carrier being not located (part 11), and a SOLIDWORKS Inspection add-in file can store such a table with an entry that differs above and below. No stored file known to the project shows `Uniform` applied, since a SolidWorks dimension stores no default deviation. The Creo decoder states `general_tolerance` from the model's settings: `linear` as `Iso2768` with the class where the standard is ISO and a class is set, else as `ByDecimals` from the linear array, and `angular` as `ByDecimals` from the angular array, converted from degrees to radians (0.5° is 0.00872665 rad). It omits a stored zero entry of an array, which states no deviation. A Creo dimension displayed as nominal states `General` where its stored slots equal what the rule in force gives it, and otherwise states `Deviations` from its slots, so that its value is kept: the lengths of ISO models that hold the per-decimals entry (no field marks which rule a length follows), the sizes at or below 0.5 that hold the first range's value, and a dimension whose `decimals` the array does not hold. The broken-edge table, which equals ISO 2768-1 table 2, is not stated. The SolidWorks decoder states no `general_tolerance` while the stored form of the method in force (block, general, or general block) is not located, and keeps the record as native options: the record's selector and class codes follow no field of the DimXpert preferences, and stored DimXpert codes do not follow the vendor's numbering (a fit record can store 7 where the published value is 3; part 11). The vendor's page names angular dimensions under the ISO method and gives no value. Whether the class applies table 3 is open (part 11). No other format is known to the project to store a model-level general tolerance: no Inventor, CATIA V5, NX, Fusion, or FreeCAD file known to the project stores one, and a STEP file may hold a class as a text property. A writer sends each `General` to its target's matching record: a parameter's to the target's general tolerance for model dimensions, and a PMI dimension's to its general tolerance for annotation dimensions (SolidWorks DimXpert's), never one to the other. Where the target has no such record, or one that does not hold the rule (a Creo target given `Uniform`, which Creo's class and arrays do not hold, or deviations that differ above and below, to a target whose rules are symmetric), it writes each `General` dimension's deviations, as the rule in force gives them, as that dimension's own tolerance where the target holds one, and charges `export:general_tolerance.restated` naming the definition, since a dimension the source shows as nominal is then stated; where the target holds no tolerance on such a dimension (no NX, Fusion, or FreeCAD file known to the project stores one on a model dimension, §5.12), it writes none and charges `export:general_tolerance.dropped` naming the definition. A writer to a format whose only general tolerance is the standard's class writes `Iso2768` as the class, and writes the tolerance of every `General` angle, and of every `General` length under another arm, as that dimension's own, charging `export:general_tolerance.restated`: the target's class would give an angle table 3's value by its shorter leg, which a Creo angle does not store. It also writes every `General` radius and chamfer height whose ISO 2768-1 table 2 value differs from its table 1 value as that dimension's own `Deviations`, the table 1 value, and charges the same restated form: a target that applies the standard as written gives such a radius table 2's value, where the arm gives table 1's. A writer writes `decimals` as the target's key where the target stores one per dimension (SolidWorks DimXpert dimension records), and as its displayed precision where the target stores no separate key (STEP value-format qualifiers, FreeCAD drawing dimensions); elsewhere it does not write it, and where a `ByDecimals` rule selects a dimension's tolerance by it, it writes that tolerance as the dimension's own and charges `export:general_tolerance.restated` naming the definition.
- **Component identity.** An occurrence's id comes from the source's stable instance key (SolidWorks `swID`), so it is the same in every configuration.
- **Placement in the history.** Where the source orders component placement with its features (Creo assembly features, Fusion), or keeps a component as a document object (a FreeCAD `App::Link`), the placement is a `Place` feature of the scope that names the occurrence (§6.7). The occurrence's `transform` is its base placement, the one home of the value; `Place.placement` defines it where the source stores a placement that can be bound (D56). `Place.scale` defines the scale composed with that placement where §6.7 states one. Its current placement is its resolution through the configuration that applies to it (§4, §5.11), then its current state's pose (§5.5).

For Fusion, `ExternalDocument.document_id` is the lineage URN and `version` is the version URN. An XREF definition takes these values from the `RedirectionsStream.dat` design entry whose `targetFileName` equals its `relativePath`. In a document without `RedirectionsStream.dat`, it takes them from the `Manifest.dat` reference extension entries whose target-document path equals its `relativePath`. The file root's `Storage::File.document` takes `document_id` from the manifest terminal lineage when present, else from design ordinal zero, and `version` from design ordinal zero. The reference extension's source-document path supplies the root's `path`. In an F3Z archive, the design object whose `relativePath` names the member supplies `lineage` and `about` for fields the member leaves empty. A resolved member's `Storage::File.document` retains its identity and member path. Embedded components keep `Storage::Embedded`; a stored version URN creates zero external definitions.

## 9. Writer conformance

**Instances.** A geometry writer emits, for each placed instance, the geometry of the configuration the instance selects (the current geometry when that configuration is active, else that configuration's evaluation; a missing one is a loss, `export:evaluation.missing`), under the composed placement, with the instance's bodies (§8.1) in place of the prototype's and only the bodies of its representation. A target with no per-instance bodies (Fusion, FreeCAD, STEP) receives such an instance as an occurrence of a definition of its own that holds those bodies, which keeps the geometry exactly and drops the link to the shared prototype, with a loss naming the instance; where the target stores its definitions as files, that definition is an output the writer creates (§3.4, Lowering). The writer emits each instance with the model-class records whose instance targets reach its geometry (§8). The configuration an instance selects is resolved down its path: an occurrence reached through an ancestor resolves through the configuration that ancestor selects for its prototype, then that configuration's overrides, and a scope's active configuration applies only where no ancestor selects one (§4).
**Writer conformance.** A writer's acceptance tests are W-closure-same (a document written to its own format and re-decoded keeps its content) and W-closure-cross (a document from any format written to X keeps every record X's decoder can produce).

## 10. Validation

Validation uses reference lookup and in-IR arithmetic and never refuses a decode (§3.3). It checks the rules below and the structural rules of the model records: every reference a neutral or a native record holds resolves, except a feature or container that a pick's name mentions (Names, below); loops and radial rings close, and the members of one radial ring use one edge; a wire edge, a free vertex, and each cage outside a form's `cage` belong to exactly one shell; every surface, curve, pcurve, and point carrier is reached; a subdivision cage's source associations resolve; a sidecar annotation names an entity or a record of a delta (§3.2), a stream, and a field path of the document; a periodic carrier's parameter domain is canonical; an edge's curve meets the edge's vertices at the ends of its range, in the edge's direction; a coedge's use curve meets them at the ends of its interval, in the coedge's direction; a coedge's pcurves, taken in order and mapped through its face's surface, run between them: the first begins at the start of the interval its use states and the last ends at the end of the interval its use states, in the coedge's direction, and a use that states no interval takes its pcurve's `parameter_range`, in either direction; a pcurve whose use and record state no interval is not checked; a native arena's record count, ids, links, and payload spans agree with its records; and an opaque payload and a retained record have the length and the SHA-256 digest stated for them. A radial ring of two coedges of one sense, an annotation field path the document's types do not have, and a tolerance outside the canonical range are Warnings. A rule is an Error unless it says Warning. Part 10 states no condition of a checked type (§2.8). The one-spelling rules below are also the decode wrapper's normalizer (§3.1), so a decoded document meets them by construction; validation checks them on every document.

**Coincidence.** Where a rule compares two positions of model geometry (a curve's end, a use curve's end, or a pcurve's image with a vertex; the two ends of a curve whose closure is decided, §5.6; a solved carrier with its construction), they agree where their distance is at most the coincidence allowance: the sum of three terms, or the binding floor where the comparison has one and it is larger. The first term is the tolerance in force: the largest `tolerance` of the edge and of its two vertices and, for a pcurve's image, of the face, each that states none taking `tolerances.linear` (§2.3); for the closure of the curve of an edge with no vertex, that edge's; for a tolerant intersection's stored end points, the intersection's own tolerance; and `tolerances.linear` where the rule compares no face, edge, or vertex. The second is the fit tolerance of each stored approximation that either position is evaluated through (a solved carrier's cache, a support surface's cache, a pcurve), since each lies within its own fit of the exact geometry and two of them can differ by the sum; an approximation that states no fit tolerance adds none. The third is the evaluation resolution, 2⁻⁴⁴ times the largest magnitude of a coordinate of the positions the rule compares. It bounds the rounding that binary64 arithmetic leaves on values of that size. A comparison of a vertex with an edge's curve end, a use curve's end, or a pcurve's image, and the closure of the curve of an edge with no vertex, have a binding floor: the largest of 0.01 mm, `tolerances.linear`, the `tolerance` of each face, edge, and vertex that the first term reads, and the fit tolerance of the edge's curve cache, of the use curve's cache, or of the coedge's first and last pcurves. A comparison of a procedural curve's solved carrier with a support surface's pcurve mapped through its surface, or with an offset curve's base end points moved by the offset distance (Caches, below), has a binding floor 0.01 mm larger than the largest of 0.01 mm, `tolerances.linear`, and the fit tolerance of the solved curve's cache and of the support surface's cache. No other comparison has a binding floor, and the allowance has no other term. Every `Topology` of a document (a state delta, a cage-defined feature, a witness body) is checked at that document's `tolerances`. A position that needs a carrier the IR does not hold in closed form, or a pcurve on a surface whose own parameterization the IR does not hold, is not compared.

**Partial statements.** A rule constrains what a record states. Where a record states less than a rule reads (an `Unresolved` or `Native` operation, a `Native` arm of any type, an `AnnotationDimensionKind::Other`, an `Unread` selection, a `Native` pick target, a `Native` occurrence step, a `Native` anchor, an `Expression::Source`, a partial face, a marked region, shell, or body (§5.6), a field that is `None`, an evaluation or process state with no content), the rule is not checked on what is not stated: a rule about an operation's operands, their count, kinds, or names does not fire on an `Unresolved` or `Native` operation; a rule about a selection's picks does not fire on an `Unread` selection, which satisfies a rule that requires picks; a `Native` pick counts as one pick and is of any kind a rule requires; a rule that constrains a value does not fire where the value is `None`; and no rule on a face with no loops, on the edges a `Solid` body's faces use, or on whether a shell's faces are connected fires on a partial face, on a marked shell, or on a shell or region that holds either. A rule about the partial form itself fires: a rule that requires a field to be stated or forbids it, a rule that reads an `Unresolved` operation's family (§5.4), and a rule on what a partial form carries (a `Native` pick carries a native name or a witness; a `Native` anchor occurs only where the target definition has no scope in this document).

**Bounded values.** A rule that bounds the value of a `Dimension` (§5.14), its sign, its range, or its order against another value, is an Error on a `Literal`. A bound dimension stores no value: its value in a configuration is its parameter's cache for that configuration (§5.13), with the opposite sign or the complement under `Negated`, and that is a cache (K2). So the same bound on it is a Warning in each configuration for which the cache is stated, and is not checked for another. A bound over several values is an Error where every one of them is literal, and otherwise a Warning on the values that their literals and stated caches give in a configuration. The admission of `T` (positive, nonzero, an enumerator name) is a rule of its own (Parameters, expressions, programs, dimensions, below) and is not stated again here. Any other rule that reads a dimension's value (a spelling the value would repeat, a structure that goes with the value, an index within a count) reads a literal only, unless it says that the value resolves (`is_stateless`, §5.4).

**Scope and linkage.**
- The scope holds no class without the class it requires: `design` requires `model`, and `process` requires `design`. An arena of a class the scope excludes holds no record, and no record of another class's arena references a class the scope excludes (§2.1).
- No design record references the process class (§2.1).
- No two records of different arenas outside `Topology` share an id, and no two records of one resolved state's topology share one (§2.2).
- Every `native_ref` resolves; no native record references the neutral model.
- In a decode set, the `<scope>` of every id of a record read from a component file (the records of that file's design scope, and the bodies and records its definition owns, not its `File` definition, which is a record of the file that places it) begins with the key of that file's `File` definition and `@`, and every scope that holds `@` begins with the key of a `File` definition of the document (§2.2, §3.1). Every key of `SourceFidelity.file_digests` names a `File` definition read from a component file; the root definition has none (§8.1).
- In a fragment (§2.6), every evaluation and process state holds its whole chain of bases.

**Containers, positions, evaluations, current geometry.**
- The container tree and membership (§5.2): every feature and container is a member of exactly one container or a root of exactly one scope; containers form a tree; `Rollback::Before(m)` names a member of its container; folders of one container nest or are disjoint. Dependency cycles are Warnings.
- Positions name existing records: `Start` names an ordered container, and `After` a member of a container or, as `After(Container(c))`, an ordered container `c` that is a root of its scope (§5.3). No evaluation has `of` equal to `State(After(Container(c)))` for an ordered container `c`: that state is the state at `c`'s rollback position (§5.3). In an unordered container, no current state is at `After(m)` for a member with no result of its own in the active configuration; no evaluation of configuration `c` has `of` equal to `State(After(m))` for a member with none in `c`; and no `Pinned` anchor or `StateBase::Current` is at `After(m)` for a member with none in any configuration of its scope (§5.3). `After(Container(c))` for an unordered container `c` occurs nowhere.
- Evaluation keys: at most one per (scope, configuration, `of`); `configuration` names a configuration of the scope when the scope has configurations and is `None` exactly when it has none; `Tool(f)` names a feature for which `CadIr::has_tool_body(f, c)` holds in the evaluation's configuration `c` (§5.4); the rule does not fire on an `Unresolved` or `Native` operation, or on one whose Boolean is unstated; bases form a forest.
- Which features have evaluations (§5.4, D34, D35): no evaluation of configuration `c` has `of` equal to `State(After(f))` or `Tool(f)` for a feature `f` for which `CadIr::is_stateless(f, c)` holds, a feature whose `suppressed` resolves to true in `c` or whose operation in `c` cannot change a state; every other feature may have one. An evaluation with no content has status `Stale` or `Failed`.
- No evaluation of the active configuration has `of` equal to `State(p)` for the position `p` of one of its scope's current states (§5.4).
- `StateBase::Evaluation` and `ProcessBase::State` name a state with content. `StateBase::Current(p)` names the position of a current state of the evaluation's scope, or, under a process state, of its setup's scope (§5.5). A `CurrentState.at` or `StateBase::Current` is `After(Container(c))` only where `c` is an ordered container whose `rollback` is unstated (§5.3).
- Current geometry (§5.5): every listed body is a body of `CadIr.geometry`; every body listed in `bodies` or in an `instance_bodies` entry of a definition a scope spans is in exactly one of that scope's current states or in its `unproduced`, and in no other scope's current state or `unproduced`; every `unproduced` entry is a body owned by a definition the scope spans and is in no current state; a current state inside an ordered container `c` is at its rollback position, spelled through its member where `c`'s rollback is stated and as `After(Container(c))` where it is not; a rule that orders a member of `c` against the state at `c`'s unstated rollback reads every member of `c` as before it, and no evaluation inside `c` is checked against that current state's position. Every key of `CurrentState.poses` is a path from the scope's definition, resolved against the current occurrence membership, that names a placed instance existing in that state, at a placement other than the one its configuration resolves to (D54); no path has a pose in two current states of one scope.
- A scope holds a root container that has a member, a parameter, program, sheet-metal rule, configuration, arrangement, or publication that names it, an `occurrences` entry, or a setup that names it; a scope that holds none is an Error (§5.1).
- Stored geometry (§5.10): where the state after a `Stored` feature is stored, each body its `bodies` names is a body of that state; each `tessellations` entry names a tessellation whose `of` is `Definition`, naming a definition the feature's scope spans.
- `CadIr.geometry` is closed over its own references, and so is each resolved state (§5.4, §7.9); a delta's `records` names records of its base and is closed only with it. An unordered child list (a shell's faces, a body's regions) is not stored; each stored child list is reciprocal with its children's parent pointers (D29). An edge's `ends` is `None` only where its carrier names a closed curve and states no `param_range`, and a coedge of such an edge is the only coedge of its loop (§5.6).
- In each resolved state, every name entry names an entity of that state, every owner entry a body of it and an existing definition, every member entry an occurrence that exists in that state (§6.7) and an existing definition, every instance-body entry and every pose entry a path that resolves against the state's occurrence membership, the current listing with the state's `members` applied (§5.4). An instance-body entry lists bodies of the state. A pose entry names a placed instance existing in that state, at a placement other than the one the state's configuration resolves to, which for an occurrence that a `members` entry gives another owner is `Occurrence.transform` under that owner (§5.4, D54). These checks run against the resolved state, never against `delta.records` alone.

**Names (§5.7).**
- Every `EntityRef` of a name table resolves in its resolved state's topology; the entity's kind matches the name's derived kind; `Merged` members share one kind; every entry holds a name or a native name.
- Every feature a name mentions is one the named state depends on (§5.3), counting, for a name on an instance body, the features of the prototypes that the instance path's occurrences place.
- A name entry on an entity of an unproduced body states no `name` (§5.5).
- A name in a pick may mention a feature or a container the document does not hold: one a removal deleted (§4), or one the source's own reference names after its deletion (D51). The pick does not resolve through that name, and no rule about the record it mentions (that it exists, its operation, its pattern's indices, its order) is checked on it.
- Where the feature a name mentions is in the document, `TopoName::Instance.feature` names a `Pattern` with implicit instances, of which `instance` is a valid index; a `TransformBodies` whose mode is `Copy`, with `instance` `[k]` and 1 ≤ k ≤ `count` where the count is literal; or an `Extract`, with `instance` `[1]`.
- Where the feature a name mentions is in the document, `GenerationRole::Hole` occurs only in a `Generated` name of kind `Face` whose `feature` is a `Hole`.

**Selections (§5.8).**
- `Input` occurs only in a feature's definition, in a sketch that feature owns, or in the expression of a parameter that feature owns, and the feature is a member of an ordered container. A selection of a feature that is a member of an unordered container is anchored `Current`, or `Pinned(After(m))` for another member `m` of the same unordered container that has its own result (§5.3), or `Native` (below). Process selections are anchored `Current` or `Pinned`, never `Input`.
- A `Pinned` position resolves. A `Native` anchor occurs only where the target definition has no scope in this document.
- A `Publication.target` resolves in its scope's current geometry, as a pick anchored `Current` (§5.11).
- Sketch, sketch-entity, sketch-region, sketch-frame, datum, feature, feature-result, template-input, publication, and occurrence targets exist and depend-order at or before the pick's anchored state in the scope that holds the target (§5.3): a target of the selection's own scope at or before the anchor, and a target of another scope at or before the `Pinned` position its selection names there; a back-edge inside a dependency cycle is reported as that cycle's Warning. A pick into another scope that is not pinned there, and whose target lies after the current state of that scope that would hold it, does not resolve (D51), which is a Warning.
- A `Native` target carries a native name or a witness; its `within`, where present, exists and depend-orders before the pick's anchored state in the scope that holds it (§5.3).
- An `Entity` pick resolves by the matching rule of §5.7 in its anchored state where that state is stored: the current geometry of the resolving scope (the union of its current-state extents and the extent of its unproduced bodies) for `Current` picks, process picks included; the current state's extent for a position that is a current state's position in the active configuration (§5.5); otherwise the evaluation of the anchored position, in each configuration in which the feature is active. An `Entity` pick that matches no entity of its stored anchored state is a lost operand (D51), a Warning. A `Bounded` pick's candidates are the edges between faces matching every name of its `faces`; names match with every `index` left out, and each `index` the pick states narrows as §5.7 states; `ends` narrows only among several of the candidates the indexes keep, an end name that names no entity of the state is ignored, and a narrowing that would keep no candidate is not applied (§5.7). A pick anchored `Pinned(After(Container(c)))` for an ordered container `c` resolves in the current state or the evaluation at `c`'s rollback position, read under `c`'s `placement` (§5.2, §5.3). A pick that crosses into another scope resolves in that scope's state (§5.8). An `Occurrence(path)` pick of a body, face, edge, vertex, or surface resolves in the instance bodies that its anchored state in the owner's scope holds for its instance, else in those that an assembly along its path holds, else in the prototype (§5.8). An `All` term and every rule that reads every entity of a state read that state's extent, never all of `CadIr.geometry`. A pick is not checked where its anchored state is not stored, where its resolving definition has no scope in this document, or where no state it reads holds instance bodies for its instance and an assembly feature not suppressed in that state's configuration may have changed that instance otherwise than through its definition (§5.8).
- `Picked.resolved` occurs only where the anchored state is stored, and each entry is a record of that state; the anchored state of a pick into another scope is the state of that scope it resolves in (§5.8).
- A `PickTarget::Datum` `part` of `Principal(..)` names a `Frame` datum; `Point(i)` names a `Points` datum with more than `i` points.
- `Principal.container` names an ordered container of the scope that spans the definition the pick resolves in (§5.1, §5.2).
- A `PickContext::InContext` names an `assembly` from which `own` and `target` resolve, where they are present. A `DefinitionRef` names an existing definition, and its `configuration`, where present, follows the `ConfigurationRef` rule below.
- An `OccurrencePath` resolves step by step from its root definition, against the occurrence membership of the state it is read in (§5.4, §5.8): each `Occurrence` step names an occurrence of the previous step's prototype, or of the root for the first step; every step after a `Native` step is `Native`. A step's `configuration`, where present, follows the `ConfigurationRef` rule below. A path in a nested override (base or per configuration), an instance-body entry, a representation member, or an instance target states no step configuration.
- A witness `body` is a `Topology` closed over its own references.
- Rules: an `All` or `Affected` term has no seeds, and every other rule's term has at least one seed. `Chain.end`, `Region.boundary`, and `Intersection.with` picks resolve in the selection's anchored state. A `Region` term whose boundary picks curves has a seed with a `Containing` domain. A `Picks::Rule` with one `Explicit` term, no propagation, and no exclusions is an Error (it is `Named`, D43). Two `Explicit` terms of one selection with equal propagation are an Error: the explicit items of one list under one propagation are one term (§5.8).

**Constructions (§5.9).**
- An input's subject is valid for the construction's kind: `Point`, `Direction`, and `Axis` take `Whole`; `Plane` takes `Whole`, `Origin`, `XAxis`, `YAxis`; `Frame` takes all five; `Curve` takes `Whole` and `Origin` (§6.6).
- A `ZAxis` subject carries no `Parallel`, `Perpendicular`, or `Tangent` relation; that constraint is on the whole.
- Values by relation: `Offset` has a `Length` value; `Angle` an `Angle` value; `AtParameter` a `Ratio`, `ParameterRatio`, `Length`, or `Uv` value; `Coordinates` a `Position` (point, origin), `Components` (direction, axis), or `PlaneEquation` (a plane's `Whole`) value; `Midway` none or a `Ratio`; `Radius` a `Length` value, or none with a reference; `Limit` a `Length` or `Angle` value, or none with a reference; `Native` any value or none; every other relation, `Fold` included, no value. A `PlaneEquation`'s `a`, `b`, and `c` are not all zero.
- `Midway` references hold one or two picks; `Centroid` references one or more; `Fold` references four straight edges that share one end vertex and lie in one plane, on a `Plane` or `Frame` construction with a `Whole` subject; `AtParameter` and `Coordinates` references one, or two where the second, the measuring origin, is a point; every other relation's reference holds one pick. `Radius` and `Limit` occur only on a `Curve` construction.
- A `Built` reference occurs with every relation except `Fold`; each reference, `Built` or a pick whose target states its kind, fits its relation (§5.9, What a relation reads). A nested construction satisfies every rule of this list, and its references depend-order as its outer construction's do.
- A `Whole` `Coincident` input whose reference is a whole frame occurs only on a `Frame` construction.
- No `after` step is a `Flip` with a literal `false` value, and no `Feature.placement` or `Primitive.placement` is a construction with no inputs, no bound step, and the identity as its value (§2.4).
- An input's `reversed` occurs only with `Parallel`, `Perpendicular`, `Tangent`, `AxisOf`, `Coincident` on a line, `PrincipalNormal`, `Binormal`, or `AtParameter`.
- A construction has at least one input, one step, or a resolved value.
- An input has a `reference` or a `value`.
- `resolved_in` keys name configurations of the construction's scope other than its active configuration; a construction with no inputs and no steps has no `resolved_in`.
- A datum with a `link` has a construction with one `Coincident` input or none; its `link` has no `source`, and a `document` only where the construction has no input.
- A plane or frame whose whole is `Coincident` with one planar reference has no leading Z translation in `after` (it is an `Offset` input).
- A `PlaneValue`'s `x_axis` is perpendicular to its `normal`; a `FrameValue`'s axes are orthonormal and right-handed; a `CurveValue::Arc`'s `start` and `end` lie at `radius` from `center` in the plane normal to `normal`, within the linear tolerance.
- A datum feature whose construction is one `Coincident` input on a `Principal` entity, with no `after` steps, is the only such feature for that entity and container, and every other pick of that entity in its definition picks the feature as `Datum` (§6.1, §6.2).
- Every construction in a definition references entities that depend-order at or before the feature.
- A construction's `solution` is at least 1.
- A `ParameterRatio` value occurs only on an `AtParameter` input whose reference is one pick, of an edge or of a sketch or spatial-sketch entity whose curve is neither a point nor an `InfiniteLine`. It does not occur on a `Built` reference, with a literal value of 0 or 1, or where the document states the picked curve as a line, a circle, or a circular arc: there the spelling is `Ratio` (§5.9). A datum axis, a principal axis, and an `InfiniteLine` have no ends, and a pick of one takes neither a `Ratio` nor a `ParameterRatio`. An `AxisRotate` step binds at least one `axis` component, and its components are not all zero.

**Parameters, expressions, programs, dimensions (§5.12 to §5.15).**
- Parameter names are unique per (scope, owner); `name` is `None` only for a spreadsheet cell parameter or a parameter that a sketch constraint's dimension binds.
- A parameter's `owner` is a feature or an ordered container of its `scope`, or a model attribute one of whose values is `Parameter` naming the parameter (§5.12, §8). A program's `owner` is a feature of its `scope`, and a program with an `owner` has no `stage`.
- `value`'s variant matches `kind`. A process parameter with no `kind` holds a `Number`; where its definition is an expression, that expression is `Source`, and no `Neutral` tree has a `ParamRef::Process` to it. A design parameter's `unit` occurs only with a `Quantity` kind and has its exponents.
- Every `ParameterRef` target resolves: a `Parameter` id exists; an `External` definition exists and has `External` storage. A `through` path resolves from the referencing scope's definition, or, for a process reference, from its setup's scope (part 7), and its last prototype is the target parameter's scope.
- An `External` target occurs in a `Source` token, or as the whole tree of a `Neutral` expression that states a design parameter's value (its definition, or a configuration's or an arrangement's override of it), and nowhere else: not below the root of a tree, in a program's statement, in a process expression, as an `Assign` target, or as the parameter of a process `Dimension`. The parameters of one scope whose expressions are the `External` reference to one definition and name through one path have one kind.
- A design expression or program references no process parameter (by type). `ParamRef::Process` and `ParamRef::Design` references resolve.
- A `Dimension::Parameter` or `Negated` binds a parameter of the dimension owner's scope (design dimensions). `Negated` occurs only where `T` is a signed quantity or `bool`.
- A bound dimension's parameter kind matches `T`; its cached value satisfies `T`'s admission (positive, nonzero, enum wire name) (Warning).
- Every `Neutral` tree type-checks by the semantics table of §5.13, and its root matches the parameter's kind; an `External` reference has the kind of the parameter whose expression it is.
- A `^` with a dimensioned base has a literal exponent whose products with the base exponents are integers.
- Function arity: `atan2` and `mod` 2, `min` and `max` at least 2, all others 1.
- `Text` nodes occur only as `==` and `!=` operands, `if` branches, or the root of a Text-kind expression.
- `LawParameter` occurs only inside `Law::Expression`, and a `Bend` variable only inside an `AngleRange.value`: outside it no path and no bend supplies the value.
- A `Measure` selection is anchored `Pinned`, `Current`, or, in a feature-owned parameter's expression, `Input`; `Distance` and `Angle` select two picks, the others one or more.
- A `Source` expression's token list is empty (nothing was read, §3.3) or holds at least one `Text` token. An `Unset` parameter has no `value`.
- Parameter reference cycles are Warnings; dangling references are Errors (D6).
- An integer-kind parameter's evaluated neutral expression is an integer (Warning).
- A parameter that a `RadialMeasure::Diameter` dimension binds has no `display` (§5.12). A `Driven` parameter is bound by at least one dimension (Warning).
- An `Assigned(p)` parameter names a program that exists; every `Assign` target of a `Neutral` body has `Assigned(this program)`; each such parameter is assigned on some path.
- Every `spreadsheets` record is named by exactly one feature's `Spreadsheet` operation, a feature of the record's scope (§5.12). A spreadsheet cell's parameter is owned by that feature.

**Configurations (§5.1, §5.11).**
- `active_configuration` is `None` exactly when the scope has no configurations, and otherwise names a configuration whose `scope` is this scope.
- Each path of a configuration's `OccurrenceOverride.nested` resolves from the overridden occurrence's prototype, as the paths of its base `Occurrence.overrides` do, and names a nested path at most once per list.
- Overrides name existing parameters, features, occurrences, and definitions; a configuration overrides only `Expression`-defined parameters; each parameter override states at least one of `expression` and `value`, and each feature-state override at least one field; each key of a configuration's `definitions` is a definition its scope spans, and each definition override states at least one field, a `bom_properties` entry counting as one; an arrangement's overrides hold no `definitions` entry; there is no suppression override for a parameter-bound suppression; `parent` forms no cycle and stays within one scope.
- A `DesignParameter.tolerance` occurs only on a parameter whose `kind` is a `Quantity`, and its values have that quantity; a `Deviations`' `lower` is below its `upper` wherever a `Deviations` occurs, in `Tolerance::Deviations` on a parameter or a PMI dimension, in a `Fit`'s `deviations`, and in a general tolerance (§5.12, §8, §8.1). A `Tolerance::Fit` on a parameter occurs only where its `kind` is `Quantity::LENGTH`, and a `Fit`'s `mate` has the other `zone` than its `fit` (§5.12). `Tolerance::General` occurs only on a parameter whose definition states a `general_tolerance` with the rule for the parameter's quantity, `linear` for a length and `angular` for an angle, and where that rule states an entry for the parameter: under `ByDecimals` an entry at the parameter's `decimals`, under `Iso2768` a `value` that is a `Number`, in a class range that holds its absolute value (§5.12, §8.1). A `DesignParameter.decimals` occurs only on a parameter whose `kind` is a `Quantity`. A `PartNumber::DocumentName` occurs only in an override of a definition whose `storage` is `File` or `External`: `DocumentName` reads the name of the document that stores the definition (§5.11), and a definition stored in no document of its own has none; the definition, or the configuration's override of it, states the `bom_properties` entry `Title` or the `source_name` the string is read from. A `PartNumber::ParentConfigurationName` occurs only in a configuration whose `parent` is stated.
- A definition override that names another sketch record names one owned by the same feature.
- In a `FeatureStateOverride.definition`, every `Dimension` at a place the base feature's definition also has equals the base's: a dimension difference is a parameter override (D16). The definition override restates no suppression, which is the override's `suppressed`.
- A `ConfigurationRef::Local` names a configuration of the prototype's scope; `Named` occurs only where that scope is absent or lacks the name.
- `OccurrenceDesign` keys and the occurrence keys of a configuration's or an arrangement's `overrides` name occurrences owned by a definition the scope spans (§5.1).
- A configuration's `materials` holds at most one entry with no `target`, and no two entries select one body; a `target` picks bodies of the scope's definitions, anchored `Current`.
- Each key of an `OccurrenceDesign.parameters` map is a parameter of the scope of the occurrence's prototype, and that prototype has a scope in this document; each override states at least one of `expression` and `value` (§5.1).
- An `Arrangement`'s `scope` has a design scope; its override keys name parameters, features, and occurrences as a configuration's do, and its overrides follow a configuration's rules; its occurrence overrides state no `configuration` or `prototype`; `configuration` names a configuration of its scope; each `appearances` entry states `appearance` or `transparency`, and its path, each move's paths, and each `nested` path resolve from the scope's definition; each move's step is `Translate` or `Rotate`; `moves` occur only in an `Explode` arrangement; an `Explode` arrangement states no parameter or feature override; a `Local` nested arrangement names an arrangement of the path's prototype's scope (§5.11).
- `DesignScope.active_arrangements` and each configuration's `active_arrangements` name arrangements of that scope, at most one of each kind; an arrangement that names a `configuration` is in force in no other configuration's resolved set. Each `OccurrenceDesign.arrangements` names at most one arrangement of each kind, and a `Local` entry names an arrangement of the scope of the occurrence's prototype (§5.11).

**Sketches (§6.1).**
- Each sketch's `owner` exists. A feature with a `Sketch(s)` or `SpatialSketch(s)` operation owns `s`, and owns no other sketch except those its configuration definition overrides name; a feature with another operation owns only sketches its definition names.
- A `Block` sketch is owned by a feature with a `Sketch` operation. A `Placed` sketch's resolved frame, when present, has orthonormal axes.
- Each entity's and constraint's `sketch` exists and matches the space (planar ids in planar arenas, spatial in spatial).
- An entity, constraint operand, role target, text layout entity, pattern entity, offset pair, polygon, or slot member names an entity of the same sketch.
- A `Free` entity in a planar sketch has a curve other than `Spatial`; `PlanarCurve::Spatial` occurs only as `solved` of a `Derived` entity.
- `solved` is `None` only for `Derived`, `Text`, `BlockInstance`, and `Native` forms.
- `Interpolated` solved geometry is `Nurbs`; `Conic` solved geometry is an ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola arc or a rational `Nurbs`.
- A point role (`Start`, `End`, `Center`, `Apex`, `Focus`, `Fit`, `Anchor`, `Insertion`) is held only by an entity whose curve, solved or free, is `Point`, or by a `Derived` entity with no solved curve; `Pole`, `Knot`, `MajorAxis`, and `MinorAxis` may be held by any helper entity. `Handle(i)` is held only by a construction `Line` entity, of an `Interpolated` spline with fit point `i`, and that spline's handle `i`, where `handles` holds one, has `direction: None` (D52).
- Each (of, role) pair is held by at most one entity; `Fit` indices of one spline are 0 to n−1 without gaps; `Pole` and `Knot` indices are within the NURBS's pole and knot counts.
- `Start` and `End` roles target bounded curves; `Center` targets circles, arcs, ellipses, and hyperbolas; `Apex` targets a `Conic`; `Anchor` a `Text`; `Insertion` a `BlockInstance`.
- `Instanced.instance` is a `BlockInstance` entity of the same sketch; `Instanced.of` is an entity of that instance's block definition; block instancing forms no cycle.
- `Derivation.source` is not `Unread` when `solved` is `None`.
- `Operand::Frame` occurs only in planar sketches and names `XAxis`, `YAxis`, or `Origin`; `Horizontal`, `Vertical`, `DistanceAxis::Horizontal` and `Vertical`, and `SketchPatternDirection::Angle` occur only in planar sketches. No `Model` operand picks its own sketch's `SketchFrame`.
- `Horizontal` and `Vertical`: one line, or two points. `Midpoint.point` is a point entity and `of` a bounded curve. `Concentric` operands are circular or elliptic. `Equal` has at least two members of one kind class (lines, or circular entities).
- `Contact::Ends([p, q])`: `p` bounds `a` and `q` bounds `b`; `Contact::Via(p)` is a point entity.
- `AngleSector::Directed` occurs only in planar sketches.
- `Radial.of` is a circle, arc, or ellipse; `MajorRadius` and `MinorRadius` apply only to ellipses; `AngleOperands::Sweep` names an arc or elliptic arc; `Length.of` is nonempty.
- `Distance` with `Aligned` has a non-negative value where the value is a literal.
- `SketchOffset.pairs` is nonempty; no entity is a result in two pairs; results are not sources of the same offset.
- `SketchPolygon.edges` has at least 3 lines; `SketchSlot.centers` are point entities.
- `SketchPattern.seeds` is nonempty; each non-suppressed instance has as many entities as `seeds`; no entity appears in two instances or as both seed and instance; `Linear` has one or two directions; a sketch pattern's spacing is not `UpTo`; a literal count is at least 1; instance indices are distinct and within the counts.
- `SketchRegion.outer` is nonempty; every boundary use names a non-construction curve; `fragment.index < fragment.count`.
- A `Dimension` in a sketch binds only design parameters of the sketch owner's scope. A dimension constraint whose value binds a parameter has `name: None`: the parameter's `name` is its name (§6.1). `Model` operands and `Derivation.source` follow the selection rules above.
- A `Frame` entity's `solved` is a `Point`; each of its `XAxis` and `YAxis` roles is held by at most one construction `InfiniteLine` entity of the same sketch. `XAxis` and `YAxis` roles name only a `Frame` entity.
- `Pierce.point` and the three entities of `AngleOperands::Points` are point entities. `Weight.pole` holds a `Pole(i)` role of a spline entity. `SketchPolygon.inscribed` occurs only with a `circle`, and `circle` is a circle entity of the same sketch. `DerivationMode::OntoFaces.faces` picks faces. `FixedLength.of` and `FixedAngle.of` are nonempty and name line entities. A `TextContent` whose `vertical_box` is `CapHeight` has no `vertical: Some(Baseline)`.

**Shared option types (§6).**
- No key is in both maps of one record (§6).
- A `ProfileRef` holds at least one pick. Profile picks target a sketch, a sketch region, a sketch entity, a spatial-sketch entity, a face, an edge, a curve, a surface, or a feature result. Path picks target a sketch, a sketch entity, a spatial-sketch entity, an edge, a curve, or a feature result; where the state exists, the resolved curves form one connected chain.
- `Targets::Selected` picks resolve to bodies. A feature that is a member of a `Body` container has `targets: None`. An `Apply` with `Join` occurs only where the feature's input state, where it is stored, holds a body the feature can join: a first solid feature is `NewBody` (§6).
- `BooleanOp::Assemble` occurs only in `Combine`; `Sew` occurs only in a `SolidOutput` whose `body` is `Sheet` or `None`, or in a `SheetOutput` whose `solid` is `Sheet` or `None`.
- `Span::Between` does not have `AtOrigin` at both `start` and `end`. A literal `Span::Symmetric.amount` is not zero; a literal angular amount is at most π per side or 2π in total.
- `ToGeometry.target` picks resolve to faces, surfaces, or bodies. `ToGeometry.far` occurs only where `target` picks bodies. `LimitOffset::Angle` occurs only in a `Limit<Angle>`, and `LimitOffset::Translated` only in a `Limit<Length>`.
- `WallSide::Left` and `Right` occur only with a profile whose picks form open chains, and `Inside` and `Outside` only with closed profiles and face offsets. A `Thickness::Offsets` with two literal values has `outside + inside > 0`. `ThinWall.corner_round` occurs only with a profile whose picks form open chains, and `CornerRound::Round` only with one whose picked curves are all line segments, since it states a round where two lines meet and nothing for a corner at an arc or a spline.

**Swept solids and the loft (§6.3).**
- An `ExtrudeDraft` states `end` or `start`: a draft the source stores as off is `draft: None` (§2.4). An `ExtrudeDraft` under `Span::Symmetric` has no `start`; `ExtrudeDraft.start` is `None` when the span's `start` is `AtOrigin`. `ExtrudeDraft.neutral` is `Start` only under a `Span::Between` whose `start` is not `AtOrigin`, where `Origin` would state the same body under every edit, and then `ExtrudeDraft.start` is `None`: no material lies before the neutral plane. A `HoleDraft::Angles` states `start` only where its `ExtrudeDraft` does. A `ProfileFit` states `outer` or `inner`, `outer_join` only with `outer`, and `inner_join` only with `inner`.
- `Rib.extent` is `Next`, `Amount`, `ToGeometry`, or `ToPlane`. `Rib.thickness_at` occurs only with `draft`.
- `Sweep.transition` is not `CornerTransition::Open`: `Open` is defined for a ruled surface's corner, and occurs only in `ImplicitSweep.corner` (§6.3, §6.6). `CornerTransition::Carried` occurs only in `Sweep.transition`.
- Literal `PathExtent` fractions lie in [0, 1], and `along + against` is greater than zero.
- A literal `SectionShape::Circle.inner_diameter` is less than a literal `diameter`. `SweepSection::Generated.turn` is `None` where `shape` is `Circle`.
- `HelixStart::Circle` selects exactly one circle or arc.
- A `Primitive` feature has `Feature.placement: None` (§5.10). A `PrimitiveShape::Cone` whose radii are both literal has at least one nonzero radius; literal primitive angles lie in (0, 2π].
- Loft: the section count plus present point ends is at least 2; `cross` is empty or has at least 2 sections.
- `SectionShape::Triangle.apex` occurs only in a `HelicalSection::Generated`. `SectionTurn::ZStart` occurs only with a `Square` section. `SweepOrientation::Guides(PathToFirst)` requires at least one guide, and `Guides(FirstToSecond)` at least two.
- `PrimitiveShape::Prism.sides` and `CurveDefinition::Polygon.sides`, where literal, are at least 3. A literal `Wedge` has `y[0] < y[1]`, `base[0] ≤ base[1]`, `base[2] ≤ base[3]`, `top[0] ≤ top[1]`, and `top[2] ≤ top[3]`, with `base` and `top` not both degenerate in the same axis. A `Plane` primitive's output `body` is `Sheet` or `None`.
- `LoftShape.section_law` occurs only in a loft whose section count plus present point ends exceeds two. A `LoftSmoothing` states `angle` or `deviation`: smoothing that is off is `smoothing: None` (§2.4). A guide's `influence` of `NextGuide` occurs only in a loft with at least two guides.
- `LoftShape.style` does not occur with `ruled: Some(true)`. A `Section.spine_point` occurs only in a loft with a `spine`. A `Section.trim_support` occurs only where the section's `condition` names a `Faces` support. The area stations of a `Centerline` name distinct positions, and a literal `Fraction` position lies in [0, 1].

**Dress-up and holes (§6.4).**
- `Fillet.sets`, `Chamfer.sets`, `Draft.sets`, and `Offset.sets` are nonempty.
- `Stations.points` has at least two entries; entries with `Parameter` on the same `Along` have strictly increasing fractions. `chain_start` occurs only where a station is on `Along::Chain`, and resolves to an end vertex of the chain where the anchored state exists.
- A `Variable` radius has at least one literal-positive or parameter-bound station value.
- `FilletSize::Held` occurs only in a `Faces` or `Edges` set with at least one hold.
- A literal `Rho.rho` or `CenterAndRho.rho` of a `ConicShape` lies strictly between 0 and 1. `FilletSize::ByProfile` occurs exactly where the profile is `Conic(CenterAndRho)`.
- In `FullRound`, the center selection and explicit side selections share no pick. `Faces.first.faces` and `Faces.second.faces` share no pick.
- Every `Transition.between` index is less than the set count, and `between` has at least one member: an `Intersect` or a `CornerSphere` at least two, a `Blend` exactly two, a `RollingBall` or `SweptAround` one to three, and a `Continue`, `Stop`, `StopAt`, or `Native` at least one. On a `SweptAround` with three members a single listed piece is the largest, and on one with two members `against` is stated. A `CornerSphere` transition states no `lengths` or three, one per piece it closes.
- `Corner.vertex` picks resolve to vertices; `EdgeSetback.edge` picks resolve to edges incident to the corner's vertex where the anchored state exists; `Setbacks::PerEdge` names each edge once.
- `BlendControls.keep` shares no pick with any set's edges.
- `ShellFeature.faces` selections share no pick with each other or with `removed`.
- `DraftAngle::Two` and `DraftAngle::Symmetric` require `neutral` or `parting`. A draft states at least one of `neutral`, `parting`, or a set's `fixed` (Warning). `DraftSet.faces` is `None` only when `fixed` is present.
- `HolePositions::Points.centers` is present only when a pick targets a whole sketch. `Points` picks target sketch points, vertices, datum points, or sketches.
- `HolePositions::Placed` holds at least one construction, and no construction has a `Coincident` input whose reference equals `Hole.start`.
- A `Hole` with a nonempty `series` is the operation of a definition that states `assembly`; each `SeriesStage.parts` pick resolves to a member of one of that context's selections, and no member is picked by two stages. A `StageHole::PartFeature` stage picks one part, and its feature is a `Hole` of that part's definition; that definition has one occurrence among the members of the context's selections, and the part hole's positions are the series' positions carried into the part by that occurrence's placement.
- A `Cone` states at most two of `diameter`, `depth`, and `angle`.
- Literal counterbore, countersink, counterdrill, and spotface diameters exceed the literal bore diameter. A `TangentToTangent` slot's literal `length` exceeds its literal bore diameter.
- `Dome.faces`, `Decal.faces`, and `Rip::Faces.faces` pick faces, and `Rip::Faces.faces` and `RipPath::Edges` are not empty; a `RipPath::Ruling`'s and a `RipPath::Line`'s `face` picks one face, and a `Line`'s `from` and `to` differ; a `Dome` with `points` has no `height`.
- Literal thread diameters satisfy minor < pitch < major.
- No `Thread` feature's `face` selects only a bore face of a `Hole` whose `thread` is present. A `Hole`, and a `Stated` series stage, that states `thread` states no `standard`: a tapped hole's designation is only in `thread.standard`.
- `ThreadLength::ToElement.element` and `Thread.start` resolve to faces, edges, or planes.
- `HoleBottom::Trimmed` occurs only where the hole's `extent` ends on a face: not with `Amount` or `AtOrigin`. `Draft.steps` occurs only with `parting`. A `ChamferSize::Vertex` holds three entries, whose edges meet at one vertex where the anchored state exists.

**Patterns, template instances, and body operations (§6.5).**
- `Features` seed picks target `FeatureResult`; `Faces` picks name faces; `Bodies` picks name bodies.
- A literal count is at least 1; a `List` is nonempty; a literal `seed` is below the run's literal count.
- `Fit` occurs only in a `Circular` angular run, a `Path` run, or the spacing of a `SketchPatternLayout::Circular`; `UpTo` only in a `LinearRun`.
- `LinearLayout.seed_only` occurs only where `second` is present.
- `PatternLayout::Follow` holds one pick, of a pattern feature, of a pattern in another definition through an occurrence context, or of a component pattern, and that pattern is neither the pattern itself nor one that follows it, directly or through others. `PatternLayout::Chain` occurs only in a `ComponentPattern`; `ChainLinks::Connected` holds one link per seed of its pattern, and each link's two pins are distinct axes of that seed's geometry. A `ChainLinks::Native` picks only the geometry of its pattern's seeds.
- Each `Increment.parameter` is bound by a dimension of a seed feature's definition and appears once per run.
- `Dimensions` is nonempty and each of its runs has at least one increment.
- `Table`: `parameters` is nonempty and distinct; every row has one value per parameter; row `instance` values are distinct.
- `Composite` has at least two stages. A literal `ScaleLayout.count` is at least 2, and a `Scale` stage after the first has a count that divides the number of instances the stages before it make, where they are literal.
- Every `InstanceIndex` has one coordinate per run the layout holds (none for a missing `LinearLayout.second` or `CircularLayout.radial`; under `Follow`, the followed pattern's coordinates; under `Chain`, one; a `Native` layout and a `Composite` with a `Native` stage state no count, and their indices are not checked against it), is not all zeros, and lies in each run's coordinate range (§6.5, Coordinate range). Under a literal `seed_only: true`, every index has a zero coordinate.
- Overrides name distinct indices; `Varied.parameters` is nonempty and names parameters bound by seed definitions; a `Mirror` layout has no overrides.
- `Members`: indices distinct; each member lists one feature per seed feature pick; member features exist, are not seeds, belong to the pattern's container, follow the pattern contiguously where that container is ordered, and belong to one generator; no member has `driven_by`.
- `TemplateInstance`: present roles are distinct within `inputs` and within `parameters`; each parameter exists in the instance's scope; members follow the instance contiguously in its container where that container is ordered and have no `driven_by`; every `TemplateInput` pick names an existing input of an instance that lists the picking feature as a member.
- `Combine`: `op` is `Join`, `Cut`, `Intersect`, `Assemble`, `UnionTrim`, or `Compound`; `tools` is nonempty; no pick is in both `target` and `tools`; `target` is `None` only with `Join`, `Intersect`, or `Compound`, or where the definition states `assembly`.
- `Split`: `SplitTool::Geometry.tools` is not one datum or principal pick alone (that is `Plane`); `ByTools.targets` picks bodies or faces, and is `None` exactly where the definition states `assembly`; `SplitMethod::Project` occurs only when a tool is a curve, and `SketchNormal` only when that curve belongs to a sketch.
- A `ByTools` split whose tool is `Silhouette` has `method: None`, and its `kept`, where stated, is `All` or `Native`.
- `Kept::Pieces` states at least one of `keep` and `remove`; a piece pick targets an entity of the split's targets or elements, or of a participant where `targets` is `None`; piece picks with a `Fragment` domain in one list share one `count`, and each `index` is below it.
- `SplitMode::Mutual.elements` holds at least two picks when `Named`, and its `Kept::Side` holds one entry per element when `elements` is `Named`.
- `InstanceOrientation::Rolled` occurs only in a `Path` layout, and its `reference_axis` is `Y` or `Z`. `Flex.bodies` picks bodies.
- `MoveFaces.faces`, `DeleteFaces.faces`, and `ReplaceFaces.faces` pick faces; `ReplaceFaces.replacement` is nonempty and shares no pick with `faces`.
- `TransformBodies.bodies` picks bodies or `Component` targets; `Transformation.steps` is nonempty; a literal `Copy.count` and a literal `divisions` are at least 1, and `divisions` above 1 occurs only where every step is `Translate`, `Components`, `PointToPoint`, or `Rotate`.
- `BooleanOp::Compound`, like `Assemble`, occurs only in `Combine`; a `Compound` combine has `target: None`.
- `BooleanOp::UnionTrim` occurs only as a `Combine`'s `op`.
- `RunSides::Against` occurs only in a `Path` layout's run.
- No other combine, component pattern, or mirror names the occurrence that a `Combine.new_component` names, and the combine is before every `Place` or `PlaceSet` that names it, in that feature's container chain (§5.3).
- A `Constrained` step has at least one mate, each of the kinds `Coincident`, `Parallel`, `Perpendicular`, `Tangent`, `Concentric`, `Distance`, or `Angle`, whose first connector picks a moved body. `Graft.body` picks one solid body, and `Graft.sheet` sheet bodies or faces.

**Surfacing, wireframe, forms, and sheet metal (§6.6).**
- `PatchBounds::Loops.outer` is nonempty; every inner loop is nonempty; where the anchored state exists, each loop's curves form one closed chain, and each condition's support faces meet the boundary curve. In-IR arithmetic bounds the distance of a face from a curve, and this rule and the spine-limit rule below apply, where the surface is a plane, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, or NURBS surface whose weights share one sign, the curve is a line edge between two vertices, a circle, or a NURBS curve whose weights share one sign, and rigid maps place both.
- `Patch.planar = Some(true)` holds only where every condition is absent or `Free`.
- `Knit.elements` holds at least two picks when `Named`, unless `output.solid` is `IfClosed` or `CapPlanarOpenings`. `Knit.federation`'s seeds pick elements of the knit's result. `Unsew.edges` picks at least one edge, each an edge that two faces of one sheet body share, and the picked edges divide that sheet into two pieces.
- A literal `ExtendLimit::Distance` is positive. `LineLength::UpTo` and `ExtendLimit::UpTo` select points, faces, or planes.
- `ImplicitSweep.solution` is at least 1. `SpineLimits` targets are points or planes on the spine, where the state exists and the distance bound of the patch-support rule above reads the target and the spine.
- `BoundaryFill.cells` is nonempty; each cell selection is nonempty.
- An `ImplicitSection::Conic` has two to five guides, and a `parameter` only with two; a literal parameter lies strictly between 0 and 1. `ExtendLimit::Natural` occurs only where `edges` picks loops of faces or wire edges. A `Knit.healing` occurs only with a `tolerance`. A `Bend` states at most one of `angle` and `flat_length`; each `Connect` edge selection picks one edge. `Extrude.sheet_cut` occurs only in an extrude that cuts a sheet-metal body.
- `SplineCurve.points` has at least two points, three when `closed` is `Some(true)`.
- The two `BridgeEnd.curve` selections are not the same pick with the same `at`.
- `Form.cage` holds `subds` records only, at least one, and is closed over its own references (§5.6).
- In a `CatmullClark` cage every side holds one edge, and no two edges state different knot intervals.
- `FlangeWidth::PerEdge` has one pair per selected edge when `edges` is `Named`, and `FlangeWidth::CenteredPerEdge` one width per selected edge when `edges` is `Named`. A `FlangeWidth::FromEnds`'s `first` and `second` together do not exceed the edge's length where the edge resolves (Warning). A `ConnectBetween::Apart`'s two selections are distinct, each picking one edge. A `ConnectBetween::SharedEdge` picks edges only, and its `Connect` has `double: None` and `extension: None`. `SheetMetalKind::Bend.line` picks sketch lines or edges.
- `Unfold.fixed` and `FlatPattern.fixed` select one planar face. `BendSet::Selected` selects bend faces of a sheet-metal body.
- Every `SheetMetalRuleId` a feature names is a rule of the feature's scope. A `KFactorTable` has at least one row, and its rows' ratios increase strictly. A `BendTable` has at least one block, in strictly increasing thickness; each block's `radii` and `angles` are not empty and increase strictly, and its `values` hold one row per angle, each of one value per radius. A `BendEquations` has at least one range; each range's `from` is below its `to`, the ranges are in increasing order, and no angle lies in two of them, a bound that two ranges share being inclusive in at most one, since a bend takes one range's value. Each `AngleRange.value` has the quantity `yields` states: a length under `Compensation`, `Deduction`, and `Allowance`, a dimensionless number under `KFactor`. A `ContourFlange.profile`'s picks form one open chain, and its `thickness` is `OneSide` with `Left`, `Right`, or no side, `Symmetric`, or `Native`. An `ExtrudedHole.entry` or `Stamp.entry`, where present, picks one planar face, and a `Circle` outline's `center` lies on that face's plane (Warning). A `Louver.open_edge` picks one curve of `profile`'s sketch, and a `StiffeningRib.bend` one bend face, on which its `at` lies (Warning). An `ExtendWall.edge` picks one edge. A `ContourFlange` with `edges` states no `extent`; without `edges` it states an `extent` and no `width`. Each end of a `ContourFlange.extent` is `AtOrigin`, an `Amount` with a positive value, `ToPoint`, `ToPlane`, or `ToGeometry`. Each `VertexBend.vertex` picks one vertex of `profile`'s chain where two of its pieces meet, and no two pick the same vertex; a `VertexBend` whose `radius` and `radius_side` are the flange's `bend.radius` and `bend.radius_side` restates the flange's bend (Warning). Each of a `ToolForm`'s `constraints` has a connector whose picks carry a `Definition` context that names `tool`, and `tool` names no definition the feature's scope spans. A `Flange.height_datum` occurs only with a `Distance` height or an `outline`. A `Flange` that states `outline` picks one edge and states `height_datum` `InnerSharp` or `OuterSharp`, and no `height`, no `width`, and no `angle`. A `Hem.position` is `AtEdge` or `TangentToSide`. A `Relief` states at most one of `width` and `width_ratio`. A `Rip::Along`'s `path` is not `Edges`. A `BreakCorner.corners` is not empty and picks edges of the sheet's thickness. A `Convert.fixed` picks one face of the solid `body` picks, and each `ConvertBend::Edge.edge` one edge of it and each `ConvertBend::Face.face` one cylindrical face of it. A `ConvertRip.path` is `Edges` or `Sketched`. At every position, each sheet-metal body has at most one governing rule (where bodies are resolved).
- Each `LineMode` and `CircleMode` arm's curve and surface selections resolve in the sweep's anchored state; `CircleMode::CenterAngles.angles` states both angles or neither, and its `from` only with an angle; a `LineMode::Curve.from` occurs only with an `angle`. An `EquationCoordinates` law that is an `Expression` has its coordinate's quantity, `Length` or `Angle`, and uses `LawParameter` only there.

**Meshes (§6.6).**
- A `MeshKind::Combine`'s `op` is `Join`, `Cut`, or `Intersect` where stated, and its `tools` is not empty.
- A `MeshKind::Section`'s `sketch` names a sketch record.

**Assembly operations (§6.7).**
- `Place.occurrence`, and each occurrence a `PlaceSet` lists, is an occurrence owned by a definition the scope spans (§5.1); a component pattern or mirror may also name it. Two `Place`s that name one occurrence are members of one ordered container: the first in order creates it, and each later one changes its owner and creates nothing (a cut-and-paste, §6.7). Each `Place` constraint has a connector that picks into `Place.occurrence`. `Feature.placement` is `None` on a `Place`. `Place.base` is present exactly where `placement` is, and `OwnOccurrence` occurs only where the occurrence's prototype has an occurrence of its own in the scope (§6.7).
- Every occurrence has at most one creating feature (§6.7): its first `Place` or `PlaceSet`, the `Combine` whose `new_component` names it, or, for an occurrence that none of these names, the one component pattern or mirror that lists it. The `Place` and `PlaceSet` features that name one occurrence are ordered by §5.3: of any two, one is before the other in the other's container chain.
- A `PlaceSet` lists each occurrence once, and at least two unless it keeps native options for the members its decoder does not join, where it lists at least one (§6.7).
- In a scope that spans one definition, every `Feature.component` is `None`; in a scope that spans several, it names a definition the scope spans or is `None` (not established).
- No definition is spanned by two scopes (§5.1).
- A `Joint`'s connectors resolve; a world connector has no inputs and a resolved value.
- `Motion` joints other than `Rigid` have `Frame` connectors; a `Rigid` motion's connectors may be any variant. `Coincident`, `Distance`, `Parallel`, `Perpendicular`, and `Angle` connectors are `Plane`, `Axis`, `Point`, `Frame`, or `Entity`; `Concentric` connectors are `Axis`, `Frame`, or `Entity`; `Tangent` has an `Entity` connector.
- A `PinSlot`'s `slide` is another axis than its `axis`. `AxisLimits` names an axis the motion leaves free by its `axis` (§6.7), at most once per axis. `Bounds` holds at least one bound; two literal bounds satisfy `min ≤ max`.
- `Coupling.joints` picks exactly two `Joint` features as `Feature` targets, and neither is the coupling itself. In a `Coupling` whose `joints` is absent, every connector that is a construction holds at least one input.
- `ComponentPattern.seeds` and `MirrorComponents.seeds` pick only `Component` targets. Every `ComponentInstance.occurrences` has the length of `seeds`; no instance index repeats; no occurrence repeats across instances. `MirrorComponents.results` has the length of `seeds`.
- A `RigidGroup` has at least two `members`, distinct paths from a definition the scope spans, each step an `Occurrence`.
- A definition that states `assembly`, in a feature or in a configuration's override of it (§5.11), belongs to a feature of the scope of the definition that its participants' context paths start from, or of a Fusion root scope whose `Feature.component` names the component. Its operation is no `Place`, `PlaceSet`, `Joint`, `RigidGroup`, `ComponentPattern`, `MirrorComponents`, `Stored`, `DeleteBodies`, `TransformBodies`, `Flex`, `Graft`, `Knit`, or `Mesh`, and no `Unresolved` whose `family` names one of these; it is no `Split` in `Mutual` mode and no `SheetMetal` `Convert`; every `Boolean::Apply.targets` and `Targets` in it, and its `ShellFeature.bodies`, `Combine.target`, and `SplitMode::ByTools.targets`, are `None`, and no `Boolean` in it is `NewBody`. Every pick of `AssemblyContext.participants` carries an occurrence context. No selection in it is `Named` with no pick, a selection with `Unread` picks is its only entry, no pick is in two of its selections, and its selections state one `at`. An `Affected` term occurs only among the `terms` of a selection of `AssemblyContext.participants`, in at most one selection of a context, with no seeds and no `propagation`; where that selection's `resolved` is stated, it holds no participant another entry of the context states. Where a context holds an `Affected` term, each rule that tests whether an instance is one of the context's participants (a hole series' parts, a split's piece picks, and the resulting features below) reads that selection's `resolved` where it is stated, and is not checked otherwise.
- A feature whose `driven_by` names an assembly feature that holds no `Native` participants is a feature of the definition one of its `Definitions` participants resolves in.
- A feature with `driven_by` is in a scope other than its driver's.
- Joint, rigid-group, placement, pattern, and mirror features belong to the one scope that spans the definitions owning the occurrences they name (§5.1). A decoder states the joints of a source that has no history as features of the root definition's scope (§6.7).
- A `Slot` joint's two connectors are `Entity` connectors. A `Path` joint's first connector is an `Entity` that picks a path and its second a `Point`; its `pitch_yaw` and `roll` name different axes.

**Topology and model records (§5.6, §8).**
- Every edge that a face of a `Solid` body uses is used at least twice by the faces of that body, unless the edge has no curve or a degenerate one (Warning).
- A face's `loops` name each loop once. A shell's faces are connected through shared edges or vertices. A `Wire` body's shells hold no face (Warning). A partial face, and a marked region, shell, or body, is reported at Warning under the check `topology_partial`. A region's mark names each shell once, none that its `shells` names, and each shell it names states that region. A face `Unspecified` with no loops is the only face of its shell where the shell is not marked, and its surface is no plane, cylinder, or cone, and no placed surface whose basis, through every placement, is one (§5.6, Faces and loops); a partial face beside it does not exempt it. A shell's `members` name each wire edge, free vertex, and cage once. A shell whose `members` name a cage names nothing else, no face lies in it, and it is the only shell of its body's only region.
- Each procedural surface of a `Topology` is the `construction` of exactly one of its surfaces, and each procedural curve of exactly one of its curves.
- A tessellation's `Meshed::Body` names a body of the geometry its `state` names, and each of its `faces` a face of that body. `Display` and `Definition` name a product definition whose storage is not `External`. `Pmi` names a PMI annotation whose definition is `Presentation`. An `Unresolved` tessellation states no `state`. A tessellation's `state` follows the instance-target rule below.
- An appearance `Tessellation` target, a `TriangleGroup`'s `tessellation`, a presentation item's `Tessellation`, and an `AttributeTarget::Tessellation` name a tessellation of the model. The `source_id`s a tessellation's `triangle_groups` state are distinct, and a `TriangleGroup`'s `group` is one of them. A triangle group's `face` requires that its tessellation is `of: Body`, that the face is a face of that body, that the face is one of the arm's `faces` when that list is not empty, and that no other group of the tessellation names the face. The instance-target rule that the entity is a record of the prototype does not apply to a tessellation target.
- A `Record` target names an arena of §2's `Model`, §5's `Design`, or `Topology` and an id of that arena; an appearance `Record` target names no arena whose records another arm of `AppearanceTarget` names (a product definition as a whole is a `Definition` target, an occurrence an `Occurrence`, a body a `Body`). `Drawing.direction` and `x_direction` and a camera's `orientation` are not zero. A semantic annotation's `reference_anchors` hold at most one point, or two on a `Dimension` with a `dimension_kind`. A semantic annotation's `reflex` occurs only with an angle kind, `negated` only with a kind that is not an angle, and `line_directions` only with a `Distance`, `HorizontalDistance`, or `VerticalDistance` kind. A `DirectedLocation` dimension's annotation has two targets. A stated PMI `nominal`'s quantity agrees with `dimension`: an `Angular` dimension's is an `Angle`, that of every other kind but `Other` a `Length`, and only an `Other` dimension's may be a `Ratio`. A PMI `nominal` that binds a parameter binds one whose kind is a length, an angle, or dimensionless, as its quantity is. A `PmiDimension` whose `nominal` binds a parameter that states a `tolerance` states a `tolerance` of its own only where it differs from the parameter's, compared as values in the dimension's sign: under `Negated` with the parameter's tolerance mirrored, its lower and upper exchanged and negated. An equal one is a Warning (D61). A `PmiDimension` whose `nominal` binds a parameter that states `decimals` states `decimals` of its own only where they differ from the parameter's: equal `decimals` are a Warning (D60). A datum system's references name `Datum` annotations. A `GeometricTolerance.maximum_upper` exceeds its magnitude where the magnitude is a `Length`. A `ToleranceZoneForm::Other` holds neither `cylindrical or circular` nor `spherical`, compared without regard to ASCII case. A `DimensionModifier::Other` holds none of `reference`, `auxiliary`, `statistical`, and `controlled radius`, compared without regard to ASCII case.
- Layer `parent`s resolve and form no cycle.
- A `Drawing.views` entry names a drawing record that is no `Page` and no `Template`; no list repeats an entry, and no record is reached from itself through `views`. `base_view` names a `View`, `Projection`, `Section`, or `Detail` record, and base views form no cycle. A `ReferenceTarget::Drawing` names a drawing record, and a `Curve` part indexes that record's `curves`. `Annotation` and `Pmi` targets name existing records.
- An appearance binding whose target is `Unresolved` states `source_entity_id` or `native_ref`, and its target has `path: None` and `state: None`. No `source_entity_id` is blank.
- An appearance binding states `precedence` where its target is an `Occurrence`, a `Definition` that owns an occurrence, or a `Body` or `Tessellation` whose `path` is stated, and states none on every other binding (§8). A `Definition` target names a product definition of the model and has `path: None`.
- No two appearance bindings name one target, one path, and one state with different appearances (Warning: a source may store both, and `effective_display_color` applies the first in arena order, §4).
- A point cloud's `definition` names a product definition whose storage is not `External`, and its `positions` is not empty. Its `normals` and `colors` are each empty or hold one entry per position. Its channels' names are distinct, and each channel holds one value per position.
- A `LimitsAndFits`'s `form_variance` holds capital letters only, and its `grade` is not empty. A `PmiDimension`'s `tolerance` occurs only where the dimension has a `Length` or `Angle` quantity (the one its `dimension` gives, and for `Other` its `nominal`'s, §8), and a `Tolerance::Fit` on it only where that quantity is `Length`. `Tolerance::Basic` and `SingleLimit` on a `PmiDimension` occur only where its `nominal` is stated, and `Tolerance::General` under `Iso2768` only where its `nominal` is stated. A `PmiDimension`'s `decimals` occurs only where its `nominal` is stated with quantity `Length` or `Angle`. Every context definition of one PMI annotation's targets is the same one (§8). A `Tolerance::General` on a `PmiDimension` occurs only where its annotation has a context definition, whose `general_tolerance` states a rule for the dimension's quantity (`linear` for a length, `angular` for an angle), and only where that rule states an entry for the dimension: under `ByDecimals` one at its `decimals`, under `Iso2768` a class range that holds the absolute value of its nominal; otherwise it is a second spelling of no tolerance.

**Products (§8.1).**
- Where `model` is in scope and the document is not a fragment (§2.1, §2.6), a document that holds a model record holds exactly one definition that is `File` with `source: None`, the root definition, and no occurrence places it (§8.1). Every body of `CadIr.geometry` is listed by exactly one definition's `bodies` and by no `instance_bodies` entry, or by `instance_bodies` entries and by no definition's `bodies` (§8.1). An occurrence's prototype exists. No definition is the prototype of an occurrence that it owns, directly or through the prototypes of its occurrences. An `External` definition has no bodies, occurrences, or scope; `Occurrence.representation`, `OccurrenceOverride.representation`, and `NestedOverride.representation` name a representation of the prototype they apply to.
