Decides whether the CATIA decoder lists members or one `Stored` member for another value; until then the flag stays `catia:udf_black_box`. Would settle it: an instance whose `UdfBlackBox` atom differs, with its member records present or absent; Inventor iFeatures of further designs.
125. **Creo template prompts.** How Creo pairs a group's `gp_keys` prompts with its `new_refs` inputs. An order join does not align them. Decides which `TemplateInput` each Creo prompt names; until then the roles are `None`. Would settle it: each prompt's text set against the kind of the reference it would bind.
126. **CATIA line-sweep angles.** The zero of CATIA's reference-surface angle (the documentation measures it from the projected surface normal) and of its reference-curve and centre-and-angles angles, which `LineMode::Surface.from`, `LineMode::Curve.from`, and `CircleMode::CenterAngles.from` state (§6.6). The stored modes and fields are read; the reference-surface sweeps' surfaces are not sampled. Decides those three `from` fields; until then `from: None`. Would settle it: reference-surface sweeps' surfaces sampled at a station against both zeros, through the report's join to their result surfaces; a line sweep of the reference-curve mode and a circle sweep of the centre-and-angles mode with a nonzero angle.
127. **CATIA corner pieces.** Which piece of each element a CATIA corner that trims keeps (§6.6). Each result lists cells that modify one input cell each; the wires are not decoded as geometry, so the kept pieces are not set against the tangency points; tangent continuity gives one assembly, which is inferred. Decides how a writer of another codec writes `Corner` with `trim`; until then the tangent-continuous pieces. Would settle it: one trimming corner's wire decoded, its pieces set against the tangency points.
128. **Creo bend angle.** That a Creo bend's angle dimension is its deflection on every bend (§6.6). A non-right bend's flange face turns by its dimension, not by the included angle; a 90° bend gives one result under both readings. Decides the Creo decoder's `angle`; until then the deflection. Would settle it: Creo bends of other non-right angles with stored flats.
129. **K-factor table segment of the SheetMetal add-on.** The SheetMetal add-on's new unfolder looks up a `Linear` table by searching for the bracketing segment with `while r_over_t <= values[i]`, which picks the first segment for every ratio inside a table of three or more rows, so it extrapolates that segment (§6.6). This holds at `v0.2.60-beta` and at master `c505f5ea`, and every version returns the last row's K-factor above the table. Open: whether a release of the new unfolder corrects the search, and which unfolder produced a stored flat pattern, which no file records. Decides a FreeCAD writer's output for a `Linear` table; until then it writes the table and charges a loss naming the rule where a governed bend's ratio lies inside the table beyond its first segment. Would settle it: the add-on's next release run on the same table.
130. **Assembly feature effect.** The effect of an NX assembly cut, and of Inventor assembly features in general (§6.7). An Inventor participant's part keeps its uncut body while the assembly carrier holds the cut one, and a feature on an NX promoted body changes the referencing part's copy only (§6.7). Decides the effect of an NX assembly cut's participants; until then `None`, or `Instances` where the decoder finds per-instance bodies. Would settle it: one NX assembly with an assembly cut, its target part's stored body set against the assembly's.
131. **SolidWorks coordinate mate.** Whether SolidWorks' coordinate mate class (`moMateCoordinate`) also stores coincidences of origins and coordinate systems, with their axes aligned (§6.7). The class stores a coincident mate whose two operands are component sketch points, with no coordinate-system or origin class in it. Decides the mapping of the class with other operands; until then `Coincident` of two `Point` connectors, and a class whose operands are frames stays `JointKind::Native`. Would settle it: a mate between two coordinate systems with axes aligned, its record set against a point-to-point one.
132. **NX CAM geometry and setups.** Whether an NX operation's geometry adds to or replaces its geometry group's, and whether NX means one setup per MCS or one per MCS and WORKPIECE pair. The machine and carrier nodes of NX CAM files are read, not their geometry groups. Decides `ProcessGeometry.combine` for NX (§7.7) and how the NX decoder forms setups; until then `combine: None`, and one setup per MCS. Would settle it: NX CAM files that declare setups, their operations' geometry set against their groups'.
133. **Fusion profile-loop order.** The side-token order of the Fusion profile forms §3.4's rule does not cover: loops with inner loops, trimmed pieces, circles and splines, the second side of a two-sided or symmetric extrude, and revolves; and whether the rule's start curve is the one with the largest id or the newest. The rule holds on single-loop extrudes and base flanges; the largest id and the newest curve coincide where read. Decides whether a Fusion writer names those forms' side faces; until then it names caps and the forms the rule covers, and a feature that picks another side face, or an edge beside one, is a feature whose names it cannot produce (§3.4). Would settle it: loops with inner loops, trimmed pieces, and circles, and revolves, joined the same way; a sketch whose newest curve does not carry the largest id.
134. **SolidWorks face ordinals.** The rule that assigns `n` in `Fillet(F, n)`, field `a` of `WzdHole(H, a, b)`, and the name SolidWorks accepts on a face that no rule names. `n` usually runs over 1 to N, N the selected edge count or larger, and follows neither the API edge order nor the face node order, nor throughout the stored selection order; `b` identifies the hole's position (faces of one `b` share one axis, and different values have different axes); `a` varies with the face kind; the shell's rule is settled (§5.7). Decides whether a SolidWorks writer names fillet and Hole Wizard faces and picks them by name; until then their picks are written in the unresolved-reference form (§3.4). Would settle it: the pre-fillet state from the deltas, its selection's edge order set against `n`; each `a` set against its hole's profile elements.
135. **CATIA limit-curve circle mode.** That CATIA stores the limit-curve-and-tangency-surface circle subtype, `TangentLimitRadius`, as mode 10 (§6.6). A mode-10 sweep's operands are one curve, one reference surface, a radius, and two relimiting angles, which no other subtype has; its surface is not sampled against the reference surface. Decides the CATIA decoder's `CircleMode` for stored 10; until then `TangentLimitRadius`. Would settle it: a mode-10 sweep's surface sampled at a station against its reference surface and limit curve.
136. **Dome surface.** The surface SolidWorks builds for a dome over a circular face and in its elliptical and continuous forms (§6.4). A default convex dome over an outline that is not a circle is a degree-5 B-spline cap whose highest point lies `height` above the face plane, at the outline box's centre in the surface's frame, fitting no sphere and no radial profile of the peak. Decides a writer's lowering of a dome to a target's spherical or ellipsoidal cap; until then step 3 (§3.4). Would settle it: a dome over a circular face and an elliptical dome, their cap surfaces' types and radii read from the partition.
137. **Flex laws.** How SolidWorks flex varies a twist or a taper between the trim planes, what a taper factor scales, which trim plane a stretch keeps, and whether material beyond the trims moves rigidly. No part known to the project declares a class whose name contains `flex`. Decides a writer's lowering of `Flex` (§6.5); until then step 3 (§3.4). Would settle it: one part with a flex of each kind, its states before and after the flex compared at three stations along the triad's z axis.
138. **Fusion hole tokens on few faces.** That Fusion tokens 7 and 8 are a counterbore's wall and floor and selector-2 token 10 a countersink's cone on every hole, that token 2 names a flat bottom as 4 and 5 do, and which tokens name the faces of tapered, spotface, and counterdrill heads (§5.7). Token 7 marks cylinders and token 8 planes of counterbore holes, and token 10 cones; the token-7 cylinder's radius is the counterbore radius, not the bore radius, and the token-10 cone's angle the stored head angle; the token-2 face lies at its hole's stored depth, its outward normal against the drilling direction. Decides the Fusion decoder's `Hole` roles for those tokens; until then the roles §5.7 states, and a token no rule maps is `Other` with its code. Would settle it: counterbore and countersink holes' token-7 radii and token-10 angles set against their stored head parameters; token-2 faces set against their holes' stored form; one Fusion hole of each other head form.
139. **Fusion flange and hem forms.** That Fusion stores the flange height datum as the API value plus one (1 `InnerSharp`, 2 `OuterSharp`), and that teardrop and rolled hems are as §6.6 states (§6.6). A code-1 flange's free end lies at the inner sharp's reading and a code-2 one's at the outer sharp's, where swapped labels predict the reverse; the teardrop's fold radius, return tilt, and end gap, and the rolled hem's arc, follow their values. Decides the Fusion decoder's `height_datum` codes and hem forms; until then the mappings §6.6 states. Would settle it: flanges whose heights are read against their solids; teardrop and rolled hems of other values.
140. **SolidWorks pierce on an interior crossing.** That a SolidWorks pierce relation (code 40) puts its point where its curve crosses the sketch plane where that crossing is not the curve's end (§6.1). The point lies on the curve at its crossing of the sketch plane, and a projection reading does not fit; where the crossing is the path's start, crossing and end coincide. Decides the SolidWorks decoder's mapping of code 40; until then `Pierce`. Would settle it: a pierce whose curve crosses the plane at an interior point, as a profile sketch placed part way along a sweep path.
141. **SolidWorks inner-loop taper.** That SolidWorks tapers a drafted profile's inner loops `WithRegion` in every design (§6.3). Inner-loop faces of a drafted cut or boss have the outer faces' sign of n·d, where `WithOuter` predicts the opposite. Decides the SolidWorks decoder's `ExtrudeDraft.holes`; until then `WithRegion`. Would settle it: drafted extrudes with holes in further designs.
142. **Fusion draft sign, and inner loops of other sources.** That a positive Fusion `TaperAngle` widens the outer loop of an extrude that adds material on every feature; the sign and inner-loop taper of a drafted Fusion cut; and how Inventor and Creo taper the inner loops of a drafted extrude (§6.3). A drafted Fusion extrude that adds material tapers its concentric outer and hole walls `WithRegion`, not `WithOuter`, by face-name attribution, and its positive angle widens the outer loop; a holed Fusion cut keeps only its hole walls. Decides the Fusion decoder's sign and a cut's `draft`, and the Inventor and Creo decoders' `ExtrudeDraft.holes`; until then the Fusion decoder negates the angle of an extrude that adds material and states `WithRegion`, keeps a cut's angles as `f3d:TaperAngle` and `f3d:Side2TaperAngle`, and Inventor and Creo state `None`. Would settle it: further drafted Fusion extrudes that add material and a drafted cut with an island, their walls attributed by name; per source, an Inventor or Creo drafted extrude with a hole, its inner faces' sign of n·d set against the outer faces'.
143. **Fusion operation settings below Rule H1's threshold.** The Fusion bindings of §7.3 and §7.5 that do not meet Rule H1's threshold or rest on one value: `finishingStepover` with `numberOfFinishingStepovers`, `stockToLeave` (a `pocket2d` finishing pass, and `adaptive2d` wall passes bounded by it), `verticalStockToLeave`, `numberOfFinishingStepdowns` above 1, `entry_sweep` (one value, 90°, at which a sweep and its supplement coincide), and pocket clearing's `maximumStepover` (an evened bound, never equal); `HeightFrom::ModelTop`, `closed_pass_overlap` from `finishingOverlap`, `PassTransition::Line` and `None`, `reduce_feed` from `useFeedOptimization`, and `HoleDepth` (where same-hole pairs share a bottom mode and the tip term, so `break_through` without `tip_through` is not shown). Decides each binding of the Fusion decoder; until then the bindings §7.3 and §7.5 state, the ones listed here where the stored toolpath agrees. Would settle it: per setting, operations that vary it alone.
144. **Inventor coil rotation in general.** That Inventor's coil flag `ClockwiseRotation`, the slot-3 Boolean of the coil's property record, is true for a right-handed coil in every file (§6.3). A helical face joined to its coil, its helix fitted with both ends on the end-cap centres, is right-handed where the flag is true and left-handed where it is false; the other Booleans do not separate them. Decides the Inventor decoder's `hand`; until then `Right` where the flag is true and `Left` where it is false. Would settle it: a coil of another save version or with a reversed axis, its helical face set against the flag.
145. **Fusion to-face holes.** That a Fusion hole with extent control 1 whose last construction group names a face is a to-face limit and not through all (§6.4). Its bore ends on the named face, at the exact intersection radius on a spherical face; where the body does not continue past the face, through all gives the same bore. Decides that mapping; until then `ToGeometry` on the face (§6.4). Would settle it: a control-1 hole with a face operand past whose face the body continues along its axis.
146. **Support trimming in general.** That a CATIA blend limit storing 2 in `TrimSupport` puts its support in the result (§6.3, `Section.trim_support`). The report of a blend whose limits store 2 lists new cells that are copies of its supports' faces among its result's cells, and a blend at the default lists none; where the supports were cut at the limit curve before the blend, the two readings agree. Decides the CATIA decoder's `trim_support`; until then `Some(true)` where a limit stores 2. Would settle it: a blend that trims supports not cut before it.
147. **STEP directed-location order by producer.** Which producers write a `DIRECTED_DIMENSIONAL_LOCATION` with the origin as the relating shape aspect, as ISO 10303 defines it (§8). An ST-Developer file names its relating aspect `ORIGIN`; a CATIA V5 export may store as related the datum face its own presentation draws as the origin; an Open CASCADE file's relating aspect is the shared base of a baseline chain. Decides whether a STEP decoder reads a producer's order as stored; until then it reads every file as ISO 10303 defines. Would settle it: the stored directed locations of each producer, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading: each set against its drawn origin symbol; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
148. **Creo spherical equation curves in general.** That a Creo spherical curve from equation (`csys_type` 4, instruction 4134, `rho`, `theta`, `phi` assigned) measures `theta` from the frame's +z axis and `phi` about z from x toward y, in degrees (§6.6). `theta` from −z with `phi` clockwise gives the same point set, and only a sweep's start at t = 0 puts `theta`'s zero at +z. Decides the Creo decoder's reading of the spherical form; until then the stated convention. Would settle it: a spherical curve from equation whose curve, or a feature built on it, stores points, set against the convention.
149. **NX swept interpolation in general.** That NX Swept's interpolation byte 02 is `Linear` and 04 `Smooth` on every record, and that bytes 6 and 7 of the option array do not carry the interpolation (§6.3). The label `SKIN` is shared by swept, ruled, and bounded-plane records, whose class the owning section's class list gives. Bytes 6 and 7 differ between the 02 and 04 records as byte 2 does, and a record may store 04 with the bytes 6 and 7 of an 02 record. Decides which byte the NX decoder reads for `section_law`; until then byte 2, with bytes 6 and 7 kept as native options. Would settle it: a record of three or more sections whose bytes 6 and 7 do not follow byte 2, with its surfaces read.
150. **Pipe section turn below Rule H1's threshold.** That a Fusion pipe's section turns as `SectionTurn::PathPlane` and `ZStart` state on every pipe (§6.3). `PathPlane` holds on a triangular pipe on a straight path, and `ZStart` on a square pipe on a path that leaves its plane, from a start set by the model's z axis; neither arm meets Rule H1's threshold; on a path of body edges the transport is not read; a triangle's apex side is A.12. Decides the Fusion decoder's `turn`; until then the arms where the stored faces agree, else `None`. Would settle it: square pipes on spatial sketch paths; a pipe on body edges, its section at several stations.
151. **NX symmetric-angle draft in general.** That NX's `TAPER_SYMMETRIC` draft is one angle applied from the section plane toward both limits in every file (§6.3). Stored cones and cap circles of a legacy-release file follow the profile circles under that reading, with the limits from the records. Decides the NX decoder's `ExtrudeDraft` for that class; until then both angles the class's. Would settle it: a symmetric-angle draft in a file of a later release, of another angle, its cap circles set against its profile.
152. **Rhino loft style carrier.** That value 9 of a Rhino loft's history record states its style, its values 0 and 2 being the styles RhinoCommon's `LoftType` numbers so, and the other fields of the record as read, on every loft (§6.3). Each loft's end rows and knot steps rebuild from its sections (`ChordLength`, `SqrtChordLength`; §6.3); the record's antecedent list is not always in loft order, and value 100 gives the order, as a list whose form (object ids or antecedent indices) the decoder reads as typed, carrier unread; the natural end shape does not fit values 14 and 15; value 10 is read as the simplify mode from its position only; whether the `SqrtChordLength` rule belongs to the style or to the Rhino 4 release that wrote it is A.18. Decides the Rhino decoder's `style`; until then the mapping §6.3 states, each arm where its rebuild gives the stored net, else `Native`. Would settle it: a `SqrtChordLength` loft written by a later Rhino.
153. **SolidWorks translate surface in general.** That a SolidWorks offset-from-surface end with its translate word set is `Translated` on every end (§6). Ends whose targets are not planes perpendicular to the direction separate the two readings; the face-layout block's word positions are inferred by alignment with the normal layout. Decides the SolidWorks decoder's `Translated`; until then as §6 states. Would settle it: the stored SolidWorks offset-from-surface ends on a tilted plane whose translate option takes each value, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading: the end face set against the target; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
154. **NX general pattern in general.** That an NX general pattern with point locations is `Points` with its from-point as `reference` in every design (§6.5). Such a pattern has identity rotations and every instance on a stored cylinder of the seed's radius. Decides the NX decoder's general layout; until then `Points`. Would settle it: general patterns of point locations in further designs, their instances' faces set against the translations.
155. **NX single output carrier.** Which stored value of an NX pattern record states single output (§6.5). A `Multi Instance Output` pattern record's child list holds one kind-02 child for its declared instances, where a multi-output record holds one kind-03 child per instance; among the unassigned fields only the reference-point lane count separates the two forms (5 on a single-output record, 2 or 3 on the others), besides a file edit stamp and the symmetric flag. Decides the NX decoder's and writer's reading of `nx:single_output`; until then the form is read from the child list, and the lane count stays native. Would settle it: further single-output patterns, their lane counts set against 5.
156. **SolidWorks fill optimize on other boundaries.** What a SolidWorks fill with optimize set builds over a boundary that is not four-sided, two-sided, or planar (§6.6). Tail byte a+6 set gives a degree-3 B-surface patch and clear a degree-5 one; a set fill over five edges that closes a solid is a degree-3 surface that does not lie on its own boundary. Decides what the SolidWorks decoder states for `simplified` there; until then the decoder states the flag, and a writer of another codec charges a loss for a set patch over such a boundary (§6.6). Would settle it: optimized fills over five or more edges, their patches set against their boundaries.
157. **CATIA stamp forms in general.** That the CATIA louver, flanged cutout, bridge relief, and bead read as §6.6 states on every stamp (§6.6). Decides the CATIA decoder's `Louver`, its flanged-cutout `ExtrudedHole`, `relief_length`, and `Bead`; until then as §6.6 states. Would settle it: further louvers' faces; a flanged cutout of another profile; bridge reliefs on a sheet of another thickness; a bead with unequal height and radius.
158. **CATIA K-factor formula.** Which quantities CATIA's `DINNormaFormula` binds, read as K = ½ − ¼·log10(min(100, max(5t/r, 1))) (§6.6). The body text read with its arguments as t and r does not fit; the second argument's binding is inferred, and the law's clamps at r/t of 0.05 and 5 are not read on a stored part. Decides the CATIA decoder's translation of the formula into the K-factor's expression; until then the law stated. Would settle it: the formula's relation record read for its argument bindings; a part with r/t above 5 or below 0.05.
159. **SolidWorks bend table in general.** That a SolidWorks part's stored bend table reads as §6.6 states on every part, what its angle column measures, and how a bend between its values is read (§6.6). A sheet-metal record governed by a stored table has method byte 4 with an evaluated cell; the table's blocks and its cell set against flat strips are read; stored tables include bend allowance grids by gauge and bend deduction grids by thickness, angle, and radius. Where a table's cells do not change with the angle, the angle column's measure and the law between values are not read, and SolidWorks' page says only that the software interpolates between thicknesses and between angles. Decides the SolidWorks decoder's `BendTable.angle` and `lookup`; until then `angle: None` and no axis of `lookup`. Would settle it: a part whose table's cells vary with the angle, its bends of two angles set against their flat strips.
160. **NX neutral factor in general.** That an NX sheet-metal part's flat length follows its neutral-factor expression and not its stored formula text on every flat (§6.6). A flat solid beside its formed body follows the factor; no part known to the project is saved with its allowance method set to a formula or a table. Decides the NX decoder's `KFactor`; until then as §6.6 states. Would settle it: the stored NX sheet-metal parts whose neutral-factor method, formula or table, takes each value, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading: the flat set against each; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
161. **Bend zone codes below Rule H1's threshold.** That Creo's `order_ptr.flip` bit 128 and the Inventor Fold's slot-0 value 2 are `FixedSide` (§6.6). Creo bits 64, 128, and 256 and Inventor slot-0 values 0, 1, and 2 are read (§6.6); `FixedSide` does not meet Rule H1's threshold. Decides the Creo and Inventor decoders' `zone`; until then the mappings §6.6 states. Would settle it: further Creo bends of bit 128 and Inventor folds of slot 0 = 2, each fixed flat's end set against the line.
162. **NX unsew in general.** That an NX unsew by edge splits a sheet into two bodies that each keep a copy of the edge, and which side keeps the input body (§6.6). Its input lane, its two result entries (body identities and their group nodes), and the faces and edges of each body before and after it are read; that the operand is an edge is read from its node id; a set of edges that leaves the sheet in one piece or in more than two, and which piece keeps the input body among more than two, are not read. Decides the NX decoder's `Unsew` and its outputs' order; until then as §6.6 states. Would settle it: an unsew of a sheet whose two sides were made in the other order, its bodies set against the input.
163. **Decal image orientation.** That a Fusion decal's image runs with its top toward +V, so that texture v = 0 is its top row, as the right-handed frames of its unmirrored decals imply (§6.4). The frames, flags, and texture coordinates are read; no image's content is set against its placement, so which row the stored v places at which end of V is not read. Decides the Fusion decoder's `frame` y; until then +V. Would settle it: the stored display state set against the record, over the stored files that hold each value: the file's stored preview image set against the record. Where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
164. **Relative cylinder in general.** That Fusion's relative cylinder is the smallest cylinder about its axis that holds the model and that its radial offset grows the radius, on every setup (§7.2). On a part round about its axis the smallest cylinder and the larger cross extent coincide; the offset's side is inferred; an older setup form caches no diameter. Decides the Fusion decoder's `RelativeCylinder`; until then as §7.2 states. Would settle it: a relative-cylinder setup on a part that is not round about its axis, with a radial offset, set against a toolpath that reaches the stock's outer radius.
165. **Creo workcell heads and axis readings.** That a Creo workcell's two tool tables are two heads or turrets; that axis bit 21 on a mill-turn workcell states two rotary axes, and on a two-turret lathe its second turret; and which of codes 188 and 189 is the rotary letter (§7.6). On a mill, two rotary axes follow bit 21, one bit 22, and without a bit one axis explains the tool directions (§7.6); bit 21 is set on mill-turn records whose tool table is named for five axes; codes 188 and 189 are equal where stored and follow no stored motion. Two tables are read as two heads from a drawing's names and the turning models that hold them, and no sequence's tool is set against its table; a mill-turn's count is inferred from the mills' bits and the named records; type word 9 is read as two turrets with no named record. Decides the Creo decoder's `rotary_axes` for a mill-turn and its pockets' `turret`; until then as §7.6 states, and codes 188 and 189 stay machine parameters. Would settle it: a mill-turn sequence whose tool comes from the second table, its toolpath set against the second head's frame; a 4-axis workcell whose codes 188 and 189 differ.
166. **Fusion link and transition feeds in a posted program.** That a posted Fusion program feeds code-5 moves at `noEngagementFeedrate` and code-4 moves at `tool_feedTransition` where those differ from the cutting feed (§7.5, §7.8). Both bindings are typed from the vendor's posts; no stored toolpath and no posted program shows either applied. The current vendor posts (Fanuc, Haas, Siemens 840D, Heidenhain) feed code 4 from `tool_feedTransition` where the operation holds it and from the cutting feed where it does not, and the older stock post knows only the cutting feed; no stored motion record holds a feed. Decides no type: it confirms the Fusion decoder's `Link` and `Transition` bindings; until then as §7.5 and §7.8 state. Would settle it: the `noEngagementFeedrate` of operations whose toolpaths hold code 5, set against their cutting feeds; then a posted program of an operation whose `tool_feedTransition` differs from its cutting feed and whose toolpath holds code 4, or of one whose `noEngagementFeedrate` differs from its cutting feed.
167. **Creo identical pattern ended on a surface.** Whether a Creo identical pattern (`pat_type` bit 32) recomputes a member's end where the seed is extruded up to a surface (§6.5). A bit-32 member holds copies of the leader's intersection edges and none of its own, and the members' stored surfaces are the leader's moved rigidly; where the seed is extruded up to a surface, a member's end plane may lie apart from the moved leader's while its edge rows are copies. Decides whether the Creo decoder states `Identical` for a bit-32 pattern whose seed ends on a surface; until then `Identical`, as §6.5 states. Would settle it: a bit-32 pattern of an extrude up to a surface that is not parallel to the pattern's direction, its members' end faces set against the seed's.
168. **NX draft from the start limit in general.** That NX's from-edge draft class is `DraftNeutral::Start`, the cross-section at the start limit being the profile, on every extrude (§6.3). Where the start limit lies away from the section, the side face meets the profile at the start limit, where a draft from the section does not, and lies (h − start)·tan θ off it past the start (§6.3); where the start is at the section plane, `Start` and `Origin` give one body. Decides the NX decoder's `ExtrudeDraft.neutral` for that class; until then `Start`. Would settle it: further from-edge drafts whose start limit lies away from their section, of other angles, their side faces set against their profile at the start limit.
169. **NX face region rule in general.** That NX's region-boundary face rule is the face form of `SelectionRule::Region`, a seed face with `domain: Containing(point)` and the boundary loops, on every pick (§5.8). Each pick resolves to the face under its seed point, its boundary track rows close, and the boundary may take the whole face or cut it. Decides the NX decoder's `Region` for a face rule; until then as §5.8 states. Would settle it: an NX 10 file's second item parsed, and its `OFFSET_REGION` records joined to their collectors; then a face rule whose boundary cuts several faces.
170. **NX region rule tolerance.** That the length an NX region rule stores is a copy of its file's distance tolerance, so that `tolerances.linear` stands for it and the rule needs no field (§5.8). A sketch region rule and a face pick store their file's section tolerance T; a track reference names one line, arc, or spline; the links between a region's curves lie within T. Links on arcs whose frame the reader does not take and on splines are not read; that curves within T meet is consistent with the links and is not separated from a smaller threshold. Decides whether the NX decoder states a tolerance on a `Region`; until then it states none, and a rule whose length differs from its section's keeps it in the selection's native record. Would settle it: the links on arcs and splines read.
171. **Adjusting pattern construction by application.** Which construction, `ModelSoFar` or `ModelBefore`, the adjusting pattern of Fusion and Inventor (adjust) and of NX (variational) uses (§6.5). Where a pattern's fillets and to-face ends touch only geometry made before the pattern, both constructions give the same faces; an NX meeting record may leave incomplete instances that are not the build-order prefix `ModelSoFar` leaves; CATIA keep specifications is `ModelSoFar` (§6.5). Which NX byte is the variational method is not established (one candidate byte, contradicted by a label), and the NX seed list is not resolved. Decides those decoders' `against`, and when a writer to those formats is free of the loss §6.5 names; until then `against: None`, and a writer is free of the loss where its second test holds. Would settle it: NX pattern records put through the meeting test; per application, a pattern whose seed ends on geometry another instance makes.
172. **SolidWorks ruled-surface record.** That a SolidWorks ruled surface's record closes as read: its type the u32 after the distance, 0 to 4 in the order of the API's codes (tangent to surface, normal to surface, tapered to vector, perpendicular to vector, sweep), its distance and angle the display dimensions D1 and D2, and three option words b, c, and d (§6.6). Type 2 records are those whose surfaces are inclined to a direction; c, set only on type 2, is read as the tapered type's direction flip (inferred); d is trim and knit (inferred: a record with several faces and d = 1 makes fewer bodies than faces, and one with d = 0 keeps its faces apart); b is 0 at a corner with a gap, which is `Open` (A.42). That b is connecting surfaces rests on d's reading and on a cleared corner (A.42); types 0 and 3 do not meet Rule H1's threshold. Decides the SolidWorks decoder's ruled-surface type and options; until then the type as read, and the three words as `sldprt:ruled_option_b`, `sldprt:ruled_option_c`, and `sldprt:ruled_option_d`. Would settle it: the stored SolidWorks ruled surfaces whose trim-and-knit or connecting-surface option takes each value, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading: their words set against the default's; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
173. **SolidWorks fill record fields.** That a SolidWorks fill record's mark is the u32 after the `moPMarkRecord_c` tag of its body head, and that an item's flag byte states the item's kind and its contact (§6.6). The mark is a mark id of configuration 0's deltas; the flag byte's high nibble is 1 on items that hold a body edge and 0 on those that hold a sketch or curve; its low nibble takes 0, 1, and 2 on edge items, read as contact, tangent, and curvature from its domain, no face normal being compared (inferred); tail byte a+10 is not read. Decides the SolidWorks decoder's reading of a fill's state and of its edges' continuity; until then the mark as read, and the low nibble and a+10 native options. Would settle it: the patch's normals along each edge item set against the adjoining face's, by low nibble.
174. **SolidWorks fillet option block.** That the three varying positions of a SolidWorks fillet's option block are tangent propagation (+0), keep features (+16), and attachment edges (+37, inverted) (§6.4). Against the API export, +0 equals tangent propagation, +16 keep features, and +37 is 0 where attachment edges are set and nonzero where not; no other position varies; +37 can take a value other than 0 and 1, attachment edges does not meet Rule H1's threshold, and a record whose block is not located is not read. Decides the SolidWorks decoder's `Propagation`, `BlendControls.keep_features`, and attachment edges; until then +0 and +16 as read, and +37 as the native option `sldprt:attachment_edges`. Would settle it: records whose block is not located, read for their block.
175. **Fusion hem side in general.** That Fusion's hem flip byte is 0 `HemSide::SelectedEdgeFace` and 1 `OppositeFace`, and that the picked edge decides the fold where the wall's growth side differs, on every hem (§6.6). Every vertex an unflipped hem makes lies above the sheet face that holds its picked edge, and every vertex of a flipped hem beyond the opposite face; a hem on an edge flange folds over the picked edge's face and away from the growth side. `OppositeFace`, and the picked-edge rule against the growth-side rule, do not meet Rule H1's threshold. Decides the Fusion decoder's `Hem.side`; until then the mapping §6.6 states. Would settle it: further flipped hems, and hems on walls whose picked edge does not lie on the growth face, their vertices set against the picked edge's face.
176. **Inventor bend-table deduction above 90° in general.** That an Inventor bend-table cell above 90° of deflection is a deduction between flanges measured to the outer tangent planes, `FlangeMeasure::OuterSharpThenTangent`, and that the table's angle column is the opening angle, on every part (§6.6). A bend zone above 90° has the flat width of the tangent-plane measure, where flanges measured to the outer sharp do not fit; the opening angle is read from the shape of a table's values and from Autodesk's page; a table symmetric about 90°, or a flat holding only bends of 90°, does not test the angle column's measure. Decides the Inventor decoder's `BendTableValue` and `BendTable.angle`; until then `Deduction { flanges: Some(OuterSharpThenTangent) }` and `Opening`. Would settle it: further Inventor parts with a table rule, a flat pattern, and bends above 90°; a part whose table is not symmetric about 90° and whose flat holds a bend off 90°.
177. **Inventor bend equation readings.** That an Inventor equation rule's flanges are measured as a table's are, that its `ref` codes 3 and 2 are the opening angle and the deflection, and that the two flags of a range record are its bounds' inclusion (§6.6). The rule records and `kind` 1 and 4 are read from what their expressions compute; a common rule's expressions subtract the two setbacks of Inventor's table unfolding, term for term. The flange measure is inferred from that rule's expressions, the `ref` codes from expressions, and the flags from the stored ranges covering the angles with no overlap; none is set against an unfolding. Decides the Inventor decoder's `BendEquations`; until then `Compensation { flanges: Some(OuterSharpThenTangent) }` for a rule with that rule's ranges and `flanges: None` for any other, with `ref` and the flags as read. Would settle it: an Inventor part with a flat pattern under an equation rule, its bend zones' widths set against the rule's expressions.
178. **Creo wall readings below Rule H1's threshold.** That a Creo wall of `misc_choice[0]` bit 512 is `ExtendWall`; that an attached bit-2 wall is a `ContourFlange` of `width: Full`; that an unattached bit-2 wall ends at the far end of its instruction-4487 edge; that an attached bit-8 wall is a `ContourFlange` of `width: FromReference`; that an attached wall with neither bit has its free ends on the sharp of its sketch face's side, its `Flange.outline`, and states no `angle`, its outline sketch's plane being the construction through the attach edge at an angle to the base wall whose dimension binds the type-205 dimension, stated where the plane's stored position agrees, and otherwise the dimension kept as the native option `creo:wall_angle`, which a writer of another format charges as `export:parameter.flattened`; and that a Creo flange stated without an `outline` takes `angle` as 180° less the type-205 dimension's magnitude (§6.6). A face of a bit-512 wall lies on the plane its instruction 4438 names. A bit-2 wall holds no width dimension of type 62, which bit-8 walls hold; an attached bit-2 wall spans its attach edge, flush with the edge's ends or between vertices that earlier features placed, never short of it; an unattached bit-2 wall's far end lies at the far end of its 4487 edge, and no stored dimension equals the extent; the 4487 edge is an earlier feature's, read from the hidden edge the later features leave. A bit-8 wall starts in its sketch plane at the instruction-4488 point and runs its type-62 width against the sketch's normal, the 4488 point being a datum point made just before an attached wall; instruction 10 names no edge on an attached bit-8 wall, and its 4487 edge holds the wall's span. An outline wall's free ends lie on the sharp of the sketch face's side, not on the bend's tangent line (§6.6); the type-205 dimension is ±90 or the angle between the walls; the outline sketch's plane holds the attach edge and lies at the stored type-205 angle to a plane through the edge, the base wall's own face or an earlier feature's coplanar plane; the attach edge is the sharp on the sketch face's side, inner or outer; the stored sign is the right-hand turn about the edge's stored direction, with an exception no reading explains, and a writer to Creo re-emits the stored sign (§6.6). An outline wall with no section, no bend pair read, neither face identified, or its bend not identified stays `Native`; a wall that stores no attach edge, or fits two placements, keeps `creo:wall_angle`. Decides the Creo decoder's `ExtendWall`, a bit-2 wall's `width` and `extent`, an attached bit-8 wall's `width`, a wall's `outline`, and the plane construction that binds its type-205 dimension; until then the mapping §6.6 states under Rule H1, and `SheetMetalKind::Native("creo:wall")` where the stored faces do not agree. Would settle it: attached bit-2 walls' end planes set against the ends of their attach edges; bit-8 walls whose 4487 edge does not resolve, read against their faces; native outline walls' sections and bend pairs read; bit-512 walls in further parts; binary Creo files searched for outline walls, their sketch planes set against their type-205 dimensions.
179. **Angle sense outside Creo's outline-flange walls.** Whether each source's stored construction angles turn in §5.9's positive sense, the right-hand turn about the axis's stored direction, which a decoder states where a construction's stored `resolved` agrees with it and otherwise keeps as the source's form (§5.9). The Creo outline-flange wall's stored sign follows the sense with an exception (B.178); no construction angle of another source, and no other Creo construction angle, is set against the sense. Decides, per source, whether its decoder states an angle input in §5.9's sense directly or through `Dimension::Negated` where no `resolved` is stored; until then the input's relation is `Native` under the source's name with the stored value there (§5.9). Would settle it: per source, the construction angle inputs that store a `resolved`, each set against the positive sense.
180. **Decal flags and frame normal.** That a Fusion decal's second flag byte reverses its width and its third its height, so that a frame with x along −U and y along −V and a `mirrored` that is the exclusive or of the two bytes states a decal that sets the third; and that the frame's z is the faces' outward normal at its origin (§6.4). The width runs along −U where the second byte is set, and the height is reversed where the third is; N is U × V, and the origin lies on the mesh surface. Neither flag meets Rule H1's threshold, and N is not set against the face's normal at the origin. Decides the Fusion decoder's `frame` and `mirrored`; until then as §6.4 states. Would settle it: the direction of u on decals that set the second byte; N set against the B-rep face's normal at the origin.
181. **Fusion lead, lift, and ramp bindings below Rule H1's threshold.** That Fusion's `entry_perpendicular` and `exit_perpendicular` bind `Lead.line_turn`, `Perpendicular` where true and `Tangent` where false, on a lead whose line meets an arc; the link length below which `Linking.lift` does not raise a stay-down link; which radius a pocket strategy adds to `PlungeStrategy.start_above`; and what the adaptive lead arcs that do not sit at `leadRadius` follow (§7.3). With the flag true the line is perpendicular to the cut on a lead with no arc and runs along the arc's radius on one with an arc, and with it false the line is tangent or in line; a stay-down link under a `liftHeight` above 0 rises exactly `liftHeight` or not at all, the unlifted being the short links, at a boundary of 0.48 of the tool diameter (inferred); a pocket operation may lift none of its links; a pocket strategy's first ramp does not start at the top plus the clearance, a ramp that starts higher exceeding it by the lead-in radius, and a ramp may start below the top; many adaptive lead arcs off `leadRadius` match no numeric setting of their operation, a constant 1.583 mm arc occurring with tools of 2 to 16 mm. The line with an arc does not meet Rule H1's threshold; the length limit is inferred; where the two lead radii are equal, which one the ramp adds is not separated. Decides the Fusion decoder's bindings of the three settings and of `arc_radius` on adaptive clearing; until then as §7.3 states. Would settle it: ramps that start below the top set against their stock and model tops; an operation of a strategy other than chamfering with the flag true and a lead arc; a pocket operation whose two lead radii differ; off-radius arcs set against the strategy's fixed shapes by tool diameter.
182. **Fusion toolpath attribute readings.** That a Fusion `kind 1` record standing before a cycle's first move, with no parameter after it, is a unit tag a writer can regenerate; how engraving groups its passes into `family` values; and the order of the table that opens a toolpath (§7.8). Such records stand in deep-drilling and chip-breaking cycles; one (`family`, `level`) record stands before each cutting run; every other `kind` precedes a cycle parameter and is the unit class of that parameter. The bare `kind 1` records are read by inference; the engraving grouping does not meet Rule H1's threshold; the opening table's order is a guess. Decides which attributes a Fusion decoder keeps and a Fusion writer regenerates, and no type (Rule N case (b), §7.8); until then the decoder keeps those records and the opening table as attributes. Would settle it: the bare `kind 1` records set against the dwell their cycles write; further engraving toolpaths' passes set against their `family` values.
183. **SolidWorks chamfer loop selection.** That a loop in a SolidWorks chamfer's third selection list decodes to the loop's edges (§6.4). The third list holds loops, `moCompLoop_c` objects or a class with an escaped index; the loops' edges are not joined to the chamfered faces, so the reading is inferred from the rosters, which size on edges. Decides the SolidWorks decoder's chamfer selection; until then the loop's edges. Would settle it: chamfer records' loops joined to the body's edges, set against the chamfer faces.
184. **SolidWorks sweep end flags.** That the two words of a SolidWorks sweep's closing object change no geometry a writer of another format builds (§6.3). At an end that stores 1 with the profile oblique to a planar path, the stored section stays as sketched, as under 0; no file labels the words, and a sweep with guide curves and a 1 is not read. Decides that the decoder keeps them as `sldprt:sweep_start_tangency` and `sldprt:sweep_end_tangency`, which a SolidWorks writer returns unchanged; until then that reading. Would settle it: the stored SolidWorks sweeps with guide curves whose start or end condition takes each value, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
185. **NX curve copies the decoder does not read.** That NX `EXTRACT_STRING` records decode as `Extract` of curves, with a `TransformBodies` copy where one holds an `XFORM`, on every record (§6.5). The outputs lie on their inputs within 1e-6 mm, or are the stored transform of them, a third flag marking a reflection (inferred); some records fit no reading; records in the legacy container's grammar are not parsed, and arc frames are not taken. Decides the NX decoder's `Extract` and `TransformBodies` for those records; until then each where its outputs agree, else native. Would settle it: legacy-container records parsed and set against their outputs; the collectors of records that fit no reading joined to their source parts.
186. **Creo rolled bend line face.** That a Creo rolled bend's `line_face` is read as for an angle bend (§6.6). A roll stores no instruction 403 and so no signed angle; a roll that turns away from the section's facing (toward −z of the section) does so as a positive angle bend does; whether a roll can turn the other way, and where that would be stored, is not read. Decides the Creo decoder's `line_face` for a roll; until then stated only where the stored cylinders agree. Would settle it: a rolled bend that turns toward the section's facing.
187. **Inventor shared-edge bends.** That an Inventor bend of option pair (2, 1) on one edge is `ConnectBetween::SharedEdge` in every file (§6.6). The stored edge lies between two outer sheet faces of one body; each bend adds two coaxial cylinders of the stored radius and that plus the thickness, the outer one tangent to both outer faces. Decides the Inventor decoder's `SharedEdge`; until then stated where the stored bend's faces replace the corner so, else `SheetMetalKind::Native("inventor:bend")` with the edge, radius, and option pair kept. Would settle it: a shared-edge bend at another angle.
188. **Fusion wrap setting.** That Fusion's `doWrap` binds the wrapping §7.5 states for rotary operations, with its radius from the stream's `axisSubstitutionRadius` (§7.5). The toolpath carries an `axisSubstitutionRadius` attribute where the setting is true and not where it is false; the radius's meaning is inferred. Decides the Fusion decoder's wrap; until then a named process parameter. Would settle it: true toolpaths' coordinates set against the radius.
189. **Rips below Rule H1's threshold.** The rip readings that do not meet Rule H1's threshold (§6.6): Creo's surface rip removes the picked wall, no face of the rip covering the middle of the picked face's box, its new faces on its plane, and a rip that names a side wall is not read face by face; Inventor's single-point cut is the face's ruling through the point, from points at fractions 0 and 0.5, and its point-to-point cut a line; a SolidWorks sketch rip cuts one wall through the sheet, centred on its line; Creo's sketched rip is `Projected`, its chain carried along the sketch's normal and the sheet split there with zero width, its section's flip fields recording no choice; and Inventor's `KerfSide::Right`. Decides each decoder's `Rip`; until then stated where the stored result agrees, else `Native` with the picks kept. Would settle it: Creo side-wall rips read face by face; per format, further rips of each kind set against their results.
190. **Creo axis-control readings.** The Creo readings under `ToolAxisControl` that do not meet Rule H1's threshold (§7.3). `AlongRuling` holds except near the ends, where past the face's u range the axis stays in the tangent plane and turns off the ruling; `NormalToSurface` holds on bit-21 sequences whose instruction 966 has offset 1.0, where fixed-axis sequences have offset 0, so the offset is read as a flag (guessed); coded parameters 100, 101, 236, and 259 are 0 where stored; `InPlane` holds, the rotary axis the model's z; `ThroughLine`'s axis meets the line at the foot of the perpendicular from the tool's contact point, and at a right angle where the faces are parallel to the line, where the two coincide, with axes on one parallel-face toolpath passing through one point (not explained); the sequence's edge rows bound the region the tool covers, one ball radius inset. No plane oblique to the model's axes is read. Decides the Creo decoder's `tool_axis`; until then each arm where the stored toolpath agrees, else the operation's native settings. Would settle it: a flank-milling sequence whose toolpath departs from the ruling; a 4-axis sequence on an oblique plane; a through-line sequence of another design on faces oblique to its line.
191. **SolidWorks conversion old layout.** That the counted list of the old Convert to Sheet Metal layout holds pairs of face references, and what they are (§6.6). Each element is two topology references built like the fixed face's, tag occurrences exactly twice the count, the outer class `moCompFace_c` (inferred); the pairs are not joined to the body, so whether they are bends is unknown. Decides whether the decoder states `Convert` from `ConvertFrom::Faces` with `bends` empty; until then `Native("sldprt:convert_v1")` with the face pairs kept. Would settle it: the pairs joined to the stored body's faces.
192. **Fusion conversion's second pick.** That the second pick of a Fusion conversion is the face opposite the first at the thickness (§6.6). The first pick is the face under the stored point, which is `fixed`; the second is inferred to lie at exactly the thickness. Decides how the decoder keeps it; until then the source setting `f3d:convert_second_face`, `thickness` coming from the rule. Would settle it: conversions' second picks' faces set against the first.
193. **Creo tolerance codes of text-section files, and the fit count.** Which code of a Creo text-section file is nominal-only, and how many Creo dimensions store a fit class (§5.12, §8.1). On binary files the codes are read: 1 nominal, 2 plus-minus, 3 limits, 4 symmetric, 8 symmetric superscript, joined to the file's own attributes, and the decoder states `Deviations` with `lower` = −slot 0 and `upper` = slot 1 on codes 2, 3, 4, and 8 (§5.12). A text-section file carries no attribute oracle (no `PTC_*` rows), and three numberings fit every text-section reading (the binary order; codes 1 and 3 swapped; the TOOLKIT order counted from 1, which binary files reject), under each of which codes 2 and 4 state a tolerance; the general tolerance's per-decimals rule does not separate them. A dimension with a fit class matches its stored table cell; whether a fit's deviations are `Cell` or `Own` is decided by the files' stored ISO 286 tables set against the published cells (§5.12). Decides the Creo decoder's `tolerance` on codes 1 and 3 of text-section files and its count of fits; until then it states `Deviations` on codes 2 and 4 there and no `tolerance` on codes 1 and 3, except on a record whose class matches its table cell, which states its `Fit` (§5.12), keeping the code as `creo:tol_type` and, where it states none, the slots as `creo:tol_slot_1` and `creo:tol_slot_2`. Two decoder defects stand beside these: Creo 4 saves write the limit attributes as deviations, not absolute limits, and the positive value lane decodes the prefixes `54` and `58` wrongly (0.195625 for 0.18). Would settle it: stored records with a fit class matched against their tables; each stored table's cells set against ISO 286's.
194. **Computed member names.** That a configuration's name computed by a table formula is stated as its cached text (§5.14). SolidWorks and Inventor table cells may compute the configuration's name by concatenation, each formula reading cells of its own row, with cached texts; an Inventor table's part-number cells that compute its member-name cell's text are `PartNumber::ConfigurationName` (§5.11), so only its name cells stay text. A name that drifts from its formula is not read. Decides the decoders' `ConfigurationRef::Named`; until then the cached string, the formula in the table's native record. Would settle it: a table whose name formula reads a cell that another configuration changes.
195. **Creo family-table records that are not configurations.** That the Creo family-table records below state no configuration of the part (§5.14): hidden instance objects (`inst_hidden` 1, names ending `#AF<n>`), hidden columns of type 14 and type 15, and tables of user-defined-feature groups. A hidden object is the copy of a model cut by an assembly feature, its `model_db` rows assemblies, and every hidden object's name carries `#`; type 14 marks such a part; type 15 is bookkeeping of simplified representations; a group table's rows are variants of the group, which a placed group names. Type 15's cells are not set against the representations. Decides that the Creo decoder mints no `DesignConfiguration` from them; until then that reading. Would settle it: a part with two simplified representations and a type-15 column, its cells set against them.
196. **Fusion empty part-number cell.** That an empty Fusion part-number cell is the rule that the configuration's part number is its name (§5.11, §5.14). Where the cell is empty the document's part number is the row's name, in the property archive and in the Design stream; a file that stores such a cell's row data holds `Option: 0` with the row's name, where a cell with typed text holds `Option: 1`. Where no row is renamed, a stored flag that follows the configuration's name is not separated from stored text equal to it. Decides the Fusion decoder's `part_number`; until then `PartNumber::ConfigurationName` for an empty cell, inferred. Would settle it: a table of two rows with empty part-number cells, one row renamed after the cells were set, each configuration's stored part number.
197. **Fusion pattern compute words.** That two payload words of a Fusion pattern hold its compute option (optimized, identical, adjust) and its pattern object (faces, features, bodies) (§6.5). The two words are read against the patterns' labels only. Decides the Fusion decoder's `method` and operand kind; until then that reading. Would settle it: the stored Fusion patterns whose compute option takes each value, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
198. **Flange extent readings below Rule H1's threshold.** The flange extent readings that do not meet Rule H1's threshold (§6.6): Inventor's Width extent with a reference point is `FlangeWidth::FromReference`, a record may hold a point and a width and no offset, and the face or plane the user picked is not in the record; Fusion's contour flange marks a symmetric extent, `Span::Symmetric` with `measure: Some(PerSide)`, by two head words of 1 (inferred), and a one-sided extent's side is stated only where the profile sketch's plane is read; Fusion's two-distance records are `Span::Between` with both distances, one to each side of the sketch plane, and where the two distances are equal, which of `Span`'s ends `AlongDistance` takes is not separated; and SolidWorks' open base flanges, whose extent block is read against the flange's end caps, its mid-plane form `Span::Symmetric` with `measure: Some(Total)` and its two-direction form `Between` with two depths. Where Inventor stores the picked face or plane is not read. Decides those decoders' `width` and `extent`; until then each where the stored footprint or faces agree, the native option `f3d:contour_flange_extent` for a Fusion symmetric record whose faces do not agree, `Native("f3d:ContourFlange")` for a Fusion record whose side is not read, and `Native("sldprt:base_flange")` for a SolidWorks record whose caps disagree, that keeps no cap of its own, whose caps no witness scores, or whose faces are not checked. Would settle it: further Width flanges with a reference, and their picked face; further symmetric Fusion contour flanges; a Fusion two-distance flange of unequal distances; SolidWorks blocks' faces set against their caps; further SolidWorks two-direction base flanges.
199. **CATIA keep specifications and fix together.** Two CATIA readings that do not meet Rule H1's threshold (§6.5, §6.7): keep specifications is `Adjust { against: Some(ModelSoFar) }`: its carrier is `DesignIntent` 2, and its meaning is inferred by elimination of the dialog's other options; `ModelSoFar` is inferred from the stored build order where the pattern stores per-instance copies, and is not read where it stores no build order; `DesignIntent` 1 is `Identical` (inferred); and a fix-together group is a `RigidGroup` whose members keep their stored placements, since its record stores no pose, a record may carry an unread Boolean, and a record's member list may not be read. Decides the CATIA decoder's `against`, the Boolean's reading, and those records' members; until then `ModelSoFar` where the pattern stores its build, else `None`, the Boolean kept as the group's native option, and a record whose members are not read `FeatureOperation::Native` of kind `catia:FixTogether`. Would settle it: a fix-together group whose Boolean differs.
200. **NX break corners below Rule H1's threshold.** That an NX break corner whose stored faces are cylinders is `CornerBreak::Round`, a radius `size` tangent to both edges that meet at the corner, and which stored value states the round (§6.6). Such a record builds rounds at the stored size through the thickness; a candidate method bit differs between two rounds, so it is not the shape; the picks are thickness edges where the pick-to-corner relation is read, and a record that holds one pick against several broken corners of a cutout is, under Rule H1, `SheetMetalKind::Native("nx:break_corner")`. No stored value is shown to state the round (the chamfer break is A.56). Decides the NX decoder's `shape`; until then `Round` where the stored faces are cylinders, else `CornerBreak::Native("nx:break_corner")` with the method byte kept. Would settle it: further break corners set against their faces.
201. **Fusion pass fields under Rule H1.** That Fusion's pass settings build what §7.5 binds them to on the toolpaths where the stored path does not show it (§7.5): `nullPass` true (`repeat_final_pass`); `cornerMode` `roll` and `sharp` (`corners`); `doRoughingPasses` and `doFinishingPasses` true (`roughing_passes`, `finishing_passes`); `transitionType` `curve` (`PassTransition::Arc`); `maximumRoughingSteps` on contour toolpaths with roughing on (`roughing_pass_count`); `tabWidth`, `tabHeight`, `tabShape` `triangular`, rising over half of `tabWidth` and raised over the tool's diameter at the top, `tabPositioning` `tabCount`, the centres at (i + ½) L / n along the tool-centre path, and `distance` with `tabDistance` on straight edges (`tabs`); and the chamfer depth (`chamfer`) (§7.5). A toolpath set to one of these values may lack the run, arc, junction, or tab its value names, and what such a toolpath does instead is not read. Decides the Fusion decoder's pass fields; until then each stated where the stored toolpath shows the feature it names, else `None` with the setting kept as a named process parameter. 202. **SolidWorks base flanges the record does not separate.** Which kind a SolidWorks base flange (`moSMBaseFlange_c`) is where its profile is a later sketch or its record's shape does not say, the extent and the thickness's side of an open one whose extent block is not read, the side of a base bend's radius where its faces are not read, and whether the contour's start that the thickness flag is read against is the start of the sketch's stored chain (§6.6). The profile reference resolves to its sketch; a record closed by its shape is a `Wall`, an open one a `ContourFlange`, and a record with one child and a depth of its own has no extent equal to `D2`; an open record's extent block may be absent where it stores no `D2` of its own or is of an older layout. `D1` is the bend's inner or outer radius, the radius on the profile's side of the bend, and by a separate clause, inferred, the inner radius where the profile has a sketched arc at the vertex though it lies on the outer face. The u32 47 bytes before the extent block's marker is 0 where the profile lies on one family of side faces and 1 on the other, 0 being the right of the contour run from the flange's first end face, and that start is the start of the sketch's stored chain where it is unambiguous (§6.6). Open: a profile that is a later sketch, whose reference the framing cannot number; the one-child records' kind; the open records' blocks not read, and with them their extents and thickness flags; the profile-side rule, which a SolidWorks writer uses to choose the radius it writes as `D1`, fails on blockless bends whose faces are read; that the contour's start is the stored chain's start does not meet Rule H1's threshold, and the decoder, which reads the sketch's points and drops its lines, reads the profile's chain against the first end face only where the start is unambiguous, a reading the SolidWorks writer also needs to write the flag. Decides the SolidWorks decoder's kind, `extent`, a bend's `radius_side` where its faces are not read, and `thickness`'s `side`; until then a record whose kind the decoder cannot read, a one-child record, and an open record whose block is not read are `Native("sldprt:base_flange")`, `D1` is always the bend's radius, its side stated from the cylinder `D1` equals where both cylinders are read (`Inside` or `Outside`, blockless bends `Inside` among them), and a bend whose `D1` equals neither cylinder makes its flange `Native("sldprt:base_flange")`; the thickness's `side` is stated where the block is read, the faces give the wall's side, and the profile's chain is read against the first end face, the flag is kept as the native option `sldprt:thickness_reverse` wherever the block is read, and `side` is `None` elsewhere, which a writer does not default (§2.4). Would settle it: the feature stream walked as a whole CArchive, which numbers a later sketch's reference, and with it the unread blocks read; the one-child records' profile sketches' segments read for closure; the contour's start set against the stored chain's start on further records whose start is unambiguous; the decoder's sketch reader extended to the lines, so that `side` is stated on the records whose faces give it.
203. **Creo walls in binary files.** Which kinds the Creo walls of binary files are, by the mapping §6.6 states for text-section walls (§6.6). The tools that read text-section walls read no binary records, so binary walls' bits, sections, dimensions, and surfaces are not read. 204. **Creo corner rows the decoder misreads.** The Creo decoder's reading of the type-38 and type-41 rows of a round's corners, of its tori's origins, of the tokens its tables lack, of spline point arrays, of edge rows, and of where a row ends (§6.4). With these readings every two-set junction face reads and fits an arm. Type-38 and type-41 rows read past the envelope body's `e3`, twelve local-system slots and two radii or three `fillet_srf` splines, where the decoder stops at the `e3`; on decoder-placed tori and spheres the cylinders' lane gives the same carrier, the same axis with one origin coordinate negated, or other coordinates, and with the stored reading code-7 tori lie about a listed piece's axis, where with the decoder's many lie on no surface's axis; the fillet reader misframes splines, stops at the openers `a4` and `34 xx yy`, and misreads isolated tokens; the short-float prefixes `1a`, `33`, `39` and the openers `00`, `39` are missing from the decoder's tables, and a junction face may lie on its neighbour's carrier and be no surface of the round, so the decoder may emit it as a face on that carrier. The positive seven-byte lattice for openers `4c` to `59` and `b2` is not `0x3f75 + p` but `3fb1` for `4c`, `3fb5` for `4d`, `0x3f72 + p` for `4e` to `53`, `0x3f73 + p` for `54` to `57`, `0x3f74 + p` for `58` and `59`, and `bfde` for `b2`, fitted on frames; it adds orthonormal frames, loses none, and agrees with the decoder on the slots both read; `41` is an eight-byte form of high byte `bf`, `37` one of `3c`, and `4b` a seven-byte form of `3f b0`; `1b`, `34`, and `20` are three-byte forms of `3c`, `bc`, and `3d`, and `1f` and `38` three-byte near-zero forms; a frame reader bounded at the next row head, resynchronising after an opener it lacks, reads each row's own frame where an unbounded reader takes the next row's. The lattice holds in spline point arrays too, not in parameter arrays, and there loses no row and removes most off-support centre samples; `36` is a seven-byte near-zero form, its high byte fixed by no stored row known to the project; the pcurve lane needs the constant-with-tail forms `01 K b b` and `02 K b b b`, the near-zero forms `21 26 3f`, `27 40 22`, `19 23 37 3c 1e 32`, and `1a 33 20 39`, and `a4` as seven bytes under `bf c0`, with which junction-to-end edge rows read; the edge reader keeps a row's tail only within 400 bytes of its head, which loses spline edge rows of up to 20 KB, and a tail kept anywhere before the next row head closes every visible wrapped loop; opener `0d` reads 0.25 on a torus where the decoder's lane reads it as −1 and gives a radius of 1.0. Open: tori whose coordinates differ otherwise; none of these readings is in the decoder. Decides the Creo decoder's reading of corner rows, spline point arrays, edge rows, and row ends; until then `Native("creo:12")` or `Native("creo:7")` where a junction face is not placed (§6.4). Would settle it: the decoder run with each reading, its placed corners and edges set against the rows read by hand.
205. **Fusion rigid groups joined through tables.** How the Fusion decoder joins a rigid group's members to the occurrences and poses its tables hold (§6.7). A member's final transform comes from an operation table, or from a placement record where no table reaches it; a table whose final entry holds no matrix gives the identity; a placement record equals the table's pose where the table has one entry and may differ where it has more, so it is a member's pose only where no table reaches the occurrence; record `1ABFB679` is an older snapshot, not a member's pose; a listing may name an occurrence the file does not hold. Decides the Fusion decoder's `RigidGroup` members and their occurrences' poses; until then each group with the members that resolve, an unresolved listing kept in the group's `native_options` (§6.7). Would settle it: the table forms the reader cannot parse, read; the decoder run with the join rules, each group's frame set against its members' tables.
206. **Fusion rigid groups' scope contents and names.** That the scope of each rigid group refers to occurrence references and nothing else, how many members each lists, and which store a name, which §6.7 reads (§6.7). A group's scope refers only to occurrence references, from two members to hundreds; a group's name is usually empty and sometimes a user's text; the members and their tables are B.205's. The scope contents and names are not read over the same groups whose members the decoder joins. Decides that the Fusion decoder's `RigidGroup` holds what each group stores, and its name where one is stored; until then as §6.7 states. 207. **Creo corner arms below Rule H1's threshold.** The Creo corner cases of §6.4 that do not meet Rule H1's threshold (§6.4): `RollingBall`'s r, R₁, R₂ case with R₁ and R₂ unequal, and its third face, the ball on the larger piece and on the face the pieces roll on, which `RollingBall`'s definition includes; the three-set r, R, R case on fillet corner faces; one listed set, code 12 `RollingBall` on junction faces, code 7 `SweptAround` on junction torus rows, and code-7 records `Continue`; code 4's `Continue` across unequal ends; three-set code-7 `SweptAround` against an extruded curve and with a constant ball; and `against` empty on two-set r, R, R sweeps that border another feature's cylinder their ball does not touch, `radius` binding the round they continue, and holding the outer cylinder alone on the one-set fillet. 208. **Fusion turning, thread, helix, link, and probe bindings below Rule H1's threshold.** The Fusion bindings of §7.3 and §7.5 that do not meet Rule H1's threshold (§7.3, §7.5): `Operation.radii` from the turning radial modes, the outer clearance, the retract, and the inner clearance; `RadiusFrom::Positions` on grooving passes, each plunge at its point's radius and on the side its `side` states, bound to `sideAlignment`, stated only where a toolpath agrees, and on a pass with no toolpath `RadiusFrom::Native` with the mode, below the floor of Rule H1's untestable-arm clause (§3.1); `line_turn`'s `along`, roughing and facing entries `Backward` and exits `Forward` in the axis's terms, and finishing moves `Forward` in the cut's terms where not square, `along` read only from a toolpath current against the settings, a stale one giving `None`; 209. **CATIA union-trim references.** The CATIA decoder's reading of a union trim's operands, picks, and stored inputs (§6.5). A label record carries its spec list after either the marker `32e1` or `32cc`, so a reader that looks only after `32e1` reads no spec list where a file uses `32cc`; the field reader places the generic fields `ResultIN` (the first operand) and `ResultOUT` (the result) in pick lists, and keeps only a field's first token, so it can read one of a shell's several removed faces; the cell tables and label records give the operands, the pick, and the stored inputs.
