Decides the SolidWorks decoder's `tolerance` on a kind-2 feature record with no annotation: at 3 designs or more, `Deviations` with `a` the upper and `b` the lower, stated under the clause with its count and design count; until then no `tolerance`, the kind and values kept as `sldprt:tolerance` (§5.12). No type depends on it. Would settle it: the kind-2 records joined again to the Inventor-decoded PMI of the same SolidWorks parts, counted by test case.
214. **Inventor fits whose deviations match no table read.** What the stored deviations of an Inventor fit record are where they equal no table cell read, another standard's cell or values the user typed, which decides whether the Inventor decoder states their deviations `Own`, the user's, kept through an edit, or `Cell` against another standard's table, cleared by one (§5.12). Each record's designation and deviations are read against the ANSI B4.1 cell at its nominal; no record names its standard. Decides the Inventor decoder's `deviations` arm on such a record; until then `Fit` with the designation typed, `source: None`, and `deviations: Own` with the stored values, a record at ANSI B4.1's cell stating `Cell` (§5.12). Would settle it: the stored deviations of each Inventor fit, under each standard, set against the same dimension's annotation, its cross-format twin's PMI, or a drawing that displays it, counted by design.
215. **A SolidWorks PMI dimension's decimal key.** The SolidWorks decoder's reading of a PMI dimension's `decimals`, the key a rule by decimals looks the dimension up by (§8, §8.1). The DimXpert dimension records store `BlockToleranceDecimalPlaces`, and SolidWorks semantic dimension records (`DimSemData`) store the displayed places `valPrecision`, with `tolPrecision` for the tolerance. The decoder reads `decimals` from the DimXpert record's `BlockToleranceDecimalPlaces`, and keeps `valPrecision` as `sldprt:val_precision` in the annotation's `source_settings` (case (b), §8). Open: a `DimSemData` record is not joined to the DimXpert dimension or the feature dimension a decoder states, so a PMI dimension read from a semantic record alone has no key read; and no stored dimension known to the project shows the block table applied, since no SolidWorks dimension stores a default deviation (§8.1). Decides the SolidWorks decoder's `decimals` on a PMI dimension with no DimXpert record; until then it states `decimals` from the DimXpert record and `None` where there is none (§8). Would settle it: the `DimSemData` records of SolidWorks parts joined to their DimXpert dimensions by value and kind, each `valPrecision` set against its `BlockToleranceDecimalPlaces` and the drawing's displayed places.
216. **Creo corner and patch rows no reader frames.** The Creo readings that §6.4's corners and blend patches rest on and that no reader frames or agrees on (§6.4). A junction row with an implicit count stays unframed, its walk stopping at the openers `40`, `07`, `e7`, `1e`, and `04` inside spline arrays; a type-40 `splsrf` junction row is not framed; sphere rows' frame blocks stop at the openers `1e`, `04`, or `e7` or at a `local_sys` head, their sphere tails read; type-44 rows that are `against` for fillets read as a planar two-point cubic, extruded, which the ball stays clear of, and frame as rows on one and as columns on another; inside spline arrays `4b` is seven bytes under `3f b0`, not `3f c0`, and `a4` seven bytes under `bf c0`, not `bf cf`, which give unit tangents; on the patch records `1e` is eight bytes under `bc`, `1c` a four-byte near-zero form in a plane's frame, a named cylinder row's axis its local system's column 3, where the format document's cross-product rule gives the wrong axis, `ruled_srf` rows positional replays of the prototype's local system, height, and two arcs, a plane row's `e3` found only at a token boundary, and a cylinder of R 276.625 that a reader reads as R 2; the patch faces' stored derivative arrays read several ways, so their tangency to the end piece is not read; faces that one reader counts as on the plane in `against` and another reads as not tangent to it are `Native("creo:12")` either way (§6.4). The straight-fillet distance and the tagged plane frame are reader faults, and a cylinder from these readings counts only where a fit confirms it. Open: the rows above unframed; the patches' tangency to their end pieces; the decoder's own reading of the faces readers disagree on. Decides the Creo decoder's frames for these rows; until then the corners they carry are `Native("creo:12")` or `Native("creo:7")` with their stored faces, and the code-2 records with patches `Native("creo:2")` (§6.4). Would settle it: the implicit-count and type-40 rows read with a framing that closes their walks; the type-44 frames set against the faces they carry; the patch faces' derivative arrays read one way that agrees on every sample; the faces readers disagree on graded with the decoder's reader.
217. **Document names outside SolidWorks.** What the document name of a definition stored as a file is in formats other than SolidWorks, which `source_name` and `PartNumber::DocumentName` read (§5.11, §8.1). For SolidWorks the name without its extension is inferred from a design-table cell equal to the file's stem. A Creo file name carries two suffixes (`name.prt.3`), so "without its extension" has two readings there, and no other format's stored name is set against its file. Decides each decoder's `source_name` outside SolidWorks; until then §8.1's rule as stated. Would settle it: per format, the stored strings that name a definition's own file (a design-table cell, an assembly's reference, a drawing's model reference) set against the file's name.
218. **Fusion bend and unfold readings.** The Fusion readings of a bend's angle sign and stationary face and of an unfold's references (§6.6). A bend's angle keeps its sign, and what a negative angle bends is not established; one of a bend's face groups is read as its stationary face, and an unfold's reference groups as its bend faces and its stationary face and its control as selected or all bends, none set against a stored state. Decides the Fusion decoder's `angle` on a bend with a negative angle, `fixed_side`, and the unfold's `fixed` and `bends`; until then `angle: None` with `f3d:bend_angle`, `fixed_side: None` with `f3d:bend_stationary`, and `Unread` picks with the stored references in `Selection.native` and `f3d:unfold_all_bends`. Would settle it: bends of one line with angles of each sign and each side kept, and unfolds with selected and all bends, their stored faces set against the readings.
219. **Fusion path pattern readings.** The Fusion readings of a path pattern's reordered settings record and of a role-`0x4` seed (§6.5). The decoder reads a settings record of the reordered form at the offsets of the 267-byte form, so its distance-type, flip, and orientation bytes are read on an assumption; it reads a role-`0x4` seed member's compact identity as a feature index, which can also match a topology identity. Decides the Fusion decoder's spacing, `sides`, and `orientation` for the reordered form, and its pick of such a seed; until then `Spacing::Native("f3d:path_spacing")`, `sides: None`, and `orientation: None` with the count, the distance, and the bytes as native options, and a `Native` pick with the seed's stored identity. Would settle it: reordered-form patterns with feature and face seeds whose identities collide.
220. **Fusion contour flange readings.** The Fusion readings of a contour flange's thickness side and of its bend radius where it stores no `BendRadius` (§6.6). The decoder reads Fusion's API's documented SideOne default as the profile's left, and the linked rule's first entry as the inside bend radius; neither is set against a stored state. Decides the Fusion decoder's side of `thickness` and its `bend.radius`; until then `side: None`, and `bend.radius: None` with the native option `f3d:contour_flange_rule_radius`. Would settle it: the stored Fusion contour flanges whose thickness side or rule radius takes each value, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading: their stored faces set against the readings; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
221. **Fusion rule K-factor.** Which stored value of a Fusion sheet-metal rule is its K-factor (§6.6). The decoder reads it as the finite scalar that opens the rule's material trailer, before the material name; no stored file sets that scalar against the K-factor the rule was saved with or against a governed bend's flat length. Decides the Fusion decoder's `allowance`, `BendAllowance::KFactor` from that scalar; until then `allowance: None` with the native option `f3d:rule_k_factor`. Would settle it: the stored Fusion sheet-metal rules whose K-factor takes each value, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading: the scalar set against the value set, and the flat lengths of their governed bends set against it; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
222. **Bare numbers beside a quantity where the source declares a unit.** Whether a bare number that is an operand beside a quantity, in an NX formula or in a Creo relation that creates a parameter with a declared unit, is read in the declared unit or in the part's unit, and whether Creo's units-sensitivity setting for relations changes it (§5.13). The decoder reads the declared unit under Rule H1. NX stores no evaluated value for a formula, and no Creo parameter the decoder reads from a stored file known to the project declares a unit, so neither reading is tested, and such a tree is `Source` until the reading meets Rule H1's floor. Would settle it: an NX part whose formula adds a bare number to a parameter of another unit and drives a dimension, set against its geometry; a Creo model whose relation declares a unit on a parameter that a dimension then reads, set against the dimension's stored value.
223. **A reference to a parameter of another document.** How CATIA, NX, SolidWorks, and FreeCAD store a reference to a parameter of a document that was not read. No stored file known to the project holds one. Open: whether CATIA and NX hold it as a local parameter with its own declared type and stored value (a CATIA external parameter, an NX interpart expression), and whether a SolidWorks assembly's equation manager stores a number beside a component's dimension that a line reads, as it does beside the part's own. Decides whether the decoder states the reference as a source parameter's whole expression or mints the parameter, and whether a minted parameter has a `value` (§5.12, §5.13); until then a decoder states what its file shows, and mints a parameter with no `value` where the source names the reference inside a longer expression. Would settle it: per format, one file that reads a parameter of another document, decoded without that document.
224. **Expression-bound properties not yet read.** An NX part attribute linked to an expression (§5.12): no stored file shows that the attribute's type and the expression's value are stored, so a decoder does not mint this parameter from that link. A Rhino user-text formula (`%<…>%`) is `AttributeValue::String` until a stored file shows what it evaluates to. Would settle it: an NX part whose attribute is linked to an expression, its attribute record read against the expression's stored value; a Rhino model whose user-text formula's value is known.
225. **Evaluation order of `and` and `or`.** Whether CATIA, Creo, NX, and FreeCAD skip the right operand of `and` or `or` once the left decides the result (§5.13). `docs/formats/catia.md` reads CATIA's as skipping; no stored file known to the project holds a guard whose skipped operand fails, so the reading is untested, and no reading is made for the others. Decides whether a decoder translates `a and b` as `if(a, b, false)` and `a or b` as `if(a, true, b)`. Until then `and` and `or` translate as themselves, and an expression whose skipped operand fails in the document's evaluation keeps the cache the source stores. Would settle it: per format, a stored file whose `and` or `or` guards an operand that fails at the stored inputs, with the expression's stored cache, or a vendor page that states the order.
226. **Fusion split tool extension law.** By which law Fusion continues a cut whose tool stops inside the target (§6.5). Decides `ToolExtension::Extended.method` for Fusion; until then `None`. Would settle it: a stored split whose tool is a freeform face that ends inside the target, its added edges read against the tool's carrier.
227. **Creo hole intersect id.** The `geometry1_id` of a type-76 instruction on a Creo assembly hole whose display level is top level and that no `ASMCUT_COPY` names itself. On an assembly cut the same level stores that id as the copy's key. No feature of the participant's part carries it. Decides what the id names (§6.7); until then the participant is `Instances` and the id is the feature's native option `creo:intersect_id`. Would settle it: one such hole whose id joins a record of the assembly or of the part.
228. **Creo pattern member with no intersect instruction.** That a member of a patterned Creo assembly feature that holds no intersect instruction cuts its leader's participants, at the leader's levels (§6.7). Under `pat_type` bit 8 the `ASMCUT_COPY` that names the leader holds the surfaces of every member, a member with no instruction among them. No stored file known to the project holds such a member under another pattern option, or under a leader with a part-level participant. Decides the participants the Creo decoder states for such a member; until then the leader's. Would settle it: the stored patterned Creo assembly cuts with a part-level participant whose regeneration option takes each value, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading: with the participant's part; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
229. **Rhino history commands.** Which command each stored command id names, other than Loft, and what its values state (§6.3). A record stores the id and no name, and the project has read the values of no other command. Decides which Rhino history records are typed; until then each is a `Native` operation named by its id. Would settle it: the stored Rhino history records whose command takes each value, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading: with the record each stores; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
230. **Rhino shared descendants.** Whether a Rhino file can hold one object among the descendants of two history records, which record then regenerates it, and what deleting one of the records does to it (§5.2, §5.5). No stored file known to the project holds one. Decides the Rhino decoder's current states for such an object; until then it is unproduced, with a loss naming the object and the records. Would settle it: the stored Rhino files that hold a shared descendant, their stored results (the state after each, and the state before where stored) set against each reading: each record's input and result set against each reading; where no stored file holds one, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds one.
231. **CATIA unset parameters.** Whether CATIA lists a parameter whose stored evaluation is unset and that no formula, rule, or table sets, and what a formula that reads it evaluates to (§5.12). `ParameterDefinition::Unset` is typed from the stored form of an unset evaluation (`docs/formats/catia.md`); no stored file known to the project holds one. Decides which CATIA parameters the decoder states `Unset`, and what writers write for them; until then the decoder states `Unset` for each such stored form. Would settle it: the stored CATIA parts holding a parameter that a formula reads, set and unset, the formula's records set against each reading; where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
232. **STEP styled geometric sets.** Whether a style that a STEP file assigns to a `GEOMETRIC_SET` is shown on the set's members that state no style of their own (§5.6). Decides the STEP decoder's member colours; until then the set's style stays in its native record, and the decoder charges a loss naming the set. Would settle it: the CAx-IF recommended practice for styling geometric sets, or a file with a styled set shown in two STEP readers whose source is public.
233. **Assembly appearance order across a placement.** Which way an outer statement stands against what a placed part states, in formats whose pages do not construct it: a Fusion occurrence's or root component's appearance override (an Autodesk developer: "the lower level appearance wins, but that is just a general rule"; a user's test shows a body's assigned appearance through a root override); an Inventor design view representation's appearance override (About Appearances states the order inside a part and the per-occurrence scope; a user reports a whole-occurrence override); an NX specific component colour (a Siemens employee: "Component Colour Overrides Part Colour"; the face case is unstated); a Creo component's and an assembly's own appearance (a community answer, which PTC's About Applying Appearances to Assemblies does not state); and a Rhino block member whose colour source is its parent instance (`docs/formats/rhino_3dm.md`), where another member takes its colour from its layer (§8). The candidate readings are `Nearest` for Fusion and for a Creo assembly's own appearance, `Outer` for Inventor, NX, and a Creo component's appearance, and for Rhino an `Occurrence` binding with `Nearest`, which is true only where every other member states a colour. Decides those decoders' `Occurrence`, `Definition`, and path-qualified bindings and `ArrangementAppearance` entries, and their `precedence`. Until then a decoder states none of them, and the part's own colours resolve. Would settle it: the stored display state set against the record, over the stored files that hold each value: the stored assemblies whose component carries an appearance override, the stored colours set against the part's own. Where every stored file holds one value, the fact stays unestablished until a stored file holds another.
234. **A STEP instance's or part's style, and an IGES owner's colour.** Whether a STEP context-dependent overriding style on a component instance shows over the styles of that component's own solids and faces (the recommended practice states the top-down rule for an assembly node, and for an instance only that it overrides the component's own style item, §5.1), and whether a style on a part's shape representation ranks below that part's solids (§4.2.1's priority list puts the component part above solids; the SolidWorks exports measured show the body's appearance). And which entities the colour of an IGES subfigure instance reaches under each value of its hierarchy status (applied to its subordinates, deferred to them, or set per attribute by a hierarchy property). Decides the `precedence` of the STEP decoder's instance bindings, the rank of its `Definition` bindings, and whether the IGES decoder states an instance's colour as an `Occurrence` binding. Until then the STEP decoder states `Outer` for an instance's style and a part's style as a `Definition` binding, and the IGES decoder states none. Would settle it: for STEP, one file with an instance style over a component whose faces are styled, and one with a styled part and styled solids, each shown in two systems whose source is public and that implement the practice; for IGES, one file whose coloured instance applies its attributes to a definition with coloured members.
235. **ASM support pcurve fit.** Whether the support pcurves of an ACIS intersection curve lie within the curve's stored fit tolerance of the intersection, and whether a support surface's fit tolerance bounds the distance between points of one parameter or only between the surfaces (§5.6, part 10 Coincidence). In Fusion and Inventor files a support pcurve that states no fit tolerance can end farther from the solved curve than the sum of the stated fits. Decides whether the ACIS-family decoders state a fit tolerance on an intersection curve's support pcurves; until then they state none, and the end-point check is a Warning there. Would settle it: intersection curves both of whose supports the IR holds in closed form, each support pcurve's image measured along its length against the intersection of the two surfaces and set against the curve's fit tolerance.

## Annex A. Record types stated by schema

Each type below is given by the JSON Schema of its wire form, generated from the reference implementation when this document was released and frozen with it; a change to it is a change of wire (§3.6). The declared order of a type below (§2.5, Order) is the order in which the reference implementation declares the fields and variants of its wire form. An object's `properties` and its `required` list, and a `oneOf`'s variants, are listed in that order. Each type's description states every condition a reader enforces on its values (§2.8). §5.6 states the evaluation of the analytic, NURBS, polyline, and placed carriers. A procedural definition is stated by its fields: this document states no evaluation for it beyond the solved carrier its record caches (D23).

  "description": "Document-wide provenance and exactness tables keyed by annotation key.\n\nThe key of a top-level entity is its globally unique entity id. The key\nof a record inside the delta of an evaluation or a process state is the\nid of that evaluation or process state, one space, and the record's id.\nValidation reports a key whose qualifier names no evaluation or process\nstate with a delta, or whose record that delta does not hold, as it\nreports a key that names no entity.\n\nAn entity absent from `exactness` is byte-exact.",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {

### `SourceFidelity`

```json
{
  "description": "Decode-time source digests, annotations, and retained native records.\n\nRetained identities are admitted only through checked insertion.\n\n```compile_fail\nuse cadmpeg_ir::hash::digest::Sha256Digest;\nlet mut fidelity = cadmpeg_ir::SourceFidelity::new(Sha256Digest::digest(b\"source\"));\nfidelity.retained_records().clear();\n```",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "decode_digest": {
      "description": "SHA-256 of the decode's root file.",
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Sha256Digest"
    },
    "file_digests": {
      "description": "SHA-256 of each component file, keyed by its `File` definition.",
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "patternProperties": {
        "^[a-z0-9]+:[^:#\\u0009-\\u000d\\u0020\\u0085\\u00a0\\u1680\\u2000-\\u200a\\u2028\\u2029\\u202f\\u205f\\u3000]+:[^:#\\u0009-\\u000d\\u0020\\u0085\\u00a0\\u1680\\u2000-\\u200a\\u2028\\u2029\\u202f\\u205f\\u3000]+#[^#\\u0009-\\u000d\\u0020\\u0085\\u00a0\\u1680\\u2000-\\u200a\\u2028\\u2029\\u202f\\u205f\\u3000]+(?![\\s\\S])": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Sha256Digest"
        }
      }
    },
    "content_digest": {
      "description": "SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the document the decode returned,\nabsent where that document has no canonical JSON.",
      "default": null,
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Sha256Digest"
    },
    "codec_digests": {
      "description": "The decoding codec's narrower digests, keyed as its format\nspecification lists.",
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "patternProperties": {
        "[^\\u0009-\\u000d\\u0020\\u0085\\u00a0\\u1680\\u2000-\\u200a\\u2028\\u2029\\u202f\\u205f\\u3000]": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Sha256Digest"
        }
      }
    },
    "unrepresented": {
      "description": "Union of the retained records' untyped classes.",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Sparse source locations and conversion exactness.",
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Annotations"
    },
    "retained_records": {
      "description": "Native records retained for recovery or replay, keyed by record id.",
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "patternProperties": {
        "^[a-z0-9]+:[^:#\\u0009-\\u000d\\u0020\\u0085\\u00a0\\u1680\\u2000-\\u200a\\u2028\\u2029\\u202f\\u205f\\u3000]+:[^:#\\u0009-\\u000d\\u0020\\u0085\\u00a0\\u1680\\u2000-\\u200a\\u2028\\u2029\\u202f\\u205f\\u3000]+#[^#\\u0009-\\u000d\\u0020\\u0085\\u00a0\\u1680\\u2000-\\u200a\\u2028\\u2029\\u202f\\u205f\\u3000]+(?![\\s\\S])": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/RetainedSourceRecord"
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "decode_digest",
    "file_digests",
    "codec_digests",
    "unrepresented",
    "annotations",
    "retained_records"
  ]
}
```
